Experiments show that \ours~consistently outperforms strong retrieval-based and DCI baselines, while demonstrating robust cross-lingual generalization and substantially reducing redundant corpus interactions.
authors: Rui Qi;Yunlong Liang;Yufeng Chen;Jinan Xu;Fandong Meng;Kaiyu Huang

title: EventHOI: Event-Driven Resource-Efficient Hand-Object Interaction Logging on Smartglasses
abstract: Hand-object interactions (HOIs) can be captured by smartglasses to learn how people manipulate objects in daily life. Automatic logging of these interactions from an egocentric perspective provides time-stamped evidence of daily actions for applications like memory assistance. However, continuous RGB capture and wireless transmission exceed the energy and bandwidth budgets of smartglasses. We present EventHOI, an event-driven sensing and compression system that couples selective RGB capture with HOI-aware encoding to enable egocentric logging over Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) while preserving downstream HOI logging performance. Our key insight is to use low-power event sensing both to determine when RGB capture is needed and to identify where visual detail must be preserved. A lightweight IMU-based egomotion cancellation pipeline suppresses egomotion-induced events so that residual HOI motion can guide RGB triggering and spatial compression. We build a smartglasses prototype and conduct an end-to-end evaluation of EventHOI on a 50-hour egocentric benchmark with 97 subjects and a 20-hour real-world dataset we collect from 10 participants, together covering a broad range of daily-life scenarios and environments. Compared to RGB-only baselines, EventHOI reduces always-on backend power consumption by 5.8-10.4x and uplink bandwidth by 2.9x, with minimal HOI recognition accuracy loss. The resulting RGB uplink of less than 130 kbps fits within commodity BLE bandwidth budgets, making stable BLE video streaming feasible for egocentric HOI logging. Demo video and project website: https://eventhoi.github.io
authors: Le Zhang;Kailai Cui;Hao Chen;Vlad Roznyatovskiy;Jianzhong Zhang;Anhong Guo;Kang G. Shin;Ke Sun

title: URL-Sim: Unified and Regulated LiDAR Simulation for High-Fidelity Reconstruction of Dynamic Driving Scenes
abstract: Reconstructing high-fidelity LiDAR simulation scenes from real-world driving logs is essential for cost-effective safety validation of autonomous driving systems. While simulators based on Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) achieve realistic scene reconstruction, their large-scale adoption is limited by slow rendering speeds. Recent 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) approaches have improved rendering efficiency through explicit primitive representation and differentiable rasterization. However, existing 3DGS-based methods remain largely restricted to rigid vehicles and produce redundant primitives through unconstrained densification. To address these limitations, we propose URL-Sim, a unified and regulated dynamic LiDAR simulation framework. URL-Sim constructs a dynamic Gaussian scene graph that decouples the modeling of traffic participants, including vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists, enabling accurate reconstruction of heterogeneous dynamic objects within a single framework. It further introduces a regulated Gaussian densification strategy that ranks primitives with multi-dimensional importance scores and allocates Gaussians to the most critical regions while keeping the total primitive count bounded. Experiments on the Waymo and KITTI-360 datasets demonstrate that URL-Sim achieves higher quantitative accuracy and visual quality than existing baselines under comparable primitive budgets, and accurately recovers the geometry and poses of diverse dynamic traffic participants.
authors: Kefei Qian;Xipeng Feng;Jie Li;Long Cao;Yuhan Chen;Xiangfei Huang;Guofa Li

title: SEDust: A DUSTY-Based SED-Fitting Pipeline for Dust and Mass-Loss from AGB and LPV Stars
abstract: We present SEDust, an automated pipeline for spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting and the estimation of stellar mass-loss and dust-production rates. We apply this pipeline to quantify the mass-loss and dust injection rates in the dwarf galaxy NGC~6822, focusing on long-period variables (LPVs) and pulsating asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars as major contributors to dust feedback into the interstellar medium. The total stellar mass-loss rate is found to be $(3.70 \pm 1.16) \times 10^{-3}\ M_{\odot} \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. Two alternative methods (an LPV-based estimate and DESK) give totals that differ from this value by factors of $\sim$2.3 (lower) and $\sim$2.4 (higher), respectively, which we adopt as an estimate of the method-dependent systematic uncertainty. A positive correlation between stellar luminosity, intrinsic reddening caused by circumstellar dust self-extinction, and mass-loss rate is observed. The specific mass-return rate from AGB stars is $(7.40 \pm 2.30) \times 10^{-11}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, indicating that mass return from AGB stars alone is insufficient to sustain the current star formation rate of NGC~6822. This result implies the need for external gas accretion or additional mass-return mechanisms.
authors: Hamidreza Mahani;Narges Rostami;Atefeh Javadi;Hedieh Abdollahi;Jacco Th. van Loon;Francisca Kemper;Alvaro Sanchez-Monge

title: The Invisible Gap: Romanized Indic Generation Fails Where Automatic Metrics Succeed
abstract: Hundreds of millions of Indians communicate with digital systems in romanized Latin characters -- typing "aap kaise hain" rather than native script -- yet romanized Indic generation is absent from NLP benchmarks and evaluation frameworks. We demonstrate that automatic metrics (BGE-M3, BERTScore) systematically misrepresent the quality of romanized Hindi, Telugu, and Kannada generation. We evaluate four LLMs (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 2.5-flash, Qwen3.5-35B) on 142 OpenAssistant query-response pairs. On a 72-response diagnostic subset, native speakers rate GPT-5.5 1.43 points higher than Claude Opus 4.8 on a 12-point rubric, whereas their full-dataset BGE-M3 means differ by only 0.004. Two distinct model-specific failure modes emerge: Gemini produces script spillage (16.9% of Telugu responses leak native script), while Qwen collapses to English-only output (16.2% of Kannada responses). We introduce a failure-aware evaluation policy that assigns zero to empty outputs, script-corrupted responses, and instruction collapses -- revealing failures metrics alone cannot detect. Our results show that evaluating romanized Indic generation requires a coordinated bundle: semantic similarity, script compliance, failure coverage, and native-speaker acceptability.
authors: Madhu Sudhan Rao Beesetty;Surbhi Sharma;Devesh Maheshwari;Lokesh Meesala
comment: 11 pages, 2 figures, 5 tables. All authors contributed equally

title: Training-Free Active Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language Models
abstract: Test-time adaptation (TTA) for vision-language models (VLMs) is usually studied in a fully unsupervised regime, where adaptation relies on pseudo-labels, confidence scores, or entropy computed by the model itself. This is a severe restriction on hard shifted samples: the model is asked to repair its own uncertain predictions without any external evidence. At the other extreme, supervised online adaptation assumes labels can directly train or correct the model. We study the intermediate deployment regime between these two extremes. In Active Test-time Adaptation for VLMs (Active VLM-TTA), a pretrained VLM may spend an explicit labeling budget on selected test samples, but the prediction for the current sample must be emitted before its label can be used; queried labels are therefore costed, delayed evidence for future samples rather than free correction for the present one. Under this future-only constraint, the central question is how to reuse sparse labels conservatively. We instantiate this setting with ACTive VLM-TTA for Online Retrieval (ACTOR), a training-free plug-in module that routes uncertain samples among base prediction, label query, and memory-based correction using a consistency-and-reliability check over previously queried labels. Across ten cross-domain benchmarks and a domain-transfer benchmark based on ImageNet, ACTOR consistently improves strong VLM-TTA baselines on ResNet and ViT backbones with negligible inference overhead. Our implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/kaist-dmlab/ACTOR.

title: Strong phonon-coupled trion emission in Janus homobilayer
abstract: Janus transition metal dichalcogenides with broken mirror symmetry provide a novel platform for exploring many-body effects mediated by spin-valley-phonon interactions. Strong electron-phonon coupling demands a precise match between a strong effective dipole moment and nanometer-scale charge confinement. Here, we report thermally robust and enhanced trion emission in a symmetric bilayer WSeS with an S/S stacking configuration. The inward-pointing antiparallel built-in electric fields induce a strong electron confinement effect at the interface, driving dominant trion emission at cryogenic temperatures. Furthermore, a massive electron-phonon coupling strength (3.9) resonant with the optical phonon A_1^2 energy (51 meV) contributes to the thermal stability of this trion emission at elevated temperatures. By tailoring the interfacial architecture in Janus WSeS homobilayers, this study overcomes the thermal decoherence limits inherent to traditional semiconductor systems, offering novel insights into room-temperature many-body interactions.
authors: Tianyishan Sun;Dingkun Bi;Haonan Wang;Hiroto Ogura;Yanlin Gao;Mina Maruyama;Susumu Okada;Shiro Entani;Kenji Watanabe;Takashi Taniguchi;Kazunari Matsuda;Toshiaki Kato

title: Quantum-Enhanced Classical Communications for DPMZM-based NG-PON2 Systems
abstract: This paper presents a framework for integrating quantum detection techniques into a Dual-Parallel Mach-Zehnder Modulator (DPMZM)-based Next Generation Passive Optical Network 2 (NG-PON2) communication system. We present a system model for the DPMZM-based NG-PON2 quantum communication system and characterize its signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), demonstrating its superiority over conventional MZM-based systems. We analyze the performance of various quantum modulation techniques, including binary phase-shift keying, quadrature phase-shift keying, and M-ary quadrature amplitude modulation. A comprehensive analytical framework is developed to evaluate the SNR, BER, and mutual information for both classical and quantum detection schemes within the DPMZM-based NG-PON2 quantum communication system. Our simulation results show that quantum detection significantly outperforms classical detection, and the DPMZM architecture further enhances the performance over the baseline MZM architecture by improving the effective modulation efficiency and receiver sensitivity.
authors: Parvin Kumar;Sourav Banerjee;Neel Kanth Kundu;Umesh Sharma

title: GlobalPuzzle: Globally Informed Genetic Search for Eroded Jigsaw Puzzle Reassembly
abstract: Jigsaw puzzle reassembly remains a highly challenging task, particularly when piece boundaries are irregularly eroded to simulate damage to cultural artifacts. On the GAP benchmark, existing methods achieve a perfect assembly accuracy of only 0.3% on $5 \times 5$ puzzles, whereas humans can solve jigsaw puzzles with remarkably high accuracy. Humans typically approach puzzle solving by identifying potentially adjacent pieces, evaluating the current assembly, and iteratively performing complex operations such as adding pieces, replacing incorrectly placed pieces, and moving entire connected groups of pieces. However, existing methods face a fundamental limitation: approaches that leverage global visual information typically predict piece arrangements directly, making it difficult to explicitly perform such complex iterative operations, while search based methods can rearrange pieces but primarily rely on pairwise boundary compatibility, lacking global visual information to evaluate and guide the search process. To bridge this gap, we propose GlobalPuzzle, a jigsaw puzzle reassembly framework that integrates global canvas level evaluation, action guidance, and genetic search. By incorporating global visual information into the evaluation and optimization of candidate assemblies, GlobalPuzzle aims to resolve ambiguous adjacency relationships that are difficult to determine from irregularly eroded piece boundaries alone, enabling flexible, globally informed reconstruction.
comment: 22 pages (10 pages main paper and 12 pages supplementary material), 16 figures

title: Large Language Model Deployment on Resource-Constrained Edge Devices: A Practitioners Survey
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed many areas of artificial intelligence (AI), but their substantial resource requirements limit their deployment on mobile and edge devices. Although LLMs have demonstrated impressive capabilities in various applications, the next challenge is deploying these models on resource-limited edge devices. Recent innovations in software optimizations and specialized hardware have made it feasible to deploy LLMs on edge devices. Edge deployment offers benefits including local data processing, cost savings, reduced latency, and personalized responses. This paper reviews the latest techniques that make the deployment of LLMs on edge devices feasible.
authors: Rahul Maliakkal;Yashasvi Makin;Plawan Rath;Rohit Jain;Ankur Sadhoo

title: Emo-LiveSync: Real-Time Universal Lip Synchronization with Explicit Emotion Control
abstract: Lip synchronization, the task of generating realistic lip movements synchronized with audio signals, is fundamental to applications such as film dubbing, virtual avatars, and digital content creation. Recent GAN-based methods offer computational efficiency but often lack visual fidelity, while diffusion-based approaches achieve high-quality results at the cost of substantial computational overhead. Moreover, most existing methods are limited to photo-realistic human faces, restricting their applicability to stylized characters and non-human entities. In this paper, we propose an efficient universal lip-sync video generation framework that achieves high-quality results without compromising computational efficiency. We build on LivePortrait, a warp-based portrait animation model, and introduce a training strategy that aligns audio signals to an implicit motion space by distilling knowledge from a pre-trained video-to-motion model. This enables real-time inference while maintaining high visual fidelity, and naturally generalizes to diverse stylistic characters beyond photo-realistic humans. Furthermore, we introduce an expressive control gate that enables explicit manipulation of emotional expressions for content enrichment. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in both visual quality and lip-sync accuracy while ensuring real-time inference.

title: UniRGBA: Unifying RGB and Alpha in Pretrained Video Diffusion Models
abstract: Recent advances in video diffusion models have achieved remarkable photorealistic RGB synthesis, yet generating videos with a native alpha channel remains an open challenge. Existing approaches often rely on matting-style data and non-native RGBA designs, causing them to specialize in real-object scenes and to degrade severely on visual-effect content whose semi-transparency is spatially non-local and non-elliptical. We present UniRGBA, a unified framework whose key insight is that RGBA generation does not require a dedicated alpha encoder or complex latent-space restructuring---a minimal, targeted extension of the existing RGB pathway is sufficient. UniRGBA-VAE extends a causal video VAE to 4-channel RGBA via zero-initialized channel expansion, symmetric selective layer unfreezing (5% trainable), and a six-term progressive reconstruction loss anchored by a KL reference loss that prevents latent drift, followed by a two-stage schedule that introduces a lightweight GAN objective. We then apply standard DoRA to the pretrained DiT, reusing the unified 4-channel latent without any alpha-specific architectural changes. On a visual-effect RGBA benchmark, UniRGBA substantially outperforms Wan-Alpha on RGBA reconstruction while preserving RGB fidelity. For generation, UniRGBA outperforms Wan-Alpha on RGBA text-to-video tasks and matches or surpasses the original pretrained Wan2.1 backbone on RGB-only metrics, demonstrating that native alpha support can be integrated without compromising the underlying RGB prior or the model's architectural versatility.

title: Does Reasoning Improve Psychological Depth in Large Language Models?
abstract: Benchmark gains from reasoning-enhanced large language models encourage the assumption that these models should broadly perform better on complex generative tasks, but this remains underexplored in open-ended, creative domains shaped by nuances of reader experience. We tested this assumption through the lens of psychological depth in short stories. We compared DeepSeek-R1 vs. DeepSeek-V3, our closest available contrast for reasoning-oriented post-training, and GPT-5 vs. GPT-4o, through 60 blinded pairwise evaluations in which seven human annotators and an ensemble LLM-as-a-Judge rated prompt-matched story outputs. Human evaluations showed no universal reasoning advantage: GPT-5 was slightly preferred over GPT-4o (60.0-62.9% across two reasoning-effort settings), whereas DeepSeek-R1 fell behind DeepSeek-V3 (42.9%). Although this pattern was marked by low inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff's $α= 0.070$), our annotation-quality checks suggested genuine evaluative subjectivity, plausibly reflecting distinct annotator decision schemes rather than annotation failure. In contrast, the LLM-as-a-Judge showed a strong pro-reasoning bias (98.3% of pairs vs. 55.2% of human votes), consistent across its five configurations and partly tracking sentence length. These findings suggest that, at the frontier, reasoning-related quality differences are small enough to be dominated by reader subjectivity, and that LLM-as-a-Judge evaluators can obscure this subjectivity in nuanced creative-generation tasks.
authors: Ruichen Zheng;Yihe Wang;Fabrice Harel-Canada;Sara Khosravi;Zeynep Senahan Yildiz;Amit Sahai;Nanyun Peng

title: Fair Selection of Generalized Nash Equilibria: A Comparability Perspective
abstract: Generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problems model self-interested agents coupled through their costs and shared constraints, and arise throughout control applications that allocate a scarce common resource. Such problems typically admit a continuum of equilibria, so any implementation must \emph{select} one. This selection is not neutral: it decides how the cost of the shared constraint is distributed among the agents, a decision often expected to be fair. The variational GNE (v-GNE), which charges all agents a uniform shadow price, is the conventional choice and is frequently advocated as fair. Through the lens of \emph{comparability} from social choice theory, we show that the GNE set itself requires no inter-agent comparability of costs, whereas the v-GNE implicitly assumes cardinal unit comparability, one of the stronger notions. We then introduce the fair GNE (f-GNE), which selects an equilibrium by explicitly optimizing a fairness metric matched to the comparability at hand, and give constructive routes to compute it for single-constraint and linear-quadratic games. An electric-vehicle charging game serves as a running example throughout this self-contained tutorial.
comment: Book chapter, 25 pages, 4 figures. To appear in Socio-Inspired and Socially Aware Control for Complex Systems, Springer

title: ProtoCouncil: Multi-Encoder Anatomical Prototypes for Prostate Cancer Detection in Micro-Ultrasound
abstract: Purpose: Micro-ultrasound ($μ$US) is a promising modality for prostate cancer (PCa) detection, but identifying suspicious tissue depends heavily on clinical experience. Models trained on sparse, noisy core-level pathology offer little insight into their decisions and can fail under domain shift. Clinical use needs a traceable decision process and a flag for uncertain predictions. Methods: We introduce ProtoCouncil, in which three foundation encoders (MedSAM, DINOv3 and V-JEPA 2.1) learn case-based prototypes at three anatomical levels: whole gland, needle track and gland sectors. Prototypes are projected onto real training-core regions, and label-free fusion keeps every class logit as a bias plus an exact sum of prototype similarity contributions. Encoder disagreement triggers selective prediction. Results: In five-fold patient-level cross-validation (6,588 cores, 693 patients), ProtoCouncil reaches 82.9% AUROC for clinically significant PCa (csPCa, Grade Group $\geq$3), 4.3 points above the best previously published method. In zero-shot evaluation on two external cohorts, ProtoCouncil achieves higher all-cancer and csPCa AUROC than all previous methods. Nearest same-class exemplars match test-core tumor involvement better than random same-class cases. Externally, csPCa accuracy falls from 79% when encoders agree to 27% when two oppose the fused call. Abstaining on disagreement raises balanced accuracy by 7 and 15 points, while retaining 58% and 54% of the cores. Conclusion: ProtoCouncil grounds core-level predictions in exact similarity-based evidence from real, anatomically indexed training cases, which makes its reasoning interpretable. It achieves the highest csPCa AUROC across three cohorts and identifies unreliable predictions through encoder disagreement.
authors: Mohammad Mahdi Abootorabi;Nooshin Maghsoodi;Armin Saadat;Obed Dzikunu;Zhuoxin Guo;Hannes Cash;Ferdinand Luger;Adam Kinnaird;Brian Wodlinger;Parvin Mousavi;Purang Abolmaesumi

title: Real-Time Short-Response Selection for Spoken Dialogue Systems
abstract: To realize spoken dialogue systems that can interact naturally with users, it is important for the system to respond to user utterances at appropriate timings. To achieve such natural turn-taking, the system needs not only to predict appropriate response timings but also to mask delays caused by language generation and speech synthesis so that they are not perceived by the user. We propose a real-time short-response selection task that can be integrated with existing turn-taking models to mask generation delay. To address this task, the proposed model learns the mapping between dialogue context and short responses using contrastive learning. When a turn-taking event is detected, the system selects a response from a set of pre-generated candidates. The selected response is played while the main response is being generated. Experimental results show that the proposed method learns to select short responses based on dialogue context, outperforming random and LLM-based baselines. Moreover, integrating response selection maintained turn-taking prediction performance and added minimal processing overhead.

title: OmniLatent: Unified Latent for 3D Part Modeling
abstract: 3D part decomposition is a central capability for editable asset creation, yet existing workflows typically segment a completed mesh as a post-processing step, making the result sensitive to geometric artifacts, texture ambiguity, and limited part-level annotations. We present OmniLatent, a unified latent modeling framework for 3D part decomposition. Instead of predicting part labels in isolation, OmniLatent learns a shared latent space that jointly encodes geometry, deformation, appearance, and binary part IDs, allowing data-rich geometric and visual priors to support data-scarce part learning. Given a single input image, the base model generates geometry, deformation, texture, and surface part IDs in one pass, producing a part-aware 3D asset without a separate segmentation stage. We further tune the pretrained model for two extensions: a point-prompt adapter that maps arbitrary 3D point prompts with binary part IDs into latent tokens for full segmentation, refinement, and part subdivision, and an amodal part completion model that completes partial surface masks into a coherent full-object decomposition through dynamic per-part token allocation, cross-attention to the given geometry latent, and alternating part-local and global attention. Extensive experiments show that OmniLatent produces semantically meaningful part segmentations with precise boundaries, supports interactive part editing, and completes partial part observations while preserving global object consistency.
authors: Yunhan Yang;Yunfei Zhao;Zeqiang Lai;Jiachen Xu;Minxiu Wang;Xintong Han;Xiangyu Yue;Xihui Liu;Chunchao Guo

title: Resolvent-Diagonal Energy of Isospectral Jacobi Matrices
abstract: We study the minimum squared resolvent diagonal among Jacobi matrices with prescribed eigenvalues. For the zeros of $P_n^{(α,β)}$, we construct a canonical realization and bound its asymptotic cost against the optimum. Its rescaled inverse converges to the Green operator of a reflection-symmetric singular Schrödinger operator with Bessel-zero spectrum. A Green-coordinate identity places this construction and all finite realizations in the same density framework. Mass-constrained spectral problems then give computable lower bounds. The bounds meet at $α=1/2$, with optimal energy $2/15$, and have first-order contact with derivative $-13/75$. We classify the constrained extremal profiles and the three endpoint geometries of the canonical density. Two polynomial families with the same limiting edge spectrum have different limiting optimal energies. For Nesterov momentum $(s-1)/(s+1)$, the optimal leading endpoint Hessian-drift gain among nonnegative-link Jacobi realizations is $\sqrt{2}$ times the original gain. An explicit isospectral flow strictly improves the standard one-sided realization for $α>-1/2$, $α\ne1/2$.
comment: 56 pages, 2 figures, link to Lean formalization

title: Robustness as a Transferable Skill: Cross-Task Adversarial Defense for Vision-Language-Action Policies
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies are vulnerable to adversarial visual perturbations, while defenses often require task-specific adversarial fine-tuning. We investigate whether robustness learned on source manipulation tasks can protect independently specialized target policies without target-side adversarial training. We first show that even a single source defense update improves robustness on held-out tasks, establishing cross-task defense reuse independently of multi-source aggregation. To combine source updates, we introduce Source-Norm Transferable Robustness Vector (SN-TRV), which retains the direction of their mean while calibrating its magnitude using source-update norms. The resulting update is applied to the target visual encoder without target adversarial data, target-side gradient optimization, or additional inference modules. Evaluations across three VLA backbones, fixed and adaptive attacks, and different source defense recipes show improved robustness over naive averaging and identify limits in attack coverage. Physical PiPER trials increase average success under printed adversarial patches from 20.3% to 45.8%.
authors: Jinquan Zhang;Run Yang;Dongfu Yin;Qiang Lai;Yufeng Yan;Pengshuai Yin;F. Richard Yu

title: Grounding-Aware Judge Reward Reinforcement Learning for Out-of-Domain Face Anti-Spoofing
abstract: Face Anti-Spoofing (FAS) must distinguish genuine faces from presentation attacks. A unified Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) is an attractive solution: it detects physical attacks (print, replay, mask) in one model and produces interpretable forensic evidence via Chain-of-Thought (CoT). A central obstacle to post-training such a model with reinforcement learning is that FAS reasoning has no rule-verifiable ground truth: only the binary verdict is checkable, while the reasoning chain cannot be verified by any hand-crafted rule. Optimizing the verdict alone is therefore a sparse, hackable signal. The model can reach the correct answer through a shortcut such as a false-rejection bias, which does not generalize. We address this with a grounding-aware judge reward. A 32B vision-language judge scores each reasoning chain against the image on evidence anchoring, logical coherence, and domain knowledge, turning the image itself into the verification signal. The reward is applied in a Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) stage after CoT supervised fine-tuning. It is the judge, rather than the RL objective, that supplies the process supervision a verdict-only reward cannot. Our study starts from a model that already performs well In-Domain (ID) after CoT-based supervised fine-tuning and asks how to improve its Out-of-Domain (OOD) generalization. We find that grounding-aware rewards are an effective means to that end. We validate the method on OOD generalization, where the reward reduces ACER on two physical benchmarks (LCC-FASD 0.288 to 0.273, MSU-MFSD 0.431 to 0.409) while preserving ID accuracy (CelebA-Spoof 0.033 to 0.035). Against ResNet-50/101 and CLIP-ViT-B/16 baselines, the MLLM dominates ID and matches or surpasses the strongest baseline OOD. To our knowledge this is the first use of LLM-as-judge process supervision for FAS.

title: Phosphorus-rich star formation in giant molecular clouds hosting primordial globular clusters
abstract: Recent observational studies have identified phosphorus-rich (P-rich) stars ([P/Fe]>1.0) in both Galactic globular clusters (GCs) including three confirmed cases and the field population. Using analytical models of GC formation, we investigate a scenario in which P-rich stars form from pristine gas in GC-forming giant molecular clouds (GMCs) polluted by oxygen-neon (ONe) novae within and surrounding the GMCs. Within this framework, we model the chemical abundance patterns of P-rich stars using diverse chemical yield sets for ONe novae while varying the dilution factor (Fdil), defined as the ratio of pristine gas mass to total ONe nova ejecta mass. The principal results of our models are as follows: Across a wide range of Fdil, most models display positive correlations between [P/Fe], [N/Fe], [O/Fe], [Al/Fe]$, [Si/Fe], [S/Fe], and [Si/S]. The [Ce/Fe] ratios in P-rich stars can reach values up to 1 if the GMCs are additionally polluted by interacting low-mass asymptotic giant branch stars.P-rich star formation is highly unlikely in environments with a low interaction frequency between GMCs and ONe novae. P-rich stars exhibit anomalously low 14N/15N, 16O/17O, and 16O/18O isotopic ratios, offering a clear observational diagnostic to test this scenario. Assuming that P-rich Galactic field stars originate from GCs, we discuss the origin of their chemical abundance patterns. We suggest that the existence of P-rich stars provides direct evidence that GC-forming GMCs were polluted by pre-existing stellar populations.
comment: 17 pages, 13 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS

title: Failure Profiling and Reachable Trajectory Selection for Reasoning Distillation
abstract: Training smaller language models on reasoning solutions generated by a larger teacher model is the prevailing approach for transferring mathematical reasoning capabilities. However, the student tends to overfit the output distribution of the teacher and generalizes poorly when its own behavior at inference time deviates from the training data. Recent methods attempt to bridge this gap by incorporating error data, yet the corrective trajectories still reflect the reasoning patterns of the teacher, which the student cannot reliably reproduce, leaving the distribution mismatch largely unresolved. We propose a method, Failure Profiling and Reachable Trajectory Selection (FPRT), built on the insight that effective training data should be jointly determined by what the student fails on and what it can realistically learn. Our method first profiles the failure behavior of the student on each problem through repeated sampling, characterizing it in terms of error rate and error consistency to reveal qualitatively distinct failure modes. Each mode demands a fundamentally different training signal. The diagnosed mode then guides candidate generation from the teacher via distinct prompting strategies tailored to each failure type. Among the correct candidates, our method selects the one whose initial reasoning steps after the point of divergence are most reproducible by the student. These first corrective steps constitute the primary bottleneck, while the remaining steps follow an already corrected context and can therefore be continued more readily. This contrasts with standard reranking approaches, which score the trajectory as a whole and thereby dilute the signal at the critical reasoning transition. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves the SOTA performance across the five benchmarks on both student backbones.
comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. The source code and trained weights are available at \url{https://github.com/visresearch/FPRT}

title: DobotTrack: Target-Grounded Vision-Language-Action Learning for Embodied Person Tracking
abstract: Language-guided embodied person tracking requires a mobile agent to identify a target from a referring description and consistently follow the target under egocentric observations. We present DobotTrack, a target-grounded vision-language-action (VLA) framework that integrates auxiliary grounding supervision with efficient temporal modeling. We systematically investigate five auxiliary tasks---person segmentation, bounding-box grounding, visual-spatial classification (VSC), future DINO feature prediction, and future-frame prediction---and adopt complementary mask and bounding-box supervision to enhance target delineation and localization. We introduce Q-identity, a target-conditioned historical visual compression module that leverages target-grounding predictions to selectively preserve identity-discriminative appearance features and spatial cues in compact historical tokens. On EVT-Bench, our 0.8B-parameter model achieves an average success rate of 77.9%, exceeding OmTrackVLA by 16.9 percentage points across the three tasks. We further construct a real-world person-tracking dataset collected using a quadruped robot, comprising 126 episodes and 596,323 mask-annotated frames. The target masks enable automatic derivation of bounding boxes and visual-spatial labels encoding horizontal position and apparent image scale, providing additional grounding supervision without separate manual annotation of these labels. Together, our framework and annotation pipeline support learning target-grounded tracking policies from simulated and real-world data. Code is available at https://github.com/Dobot-Team/dobot_track.
authors: Shengjun Deng;Yinghan Zhang;Chengrui Wei;Liu Liang;Songyuan Liu;Pengkun Zheng;Yajun Zheng;Ying Zhang;Yuan Tian;Xi Li;Teng Wang

title: Dynamical formation of Gaia neutron star binaries in star clusters as a phase-dependent process
abstract: Gaia has discovered dormant compact-object binaries in which the compact object shows no observable interaction with its luminous companion. These systems, hereafter Gaia BHs and Gaia NSs for black hole (BH) and neutron star (NS) companions, provide a new probe of compact-object binary formation. These detached systems are difficult to produce through standard isolated binary evolution alone, and their formation pathways remain unclear. Previous $N$-body studies have shown that Gaia BH-like objects are formed efficiently in star clusters, while Gaia NS-like objects are not. This has been attributed to the BH subsystem dominating the cluster core. We performed direct $N$-body simulations of $10^4 \mathrm{M}_\odot$ star clusters in a Galactic tidal field and investigated how NS-main-sequence (NS-MS) binaries form during the late BH-depleted phase. We found that NS-MS binaries satisfying Gaia-sensitive criteria form only after BH depletion. NSs are present in the core throughout the evolution, but the strong encounters there are monopolized by the BH subsystem until it is depleted. Our results show that the dynamical formation of Gaia-sensitive NS-MS systems is not prevented in star clusters, but delayed relative to Gaia BH-like systems.
authors: Ryutaro Iwakura;Long Wang;Ataru Tanikawa;Takayuki R. Saitoh;Yoko Funato;Junichiro Makino
comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in ApJ

title: Language, Not Code Abstraction: Natural-language Training Shapes Brain-aligned Geometry
abstract: Code-trained language models produce positive brain scores, which raises the question of whether abstract structure learned from programming languages can substitute for natural-language training. We trained 25 GPT-2-small models on TinyStories, Python, C functions, x86-64 assembly, and the corresponding machine code, and scored them using a shared tokenizer and encoding procedure against matched random-weight models. On Pereira-243 and Tuckute2024, TinyStories exceeds the mean of the four code models by $Δr = 0.053$ and $0.059$ (Holm-corrected $p<0.001$), while code training leaves alignment near the random-weight level. The language advantage is benchmark-specific: Blank2014 shows no corrected language-code difference, and Fedorenko2016 shows no language benefit. Geometry tracks the encoding result on Pereira-243: TinyStories seeds converge on the most similar representations, and its fit-free correspondence with neural dissimilarity peaks at $ρ= 0.14$, twice the code and random-weight levels. Binary-trained models have about three effective dimensions, so seed agreement alone does not imply neural correspondence. Updating only the embedding matrix on English improves mean-over-depth alignment for every code model more than an equal update on its own corpus. Within this architecture and training setup, natural-language training produces a distinct representational geometry with closer neural correspondence on Pereira-243
comment: Accepted for the Neureps Workshop at NeurIPS 2026

title: Symmetry-Gated Sliding: Decoupling Interlayer Translation from Polarization Reversal in Boron Nitride Ferroelectrics
abstract: Electric-field-driven polarization switching in sliding ferroelectrics depends on how local interlayer motion is accommodated by the surrounding structure. Yet the relationship between sliding, domain-wall (DW) propagation, and collective domain evolution under changing vector fields remains unclear. Here, we show that local symmetry governs the coupling between field-induced forces and interlayer sliding, while DW connectivity determines how local motion contributes to net domain conversion. These effects are examined across three structural scales, from monodomains and isolated DWs to reconstructed moire networks. We investigate bilayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) using molecular dynamics with a machine-learning interatomic potential that incorporates field-dependent electric enthalpy. An initially monodomain bilayer switches through directional wrinkling and interlayer sliding, while the barrier along a constrained flat path remains finite. Pre-existing DWs propagate with velocities governed by their shear and tensile character, and an additional in-plane field tunes wall velocity and width according to its orientation. In reconstructed triangular moire networks, shared junctions and boundary curvature mediate domain evolution and recovery after field removal or reversal. Most strikingly, a rotating in-plane field translates the layers and displaces the moiré nodes by approximately 1 AA yet leaves the AB/BA domain-area ratio without detectable change, because threefold connectivity cancels the contributions of individual walls. We term this response polarization-silent sliding. These results distinguish local sliding, DW translation, and net domain conversion as different responses to electric fields and establish how local structural symmetry and DW connectivity shape their selective control.

title: Constrained Nested-Logit Pricing: An Exact Reformulation and Global Optimization Method
abstract: Sellers must price substitutable products while meeting operational requirements such as price limits and sales targets. Nested logit captures stronger substitution among similar products, but these requirements can undermine the structure used to solve unconstrained pricing problems. We develop an exact reformulation and a global optimization method for a fixed assortment with price bounds and weighted price caps. The key novelty is to concentrate the difficult interactions at the nest level while retaining convex optimization over individual products, without discretizing prices or approximating demand. This structure makes the number of nests, rather than products, govern the exponent in a conditional worst-case complexity bound. The method returns feasible prices together with a bound on how much profit could still be gained, allowing decision makers to assess solution quality even when computation stops early. Extensions cover purchase-probability bounds and price-order rules, with explicit accounts of their computational cost. In synthetic experiments, the method certifies solutions for assortments of up to 500 products with few nests. Projecting unconstrained prices onto the feasible set loses up to 32.60% of profit relative to direct constrained optimization, highlighting the value of jointly optimizing substitution and feasibility.

title: Perfect Wave Transfer in Nonconformal Tomonaga-Luttinger Liquids
abstract: Perfect wave transfer (PWT) reproduces spatial reflection at a common finite time under a fixed Hamiltonian. We classify this process for open compact bosons and inhomogeneous Tomonaga--Luttinger liquids, distinguishing transfer of oscillator and neutral observables from transfer on the charged field algebra. In the single-charge model, the first two notions coincide. Global transfer additionally requires rephasing of the compact zero mode. For regular reflection-symmetric channels, exact oscillator transfer forces an odd multiple of the optical crossing time and a strictly ordered, parity-compatible spectrum differing from the conformal ladder at only finitely many levels. This spectral condition is also sufficient when the Robin boundary data induced by the physical profile are included. Requiring Neumann conditions after the Liouville transformation instead forces conformality. We construct an explicit, regular one-defect family for every $r>1/2$. Its transfer parameters are precisely the reduced fractions $r=p/q$ with odd numerator and denominator, with shortest transfer time $pL/v_0$. At the delay $3L/v_0$, the $r=3/5$ profile has numerical contrast $K_{\max}/K_{\min}\simeq 12.913$, compared with $81$ for $r=3$. Two independent conservative discretizations show second-order convergence on fixed mode bands. Occupation- and charge-constrained error estimates quantify robustness, while an exact homogeneous-chain calculation explains the $J^{2/3}$ resolved-band scale also observed in the engineered channels. These results provide a spectral design method and finite-device benchmarks for quadratic quantum channels. An interacting microscopic realization remains open.

title: Frontier3DBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for 3D Creation across Objects, Scenes, and Interactive Open Worlds
abstract: Coding agents combine visual understanding with program execution, offering a new route to automated 3D creation. By translating images and instructions into editable programs, they bring reconstruction, generation, and editing into a shared workflow. Yet existing benchmarks fragment evaluation across task scopes and protocols, leaving their capabilities across construction levels unclear. We propose Frontier3DBench, a unified benchmark of 145 tasks across 9 categories spanning object, scene, and interactive open-world creation, with joint evaluation of appearance, structure, and behavior. Experiments with 11 model-harness configurations reveal strengths that vary by level: GPT-6.1-sol leads the object and scene levels and achieves the highest overall score of 66.02/100, whereas GPT-6-astra leads interactive world construction. However, all configurations score lower on reference reconstruction than on text-driven generation in object and scene tasks. Producing plausible content thus remains easier than reproducing specified geometry, layouts, and visual details. Moreover, generated worlds average 83.08/100 on local mechanisms but only 20.82 on motion clearance and 30.26 on stateful workflows: individual mechanisms often function, whereas complete activities that require coordinated actions and persistent state remain difficult. These results identify reference fidelity and coordinated activity completion as central bottlenecks for coding agents in 3D creation.
authors: Xinjie Lin;Qingle Liu;Wenyi Li;John Lam;Xiaoqiu Wang;Deyao Hong;Mingju Gao;Zheng Jiang;Yizhe Chi;Youjie Zheng;Calvin Xiao;Kaisen Yang;Huan-ang Gao
comment: 19 pages, 7 figures, 4 tables. Project page: https://lab.einsia.ai/frontier3dbench

title: Did I See It or Think It? Probing Reality Monitoring in Vision-Language Models with Concept Injection
abstract: Recent work tests whether language models can introspect by injecting a concept direction into their activations and asking whether they notice it and can name it. These studies are text-only. Vision-language models (VLMs) face an additional problem, known in cognitive psychology as reality monitoring: they must keep internally generated content separate from what they actually see. We therefore ask: can VLMs distinguish injected concepts from image content? We introduce a paradigm that varies the image and the injected concept independently. On each trial, the model reports what it sees, whether a thought was injected, and what that thought is. This design scores both whether the model identifies the concept and which source it assigns to it. Across six VLMs, only Gemma-3-27B reliably identifies injected concepts (35% vs. 3% for steering alone), with almost no false alarms. Even then, the source it reports is fragile. Strong or visual-pathway injections are reported as seen, and a visible object nearly eliminates correct thought reports. The same failure appears in ordinary captioning, where injected objects appear in up to 87% of captions of real photographs. Evaluating multimodal self-reports therefore requires checking both their content and their reported source.

title: Supporting Data Center Grid Integration via Co-Optimized Battery Energy Storage Sizing and Capacity Allocation
abstract: Interconnecting large data centers can be delayed by grid requirements on demand flexibility, ramping limits, and ride-through performance. This paper proposes an optimization-based framework to size a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) that accelerates data center grid integration by providing BESS capacity required to meet selected flexibility and grid-support requirements. The model co-optimizes BESS power rating and energy capacity while allocating capability across three services: (i) demand response over a specified duration, (ii) mitigation of high-magnitude, high-frequency load fluctuations through reserved active power with zero net state-of-charge change, and (iii) voltage support via reactive power capability at the point of common coupling. Minute-level operational scheduling enforces state-of-charge feasibility and load ramp constraints, and incorporates a controllable queue of delay-insensitive computing tasks to enhance flexibility. A case study using a real data center load profile demonstrates the proposed method and quantifies the BESS power-energy requirements and operational trade-offs needed to satisfy the multi-service constraints, providing practical guidance for interconnection planning and deployment.

title: Seeing vs. Counting: Complexity Twins Show Where Multimodal LLMs Fail on Diagrams
abstract: When a multimodal LLM miscounts in a diagram, does it fail at seeing or at counting? Existing visual graph and puzzle benchmarks vary visual density and algorithmic hardness together, confounding the two. We pair counting questions about the same drawing that sit in different counting-complexity classes, such as its spanning trees (a determinant) and its simple paths (#P-complete), and use a transcription probe and a text-only control to separate reading from computing. We test Gemini, Gemma and Qwen3-VL models; for the Gemini models, the answer depends on how the model computes. In chain of thought, most of them read small drawings correctly and then fail at counting, at a rate set far more by the size of the answer than by its complexity class (for the primary model, the odds of an exact answer fall 2.38-fold per decade of the answer). Given code and an exact transcription, the primary model counts correctly even on 10x10 grids, and reading becomes the bottleneck: a single view misses horizontal edges, and a second reading of a rotated copy with crop checks reads 86/96 large grids exactly, against 57/96 when the upright reading is simply repeated.
comment: 8 pages main text + 96 pages appendix (107 pages in total, including references)

title: Calibrating your confidence requires thinking of all the ways you could be wrong
abstract: A primary limitation of modern deep learning is the miscalibration of model confidence; traditional architectures fundamentally lack a mechanism to quantify their own uncertainty. Larger models and larger datasets mitigate this issue, but they do not resolve the underlying structural deficiency. Bayesian methods offer a principled uncertainty-aware learning framework through stochastic parameters. Yet, despite the established benefits, the inherent computational overhead often compromises either scalability or quality. This trade-off currently prevents the widespread adoption of Bayesian methods. This Thesis bridges the gap between high-quality and low-complexity by introducing a novel distribution on parameter space: a degenerate Gaussian whose covariance is a projection matrix aligned with the null space of the Fisher information matrix. We demonstrate the scalability of this Bayesian posterior through two numerically efficient algorithms: one for posterior sampling and another for the direct computation of predictive confidence. Empirically, we show State-Of-The-Art confidence calibration and out-of-distribution detection for large models. We provide theoretical grounding for this approach. We study the degeneracies inherent in Amari's information geometry and highlight its most relevant component: the split of parameter's perturbations into two orthogonal subspaces. From this perspective, our posterior naturally emerges as the simplest choice that captures this split, assigning unitary variance to one subspace and zero variance to the other. Moreover, through the tools of differential geometry, we utilize this split to identify and rectify a critical misalignment issue of the non-linearized Laplace Approximation. Finally, with a focus on PAC-Bayes generalization bounds, we pave the way for a deeper understanding of the learning capabilities of overparametrized models.
comment: PhD Thesis, Technical University of Denmark (DTU), 2026

title: UniMore: Fine-Grained Supervision for Unified Understanding and Generation
abstract: Unified multimodal models combine image understanding and generation within one system, creating an opportunity to improve both capabilities through paired image--text supervision. We examine the outputs of a pretrained unified model in both directions and observe a loss of specificity: generated images can contain the requested objects with incorrect attributes, while captions identify a scene without expressing its distinguishing details. These failures call for supervision that specifies both the visual content to realize and the descriptive differences to distinguish. We propose UniMore, a post-training method that derives these complementary learning tasks from the fine-grained content of image--text pairs. The generation route predicts grounded crops from their corresponding phrases, matching the scope of the condition and visual target while using the native visual objective. The understanding route combines positive-caption fitting with ranking against captions that omit or alter details, conditioned on the full image. The two routes are optimized independently, and their learned updates are combined into a single unified model without changing its inference procedure. Experiments show gains across multiple understanding and generation benchmarks.
authors: Haoyue Bai;Yinyi Luo;Yicheng He;Qingsong Wen;Sharon Li;Jindong Wang

title: Same Facts, Different Remedy: Linguistic Profiling and Arbitrariness in LLM and System One Decisions
abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to resolve consumer complaints, and the way complainants write varies with age, education and socioeconomic status (SES). We audit three remedy-decision systems using sociolinguistic rewrites of US consumer financial complaints that are instructed to preserve every fact: two generative LLMs that return a single label (GPT-4o-mini and GPT-5-mini) and a probabilistic "System One" model that returns a distribution over remedies (Jev). Using pre-registered hypotheses tested once on held-out complaints, we separate two phenomena that single-label audits conflate. At the group scale, older, college-educated and higher-SES styles receive slightly more generous remedies; these effects replicate but are small, with every monetary-remedy gap within 0.5 percentage points. At the individual scale, two style versions of the same complaint receive different monetary decisions 2.6-6.3% of the time. In a variance-component analysis of the probabilistic model, persona components shared across the two rewrite models account for about 1.6% of within-complaint variation. The persona gaps are associated mainly with delivery (vocabulary, grammar, politeness) rather than content. Positive controls show that all three systems respond 49-387 times more strongly to remedy-relevant facts than to style. Rewriting every complaint into one standard style reduced GPT-4o-mini's education and SES gaps by 94% and 87% while retaining fact sensitivity, but reversed two of the probabilistic model's gaps and did not make individual decisions more stable. Independent LLM auditors flagged material fact changes in 3.3% and 11.7% of rewrites, and instability persisted among unflagged rewrites. Fairness audits of LLM decision systems should report group disparities and individual instability as separate outcomes.
comment: 29 pages, 7 figures. Code, prompts and pre-registrations: https://github.com/colinpriest/llm-jev-linguistic-profiling

title: Enforcing Symmetries on Pre-trained ML Models for Physics
abstract: Post-hoc group averaging (or test-time augmentation) is a simple way to impose symmetry on a trained predictor without changing its architecture or retraining it. For finite and compact groups, averaging over a normalized Haar measure on the group gives the Reynolds operator: a canonical projection onto invariant or equivariant predictors with known non-increasing risk guarantees under certain assumptions. This paper provides numerical experiments on physics emulation models that demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach in this setting. We then extend this framework to non-compact group symmetries. For non-compact groups, the Haar measure cannot be normalized, so group averaging cannot be defined in the same way. We replace it with three alternatives: the Weyl unitary trick (which requires complexifying the space and extending the predictor), a data-dependent orthogonal projection (which involves a non-trivial optimization on the space of invariant or equivariant functions), and a frame averaging approach (which involves mapping each point to a set of orbit representatives). We illustrate the constructions theoretically and empirically on the unit-rescaling group and the Lorentz group. Our results show that in the non-compact case, the Weyl trick and frame averaging do not provide a consistent improvement over the baseline, except where the test data is out-of-distribution (an orders-of-magnitude improvement in this case) and, for the Weyl trick, in low-data regimes. The orthogonal projection can provide improvements in-distribution and out-of-distribution. We also observe that models trained directly on invariant features matched or beat the projection of an unconstrained one. We conclude that post-hoc symmetrization extends to non-compact groups, but it does not consistently outperform training a symmetric model.
authors: Wenjie Zhou;Valentino F. Foit;David W. Hogg;Soledad Villar

title: LEF-JEPA: Denoising-Trained Latent Energy Fields for Spatial Representation Learning
abstract: A joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) that applies prediction supervision only at masked positions struggles to clearly capture object shapes and boundaries in its latent representations. We further observe that some existing methods improve spatial structure while also retaining rich variations in texture and color. However, preserving more low-level visual information does not necessarily make representations better suited to prediction and action. This raises a key question: how can we strengthen the spatial structure in latent representations that supports prediction and action without over-encoding these details? We introduce LEF-JEPA, which learns spatial structure through target-guided latent recovery and transfers this supervision to the visual encoder through a relative-energy constraint; the energy module is used only during pretraining and adds no inference overhead. To reduce the cost of energy optimization during pretraining, we further construct a conditional Ising Hamiltonian that allows low-energy-state search to be performed by specialized Ising solvers. On physical hardware, we validate the feasibility of achieving lower forward latency with fewer local updates. Under a unified CIFAR-10 pretraining and frozen-encoder evaluation protocol, both realizations outperform V-JEPA2.1 in image classification, foreground segmentation, and visual planning.
comment: 14 pages, 7 figures, 7 tables. Includes supplementary material

title: Native point defects in rock-salt and wurtzite MnSe: formation energies across the growth window and spin splitting in the A-type order
abstract: Manganese selenide grows both as rock-salt $α$-MnSe, a type-II antiferromagnet, and as metastable wurtzite w-MnSe, whose magnetic order has not been measured. We compute the neutral Mn and Se vacancies and the two antisites of both polymorphs with density functional theory plus a linear-response Hubbard $U$, between the Se-rich limit bounded by MnSe$_2$ and the Mn-rich limit set by the measured formation enthalpy. In $α$-MnSe the Mn vacancy is lowest over most of the window (0.92 eV under Se-rich conditions), consistent with its p-type conduction. In w-MnSe, the Se antisite is lowest under Se-rich conditions, narrowly in the A-type order and clearly in the stripe order, and the Se vacancy is lowest under Mn-rich conditions. The Se vacancy has nearly the same formation energy in both polymorphs, whereas defects that change the number of Mn atoms differ by 0.4-1.1 eV, although DFT+$U$ places wurtzite below rock salt, contrary to experiment. A spin-degenerate stripe order lies 14 meV per formula unit below the altermagnetic A-type order of w-MnSe, and the formation energies shift between these orders by up to 0.24 eV, most for the Mn vacancy. Three of the four defects leave an uncompensated moment of 3-5 $μ_\mathrm{B}$. In the A-type order, band unfolding shows that the sign-reversing splitting of the most strongly split band, about 230 meV and 3 eV below the valence-band maximum, keeps its peak height within the 8% scatter of the analysis at 3% defects, while points on its shoulders move by up to about 70 meV. Band-edge states are not resolved.

title: Identifying Chemically Coherent Stellar Families in the Galactic High-α Disk with Low-Resolution Spectroscopy
abstract: Identification of chemical substructures in the Galactic high-α disk provides valuable insight into its formation history. In this work, we demonstrate the capability of low-resolution spectroscopy for this purpose by applying DBSCAN clustering to 87,275 red giants in the high-α disk using 18 elemental abundances derived from LAMOST low-resolution spectra (R~1800). We assess the effectiveness of this approach by comparing the clustering results from the low-resolution data with those obtained by applying the same procedure to high-resolution survey abundances and to mock catalogs. These comparisons suggest that, despite the relatively large uncertainties in individual elemental abundances derived from low-resolution spectra, the astrophysical coherence among different elements provides sufficient information to identify chemically coherent families that may share similar enrichment histories without necessarily sharing a common birth environment. After scanning the parameter space of the DBSCAN procedure and merging the results from different parameter combinations, we identify 133 candidate chemical families containing 4,642 unique stars (5.3% of the high-α disk sample). These families exhibit diverse multi-element abundance patterns, with particularly prominent differences in neutron-capture elements at nearly identical [Fe/H] values. These families therefore offer new constraints on the diversity of chemical enrichment pathways and on the assembly history of the high-α disk.
authors: Tianmin Wu;Maosheng Xiang;Jianrong Shi;Tiancheng Sun;Meng Zhang

title: Refer-CityFlow and M3Track: A Benchmark Dataset and Reference Framework for Language-Driven Multi-Target Multi-Camera Tracking
abstract: Referring multi-object tracking enables users to specify targets through natural language, but existing Refer-MOT benchmarks primarily focus on single-camera settings. We formalize Referring Multi-Target Multi-Camera Tracking (Refer-MTMCT), where free-form queries specify identity-consistent trajectories to be recovered across a network of sequential, sparse-overlap cameras. We introduce Refer-CityFlow, a benchmark built on CityFlow's global cross-camera identity annotations and augmented with language queries requiring joint language grounding, cross-camera association, and spatio-temporal reasoning. Refer-CityFlow covers 96 videos from 40 roadside cameras with 660+ identity-consistent cross-camera trajectories, 4,362 trajectory-level descriptions, and 7,699 queries, including 1,699 real-user queries collected from 50 participants. Reference experiments on the four-camera Scenario 02 show that single-camera referring trackers reach 14.95-18.28 HOTA on real-user queries, while the evaluated cross-view method achieves about 0.05 HOTA in direct transfer. To establish reference performance, we provide M3Track, a modular multimodal reference framework in which a large language model (LLM)-based agent orchestrates interchangeable detection, tracking, and cross-camera association modules. M3Track reaches 44.10 HOTA and 65.40 IDF1 on the same real-user query set. The project repository is available at https://github.com/phuongnguyen194/Refer-CityFlow-and--M3Track.
authors: Phuong T. Nguyen;Hao Vo;Tam Bang;Hoang K. Tran;Hoang-Minh Dau;Mahshid Malazizi;Tuan-Anh Hoang;Mina Sartipi;Thanh-Nam Doan;Ngan Le;Hoang H. Nguyen
