title: Coverage Hides Churn: Auditing and Preserving Conformal Decisions as VLM Label Registries Grow
abstract: Vision-language classifiers can learn new labels from text alone, so the label lists they serve keep growing. We show that this growth silently changes conformal decisions about old labels. Common softmax-based conformal scores compare each label with an average over all labels; adding labels changes that average, and with it the score of every old label, even when the model, the image, and the old calibration data stay the same. Recalibrating after the update keeps the coverage guarantee, yet across eleven settings it changes at least one old decision on 53-90% of new images. Coverage cannot reveal this, because it checks only the true label: in five controlled settings that keep the old calibration, so that only the normalizer changes, old-class coverage moves by at most 0.01 while 60-67% of images change. We propose a lifecycle audit that measures these changes alongside coverage and set size, and a simple fix, PrefixCP: each class keeps the label registry that existed when it was added. Its old decisions then never change, each class keeps exact class-conditional coverage under exchangeability, and one prefix scan computes all historical normalizers at once. PrefixCP recovers 40.9-58.5% of the set-size gap between never updating the reference and recalibrating, which gives smaller sets but changes old decisions.

title: Degree-Equalized View-Graph Selection under Tight Pair Budgets
abstract: Fully matching all image pairs in Structure-from-Motion is quadratic in the number of images, so practical pipelines pass a budgeted subset to the final matching and reconstruction backend. One-shot selectors score candidates with image retrieval, cheap geometric probes, or a learned prior and finalize B pairs before full matching. Their priorities do not account for the degree already allocated to each image, which can concentrate edges on a few images. Across nine large 1DSfM internet photo collections at B=2N, the coverage top-B selector leaves 54% of covered images with realized degree at most two. Reconstruction can then fail even when the selected graph is nearly connected and almost fully verified. Our training-free greedy rule, Degree-Equalized Allocation (DEAL), exponentially downweights pairs whose endpoints are already well covered. On these collections, DEAL improves the one-shot selector built on the same prior (from 0.776 to 0.929) and matches the mean registered-image ratio of an SfM-supervised edge prior under the shared backend (0.929 vs 0.930), without training. On the largely saturated 38-scene standard benchmark suite, DEAL gives the highest mean among the evaluated training-free selectors (0.875 vs 0.858 one-shot).

title: ReviewMap: Mapping Evaluative Acts and Automation Boundaries in Peer-Review Comments
abstract: Peer-review comments check what a paper does and judge why it matters, but no existing scheme distinguishes these two evaluative acts. We argue that making these acts explicit and measuring how reliably LLMs identify them is a prerequisite for responsible LLM-assisted review analysis: humans need to inspect review judgments and their grounds. This defines a more honest mission for NLP in peer review than full automation. We present ReviewMap, a framework that classifies each comment as assessment of claims and scholarly standards or calibration of contribution value and venue fit, with finer-grained attributes applied conditionally by act type. Applied to 500 ICLR~2026 papers through multi-model LLM consensus, the act layer proves reliably automatable under the operational guideline (inter-model $κ\geq 0.75$), supported by five-human validation on 470 development comments, while the attribute layer requires human oversight, defining a measured automation boundary. At the corpus level, 17% of reviewer-paper instances contain no panel-coded calibration, and the panel-coded calibration share is nearly $3\times$ as high in Strengths as in Weaknesses. This boundary informs three affordances: a review guideline that operationalizes the assessment-then-calibration workflow for reviewers, a per-comment rebuttal strategy scaffold for authors, and a discussion-phase dashboard for area chairs.

title: MEvince: Knowledge-Constrained LLM Reasoning for Technique Identification from Malware Reports
abstract: Mapping behavioral intelligence in malware analysis reports to ATT&CK techniques supports threat analysis and defense, but reliable identification remains challenging. Supporting evidence is often scattered across long, heterogeneous reports, while closely related techniques share behavioral cues and differ only in subtle but decisive details. While large language models (LLMs) can use external knowledge to interpret reports, they may assign techniques based on plausible associations rather than sufficient evidence. We present MEvince, a knowledge-constrained LLM reasoning framework for report-level malware technique identification. Its core is a shared behavioral representation connecting report observations to technique definitions. This representation is built through agentic mining of technique documentation and supports two online stages: 1) primitive-guided extraction uses behavioral primitives to structure LLM-extracted observations, link them to source passages, and group dispersed evidence; 2) evidence-aligned retrieval matches this evidence to technique profiles through the same concepts, retaining likely candidates and confusable alternatives for LLM comparison of distinguishing behaviors. Controls at both stages validate evidence references and check technique-specific requirements. The representation also supports adaptation without parameter updates, where offline agentic audits diagnose concept weaknesses and refine extraction or retrieval policies. We evaluate MEvince against 11 baselines spanning four method families using a dataset of 610 public malware reports referenced by MITRE ATT&CK. MEvince improves exact-ID F1 over the strongest baseline by 17.4%, and its concept-guided retrieval increases gold-label candidate coverage from 31.6% to 47.9%. With a small adaptation set, offline refinement yields further gains and outperforms baselines that update model parameters.
authors: Hongyu She;Yiling He;Mengda Xie;Yiping Liu;Xingzhi Qian;Zhan Qin;Lorenzo Cavallaro

title: Compact Motion Embeddings for Feed-forward Unified Human Animation
abstract: Animating a reference image with a driver's motion requires a motion representation that captures face, hand, and body articulation but excludes the driver's appearance. Most body animation methods take motion from external pose estimators and render it with many denoising steps; compact learned motion representations mostly cover the face. We present FUHA, a real-time-capable feed-forward transformer that learns a compact motion embedding of the whole human and uses it for face, upper-body, and full-body animation. A Q-Former compresses the driver's features from a frozen visual encoder into this embedding. To disentangle motion from appearance, a novel contrastive loss pulls it toward the motion embedding of the driver's rendered keypoint image and away from that of the same person in another pose. At inference time, FUHA needs no external pose estimators, keypoints, or parametric body models. As a retrieval key, the motion embedding matches body pose better than the learned global embeddings of ten vision encoders. Its same-person retrieval rate is 0.1%, against 9.5% for its own DINOv3 backbone. On our upper-body benchmark, FUHA outperforms all baselines on every self-reenactment metric and on cross-reenactment identity similarity. It is competitive on face and full-body and runs at up to 38.9 FPS at 512x512 on a single RTX 4090.
authors: Seonwook Park;Hyunsoo Cha;Amrita Mazumdar;Shengze Wang;Tianye Li;Hanbyul Joo;Koki Nagano;Shalini De Mello

title: Localization Does Not Imply Steerability: A Mechanistic Study of Sign Errors in LLM Mathematics
abstract: When large language models do multi-step mathematics, a characteristic failure recurs: the model writes one wrong sign token mid-computation -- a cofactor sign, the minus of a recursive integration-by-parts step -- then executes the rest of the arithmetic correctly, and the answer comes out wrong. We ask where inside the network that sign is written. Across six open models spanning 14B to 675B parameters, a per-layer readout shows the wrong sign is committed late -- by MLP layers in the last quarter of the network (70-100% per model and task), a pattern present, where tested (Qwen), in the base model before instruction tuning. The mechanism varies: some models carry fixed "minus-stamp" layers that push a minus regardless of the right answer, others carry amplifiers of whichever sign was already chosen, and Qwen adds a downstream rescue layer that opposes the stamp. The circuit is causal: subtracting a single sign direction from the residual stream flips 13 of 14 held-out minus-written integration-by-parts errors on Llama-3.3-70B, with flips replicating on Qwen, Gemma, and Mistral-Small (24-70% per cell), and with representation-level specificity -- the same dose breaks correctly-minus answers while sparing correct-plus answers where the direction is surgical (0/72 on Llama), and matched random-direction and control-layer interventions are null. Core claims were preregistered with pass criteria frozen in git before held-out data was seen: 23 of 29 checks passed, all misses reported. But causality is not uniform: Phi-4 implements an equally well-localized circuit at the same late depth, yet the identical intervention flips almost nothing -- the sign is written redundantly across ~15 layers with margins several times larger (median 17.8 logits). Localization, we conclude, does not imply steerability: two models can share a circuit location yet differ enormously in how overturnable it is.
comment: 61 pages. Code, per-case results and preregistration: https://github.com/signcircuits-experiments/sign-circuit-scaling

title: Kinematic analysis of a double-closed-loop four-bar chain-based leg for a multimodal quadruped-pentarotor robot
abstract: This paper presents the kinematic modeling and singularity analysis of a three-degree-of-freedom, double four-bar closed-loop quadruped leg mechanism. This leg is essential for transitioning between the two operational modes; therefore, it is examined in both joint and task spaces, leading to the development of its Jacobian matrix, which is vital for designing the gaits required for terrestrial mode and mid-air aerial reconfiguration (for aerial mode). Various gaits are devised for the system's motion in the MATLAB simulation, and their practical implementation on the single-leg test rig is demonstrated.
comment: Journal paper submitted to Robotica with ID:ROB-2026-0373

title: Recursive Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Role-Playing Dialogue
abstract: Long-horizon role-playing dialogue requires consistent character identity, reliable memory, and context-sensitive interaction. We present a bounded recursive self-improvement (RSI) framework that revises original-character memory, stable persona instructions, and a policy for constructing turn-level prompts. Repair outcomes also inform revisions to the updater's diagnostic rules, edit routing, and candidate selection. We specify the updater as a versioned policy with explicit inputs, editable fields, acceptance gates, and stopping conditions. An internal evaluation covers 50 original characters and five models, with two 100-round conversations per character-model pair: 500 conversations per condition. Across the pooled evaluated replies, the bad-response rate decreases from 14.00% (6,973/49,824) to 4.94% (2,459/49,793), a 9.06-percentage-point reduction and a 64.71% relative reduction. In 600 blinded human comparisons, RSI receives 294 wins, 187 ties, and 119 losses, yielding a 71.19% win rate among decisive judgments. The results support improved aggregate dialogue quality for the complete framework on the internal test distribution.

title: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance
abstract: Language agents increasingly work for users on the open Web, and finance is where trusting them is hardest. The data must come from the Web, the strategy lives in the user's head, and correctness depends on time, so an agent can fail silently: a strategy the user never asked for, unverified data, or a backtest that uses the future yields a report as convincing as a correct one. Existing benchmarks close the world somewhere, fixing the task, the data, or the timeline, and thereby remove these failures instead of measuring them. We introduce FINCOSMOS, an open-world evaluation paradigm for agents doing financial work. A simulated user holds a hidden strategy sampled from a compositional grammar and reveals it only when asked. The agent receives no data, so it must acquire data from the Web, build its own backtest under a data cutoff, and deliver verifiable results. Grading needs no reference answer. Programs verify point-in-time correctness and recompute every reported metric, the delivered strategy is checked against the hidden specification, and a run is accepted only when the user is satisfied and none of 15 veto checks fails. Across four coding agents and a model without tools in 150 sessions, no session is accepted: every session that the simulated user signed off fails a program check, and agents raise only 54--64\% of the details they were not told. Human experts attribute 88.33\% of failures to the agents. With FINCOSMOS feedback, an agent with persistent memory learned all ten tasks.
authors: Yupeng Cao;Xueqing Peng;Lingfei Qian;Haohang Li;Yangyang Yu;Anke Xu;Wenbo Cao;Yan Wang;Yuechen Jiang;Yuyan Wang;Zhuohan Xie;Yankai Chen;Zehan Li;Jimin Huang;Xue Liu;Jian-Yun Nie;Sophia Ananiadou

title: FREE-LIVO: Physically Decoupled Yet Tightly Coupled LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry
abstract: LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry (LIVO) integrates complementary LiDAR, camera, and IMU measurements to achieve robust state estimation. However, most existing methods assume a fixed relative pose and accurate time synchronization between sensors. Toward modular and heterogeneous robotic systems, this paper presents FREE-LIVO, a tightly coupled odometry method that requires neither a rigid LiDAR-camera rig nor LiDAR-camera time synchronization. The proposed method uses a pretrained image feature matcher to establish correspondences between a camera image and a dense LiDAR intensity image generated from a single LiDAR scan using a generative model. From the resulting 3D point-to-pixel correspondences, we construct reprojection factors that directly constrain LiDAR and camera poses at different acquisition times. These factors are jointly optimized in a single factor graph together with constraints from point cloud registration, visual feature tracking, and the IMU measurements associated with each sensor. On six sequences from the public M3DGR dataset, FREE-LIVO achieves an average absolute trajectory error (ATE) RMSE of 0.45 m without provided LiDAR-camera extrinsic parameters and exhibits minimal accuracy degradation under time synchronization errors of up to 0.5 s. Furthermore, experiments with the LiDAR and camera mounted on separate robots demonstrate that the method can jointly estimate the trajectories of independently moving sensors.
authors: Reon Tabata;Kenji Koide;Shuji Oishi;Taku Okawara;Mizuho Aoki;Aoki Takanose;Masashi Yokozuka;Jun Miura

title: Information-Spectrum General Formulas for the Capacity Region of Classical-Quantum Multiple Access Channels
abstract: For classical-quantum multiple access channels (cq-MACs) with two senders, we give several general expressions for the capacity region, valid for arbitrary sequences of channels. In the case of asymptotically vanishing error ($\varepsilon=0$), the capacity region is expressed in terms of spectral inf-mutual information rates. For every $0\le\varepsilon<1$, the $\varepsilon$-capacity region is expressed in terms of a quantity defined through a linear combination of three alternative hypotheses. In particular, the outer bound of Kubo and Nagaoka (2015) is tight. Our results include the quantum counterpart of the general formula of Han (1998) for the classical MAC. The most important ingredient is the one-shot inner bound of Sen (2021), which we apply to each member of an arbitrary channel sequence.

title: The Last Mile to the Real World: Agent-Native Primitives as Reusable Building Blocks for Solving Real-World Tasks
abstract: How can an agent handle a real-world task end to end? Frontier models with their own harnesses still fall short on real-world benchmarks: on Terminal-Bench 4.0, GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex resolves 37.3% of the tasks and Claude Opus 5 with Claude Code 51.8%. These tasks fail at the step from reaching a resource to applying it, which we call the last mile to the real world. Existing approaches put the resource within reach but leave the competence to apply it with the caller, so each harness rebuilds that competence. We introduce agent-native primitives, reusable units that equip a resource with a resident LLM that applies it in context and communicates with other primitives, and HEELO (Harness Engineering around Evolving Agent-Native Primitives for the Last Mile to Real-WOrld Tasks), a harness engineering framework that builds each task's harness from a library of such primitives. HEELO composes the primitives a task needs into a task-specific graph, verifies the result against evidence from the environment, revises the primitives a failure implicates, and admits new or improved primitives after validation. We instantiate HEELO with eight primitive families, each built for one kind of task, and evaluate them on more than twenty benchmarks. Dev-Primitives raise Terminal-Bench 4.0 resolution from 37.3% under Codex to 55.5% on the same backbone, Harness Primitives composed per task raise Terminal-Bench 2.0 Pass@1 from 60.0% for the seed harness to 72.2%, Tool Primitives raise ToolBench pass rate from 55.8% to 75.1%, and Navigation Primitives raise GAIA-Text-103 accuracy from 45.6% to 58.3%. On the 46 real-world tasks of our heelo.dev platform, Claude Opus 5.5 with Claude Code and GPT-6.1 Sol with Codex complete 9 each on their own and 39 and 35 when connected to HEELO through our MCP server, with 1.9$\times$ and 2.3$\times$ less time and 1.55$\times$ lower cost per completed task.
authors: Haibo Jin;Peng Kuang;Xiaopeng Yuan;Lucheng Fu;Jerry Wang;Xucheng Yu;Yaoning Yu;Dehao Wu;Runguo Li;Colin Su;Jingxuan Sun;Xuyang Liu;Haojing Luo;Haohan Wang

title: Probing Non-Abelian Topology through Quench Dynamics
abstract: Quench dynamics offer valuable insights to topological matter, wherein the emergent topological phenomena serve as a dynamic probe to the topology of static Hamiltonians. While such a practice has been widely applied to detect the Abelian band topology or the Euler-class topology of band nodes, little is known regarding the quench dynamics of non-Abelian topological insulators in multiband systems, where the intertwining geometry of all eigenstates necessitates the description of noncommutative topological charges. Here we propose a quench protocol for non-Abelian topological insulators, so that the underlying topology can be systematically probed using dynamic signatures. Specifically, we develop a band-projection scheme to extract the gap-resolved topology from dynamic skyrmions in the emergent quasimomentum--time manifolds of the quench processes. These skyrmions are characterized by a series of gap-resolved dynamic Chern numbers, which enable us to reconstruct the full non-Abelian topology of the post-quench Hamiltonian, including the global non-Abelian topological charge and edge-state patterns under the open-boundary condition. Our proposal offers dynamical access to non-Abelian topology in multiband systems, and can be readily implemented using photons or cold atoms.

title: Latency-Aware Adaptive Best-of-$N$
abstract: Test-time compute (TTC) improves language model responses by spending additional computation at inference time, and the right amount of compute depends on the prompt. Adaptive TTC methods allocate compute based on signals of response quality such as observed rewards, often by stopping once the signal exceeds a fixed threshold, and generally measure cost by the number of generations or tokens. But in online serving, latency is also a cost: it grows with server load, so a method using a fixed threshold spends too little compute when generation is fast and too much when it is slow. For Best-of-$N$ sampling, a widely used TTC method, we propose a two-stage adaptive algorithm that draws an initial batch, then uses the observed rewards and the batch's latency to decide whether to draw a second batch and at what size by comparing expected improvement against predicted cost: it draws one when the first batch's best reward is below a threshold that decreases with the first batch's latency, without explicitly measuring server load. We map each reward to its value under the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of the prompt's reward distribution, so the same tradeoff parameters can be reused across tasks; a regression fitted offline on other prompts predicts a distribution for the CDF value of the first batch's best reward, giving the expected improvement in closed form. We evaluate the method by simulation on a preference-based alignment benchmark, measuring generations-equivalent cost: generations plus latency, converted to generations. The method reaches Best-of-$N$'s reward at lower generations-equivalent cost, and conditioning on the measured first-batch latency saves at least as much of that cost as fixed-threshold (latency-unaware) baselines, and more when latency is highly variable, when it grows with batch size, and when the second batch's latency is highly predictable from the first's.

title: Bell Test and Quantum State-Space Geometry
abstract: We explore a minimal phenomenological model of coupling between the geometry of the classical spacetime and the quantum state space. Assuming a simple structure of the combined manifold, bilinear interaction between the corresponding geometric scalars and the simplest case of the two-qubit entanglement dynamics, we derive an illustrative upper bound on the geometric coupling constant from the requirement of the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality violation over a finite time interval.

title: Elimination of quantum causal confusion in the presence of dual states
abstract: There is a rich class of bipartite quantum correlations between qubits which are consistent both with measurements performed in parallel and measurements performed in sequence. This phenomenon has recently been termed \emph{quantum causal confusion}, which is made mathematically precise by the notion of a dual state---a bipartite density operator whose associated correlations are causally ambiguous. A natural question is then whether or not the spatial and temporal scenarios associated with a dual state are fundamentally indistinguishable from a causal perspective. Here we show that as long as the reduced density operator of a dual state is oblique---meaning that all coefficients in its Pauli expansion are non-zero---then the underlying joint probabilities giving rise to such causally ambiguous correlations will differ in the spatial and temporal scenarios. Specifically, the temporal joint probabilities will inherently violate the no-signalling condition, thus eliminating quantum causal confusion. Moreover, as oblique states form an open dense subset of the Bloch ball, the elimination of quantum causal confusion is the norm rather than an exception.

title: Demystifying Graviton Detection
abstract: Detecting single gravitons is possible through the extraction of discrete energy quanta from passing gravitational waves. For decades, this was considered hopeless, with estimates suggesting a detector the size of Jupiter. Here, I explain how these earlier estimates relied on the highly inefficient electron ionization process, while the absorption through the full mass quadrupole of a macroscopic system can bring graviton detection within experimental reach. Operating in the LIGO frequency band solves the challenges of graviton sources and noise suppression, allowing gravitons to be extracted from known passing gravitational waves and detection events to be heralded by classical gravitational-wave observations. Combined with the ability to resolve single energy quanta in macroscopic systems, such as in quantum acoustics, this opens a realistic path toward graviton detection. I also discuss the general limitations of particle detection in establishing an underlying quantum theory, illustrated by an energy-nonconserving semiclassical alternative. Nevertheless, the semiclassical alternative is not standard classical wave physics, and extracting $E=\hbarω$ from a passing wave constitutes bona fide particle detection. This opens the way not only to the first detection of individual gravitons, but also to experimentally probing linearized quantum gravity and the graviton counting statistics of gravitational waves.
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures. Extended author version of article published in Physics Today

title: Two-stage residual learning for calibrated uncertainty in solar irradiance forecasts
abstract: Accurate forecasting of renewable generation requires not only point predictions but also reliable estimates of the uncertainty attached to them, particularly at extended horizons. Machine learning models are increasingly used to predict solar output, but they typically report a single value and capture the associated uncertainty poorly. The standard remedy is to train a model to predict the parameters of an assumed probability distribution directly. Here we develop an alternative two-stage method, motivated by synthetic solar signal generation, in which the forecast error is modeled separately from the expected irradiance. A first long short-term memory (LSTM) network predicts the expected global horizontal irradiance, and a second network models the distribution of the forecast error, which is added back to the mean to give both the forecast and its uncertainty. Using historical weather data from the National Solar Radiation Database and a probability integral transform evaluation, we show that explicitly modeling the error brings the predicted standard deviation markedly closer to the historical value, reducing the deviation between the two by 34.6 percent for a standalone LSTM and by 56.5 percent when the LSTM is coupled to Gaussian process regression, the most reliable of the configurations tested. Because the method models the total forecast error directly, it captures the full predictive uncertainty that matters for decisions, rather than only the model contribution that dropout-based approaches estimate.
authors: RR Flanagan;E Kasha;PW Talbot;AS Epiny;MR Deinert

title: VIPA: View-Invariant Projector-Based Adversarial Attack
abstract: Projector-based adversarial attack aims to physically manipulate real-world scenes by projecting adversarial patterns, thereby causing deep image classifiers to produce incorrect predictions. However, existing stealthy projector-based adversarial attack methods model the project-and-capture process in a single and static view, limiting their view-invariant capability and practical applicability in dynamic environments. In this paper, we introduce View-Invariant Projector-Based Adversarial Attack (VIPA), a novel method designed to overcome these limitations by achieving both view-invariant and classifier-agnostic adversarial attacks in the physical world. We first leverage a view-invariant projector-camera system simulation method to model the physical interactions between projected patterns and real-world surfaces. To ensure robustness and stealthiness of the attack across different views, VIPA optimizes adversarial projections by aggregating simulated attack losses from multiple views. This joint optimization across diverse views helps maintain robustness regardless of the viewpoints. Finally, the optimized patterns are physically projected into real-world scenes, where they successfully fool various classifiers from different viewpoints, thereby enabling robust and practical view-invariant adversarial attacks. Our experiments in both targeted and untargeted attacks demonstrate that VIPA consistently achieves higher attack success rates than existing methods, while also enhancing stealthiness and ensuring minimal perceptual degradation across all tested views.

title: Information flow control in hybrid quantum networks
abstract: Quantum resources can change the dynamical features and operational behaviors of conventional networks. Long-distance entanglement supports information transfer between nodes lacking a direct connection. This entanglement link not only modifies the stationary effective connectivity of the network but can also be used to suppress undesirable classical dynamics. By examining information flow control mechanism, we demonstrate that classical collective behavior can be well-balanced by altering the initially distributed entanglement. We show the entanglement thresholds for two distinct control approaches: linear response control and Lyapunov functional controllability.

title: PolyGPT: A Decoder-Only Transformer for Polymer Electrolyte Design
abstract: Designing polymer electrolytes requires control over both material properties and chemical structure. Here, we present PolyGPT, a Transformer with 38.3 million parameters that generates polymer repeat units from optional property targets, requests to include or exclude a specified chemical feature, and an electrolyte-domain condition. Using the model selected by validation loss, we compared unconditional generation with requests for electrolyte-associated structures, a low glass-transition temperature (Tg), or both. Unconditional and electrolyte-only generation achieved structural validity of 99.46% and 99.59%, respectively. However, electrolyte conditioning increased repetition: uniqueness among valid outputs fell from 99.99% to 51.74%. At a Tg target of 246.11 K, we compared generation with and without electrolyte conditioning, and adding the electrolyte condition slightly reduced the predictor-estimated mean absolute error from 26.97 to 26.07 K, but the fraction of all attempts yielding distinct valid polymers within 50 K of the target fell from 82.35% to 32.31%. When we also required absence from the training catalog, these yields were 59.90% and 19.71%, respectively. The lower yield persisted with a tighter 25 K tolerance. Domain conditioning also weakened control of inclusion requests: the mean fraction of attempts producing valid polymers containing the requested chemical feature fell from 94.27% to 31.27%. Across nine checkpoints, earlier models sometimes produced more distinct, catalog-unseen polymers meeting the Tg target: 10,000 checkpoint model with electrolyte conditioning and 30,000 checkpoint model without it. Together, these results show why property error alone is insufficient for evaluating conditional polymer generation. It must be considered alongside repetition, training-catalog novelty, and whether combined design requests are satisfied.

title: IMUDINO: Self-distilled Foundation Model for Inertial Sensing
abstract: We present IMUDINO, the first foundation model (FM) for inertial sensing to achieve competitive performance across diverse sensing tasks including human activity recognition (HAR), health, motion capture, and odometry. Prior inertial FMs often focus on one subfield of inertial sensing and sometimes underperform state-of-the-art supervised methods (e.g., in HAR), making their scope considerably narrower than FMs for vision and natural language. Moreover, they often require fixed input length and sampling rate, and generalize poorly to unseen sensor locations. To build a general-purpose foundation model for inertial sensing, we adapt the DINO self-supervised learning (SSL) paradigm to inertial data through a set of semantics-preserving motion transformations that simulate variations in motion pattern and sensor setup. For model architecture, we use a plain transformer encoder with frequency-aware positional encoding that natively supports varying input length and sampling rate. This simple setup proved remarkably effective for learning global and dense features generalizable across users, sensor setups, tasks, and, in the case of robot odometry, embodiments. We hope IMUDINO can serve as a backbone for inertial sensing and kickstart the development of general-purpose inertial FMs.
authors: Zhoutong Ye;Chengwen Zhang;Zixuan Wang;Xufeng Jian;Zhe He;Qingyang Wan;Xutong Wang;Jiaqi Liu;Mingze Sun;Yu Mei;Chun Yu;Yuanchun Shi

title: Safe Output-Regulation Flows for Constrained Optimization via Control Barrier Functions
abstract: Control-theoretic approaches to constrained optimization have been widely studied by interpreting optimization algorithms as dynamical systems. This paper formulates constrained optimization as an output-regulation problem with state constraints, where equality-constraint residuals are treated as regulated outputs and inequality constraints as state constraints. Proportional--integral feedback is employed to drive the equality-constraint residuals asymptotically to zero, while a control barrier function (CBF) safety filter is used to ensure inequality safety throughout the optimization process. We establish feasibility of the CBF filtering program throughout the inequality-feasible set and local exponential convergence of the resulting flow. Under stronger global conditions, we further prove convergence from an entire connected component of the inequality-feasible set. Since exact implementation of the flow requires solving a CBF quadratic program at each state, we further develop a flow that approximates the CBF solution through multiplier updates. Moreover, we provide a unified formulation encompassing the two proposed flows and projected primal--dual dynamics. Numerical examples demonstrate convergence, safety, and computational tradeoffs of the proposed flows.
authors: Zihao Ren;Bingqi Liu;Lei Wang;Hongye Su;Guodong Shi

title: TRiST: Topology-Reinforced Swin Transformer for Medical Image Analysis
abstract: Medical images contain topological patterns, such as connected components and loops, at scales ranging from small lesions to organ boundaries. Although hierarchical Vision Transformers have advanced medical image analysis, they do not explicitly incorporate topology throughout their multiscale representations. We propose Topology-Reinforced Swin Transformer (TRiST), a framework that integrates topological information into feature construction, refinement, and attention. First, a Hierarchical Multi-Scale Topology Representation algorithm computes 2D persistent homology (H0 and H1) independently at four native Swin stages, producing descriptors aligned with each stage's token grid rather than downsampling fine-scale topology. Second, a Band-Aware H0/H1 Residual Refinement module uses gated residual networks to process short-, medium-, and long-persistence information separately. Third, a Persistence-Band Progressive Attention Bias converts stage-specific descriptors into learned key-saliency scores that directly modify shifted-window attention logits. We instantiate TRiST as Topo-SwinV2-B for classification and Topo-Swin-UNet for segmentation, preserving the underlying Swin-based backbones. Experiments on five medical image datasets show consistent improvements over Swin-based baselines and competitive performance relative to existing topology-augmented methods.
authors: Pengfei Gu;Huimin Li;Guangyu Meng;Hao Zheng;Haoteng Tang;Bin Fu;Danny Z. Chen

title: Cross-Family Mode Coupling and Localization Reversal in Phononic Crystal Defect Dimers
abstract: Defects in phononic crystals confine elastic vibrations within bandgaps, enabling waveguiding, sensing, and energy harvesting. Coupling defects offers control over the spatial distribution of vibration, but how interactions between nearby modal families determine defect preference remains unclear. We examine localization reversal in dimers whose single defect supports a nearby $B_1$ singlet and $E$ doublet: softening one defect shifts a continued modal branch toward its unchanged partner. In off-axis and diagonal layouts, this reversal accompanies family exchange, with opposing $B_1$ and $E$ contributions to the defect-mass difference nearly cancelling at the threshold. Deleting cross-family stiffness and mass blocks removes reversal, while omitting cross-family observable terms at fixed states preserves it, identifying modal redistribution as the dominant mechanism. At the off-axis softening endpoint, independent channels predict the opposite preferred defect despite a $0.16\%$ frequency difference from the full-order solution. Nominal operators retaining the complete singlet-doublet space predict selected softening-branch thresholds with errors below $1.1\%$ against independent full-order sign brackets, without fitting detuned trajectories. These results link localization reversal to modal-family exchange and physical defect-mass balance, and show that frequency agreement alone does not guarantee localization accuracy.
comment: 29 pages. This preprint presents the primary singlet-doublet system. The journal manuscript additionally includes a contrasting material system

title: MessyNav: Zero-Shot Navigation via Manipulation in Messy Environments
abstract: Real-world environments are messy, with paths often blocked by everyday objects like chairs and toys, requiring robots to perform interactive navigation by manipulating obstacles to clear a path. Existing methods rely on extensive simulation-based learning or per-scene instructions specifying which objects to avoid or manipulate. They struggle to generalize across novel objects, diverse environments, and varied contexts such as a cart of fragile glassware that should be avoided while an empty one can be pushed. We formalize this problem as open-world interactive navigation and present MessyNav, a zero-shot framework based on vision-language models (VLMs). At its core, MessyNav performs explicit VLM-based affordance reasoning before task planning to decide whether to swipe, pick up, or avoid an object and produce a high-level plan. Evaluated on a mobile manipulator across real-world indoor and outdoor environments, MessyNav improves success rate by 27 percentage points (pp) over the strongest baseline in real-robot trials and achieves statistically significant gains in a larger-scale offline evaluation, without task-specific training.
authors: Kenneth Llontop;Cherie Ho;Dylan Zhou;Anuva Banwasi;Priya Sundaresan;Carlota Parés-Morlans;Jeannette Bohg

title: Truncated backpropagation through time induces a two-sided gradient turnpike property
abstract: Truncated backpropagation through time reduces the computational burden of training recurrent models by restricting gradient computations to shorter temporal contexts. This induces two distinct boundary effects: missing past information perturbs the forward state evolution, while truncating the backward recursion omits future information. This motivates decoupling the interval over which gradient contributions are averaged for the parameter update from the surrounding temporal context over which they are computed. Under exponential decay of the state-transition Jacobians and mild regularity conditions, this leads to a two-sided gradient turnpike property: the error between truncated- and full-context gradient contributions decays exponentially with the distance from both context boundaries. We derive bounds for the averaged update gradient, yielding guarantees on gradient alignment and approximate full-context stationarity; under unbiased interval sampling and a Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition, these further imply a bound on the resulting optimality gap. Numerical experiments on the Wiener-Hammerstein benchmark illustrate the role of past and future context and the trade-off between predictive performance and computational cost.

title: Structured Quantum Hardness from Unstructured Assumptions
abstract: Whether useful structured hardness can arise from unstructured assumptions is a fundamental question in complexity and cryptography. The longstanding Bennett-Gill question asks whether $\mathsf{NP}\cap\mathsf{coNP}$ remains hard relative to a random oracle; [GIKKLS, STOC 2023] recently gave a conditional affirmative answer in the classical setting. We establish the quantum analogue: if $\mathsf{UP}\not\subseteq\mathsf{BQP}$, then $\mathsf{NP}^{O}\cap\mathsf{coNP}^{O}\not\subseteq\mathsf{BQP}^{O}$ with probability $1$ over a random oracle $O$. Beyond extending the classical result, this separation has a distinctly quantum significance: Shor's algorithms defeat canonical number-theoretic hardness candidates, while lattice assumptions and other leading post-quantum cryptographic assumptions do not directly supply hard languages with two-sided classical certification on every input. Our conditional oracle separation provides evidence that such structured quantum hardness can nevertheless arise from unstructured sources. Complementing this result, we rule out fully black-box quantum reductions of worst-case quantum hardness in $\mathsf{NP}\cap\mathsf{coNP}$ to post-quantum injective one-way functions and indistinguishability obfuscation. This barrier excludes a broad class of black-box approaches to deriving structured quantum hardness from generic cryptographic primitives, providing partial evidence that the non-black-box techniques in our first result are essential.

title: A Novel Asymmetric Distributed Voltage Regulation Scheme to Enhance the Utilization of Distributed Energy Resources
abstract: Passive voltage regulation in distribution grids using distributed energy resources (DERs) is becoming the standard for feeder voltage management in both under-voltage and over-voltage scenarios. Their simple control, ease of implementation, and fast response make them ideal for distribution feeders with high-DER penetration. This paper proposes a novel distributed voltage control for DERs based on the voltage at the point of common coupling, inverter rating, and operating active power. The proposed control is designed to utilize feeder inverters efficiently to reduce the burden on the inverters in both under-voltage and over-voltage operations and increase the fairness in reactive power ($Q$) support in over-voltage operations. The proposed control is implemented in static and dynamic simulations of a real feeder to validate the performance. Results for the under-voltage scenario are also presented in the paper.

title: Kinematic Hypothesis Context: Embodiment-Conditioned Learned Video Coding for Bandwidth-Limited Robot Policy Uplinks
abstract: Robots increasingly run large vision-language-action policies on remote servers, making the camera uplink the bottleneck. Existing video codecs spend bits on content the receiver could predict: the robot's own motion. We introduce the kinematic hypothesis context, a zero-rate conditioning signal that both ends build from joint states, the robot model and the camera calibration. Ego-motion homographies, per-link robot reprojections, an end-effector plane and a background memory warp the previous reconstruction into hypotheses that condition a learned video codec. We prove that history-only and global-pose conditioning with a limited receptive field cannot access this information under large motion, and that coding gains become task gains at the policy's success cliff. On LIBERO, the context saves 23.9% bit rate over a capacity-matched history-conditioned codec and 40-56% over x264, x265 and SVT-AV1, and needs 23.2% fewer bits than DCVC-RT at equal policy action deviation; trained to lower rates, it matches DCVC-RT in PSNR. In closed loop at equal rate, OpenVLA-OFT success nearly doubles from 22.8% to 43.1% at 6 kbps (72.6% with lower-rate training, 23.6 points above DCVC-RT), pi_0.5 success rises from 55.5% to 77.4%, and the gain grows under packet loss. The context transfers across three codec hosts and to real robot data.
comment: 15 pages, 12 figures. Preprint; supplementary material and code to be released upon formal publication

title: Spectral symmetry fingerprints in equivariant representations
abstract: Symmetry governs the organization of physical structures, while symmetry breaking reveals their transformations. In geometric deep learning, symmetry imposes rank constraints on equivariant representations, limiting the expressive capacity of equivariant graph neural networks (GNNs). Here we show that these constraints can instead be exploited: the singular-value spectra of equivariant representations provide a unified fingerprint of structural symmetry. We introduce spectral symmetry fingerprints (SymFP), which enable discrete point-group identification through rank-template matching and continuous symmetry analysis by quantifying spectral energy beyond target rank constraints. SymFP is orientation invariant and architecture agnostic, enabling a parameter-free GNN implementation. Its spectra can be reused across multiple target groups, and the resulting leakage scores satisfy subgroup monotonicity. Across synthetic structures, molecules, coordination complexes and large biological assemblies, SymFP accurately identifies point groups, tracks controlled symmetry breaking and reveals local and degree-resolved symmetry changes that can be obscured by global geometric measures. These results establish the spectral structure of equivariant representations as a general framework for characterizing symmetry across physical systems.
authors: Jiacheng Cen;Anyi Li;Ning Lin;Zihe Wang;Ji-Rong Wen;Wenbing Huang

title: PSGAgent: Enhancing MLLMs' Dynamic Visual Perception for Panoptic Scene Graph Generation via Agentic Reasoning
abstract: Panoptic Scene Graph generation (PSG) requires holistic yet fine-grained reasoning over complex relations among objects. However, current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) applied to PSG suffer from a perception bottleneck: they function as static observers limited by fixed-resolution views. As a result, models often overlook critical relations involving small or peripheral objects and struggle to differentiate ambiguous predicates in complex scenes. To address these limitations, we propose PSGAgent, an agentic framework that enhances visual perception for PSG through a think-act-observe loop. PSGAgent allows MLLMs to dynamically refine their visual perception using two tools: a Region Zoom-In Tool for local exploration of small or boundary relations and a Visual Highlight Tool for relation-focused segmentation that filters out irrelevant contextual noise. To optimize decision-making, we construct a two-stage training pipeline. First, we create a high-quality, error-aware Multimodal Chain-of-Thought (M-CoT) dataset that provides robust supervision for cold-start learning. Then, we design a novel hierarchical reward mechanism integrated with Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) to enable strategic and adaptive tool usage. Extensive experiments on the PSG benchmark show that PSGAgent achieves SOTA performance, demonstrating strong capability in both holistic and fine-grained scene understanding.
authors: Qingyun Liu;Yuankun Liu;Jiaye Feng;Jie Huang;Zonghong Dai;Haochen Li;Jingkun Wang;Weiping Li;Tong Mo

title: Random Reshuffling for Smooth Convex Optimization: Dominates Stochastic Gradient Descent
abstract: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is one of the most classical optimization algorithms with favorable theoretical guarantees, yet its practical implementation differs subtly from its well-known form and is often referred to as Shuffling Stochastic Gradient Descent (Shuffling SGD). A particularly popular strategy in Shuffling SGD is Random Reshuffling (RR), which has achieved great empirical success. Despite its strong performance, RR has long been considered a heuristic due to a lack of theoretical support. Over the last decade, people have finally established provable convergence rates for RR, thus justifying its observed superiority. However, for smooth convex optimization, two clouds over the convergence theory of RR remain. According to current theory, Shuffling SGD under RR converges only when the stepsize is smaller than a threshold proportional to $1/n$, where $n$ is the number of summands in the objective (or the number of data points). Consequently, the optimally tuned theoretical rate of Shuffling SGD under RR is strictly worse than that of SGD when the number of epochs is smaller than another threshold proportional to $n$. These two restrictions heavily limit the applicability of existing theories and leave a critical mismatch with practice. In this work, for the first time, we prove that RR dominates SGD in smooth convex optimization for any reasonable stepsize after any finite number of epochs, thereby addressing a longstanding open question. Moreover, we establish new algorithm-dependent lower bounds for RR and SGD, respectively. Altogether, these results yield (nearly) sharp worst-case characterizations of RR and SGD. Furthermore, we develop a shuffling-based method to optimize functions satisfying the quadratic growth condition, a strict relaxation of strong convexity, and derive a new complexity bound improving existing results proved under stronger assumptions.

title: Weak Values in Postselected Quantum Trajectories
abstract: Weak value (WV) describes the amplified response of a meter when the measured system undergoes postselection. While conventional WV theory mainly rests on a single system-meter interaction setting, it remains unexplored whether WV can act as an effective pointer for sequential quantum measurements under postselection. Here we introduce the concept of WVs to the setting of sequential quantum measurements and quantum trajectories. We find that WV naturally emerges in postselected quantum trajectories of sequential weak measurements, by establishing a connection between the WV of the measured observable and the postselected statistics of quantum trajectories. Using sequential weak measurements on a qubit or an oscillator implemented by Ramsey interferometry with an ancilla qubit, we show that postselection shifts the collective record polarization away from the unconditioned ones, with an effective bias described by the WV. Our predictions are feasible to test in various platforms.

title: Dynamic Watermarking and Action-Conditioned Latent Dynamics for Secure Vision-Based Controllers
abstract: Replay attacks are difficult to detect in vision-based control systems because previously recorded observations can remain plausible while the physical system follows a different trajectory. This paper develops an adaptive dynamic-watermarking framework for detecting replay attacks against vision-based controllers. A private Gaussian watermark is added to the nominal control input, and a control input-conditioned latent dynamics network (LDN) predicts the corresponding evolution in a compact latent space learned from image observations. Attack evidence is obtained from the discrepancy between the predicted latent response and the latent representation of the received image observation. A reinforcement learning policy adjusts the watermark covariance using the latent state and detector confidence, thereby balancing attack detectability, watermark energy, and control distortion. A Lagrangian penalty on task-specific safety costs is included during training to limit the adverse effect of the excitation. The framework is evaluated on a vision-guided UR5 manipulation task in which the robot reaches a target while avoiding a moving human arm under nominal and replay-attacked observations.
authors: Aditya Parameshwaran;Navid Aftabi;Abhishek Hanchate;Satish T. S. Bukkapatnam;Dan Li;Yue Wang
comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, Submitted to ACC 2027 conference

title: Higher-order topological quantum battery
abstract: A quantum battery is a next-generation energy-storage device that exploits genuinely quantum properties such as superposition and coherence. We propose a second-order topological quantum battery coupled to a photonic crystal described by the breathing-Kagome model, where optical loss is present on all lattice sites while nonlinear gains are introduced selectively at the output sites. Under these realistic non-Hermitian conditions, the system exhibits a clear topological phase transition manifested in both the ergotropy and the charging power. Remarkably, perfect work extraction is realized in the topological phase, where the maximum value of the ergotropy is quantized and acts as a good topological-phase indicator. The triangular geometry coherently distributes energy into two quantum batteries, where mirror-symmetry-protected phase synchronization gives rise to collective energy storage.

title: Extensions of the Haldane gap proof: higher dimensions, near degeneracy, fermions and tensor-network states
abstract: A recent remarkable paper by OpenAI showed that the spin-one Heisenberg chain with periodic boundary conditions has a spectral gap in the thermodynamic limit. The proof elegantly deduces this gap from the Hamiltonian's spectrum on a finite system. This basic idea is an inequality involving the purity of the original Gibbs state and a dual Gibbs state that is defined via space-time rotation. Here we consider a few generalizations of this purity bootstrap argument. We first extend it to arbitrary spatial dimensions. Our main result uses the space-time duality between symmetry generators and symmetry twists to obtain upper bounds on the splitting of nearly degenerate low-energy states, together with a nonzero gap above them, from finite-system information. As applications, we show that finite-system calculations for the 2+1-D toric code in a field and the 2+1-D transverse-field Ising model establish parameter regimes with four and two low-lying states whose splittings are bounded from above by $e^{-cL}$ and $e^{-cL^2}$ respectively for arbitrarily large system size $L$, while the gap above these states remains nonzero in the thermodynamic limit. Next, we extend it to fermionic systems and use a finite calculation to establish a symmetric mass generation phase in a $2+1$-D fermionic model. Finally, we apply the bootstrap to tensor-network states and establish exponential decay of connected correlations of all local operators in the symmetric square-lattice spin-one state introduced by Jian and Zaletel.

title: Changepoint localization via nested exchangeability tests: from point estimates to confidence intervals
abstract: We study distribution-free uncertainty quantification for a changepoint estimate in an offline setting. We observe a sequence with a single changepoint and are given an estimate of its location. The pre- and post-change segments are independent and each consists of i.i.d. (or, more generally, exchangeable) observations from arbitrary and unknown distributions. We introduce Changepoint LOcalization via Nested Exchangeability testing (CLONE), a novel method for constructing distribution-free confidence intervals around that estimate by testing exchangeability in nested windows centered at the reference estimate. Under these assumptions, CLONE provides finite-sample coverage for any black-box reference estimator. Using a geometrically shrinking radius grid, CLONE requires only $O(log n)$ permutation tests. We characterize optimal scores for the framework and provide practical recommendations that result in sharp confidence intervals. Under mild assumptions, CLONE confidence intervals have asymptotically vanishing normalized length. Simulations and experiments on image and text data support our theoretical findings.

title: FreePath: Neural Mean Free Path for Image Dehazing
abstract: Single image dehazing requires recovering scene radiance from visual responses that are weakened and veiled by participating media. Existing methods either invert explicit scattering variables, which can be unstable under complex scenes, or learn direct restoration mappings, which often discard the physical organization of haze formation. We present \emph{FreePath}, a neural mean free path framework for image dehazing. Instead of estimating atmospheric parameters, FreePath represents dehazing as feature space path state restoration, inspired by the expected distance a visual response can propagate before interacting with haze. Within a residual encoder and decoder, the Mean Free Path Residual Block learns path and collision fields to guide haze constrained correction, while FreePath State Conservation Integration preserves restored path states during deep feature aggregation. Experiments on paired CDD-11 haze images and real RTTS scenes show that FreePath consistently improves full reference fidelity, no reference perceptual quality, and visual faithfulness over representative dehazing baselines.

title: Vis2State: Visual Reasoning through Executable State Abstractions
abstract: Solving visual puzzles requires both accurate interpretation of visual evidence and reliable computation under task-specific rules. Embedding visual assumptions and task constraints directly in solving code makes the represented problem difficult to inspect and revise independently. We introduce Vis2State, a training-free agentic framework that abstracts visual puzzles into explicit, revisable problem states linking visual inspection and execution. Visual inspection guides state construction and refinement, while generated programs solve the represented problem. The model constructs both the state and the program without predefined puzzle schemas or solving procedures. Inspection and execution feedback allow it to revise the problem representation and solving procedure independently. Vis2State achieves the state-of-the-art performance on four benchmarks. Cross-model evaluation further demonstrates consistent gains. Ablations, error analyses, and fixed-program state interventions further support the effectiveness of the state-centered design. The code will be made publicly available to facilitate future research.

title: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence
abstract: We present \textbf{WeLM-Image}, a unified image foundation model that integrates multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis. Designed for single-GPU deployment in WeChat's large-scale consumer applications, the model processes text, reference images, and target latents as one interleaved sequence. A Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone combines shared attention with independent understanding and generation parameters to limit optimization interference. Equipping each path with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) modules provides sparse capacity, with 31.7B stored parameters and approximately 5.4B generation parameters activated per target latent token. A generation-oriented data engine combines a knowledge-grounded visual vocabulary with large-scale visual clustering to balance semantic coverage and editing tasks, while training-time evaluation guides iterative data refinement. Bilingual annotations and verified editing supervision support progressive training up to native 1.5K resolution. We optimize generation and editing separately with rubric- and checklist-based rewards, then consolidate the specialized policies through noise-aware on-policy distillation. In the reported overall comparisons, the 1536-resolution model ranks first among the evaluated open-source models on PRISM-Bench, Qwen-Image-Bench, and UnicBench. MeanFlow-based few-step distillation yields WeLM-Image-Turbo, which generates a $1024\times1024$ image in 4.98\,s on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU using eight guidance-free steps.
authors: Canmiao Fu;Chen Li;Guohui Zhang;Hao Lu;Hongyang Wei;Huadong Wu;Huaisong Zhang;Hubery Yin;Liyuan Cui;Qixin Yan;Tong Shao;Xiaoqiang Zhou;Xinhang Leng;Ying Zhang;Zhenhai Liu;Zhipeng Huang

title: Certifying the Rydberg-exposure limit of a globally driven controlled-Z gate
abstract: Rydberg excitation enables entangling gates in neutral-atom quantum processors but also exposes them to spontaneous decay. Whether this exposure can be made arbitrarily small through pulse shaping and longer gate times has remained unresolved. We show that an exact controlled-$Z$ gate driven by a single global laser has an irreducible Rydberg-exposure cost in the perfect-blockade regime. The product of the maximum Rabi frequency $Ω_{\max}$ and the average time $T_R$ spent in the Rydberg state is bounded below by $2.9312$, independent of pulse shape and duration. We derive this bound using a sum-of-squares certificate, strengthened by constraints imposed by the shared drive. Using interval arithmetic, we also certify the existence of an exact gate pulse with $Ω_{max} T_R<2.9359$. The unrounded bounds differ by less than $0.16\%$. The bound identifies a fundamental cost of shared-drive entangling dynamics and establishes a benchmark against which future gate-control strategies can be assessed.
authors: Yusheng Zhao;Han Wang;Mingrui Jing;Zhongyi Ni;Hongshun Yao;Xin Wang;Jie Wang;Jinguo Liu

title: FFMT: Frequency-Factorized Multi-Rate Tokenization for Music-to-Dance Generation
abstract: Dance motion combines slowly varying body configurations with rapid local movements. We investigate how explicit temporal-frequency decomposition can guide the temporal resolution and codebook capacity of discrete motion representations. We introduce frequency-factorized motion tokenization (FFMT), which separates root-relative motion into a low-frequency choreographic scaffold and a complementary high-frequency residual. FFMT uses a lower token rate and a smaller codebook for the low-frequency component, and a higher token rate and a larger codebook for the high-frequency residual. This representation further induces a plan-then-articulate autoregressive factorization: low-frequency tokens establish coarse choreography, while high-frequency tokens realize local motion details conditioned on the generated plan and music. Experiments on AIST++ and FineDance show strong distributional fidelity while preserving realistic diversity and music--motion synchronization. Ablations consistently support frequency factorization, asymmetric temporal allocation, and low-to-high conditioning.
authors: Qirong Guo;Ruijie Li;Zeyan Li;Sicheng Shu;Guanzhi Ding;Weihang Ding

title: Distributed Robust Model Predictive Control for Optimal Consensus of Unknown Multiagent Systems with Event-Triggered Communication
abstract: In this paper, we study the optimal consensus problem for multiagent systems with unknown dynamics. We propose a robust model predictive control (MPC) framework that jointly optimizes the control input and consensus sequences while enforcing state and input constraints. Within this framework, noisy offline data are used to construct nominal prediction models and quantify the associated uncertainty, which is explicitly incorporated into the robust MPC design. To solve the resulting optimization problem at each MPC update with reduced inter-agent communication, we develop a distributed gradient-projection alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm with an event-triggered information exchange mechanism and establish its convergence to the optimal solution. Furthermore, sufficient conditions are established to guarantee robust constraint satisfaction and practical consensus of the closed-loop multiagent system. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

title: Spin-Exchange-Controlled Nonclassical Light in Cavity Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
abstract: Controlling nonclassical light while maintaining a finite cavity response requires selective suppression of unwanted multiphoton excitation. We investigate a ring-cavity system containing two three-level emitters coupled by a coherent spin-exchange interaction, where electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) provides resonant access to a dark-state polariton. The exchange interaction shifts the polariton resonance while modifying the dressed two-photon excitation pathways. Strong photon antibunching emerges when the one-polariton resonance nearly coincides with a destructive-interference minimum of the second-photon transition amplitude. By jointly tuning the exchange interaction and control-field strength, pronounced photon blockade with a finite intracavity population can be sustained over an extended interaction range. We further show that the relative cavity-coupling phase redistributes optical coupling between symmetric and antisymmetric collective channels with opposite exchange shifts, allowing the photon statistics to switch between antibunching and bunching at fixed exchange strength. This mechanism provides a possible route to tunable nonclassical-light sources based on coherent control of collective excitation pathways.
authors: Jing Tang;Junyu Su;Jie Chen;Ziyang Li;Yuangang Deng

title: Is Morphology All You Need? Quantifying Imprints of Past Star Formation in the Present-Day Morphologies of Galaxies
abstract: The next generation of galaxy surveys will bring a plethora of new observations, a vast majority of which will be observed with a few photometric broadbands, limiting the information we can infer from traditional SED fitting methods. To maximize the scientific value of these surveys, techniques that can go beyond traditional summary statistics in extracting information from galaxy observations are needed. Moving beyond integrated photometry, we introduce the Katachi-PRIME method to do spectral energy distribution (SED) based inference that jointly incorporates morphological and SED information. Katachi-PRIME uses implicit likelihood inference (ILI) to incorporate realistic morphological priors from gri broadband images, to make predictions of: stellar mass (M$_*$), specific star formation rate (sSFR), redshift (z), age (t$_{50}$), dust attenuation (Av), and gas-phase metallicity (12+log(O/H)) of the galaxy. We find that this improves constraints compared to traditional 5-band photometry. We then use the learned morphological priors to examine the extent to which morphology encodes information about past star formation, finding a stark dichotomy in how morphology encodes star formation history. While the stable morphologies of main-sequence and quiescent galaxies can predict past star formation out to $\sim 4-7$ Gyr and $\sim3-5$ Gyr, respectively, starburst and green-valley populations above and below the main sequence tend to experience structural disruptions that obscure all but the most recent star formation activity. Methods like Katachi-PRIME maximize the scientific value of future telescopes by providing broad-baseline SED-level property estimates by incorporating morphological information.
authors: Juan Pablo Alfonzo;Kartheik G. Iyer;Masayuki Akiyama;Camilla Pacifici;Abdurro'uf;Suchetha Cooray;Novan Saputra Haryana;Marc Huertas-Company;Christopher C. Lovell;Rachel Somerville;Joshua S. Speagle;John F. Wu;Mikaeel Yunus

title: EnvOpt: Automated Optimization for Agent Environments
abstract: An LLM agent's cost and success depend on its model, its harness, and its environment. In addition to the widely studied directions of parameter tuning and harness optimization, we propose the third direction: optimization over stationary environments. Agents are often deployed in rich environments shared by many tasks, such as a company's Slack workspace or a complex collection of data sources, documents or tickets. We call these environments stationary environments. We introduce EnvOpt, a method for automated end-to-end optimization of stationary environments for any given model and harness, using real or synthetic tasks without needing any graders or reference answers. On AutomationBench, EnvOpt reduces the cost of Claude Haiku 4.5 by 72.7% and raises its pass rate by 14.34%. The same environment transfers to Opus 5, cutting its cost by 68.1% with a 1.34% gain. Added on top of Meta-Harness's optimized harness for Haiku 4.5, it lowers cost by a further 83.4% and adds 11.17% accuracy over Meta-Harness alone. Across 5 benchmarks, EnvOpt significantly reduces the cost of agents while improving or maintaining pass rate, and is transferable to different models and different harnesses. We also discuss common successful and rejected environment optimization strategies during automated optimization. More broadly, our results show that how information is represented to an agent shapes both its cost and its success, making the environment worth optimizing in addition to the parameters and the harness.
authors: Mingxuan Li;Huanzhi Mao;Qiuyang Mang;Hanchen Li;Joseph E. Gonzalez;Alex Dimakis

title: Operational Characterizations and Resource Structure of the Interactive Weight of Quantum Instruments
abstract: Quantifying the interactivity of quantum instruments is fundamental to understanding their resource structure and operational capabilities. Here, we introduce the interactive weight of quantum instruments as a resource quantifier that measures the minimum fraction of an instrument that cannot be explained by non-interactive components. Through quantum-information tasks including quantum-state recovery, positive linear loss games, and environment-assisted input-blind extraction, we establish quantitative bounds on the interactive weight of quantum instruments and exact operational characterizations of its complementary quantity, the maximal non-interactive content. In particular, we extend environment-assisted input-blind extraction to the setting of restricted environmental access and develop a corresponding framework. Within the allowed-operations framework introduced by Hsieh et al., we establish fundamental resource-theoretic properties of the interactive weight of quantum instruments, including faithfulness, convexity, and monotonicity under deterministic allowed operations. Furthermore, we prove that the maximal non-interactive content satisfies exact multiplicativity under independent parallel composition, yielding necessary constraints on multicopy resource conversion and establishing the finite-copy maximal-weight distillation no-go result under deterministic allowed operations. These results establish a unified theoretical framework for the interactive weight of quantum instruments from the perspectives of resource quantification, operational interpretation, and resource conversion, providing systematic theoretical tools for the quantitative comparison and conversion of interactive quantum instruments.
authors: Yongxi He;Xin Hong;Yu Luo;Xiangzhen Zhou;Shenggang Ying

title: Continuous-time q-Learning for Finite-Horizon Portfolio Choice with Optimal Stopping in Jump-Diffusion Markets
abstract: We develop a structured continuous-time q-learning framework for finite-horizon investment and optimal stopping under jump-diffusion dynamics with unknown parameters. A penalty approximation transforms the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman variational inequality into an HJB equation with a binary control for the stopping penalty. An auxiliary state incorporates the resulting control-dependent discount factor into a Markovian formulation. We randomize controls on the mixed action space and introduce Shannon entropy regularization, establishing policy improvement and martingale characterizations of the continuous-time q-function. These results motivate a structured q-learning algorithm that constructs the q-function from the penalty HJB equation and jointly learns the value function and unknown generator parameters from sample paths. We apply the method to portfolio choice with optimal stopping in a simulation study. We further conduct a two-asset empirical study, evaluating learned strategies on bootstrap paths from held-out test returns versus an MLE-finite difference benchmark.

title: A Synchronized Tri-Modality Wireless System for Multi-Point Non-Contact Cardiac Monitoring
abstract: Cardiac physiological monitoring is fundamental to evaluating cardiovascular health and diagnosing related diseases. Non-contact radar sensing can capture chest-wall vibrations with spatial specificity, enabling localized physiological monitoring and cardiac assessment. Progress, however, has been limited by the absence of a reliable, research-grade hardware platform for rigorous validation of radar-based methods. Prior systems typically pair radar, namely Doppler cardiography (DCG), with only electrocardiography (ECG) or other coarse references, providing no direct mechanical ground truth and thus constraining fine-grained evaluation of radar outputs. We present a tri-modality wireless system that integrates ECG, seismocardiography (SCG), and DCG under a unified acquisition and control framework for time-aligned recording and analysis. The tri-modality system combines miniaturized wearable ECG/SCG modules with a high-resolution mmWave radar module, supporting spatially resolved sensing and subsequent feature extraction. To our knowledge, this is the first integrated ECG--SCG--DCG hardware system for comprehensive cardiac monitoring; it enables multi-point thoracic acquisition, achieves precise cross-modal synchronization, and maintains specifications suitable for wearable operation. Experiments on a linear-motion platform show close agreement between DCG- and SCG-derived displacements, confirming accurate displacement measurement. Human-subject studies further demonstrate cross-modal consistency and robust extraction of feature points, establishing ECG as the electrical anchor and SCG as the mechanical ground truth for DCG. Overall, the system provides a rigorous, spatially resolved validation platform that advances non-contact cardiac sensing and supports next-generation radar-based monitoring.
authors: Wei Ren;Kaili Zhao;Huansheng Yi;Miaoyang Hu;Jianqi Wang;Canhua Xu;Fugui Qi

title: MIKU: Material Invariance and Knowledge Unification for PBR Generation
abstract: High-quality material generation for physically based rendering (PBR) remains challenging because datasets and synthesis pipelines lack standardized representations. Differences in material definitions, rendering conventions, and parameterizations lead to unstable and physically implausible results. We propose MIKU, a unified framework for standardized PBR asset representation and physically consistent material generation across diverse 3D content domains. Its core is a unified processing pipeline that standardizes the workflow from data preprocessing to final texture synthesis, maintaining consistent geometry and texture representations. A normalization scheme harmonizes heterogeneous material parameterizations in a common representation space, enabling robust cross-dataset training and inference. Building on this formulation, we train a novel physically aware diffusion model for PBR texture generation within a two-stage multi-view synthesis framework. First, geometry-aware albedo generation synthesizes multi-view albedo maps under explicit geometric guidance to ensure cross-view appearance consistency. Second, metallic-roughness generation uses the diffusion model to predict physically plausible roughness and metallic maps conditioned on the generated albedo and unified representation. Trained end-to-end on standardized data, the model learns to generate materials that respect category-level material priors and semantic part boundaries. By decoupling representation standardization from appearance synthesis, MIKU substantially improves material generation stability and physical consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art texture quality and semantic consistency across object parts, advancing automated material generation for 3D content creation.
authors: Yajie Bao;Jiaye Fu;Youtian Lin;Shuang Wu;Jiachen Qian;Feihu Zhang;Xun Cao;Yao Yao
