title: Rotating two-dimensional Bose--Einstein condensates in power-law traps: collapse, Thomas--Fermi scaling, and the inverse-square endpoint
abstract: In two dimensions, the kinetic and contact energies scale identically under dilation, a trap $V=r^s/s$ as $λ^{-s}$. We follow this balance through the power-law family $-2\le s\le4$, $s\neq0$, for both signs of the coupling $g$, with rotation, using scaling bounds, radial solutions, Bogoliubov spectra, and two-dimensional imaginary-time states. Attraction collapses the cloud at the Townes coupling $g_{*}$ in every trap, with width $\ell\proptoδ^{1/(s+2)}$, $δ=1-|g|/g_{*}$; repulsion spreads it to a Thomas--Fermi (TF) radius $\propto g^{1/(s+2)}$. A rotating collapse leaves the axis once the rotation frequency $Ω$ exceeds its dipole frequency, which softens only for $s>2$; in a quartic trap this happens at $δ\simeq0.32\,Ω^6$, within $3\%$ of the Bogoliubov threshold; it then collapses on the minimum ring of the rotating-frame potential, which also empties a repulsive TF cloud at $Ω=(3g/π)^{1/6}$. For repulsive vortex states the TF energy error splits exactly into a density-gradient and a flow part of comparable or larger size. At $s=-2$ only the cutoff sets a length: the energy is exactly covariant with it, the condensate falls to the center for both signs, and repulsion leaves a halo of density $\propto1/(gr^2)$ whose extent grows exponentially with $g$. Near collapse, split-step imaginary time has a first-order stationary bias invisible to residual tests.

title: Amortized Nonlinear Variable Selection with Prior-Data Fitted Networks
abstract: Variable selection is an important task for interpreting potentially complex systems in fields such as biology, business, and sociology. The importance of variable selection has attracted considerable attention in statistics and machine learning. In this paper, we are mainly interested in model-agnostic variable selection for identifying variables that have general nonlinear dependence on the response. We propose MambaPFN, short for Model-Agnostic Markov BlAnket selection with Prior-data Fitted Networks, which is built upon the Transformer, a building block of many popular large language models. Specifically, we consider a functional-mapping perspective on variable-selection learning, in which the Transformer is treated as a learnable mapping from a dataset to its relevant variables. To learn this mapping, MambaPFN introduces three new components: (i) a faithful, rich, and scalable scheme for generating pretraining data, (ii) an objective that targets each variable's posterior inclusion probability, and (iii) a modified Transformer architecture tailored to variable selection. Once pretrained, MambaPFN is applied to new datasets without parameter updates. Empirically, MambaPFN achieves desirable variable-selection performance in simulation studies and exhibits a scaling law---more pretraining datasets and larger models can continuously improve its performance. Applied to a Facebook comments dataset, MambaPFN selects the fewest variables and achieves the highest computational efficiency and predictive performance, improving upon the best baselines by about 20%.

title: Mitigating small gaps in quantum annealing through recursive $XX-$catalyst construction
abstract: The introduction of $XX-$interactions, typically in the form of an additional catalyst Hamiltonian, has shown promise as a tool for gap enhancement in quantum annealing, allowing the algorithm to obtain optimal solutions with shorter run-times. However, the optimal placements of these couplings within the problem graph has been found to be highly setting-dependent. In this work, we propose an iterative catalyst-construction protocol for the removal of a common quantum annealing bottleneck known as perturbative crossings. The method utilises the measurements returned by successive annealing runs to effectively steer the algorithm away from the local optima in which it becomes trapped. First, we motivate a framework for $XX-$term selection based on perturbation theory and establish its effectiveness at removing perturbative crossings on scalable toy instances with up to $39$ spins, demonstrating a consistent performance both with increasing system size and number of local optima. We then simulate the recursive catalyst-construction method on a test set of $18-$spin maximum-weight independent set problems that are generated to produce annealing spectra with multiple perturbative crossings. We find that the protocol significantly outperforms both catalyst-free annealing and annealing with catalysts containing randomly selected $XX-$terms.
authors: Natasha Feinstein;Sebastian Schulz;Robert J. Banks;Roopayan Ghosh;Kristel Michielsen;Sougato Bose;P A Warburton

title: Feeling of Knowing in Large Language Models
abstract: Post-training updates change what large language models (LLMs) can answer, but may leave their answerability judgments misaligned. We study this knowledge-judgment desynchronization through functional feeling of knowing (FoK), which supports selective generation, retrieval triggering, and model routing without implying subjective experience. We propose two trainable channels: a knowledge channel that changes answerability and a FoK channel that judges the current knowledge state. Three stages train them: on-policy supervised fine-tuning (OP-SFT) updates knowledge from corrected on-policy answers; knowledge-delta FoK training (K$Δ$-FT) adapts judgments across intermediate knowledge states; and FoK-guided policy optimization (FGPO) trains the subsequent answer or explanation. Factual-QA experiments, cross-dataset evaluation, and three sequential updates show that explicit FoK alignment improves judgment quality on updated knowledge. MMLU and ARC-Easy separately assess capability preservation.
authors: Zichuan Fu;Xian Wu;Jingtong Gao;Wenlin Zhang;Jiaxuan Li;Binhao Wang;Yimin Deng;Guojing Li;Xiaopeng Li;Derong Xu;Yefeng Zheng;Xiangyu Zhao

title: UniFlow: Unified Multi-Scale Flow Matching for Time Series Generation
abstract: Real-world time series exhibit complex dynamics across multiple temporal resolutions, yet effectively incorporating multi-scale information into generative modeling remains challenging without increasing generative complexity. We propose UniFlow, a unified framework that integrates multi-scale representation learning with efficient non-autoregressive generation through a shared-semantic discrete interface. Specifically, a multi-scale tokenizer employs shared-index voting to consolidate complementary temporal information into a single public-ID sequence, while scale-specific codebooks preserve the information required for reconstruction. Building on this unified representation, we develop geometry-aware categorical flow matching, which initializes transport from learned low-rank anchors and generates public identities non-autoregressively. This design captures multi-scale temporal structure without requiring multiple generative token streams or sequential token decoding. Experiments across four benchmarks and both short- and long-term settings demonstrate improved generative fidelity, strong cross-scale consistency, and substantial inference speedups over representative autoregressive and diffusion-based baselines. Code is available at https://github.com/kkking-kk/UniFlow
authors: Shibo Feng;Wei Li;Songhua Liu;Min Wu;Chunyan Miao;Peilin Zhao

title: Assignment-Free Swarm Navigation via Adaptive Target-Field Planning and Mean-Shift Exploration
abstract: Mean-shift exploration enables assignment-free swarm shape assembly, but obstacle-constrained navigation additionally requires coordinated adaptation of the desired morphology and its physical execution. This paper presents an environment-adaptive navigation framework that integrates target-field planning, execution regulation, and morphology-preserving mean-shift exploration. A feasibility-aware graph search plans the position, orientation, and morphology of an unlabeled target field without specifying robot-specific goals. An execution-regulated reference manager adjusts field progression and morphology switching using swarm entering, coverage, and lag metrics. A moving-frame controller separates prescribed rigid motion from local mean-shift redistribution and incorporates neighbor interactions and obstacle responses. Simulations and hardware experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework coordinates morphology transitions and collective motion for assignment-free swarm navigation through cluttered environments.

title: Radial distortion homography estimation from affine-covariant or orientation-covariant features
abstract: We present minimal solvers for joint homography and radial distortion estimation using affine- or orientation-covariant features. The core contribution is a set of novel constraints that exploit local feature geometry inherent to affine descriptors, enabling solvers that require fewer correspondences than point-based methods. Using modern robust estimation frameworks, we demonstrate that the proposed solvers are advantageous to the current state-of-the-art with a significant speed-up in the presence of outliers while maintaining comparable or superior estimation accuracy. The proposed solvers are tested on both synthetic and real images containing challenging fisheye distortions.

title: How to Look Inside the Black Box: A Survey of Yu. E. Nesterov's Contributions (On the Award of the 2026 Gauss Prize)
abstract: On July 23, 2026, at the opening of the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia, the International Mathematical Union announced the award of the Gauss Prize to Yurii Evgenievich Nesterov -- an award for mathematical work with significant applications outside mathematics. This article explains the mathematical content of the recognized work of Yu. E. Nesterov and traces its influence on modern computational practice. The exposition is based on a concept that Yu. E. Nesterov himself regards as one of his main results: the classical complexity theory of convex optimization is oriented toward a black-box oracle, but its pessimistic bounds can be overcome by using a priori information about the internal structure of the objective function. We trace Yu. E. Nesterov's scientific career, then introduce the language of oracle complexity together with a classification of objective function models (geometric, algebraic, and structural), and subsequently discuss his main results in chronological order: the fast gradient method, fast automatic differentiation, the theory of self-concordant barriers and polynomial-time interior-point methods, the $π/2$ theorem, the stable dynamics model of traffic flows, the smoothing technique, primal-dual methods, cubic regularization of Newton's method, the modified Gauss--Newton scheme, coordinate descent methods and methods for huge-scale problems, gradient-free methods, universal gradient methods, implementable tensor methods, and "superfast" methods. Each topic is accompanied by historical background, precise statements specifying the problem class, oracle, and type of guarantee, examples, and a discussion of the current state of the art.
authors: A. V. Gasnikov;A. Yu. Gornov;D. M. Dvinskikh;Yu. V. Dorn;D. I. Kamzolov;Yu. V. Maximov;V. V. Matyukhin;R. F. Hildebrand

title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing Detection with Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks
abstract: This work investigates the application of Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks to the binary classification of sleep-disordered breathing events in time-series data, aiming to distinguish between apneic and normal breathing episodes. A variational classical--quantum architecture is proposed and evaluated against classical Recurrent Neural Network models. Experiments were conducted on multiple real-world datasets with varying levels of complexity to assess the strengths and limitations of the quantum approach. In the comparative analysis, both classical and quantum models showed comparable performance. The quantum model achieved superior performance on the smallest dataset, while yielding slightly weaker results in the most complex setting. However, the quantum approach exhibited notable strengths, such as competitive performance despite a drastically reduced parameter count and low-qubit regime, as well as good generalization capabilities. These results suggest that, despite current hardware and algorithmic limitations, variational quantum recurrent models represent a promising alternative for time-series classification as Quantum Computing technologies continue to mature.
authors: Alejandro Mayorga-Redondo;José Daniel Viqueira;Diego Alvarez-Estevez;Eduardo Mosqueira-Rey;Andrés Gómez

title: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression
abstract: Large reasoning models achieve strong performance on challenging tasks, but their long chain-of-thought often incurs substantial inference costs by continuing to deliberate after sufficient information has been obtained. Existing reasoning compression methods primarily operate on reasoning trajectories, paying less attention to the local decision of whether further reasoning is necessary given the current state. We propose LoCo, a local preference learning method for reasoning compression. LoCo detects candidate overthinking states from the model's own traces, freezes the corresponding reasoning prefixes, regenerates shorter verified continuations from the same states, and trains on the resulting state-conditioned preference pairs with DPO. This formulation teaches the model when to continue reasoning and when to conclude, rather than simply encouraging shorter trajectories overall. We construct training data entirely from self-generated mathematical traces and evaluate LoCo on five mathematical and three code generation benchmarks. LoCo reduces completion length by 41.7\%--45.4\% on mathematics and 23.4\%--36.3\% on code, while maintaining or improving accuracy and achieving the best AUC across all code benchmarks. LoCo consistently improves the accuracy-efficiency trade-off on mathematics and transfers effectively to code generation despite math-only training, demonstrating the cross-domain generality of local preference learning for reasoning compression. The code and model will be publicly released at https://github.com/MuyaoYuan/LoCo.
authors: Muyao Yuan;Liyan Xu;Weizhan Zhang;Muyan Jiao;Jiangnan Li;Jinchao Zhang;Jie Zhou

title: NightIQA: A Comprehensive Dataset and Benchmark for MLLM-Based Nighttime Image Quality Assessment
abstract: Nighttime images are inherently susceptible to complex, compound degradations, making accurate quality assessment exceptionally challenging. Score-based IQA methods condense quality into a single number, lacking the multi-dimensional, language-grounded reasoning required for nighttime evaluation. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) offer a more comprehensive alternative, yet remain constrained by a critical data gap: existing real-world IQA datasets are overwhelmingly daytime-centric and often built from outdated captures, while synthetic alternatives lack nighttime-specific degradation modeling, yielding artifacts far removed from authentic nighttime conditions. To bridge this gap, we present NightIQA, a dataset and benchmark suite purpose-built for MLLM-based nighttime IQA. It comprises three core components: NightIQA-Real, a real-world dataset of 1,769 high-resolution images that we captured ourselves with modern equipment, encompassing six canonical distortion types and structured multi-dimensional annotations; NightIQA-Bench, a benchmark of 1,078 visually grounded multiple-choice questions tailored to MLLM-based nighttime IQA, organized around a four-level evaluation hierarchy spanning Perception, Technical Assessment, Localization, and Reasoning; and NightIQA-Syn, an inherently scalable, scene-aware synthesis pipeline that jointly models global-level and instance-level degradations, with an initial release of 80k high-fidelity images alongside the full generation code. Fine-tuned on NightIQA with Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), Qwen3-VL-8B outperforms open-source IQA methods and achieves higher overall accuracy than leading closed-source models, highlighting the value of domain-specific data and structured supervision.
authors: Yiding Tian;Jiaojiao Yi;Jiayuan Lu;Pufan Xu;Jinlin Wu;Changyuan Wen;Hongyuan Yu

title: Asymptotic Optimality of $cμ$-Rule for LLM Inference Scheduling under Memory Constraint
abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference, the process by which a pre-trained model receives an input prompt and generates output tokens sequentially, has become increasingly important with the widespread deployment of LLM-based applications. As inference workloads continue to scale, GPU memory has emerged as a critical bottleneck: the long input prompts and generation sequences common in agentic and reasoning workloads lead to substantial key-value (KV) cache usage. In this paper, we study the resulting online scheduling problem from a queueing perspective. Requests arrive stochastically with heterogeneous prompt and output lengths, undergo prefill and autoregressive decode, and compete for a finite KV-cache capacity. Unlike classical queueing models, the duration of a processing step depends on both prefill computation and KV-cache I/O, so service capacity is jointly determined by computation, memory access, and memory occupancy. We develop a fluid model that reduces the system to a multiclass single-server queue with effective service rates capturing computation, memory access, and memory capacity. This fluid analysis yields a $cμ$ priority rule, where the effective service rate $μ$ is jointly determined by computational speed, memory bandwidth, and memory capacity. We prove that this rule minimizes cumulative holding cost in the fluid model and, for a finite workload, also minimizes completion time and maximizes full-run output-token throughput. We then construct a feasible scheduling policy for the original finite system and prove that its scaled dynamics converge to the optimal fluid policy. Finally, experiments on a real LLM serving engine using an NVIDIA H800 show that practical implementations of the proposed priority rule substantially reduce average latency while maintaining high throughput relative to existing scheduling policies.

title: Where Is the Truth When AI Agents Disagree? Dependence-Aware Belief Propagation for Unsupervised Truth Discovery (Extended Version)
abstract: LLM agents often give conflicting answers to the same question, and many deployed agents are variants of one base model, so their errors are correlated. We study truth discovery among such agents: inferring the true answer and each agent's reliability without labels. Classical truth-discovery and crowdsourcing estimators reward an agreeing bloc and can fall below majority vote. We propose BP-TD, which adds per-agent decorrelation weights to mean-field variational inference on a one-coin Dawid-Skene model, so that agents sharing a base model count together as about one vote. Its first iteration is exactly a weighted vote; later iterations estimate agent reliability. With 13 local agents on MMLU, BP-TD beats majority vote without any labels (0.716 vs. 0.624 on 160 questions; 0.707 vs. 0.674 on 10,000) and ranks agents by their true accuracy, which classical estimators invert. The gain depends on the pool: over 2,852 sub-pools of four benchmarks, decorrelation helps when the largest correlated bloc is weaker than the other agents and hurts when it is the strongest, and we found no label-free statistic that tells the two cases apart. Labels change the picture quickly: with 20 labelled questions, selecting the single best agent is more accurate than every aggregator we tested on MMLU, ARC and TruthfulQA.

title: Generic factorizations and alternating direction method for fixed-rank approximation of matrix polynomials
abstract: We present an algorithm for approximating a given matrix polynomial of degree $d$ by a matrix polynomial of prescribed rank and degree at most $d$. The method builds on recent advances in the theory of generic eigenstructures and factorizations of matrix polynomials with bounded rank and degree. We also give a specialized treatment of the case of matrix pencils (degree one matrix polynomials), motivated by its particular theoretical and practical importance. Lastly, numerical experiments are reported to assess the performance of the proposed approach and to compare it with existing methods.
authors: Sweta Das;Andrii Dmytryshyn;Froilán M. Dopico;Mårten Gulliksson

title: Training Specialist LLMs on Your Phone: Forward-Only Optimization via Block-Spectral Coordinates
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) on personal devices keep user data local, but limited memory restricts their general capability. Since most user-specific tasks do not require the breadth of frontier models, a practical solution is to adapt a shared on-device model into lightweight specialists. However, backpropagation is prohibitive in memory, and users rarely provide labeled data. We present MobileSpec, a system that trains specialists with forward passes alone and learns from automatically checked task outcomes, as in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Because forward-only updates are built from random perturbations, training is efficient only when these perturbations resemble the weight changes of RLVR, which largely preserve the singular values of pretrained weights and rotate their singular vectors. The core algorithm of MobileSpec, FuRA-S, produces such perturbations while training only the block-spectral coordinates of pretrained weights, namely the singular values of their column blocks. As we show theoretically and empirically, rescaling these blocks independently shifts their relative contributions to each weight matrix and thereby rotates its singular vectors. Since this update can be rewritten as a transformation of the layer input, FuRA-S also adapts INT4 models without modifying their weights. With specialists of only 1-5 MB that update 0.015-0.05% of the parameters, MobileSpec raises the success rate of a phone-use agent from 6-23% up to 89-100% and trains a personalized 8B model on an iPhone 16 Pro overnight. On RLVR benchmarks, FuRA-S is competitive with full-parameter evolution strategies (ES) and outperforms ES over LoRA adapters and quantized ES on INT4 models.
authors: Liyan Tan;Yequan Zhao;Ziyue Liu;Yupeng Su;Ruijie Zhang;Zheng Zhang

title: Plug-and-Play Sensor Evolution in Software-Defined Vehicles through Asset Administration Shells
abstract: Software-defined vehicles (SDVs) promise continuous software evolution, but sensor integration in deployed vehicles still depends on manual configuration, hardware-specific drivers, and repeated application-side adaptation. Existing standards address only parts of this problem. AUTOSAR standardizes selected sensor interfaces, the Vehicle Signal Specification (VSS) standardizes signal semantics, and Asset Administration Shells (AAS) standardize digital asset descriptions. However, these building blocks are rarely combined into an end-to-end onboarding path for sensors attached after vehicle deployment. This paper presents an AAS-driven plug-and-play sensor integration framework for safety-supervised sensors. Each sensor is represented by an AAS that combines hardware identification, interface metadata, VSS mappings, and references to containerized driver and optional application software. After physical connection, an edge gateway identifies the device, retrieves the matching AAS, deploys the referenced software, and publishes the resulting data under stable vehicle signal paths. A prototype on a resource-constrained edge gateway connected to an RR100 UGV demonstrates automated integration of a USB camera and an ultrasonic sensor. Across repeated integration cycles, the prototype reaches operational state in about 2s, shows no failed events, and keeps applications independent of hardware-specific interfaces. The results indicate that the introduction of AAS as an executable onboarding contract enables automated runtime deployment of sensor drivers in SDV environments.
comment: Peer-reviewed and Published in the 2026 IEEE 31st International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA)

title: ReSI-Math: Exploring Recoverable Capability Frontiers for Efficient Reasoning Improvement
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an effective approach for improving mathematical reasoning in large language models. However, a fundamental question remains: when a model fails to solve a problem, does it truly lack the underlying capability? In this work, we reveal that direct failure does not necessarily imply inability. Some reasoning failures can be recovered by exploring the model's own trajectories, exposing a recoverable capability frontier: a policy-dependent region where solutions are not reliably generated through direct decoding but can be elicited through trajectory-level search. Based on this observation, we introduce ReSI-Math, a framework that explores recoverable capability frontiers and converts recovered capabilities into data-efficient RLVR supervision. ReSI-Math uses Self-Judge-guided evolutionary search to identify recoverable failures under a fixed policy and adaptively selects frontier problems for sequential RLVR as the policy evolves. On Qwen3-VL-8B, correct-incorrect trajectory crossover produces 272 verifier-confirmed correct offspring from 621 attempts (43.8%). After three sequential one-shot RLVR stages, the MATH500 and WE-MATH average improves from 78.71 to 80.16. Under matched single-problem RLVR, random selection reaches only 53.31 versus 54.16 for frontier-guided Q1.
authors: Yao Cui;Zhen Yang;Yuandong Wang;Yangfu Zhu;Tianyu Wo;Zhenzhou Shao

title: LIPS-PC: Learning Illumination Patterns for Single-Pixel Classification
abstract: In single-pixel (ghost) imaging, known illumination patterns probe an object and a detector with no spatial resolution returns one number per pattern. Each measurement costs acquisition time and photons and, for ionizing probes, contributes to delivered dose. Motivated by automated radiographic defect screening, where a class label suffices, we introduce Learning Illumination Patterns for Single-Pixel Classification (LIPS-PC). The patterns are learned end-to-end while the measurement operator remains one fixed linear matrix, identical for every input. We parameterize it as a residual correction to a two-dimensional discrete cosine transform (2D-DCT), $D=D_{\mathrm{base}}+Δ$, and jointly train the correction and a compact classifier using cross-entropy, without a reconstruction objective. This yields a task-driven linear embedding through optimization. We evaluate LIPS-PC numerically on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST under a controlled protocol, then on RIAWELC, a real industrial X-ray weld-radiograph dataset. Across five budgets, $M\in{8,16,32,64,128}$, corresponding to sampling ratios from below 1% to 12.5%, the learned operator outperforms the best tested fixed transform by 9-15 percentage points at $M=8$ on all three datasets. Its eight-measurement accuracy requires roughly 16-32 measurements with the best fixed transform, indicating a $2\times$ to $4\times$ saving at comparable accuracy. The advantage generally shrinks as $M$ increases, with a small reversal on RIAWELC at higher budgets. These results show that learning what to measure is especially valuable when measurements are scarce.

title: Bulk and edge states in Fibonacci-Bose-Hubbard clusters
abstract: We study the one- and two-boson energy subspaces of finite open Bose--Hubbard chains with Fibonacci-modulated hopping and zero on-site potential. Their spectra exhibit a hierarchy of bands and gaps, and a critical zero-energy mode for odd lengths, in agreement with prior research. For the singe-excitation subspace we find two families of length-invariant finite-energy states localized at the left cluster boundary. For the two-boson subspace, we report both doublon and separated-pair excitations in the form of Tamm/Shockley states localized near either end. In particular, the right-edge doublon states occur across all Fibonacci generations whereas the left-side states appear every second generation. We check numerically that the second-order perturbation theory accounts well for the structure of the spectrum and the edge states in the doublon subspace in the strong-coupling regime. The results are useful for future explorations of many-body physics beyond numerical tractability, specifically using near-term Josephson quantum simulators.
authors: G. P. Fedorov;E. E. Konopleva;O. V. Astafiev

title: Temporal stretching of single-photon pulses by intra-cavity frequency conversion
abstract: Spectral bandwidth and frequency mismatch between quantum light emitters and quantum components is a common problem in the realization of hybrid quantum information networks. Here we propose a simultaneous solution to both of these problems by using a free-space cavity with an embedded nonlinear crystal that, through frequency conversion, facilitates perfect coupling into a cavity mode. The slow leakage of the cavity effectively stretches the photon pulse, resulting in a much longer photon pulse at a different wavelength. We show that the amount of stretching is strictly limited by the finesse and length of the cavity. Including realistic internal losses in the cavity, we show that it is possible to stretch a photon by at least two orders of magnitude with high efficiency. The proposed setup can thus constitute a valuable addition to the toolbox of quantum information technologies.
authors: Mathias L. H. Korsgaard;Eva M. González-Ruiz;Anders S. Sørensen

title: Pixel-space video generation with U-JiT
abstract: Latent diffusion and flow matching models are ubiquitous in state-of-the-art generative video models. While highly effective, relying on pretrained autoencoders to compress the data into a lower-dimensional latent space also comes with drawbacks. First, training proceeds in two stages: autoencoder pretraining, with compression and reconstruction objectives, followed by latent generative model training, precluding fully end-to-end training. Second, autoencoders also lead to an inherent loss of signal, and the trade-off between reconstruction quality and generative performance in the latent space is still an active area of research. In this paper we explore the viability of generative video models directly in pixel space. We analyze recent approaches in pixel-space generative modeling of images that rely on basic transformer designs, and identify several shortcomings that limit their effectiveness for the high-dimensional pixel-space video generation. To overcome these limitations, we propose a UNet-like transformer architecture along with improvements to the training recipe and sampling strategy. We conduct controlled experiments, training latent and pixel-space models from scratch on Kinetics-600. For the standard frames-to-video task at 128 resolution, our U-JiT model improves generative FVD by 27% over prior state-of-the-art results, and by 14% against the JiT pixel-space baseline. Scaling to higher 256 resolution, we find the improvement over pixel-space and latent-based models grows as we increase the spatiotemporal compression rate up to $64 \times 64 \times 8$. Finally, we find that U-JiT improves per-frame FID by 27% over latent models and 61% over pixel-space models on class-to-video generation, with respectively 9% and 56% reduction in FVD.

title: TriMedium: A Cross-Medium Simulator for Embodied Networking Across Air-Ground-Sea
abstract: Embodied intelligent applications have expanded from air and ground into maritime environments, where missions such as coastal reporting require coordination among underwater sensing, surface gateways, and aerial relays. Yet field trials remain costly, and existing simulation tools make it difficult to study how cross-medium communication affects cooperation among these platforms. We present TriMedium, an integrated Air-Ground-Sea simulator for cross-medium embodied networking. TriMedium has three design elements. First, it provides a shared three-dimensional world where aerial, terrestrial, and underwater entities coexist, so underwater agent motion and visual observations stay geometrically consistent with air and ground nodes. Second, it uses a common simulation clock that preserves observation timestamps while scheduling delayed communication and computation, clarifying when the shore receiver obtains each observation. Third, modular quantization and compression interfaces accommodate heterogeneous telemetry and image pipelines, while integrity checks separate intentional lossy distortion from incomplete or corrupted delivery. Three case studies validate TriMedium. Multimodal data delivery tests telemetry and image pipelines, scene construction examines cross-domain spatial consistency, and positioning assesses geometric accuracy under delayed communication. Together, they show TriMedium enables embodied networking by quantifying cross-medium delivery dynamics and fidelity across heterogeneous payloads.
authors: Ruizhe Dang;Jiayi Su;Wenlihan Lu;Weijie Yuan;Shijian Gao
comment: 6 pages, 6 figures. Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027

title: Multi-experiment identification from short repeated transients:the human response to pushes in a Tai Chi posture
abstract: The effect of Tai Chi postures on the mechanical response of the body to external pushes is usually assessed with clinical balance scores, which say little about the underlying dynamics. We identify, for five subjects and eight postural conditions, linear models from the mechanical work transferred by a pendulum hitting the forearm to the change of the antero-posterior ground reaction force. Each trial contains 10 to 16 impacts, and each impact yields a transient of 0.55\,s only. Building on earlier analyses of these data, we improve the processing chain in three ways. The input is related to the energy lost by the pendulum and its repeatability is quantified. The output is defined component-wise, which makes it independent of the zeroing of the force plate. Finally, the impacts are stacked in a multi-experiment least-squares problem and validated on unseen impacts. Tenth-order ARX models then reach a median leave-one-impact-out fit of 65\%, against 72\% for the repeatability of the response itself, and never require stability enforcement, unlike estimation on averaged impacts. Closing the eyes lengthens the identified delay by about 70\,ms in all subjects, and the Tai Chi posture increases the antero-posterior force transmitted per joule in four of five subjects. Surface EMG envelopes show a tonic co-activation of the lower-leg muscles in this posture, a smaller reactive triceps burst and a fast habituation of the tibialis response. Together, they point to a stiffer, anticipatory postural strategy.
authors: Emmanuel Witrant;Olivier A. J. Martin;Pascal Bellemain

title: Beyond Local Refinement: Wide-Area Precise Cross-View Localization
abstract: Fine-grained cross-view localization aims to precisely localize a ground camera against geo-referenced aerial imagery, but current methods typically assume a narrow geographic prior, substantially limiting their applicability when upstream localization remains coarse. To bridge this gap, we study this task over much larger aerial regions. However, this seemingly simple extension fundamentally changes the localization problem: the growing disparity in spatial extent between ground and aerial views makes reliable cross-view matching difficult to establish directly, while the increasing number of look-alike locations in larger regions introduces substantial visual ambiguity. To address these challenges, we propose RingMatch, a search-and-verification framework for wide-area cross-view localization. RingMatch first leverages predictive uncertainty to uncover plausible locations and progressively zooms into their surroundings to obtain increasingly fine-grained evidence, yielding a compact set of promising candidates. We then introduce the depth ring, a novel geometric representation that reveals subtle variations in the spatial layout around a location and serves as a view-shared spatial signature for an LVLM verifier to resolve residual ambiguity. To benchmark this setting, we construct VIGOR-Pro by composing VIGOR aerial tiles into contiguous regions with spatial extents of up to 400 m. Experiments show that RingMatch maintains strong localization performance as the aerial region expands, consistently outperforming representative end-to-end and retrieval-based methods.
authors: Qingguo Hu;Xinyu Ma;Yujie Lin;Yaoxiang Wang;Qi Shi;Zonghao Guo;Chi Chen;Jinsong Su

title: iMED: A Multi-Endoscope Dataset for Surgical 3D Perception
abstract: We introduce iMED, the first synchronized multi-endoscope dataset for robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery (RAMIS), designed to address a fundamental limitation in surgical vision benchmarking: the absence of independent held-out viewpoints. Existing surgical datasets capture single-trajectory sequences from a single endoscope, making it impossible to distinguish geometric generalization from photometric interpolation along a narrow forward-facing path. iMED provides 340 sequences ~170K synchronized timepoints with 4 views per timepoint) recorded simultaneously from two independent stereo endoscopes across ex vivo, postmortem, and live surgical settings, spanning 14 specimens with diverse anatomical regions and motion regimes. The dataset includes calibrated camera intrinsics, ArUco-based frame-wise pose estimates with uncertainty quantification, instrument segmentation masks, and rich clinical metadata. Using a train-on-one-endoscope, test-on-another evaluation protocol, we benchmark 23 state-of-the-art methods across rigid and deformable novel view synthesis, pose estimation, feature matching, and monocular depth estimation. Our experiments show that methods relying primarily on photometric supervision degrade substantially under this held-out-endoscope setting, while methods with explicit geometric regularization are more robust across views in our benchmark. Notably, large-scale foundation models transfer surprisingly well to surgical imagery, often outperforming domain-specific models, suggesting pitfalls in current fine-tuning protocols. iMED establishes a new evaluation protocol for geometric generalization in surgical vision.

title: Bounded AUKS: A Novel Evaluation Metric for Anomaly Detection via Bounded Area Under the Kolmogorov--Smirnov Curve
abstract: Recent literature widely used global metrics such as AUROC and AUPRO to quantify the detection performance. AUROC and AUPRO scores are approaching 100% in some public datasets such as MVTec AD dataset and VisA dataset, which misleadingly suggests that the pixel-level anomaly detection task has already been solved. Threshold-independent metrics represented by AUROC inherently ignore the threshold selection process, which is inevitable in practical applications. Although AUPRO restricts the False Positive rates (FPRs) to an acceptable range, extremely low FPRs can lead to increased false negative rates (FNRs). We argue that there is a lack of metrics capable of quantifying the separation between the anomaly score distributions of normal and anomalous samples, which hinders advancements in anomaly detection. In response, we propose the Bounded Area Under the Kolmogorov--Smirnov curve (Bounded AUKS), a partial integral metric that integrates the difference between TPR and FPR within a data-driven bounded range. Specifically, we introduce AUKS from KS integral as a direct measure of separability between the anomaly score distributions. The bounded range is determined only by score distributions of normal test samples. Lower bound excludes the uninformative high-FPR region. Upper bound avoids evaluation in extreme regions that aggressively push FPR towards zero, which result in a very low recall. Our experiments on 9 models across MVTec AD and VisA datasets show that Bounded AUKS can address the limitations of existing metrics and has a better performance in evaluating unsupervised anomaly detection models.

title: Nonlinearity-Induced Suppression of Dissipation in Bath-Coupled Floquet Topological Insulators
abstract: Topological insulators can host chiral, disorder-robust edge states that dissipate energy when coupled to an external bath. We show that nonlinear interactions enable all-optical control over edge-state dissipation in a laser-written Floquet topological insulator periodically coupled to a photonic bath. Although moderate nonlinearity enhances dissipation due to mode mixing, increasing the nonlinear strength to an optimal value dramatically suppresses dissipation by forming highly localized traveling edge solitons. These results establish engineered system-bath coupling and nonlinear interactions as a route to suppress dissipation of chiral topological edge transport.

title: Mass Scaling Laws for Energy-Optimal Horizontal Multirotor Flight
abstract: Multicopters are a type of aerial robot seeing extensive real-world applications but with range and endurance as critical bottlenecks. Optimization of its energy efficiency through energy-aware flight planning (e.g. cruise speed-scheduling) has hence been an important topic. The mass of the multicopter is an important factor to consider, as it has a significant impact on efficiency, and many common applications are subject to frequent mass variation due to payload change. This work derives closed-form scaling relationships between the energy-optimal steady horizontal flight behavior of a multicopter and its vehicle mass, and validates them experimentally on two multirotor platforms. Specifically, for mass-only variation, i.e., when payload changes the vehicle mass while the airframe geometry, aerodynamic characteristics, and rotor configuration remain unchanged, we show through a combination of numerical simulation, theoretical derivation, and experimental validation that (1) the energy-optimal velocity is proportional to the square root of vehicle mass; (2) the energy-optimal pitch angle is constant with respect to mass; and (3) the optimal energy per meter is proportional to mass. The analysis shows that these three relationships arise from a common mass-similarity property of the steady-state flight and rotor-aerodynamic equations. Furthermore, the obtained scaling relationships enable simple yet effective cruise-speed planning to optimize energy efficiency and extend the range and endurance of the multicopter.
authors: Ayush Patnaik;Nicolas Michel;Leonard Baursfeld;Davide Scaramuzza;Xinfan Lin

title: Controlling nitrogen incorporation in (Eu,Ba,Ca)TiO$_3$-derived perovskite-type oxynitrides through Fermi Level Engineering
abstract: Defect states directly influence not only functional properties, but also oxynitride formation during ammonolysis. Along with structural stability and charge balance, these defects can cause non-uniform nitrogen incorporation. To address this, the recently proposed Fermi Level Engineering concept provides a powerful alternative of rationalising oxynitride synthesis. By using the electron chemical potential, i.e., the Fermi level, as a unique descriptor, this approach can predict, understand, and manipulate defect formation enthalpies and charge transition levels, subsequently allowing to incorporate defect-property correlations to the concept. This work combines theoretical modelling and experimental characterisation of barium titanium oxynitrides to explain an intrinsic, self-limiting nitridation process. Progressive nitrogen incorporation causes a Fermi level downward shift, leaving further nitrogen substitution on oxygen sites energetically unfavourable, up to 0.03 N per unit formula. We demonstrate that A-site cation substitution in Eu$_{1-x}$Ba$_x$TiO$_3$- and Eu$_{1-x}$Ca$_x$TiO$_3$-derived oxynitrides can be applied to control compensation of the additional negative charge from N$^{3-}$ and keep the Fermi level high. The Eu$^{2+/3+}$ redox couple enables substitution of oxygen by nitrogen through pinning of the Fermi level at the europium charge transition level, at $\sim$ 2.9 eV above the VBM. This allows for higher nitrogen uptake of up to 0.65 per formula unit (taken from hot gas extraction) through a more controlled process. Further incorporation is then limited by an intra-Ti(O,N)$_6$ octahedra distortion due to internal bond-angle variance. These findings demonstrate that Fermi Level Engineering provides a pathway to predict and overcome intrinsic synthetic and thermodynamic limitations in oxynitride synthesis.

title: The TNG50-SKIRT Atlas: Multi-wavelength properties of galaxy discs in the TNG50 simulation
abstract: We investigate the wavelength dependence of disc scale lengths in galaxies from the TNG50-SKIRT Atlas (TSA), and assess whether the simulated galaxies reproduce the structural properties and scaling relations observed in real galaxies. We measure disc scale lengths from 1D radial surface-brightness profiles of multi-wavelength synthetic images. The disc-dominated region is defined interactively per galaxy and applied consistently across bands. We restrict the analysis to nearly face-on, star-forming galaxies and retain only systems whose r-band profiles are well described by an exponential model. The resulting scale lengths are compared to observational samples and analysed using both dust-attenuated and dust-free images, as well as intrinsic stellar population maps. We find that the majority of TSA galaxies exhibit exponential discs in realistic mock observations. TSA galaxies reproduce the observed disc scale length-stellar mass (luminosity) relation, but are systematically larger at fixed mass or luminosity. The dependence of disc scale length on morphology is weak. Disc scale lengths correlate strongly across wavelengths, but decrease systematically with increasing wavelength. When normalised by the stellar-mass scale length, TSA galaxies exhibit a monotonic trend consistent with observations over the optical-to-NIR range. Comparing dust-free and dust-attenuated images and linking the results to intrinsic galaxy properties, we find that stellar population gradients are the primary driver of this wavelength dependence. In particular, radial gradients in stellar age dominate the effect, while metallicity gradients play a secondary role. Dust attenuation further enhances the wavelength dependence at short wavelengths but is not its main origin. Residual offsets in absolute scale length indicate the remaining differences between simulated and observed galaxy structure.
authors: Abdissa Tassama Emana;Maarten Baes;Angelos Nersesian;Tolu Biressa;Andrea Gebek;Marco Martorano;Viviana Casasola;Sena Bokona Tulu

title: TEXMET: A Deep Learning Benchmark for Archaeological Textile Reconstruction
abstract: The reconstruction of fragmented historical textiles presents a significant challenge in computational archaeology. The Oseberg ship burial, dating to 834 CE, yielded hundreds of degraded textile fragments that have resisted systematic computational analysis. While deep learning has revolutionized image-based puzzle solving, progress on archaeological textiles has been limited by the lack of domain-specific datasets and systematic evaluation of modern architectures. To address this gap, we present TEXMET, a curated dataset of 18,644 historical textile images from the Metropolitan Museum of Art's Open Access collection, representing the first textile-specific benchmark for puzzle-solving research. Using TEXMET, we conduct a systematic evaluation of three state-of-the-art puzzle-solving models: JPDVT, FCViT, and DiffAssemble. Our experiments reveal that the transformer-based models pre-trained on standard datasets fail to generalize to textiles, but domain-specific fine-tuning proves highly effective. The graph-based DiffAssemble model, when fine-tuned on TEXMET, achieves 85.89% puzzle accuracy on textile data. Most significantly, applying this fine-tuned model to 45 highly degraded Oseberg fragments yields a performance increase from 26.67% to 64.44% puzzle accuracy. These results establish TEXMET as a new benchmark for textile reconstruction and demonstrate that domain adaptation is essential for applying puzzle-solving methods to imagery of real archaeological materials.
authors: Muhammad Hamza Zafar;Davit Gigilashvili;Jon Yngve Hardeberg

title: Effect of compensation on magnetic ordering in (Ga,Mn)As
abstract: The real mechanism of ferromagnetism in III-V diluted magnetic semiconductors such as Ga$_{1-x}$Mn$_x$As is still debated. The experimental results point out the realization of appreciable ferromagnetism at filling of the impurity band close to one-half that can be expressed in terms of compensation degree. Based on our recent results on the existence of two competing mechanisms of pair indirect exchange (with ferro- and antiferro alignment of Mn $d$ shells), a theory of magnetic ordering in (Ga,Mn)As is presented. The molecular-field-like equation is derived in which the effective exchange constant contains all necessary information about material, including the Mn content, the compensation degree, the crystal coordination, and the parameters of two competing pair exchange interactions. The Curie temperature depends crucially on the compensation degree. Depending on Mn content and compensation degree, three possible magnetic phases (paramagnetic, ferromagnetic, and spin-glass-like) are predicted. However, the spin-glass-like phase in (Ga,Mn)As is apparently not realized due to the additional inevitable compensation caused by As antisites. The phase transition into the ferromagnetic state occurs not only with Mn content variation but through the change of the compensation degree as well. The new mechanism of photoferromagnetic effect is predicted and discussed in the context of possible clarification of the magnetic ordering mechanism. It is assumed that the main obstacle to a possible increase in the Curie temperature is the increasing contribution of the antiferromagnetic superexchange between the nearest-neighbor Mn's, rather than compensatory (electric or magnetic) effects from Mn interstitials, as was previously stated. The comparison of our predictions with available experimental data is presented.

title: SPOD: Recovering Suppressed Temporal Evidence in Video-LLMs via Single-Pass Orthogonal Decomposition
abstract: Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs) have achieved strong performance on many video understanding tasks, yet remain vulnerable to temporal hallucination in time-sensitive reasoning scenarios such as scene transition understanding and event ordering. Existing solutions either require costly retraining or introduce inefficient multi-pass inference and external supervision at test time. In this work, we show that temporal evidence is already encoded in Video-LLM hidden representations but is not fully exploited during standard inference. Motivated by this observation, we propose Single-Pass Orthogonal Decomposition (SPOD), a training-free framework that recovers suppressed temporal evidence through analytical hidden-state manipulation in a single forward pass. SPOD consists of two components: Frame Distinctiveness Analysis (FDA), which identifies salient frames from middle-layer hidden-state geometry, and Temporal Delta Subspace (TDS), which constructs orthogonal temporal and prior subspaces from weighted inter-frame hidden-state differences. By decomposing final hidden states into temporal, prior, and residual components and rescaling them independently, SPOD enhances dynamic information, suppresses static appearance bias, and preserves complementary information. Experiments on VidHalluc, EventHallusion, and VideoMMMU show that SPOD consistently outperforms strong inference-time baselines across temporal reasoning tasks and model architectures while retaining near-vanilla inference efficiency. These results suggest that improving temporal reasoning in Video-LLMs may depend not only on additional supervision, but also on recovering temporal evidence already present in their internal representations. Our code is available at https://github.com/VioAgnes/SPOD.

title: Bayesian-optimized magnetic-field-gradient sensing with a spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Einstein condensate
abstract: Building on our previous study of the expansion dynamics of a spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Einstein condensate, we propose a scheme for magnetic-field-gradient sensing that relates the maximum rotational deflection angle of the spin-density distribution to the magnetic-field gradient. We analyze the dependence of the sensing performance on key parameters and perform a systematic parameter optimization. A Bayesian optimization algorithm is introduced to efficiently identify the optimal parameter combination, thereby enhancing the sensitivity of magnetic-field-gradient sensing. Numerical simulations under the adopted noise model show that, compared with the parameter set used in our previous work, the optimized gradiometer improves the sensitivity by a factor of five. This work provides a new route for magnetic-field-gradient sensing and offers a reference for machine-learning-assisted quantum precision measurement.

title: VISAGE: Vertex-based Intrinsic Surface Appearance GEneration via Dual-Stream Diffusion for Arbitrary 3D Heads
abstract: Recovering identity-faithful, physically based surface appearance for 3D human heads from sparse images remains challenging. Existing methods often rely on UV-based pipelines, introducing seam artefacts, or operate in image space, limiting surface consistency. We present VISAGE, Vertex-based Intrinsic Surface Appearance GEneration, a surface-based conditional diffusion framework that synthesises per-vertex albedo and roughness directly on arbitrary mesh topologies, without requiring consistent UV parameterisation at training time. VISAGE combines global spectral processing with local geodesic K-Nearest-Neighbour refinement, enforcing structural coherence while restoring detail beyond the truncated spectral basis. Multi-view RGB images condition the network via visibility-aware cross-attention, enabling occlusion-robust synthesis across the full head surface. Region-specific modules specialise in semantically demanding and distinct areas (eyes, mouth, skin and hair), while a tangent-space output projection recovers fine iris detail. We further introduce a scalable procedural augmentation pipeline that enriches raw geometry scans with physically plausible albedo, roughness and normal maps for training. The predicted attributes render directly as a single RGBA vertex-colour channel. VISAGE reduces FID by 42.7% on NPHM and 22.5% and 4.4% on zero-shot FaceVerse and i3DMM, respectively, relative to the strongest baseline, with a 7.2M-parameter core network.

title: Cycle WAM: Coupling Action and Video through Cycle Consistency
abstract: Recent advances in video modeling have driven substantial progress in world action models (WAMs). Existing approaches exploit pretrained video priors by decoding actions from latent representations or inferring them from generated videos. The underlying link is causal: robot actions produce changes in the scene, and video observations of these changes provide evidence for inferring the actions that produced them. However, existing training formulations do not by themselves ensure that actions and their predicted visual consequences are consistent, potentially limiting the use of pretrained capabilities. We treat video and action as paired modalities linked by this causal relationship and learn their correspondence through a unified training framework designed to better exploit pretrained video priors. Cycle WAM first augments video-action co-training with bidirectional conversion to reinforce cross-modal correspondence and recover forward and inverse dynamics. It then introduces a differentiable cycle-reconstruction objective to further couple the two mappings. The resulting model supports both forward and inverse dynamics, with the potential to improve performance through more effective use of pretrained video priors. Cycle WAM achieves state-of-the-art performance among comparable methods on LIBERO-Pro and substantially improves DreamZero on DROID. Comparisons with UWM characterize its inverse-dynamics performance and show sharper visual detail in the displayed forward-dynamics predictions.
authors: Qinglin Yang;Jiepeng Wang;Yuxing Huang;Haibin Huang;Kai Xu;Chi Zhang;Ruizhen Hu;Xuelong Li

title: DenseTwins: Dense Modality Decoupling for Multimodal Self-Supervision
abstract: Multimodal perception is central to many computer vision applications, including robotics and autonomous driving, where different sensing modalities provide complementary cues. Self-supervised learning offers a scalable solution for exploiting large amounts of unlabeled multimodal data. However, existing methods either neglect modality-specific information by enforcing feature-space alignment between modalities or learn only global representations without preserving spatial structure. We propose DenseTwins, a multimodal self-supervised framework that learns dense representations by explicitly decoupling the dense feature space into shared and modality-specific components. The proposed approach combines dense cross-modal correspondences with redundancy-reduction objectives, enabling the model to capture both shared semantics and modality-specific cues within a structured dense embedding space. DenseTwins jointly optimizes an intra-modal objective across augmented views and a cross-modal objective that aligns shared features while decorrelating modality-specific information. We evaluate DenseTwins across multiple multimodal benchmarks and sensing setups, achieving state-of-the-art or competitive performance across multimodal self-supervised baselines. Code available at: https://github.com/CarloSgaravatti/DenseTwins.

title: Learning from Unlabeled Photographs for General Oral Image Analysis
abstract: Oral photographs contain rich clinical information and hold significant potential for artificial intelligence applications; however, most models are trained for individual tasks and rely on costly expert annotations. We hypothesized that self-supervised training on unlabeled oral photographs could produce transferable visual representations for heterogeneous vision tasks. To test this hypothesis, we developed DOVE (Dental Optical Visual Encoder) by domain-adaptive self-supervised pretraining on approximately 530,000 unlabeled oral photographs collected from publicly accessible sources. DOVE was benchmarked against 3 established baselines across 5 classification datasets and 4 segmentation datasets, covering both frozen backbone evaluation and end-to-end finetuning. DOVE achieved the strongest overall performance, ranking best in few-shot transfer and label efficiency on most benchmarks. Under the 20-shot frozen-backbone protocol, DOVE outperformed the second best DINOv3 by 4.37 percentage points in mean macro-F1 across classification datasets and by 4.49 percentage points in mean macro-Dice across segmentation tasks. Under end-to-end finetuning, DOVE achieved at least 80% of the strongest full-data baseline's performance across most evaluation datasets using only 10% of the labeled training data. Qualitative retrieval and feature analyses further indicated better organization of image-level and spatial representations. These findings support DOVE as a generalizable and label-efficient backbone for oral vision research.
authors: Zhong-Shi Zhang;Zi-Li Yu;Xiao Xiao;Huan Liu;Gui-Song Xia;Cui Huang;Meng-Xun Li

title: Methodological Assessment of Instrumented Indentation for Spatially Resolved Mesoscale Stiffness and Creep in Short Fiber-Reinforced Injection-Molded PBT Components
abstract: Instrumented indentation enables assessment of local mechanical properties in heterogeneous polymer systems, but specimen preparation and the selected indentation protocol significantly influence the quantitative interpretation of the measured response. This study develops and evaluates an experimental methodology for spatially resolved mesoscale characterization of both unreinforced and short fiber-reinforced composites. An unreinforced material system is used as a reference material to systematically examine the effects of indentation spacing, surface preparation, maximum indentation load, temporal loading parameters, and unloading evaluation. Indentation loads of 500, 1000, and 1750 mN are investigated in complementary experimental campaigns. The apparent indentation modulus exhibits moderate sensitivity to indentation load and loading time within the studied ranges. In contrast, indentation depth and the creep-related depth increment display greater sensitivity to the applied load history. Surface polishing minimizes topographical disturbances and enables reliable identification of residual indentation profiles and pile-up. Based on these methodological findings, a final load-hold-unload protocol with an indentation load of 1750 mN, a loading time of 6 s, a holding period of 300 s, and an unloading time of 4 s is applied to both unreinforced material and short fiber-reinforced composites. The mean apparent indentation modulus increases from 2.91 GPa for unreinforced material to 6.65 GPa for short fiber-reinforced composites, while the mean depth of indentation creep decreases from 2.36 to 1.91 microns. The coefficient of variation also increases for both quantities, indicating that short-fiber reinforcement enhances mean local stiffness and introduces pronounced spatial heterogeneity in both stiffness-related and time-dependent mesoscale indentation responses.

title: Closed- and open-system characterization of the Yukawa-SYK model in real time
abstract: Strongly correlated matter without quasiparticles is central to many-body physics, quantum chaos, and quantum gravity, motivating a considerable effort toward its realization in tabletop experiments. Two challenges remain: laboratory platforms are open systems, so conformal behavior must survive dissipation, and it must be identified through measurable quantities. We address both challenges in the Yukawa-Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (YSYK) model, in which bosons and fermions interact as in, e.g., light-matter systems, but through random all-to-all couplings that drive the boson to criticality without fine tuning. Solving the model in real time using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we treat closed and open systems within a unified framework and, in both cases, consider a thermal steady state to map their phase diagrams. In addition to the known conformal and impurity (or SYK$_2$) regimes, we identify novel high-temperature regimes in which the fermions are driven by an essentially bare boson and show that their dynamics is captured by a quadratic model with time-dependent random hopping. Across all regimes, the fermionic softening of the boson is bounded by a ``criticality budget'' determined only by the Yukawa coupling and the temperature. Coupling the boson with a thermal environment induces a mass shift that deforms the boundaries between different regimes and exhausts the criticality budget, thus imposing a bound on temperature and dissipation rate compatible with self-tuned criticality. We further introduce a set of markers built from the two-point functions that separate all identified regimes, are accessible in linear response, and require no fit of the conformal exponents. We complement them with the quantum Fisher information, deriving upper bounds with and without dissipation. These results may help characterize holographic quantum matter beyond the closed setting.
authors: Alex Windey;Christian H. Johansen;Philipp Hauke;Andrea Legramandi

title: One-shot Distributed Learning via Weighted Averaging with Server-side Information
abstract: Distributed learning has drawn considerable attention due to its capability of learning from distributed data without aggregating raw observations. However, frequent exchange of model updates can become the main bottleneck of communication. Therefore, one-shot approaches where each worker fits a local model and sends it to the server to aggregate emerge. It is known that averaging can achieve the so-called pooled-data mean squared error (MSE) order of a hypothetical node that has access to data from the server and all the workers, and performs empirical risk minimization (ERM) on it. However, when the number of workers increases too fast compared to the local sample size, nonzero local estimation bias prevents averaging from achieving this order. In this paper, we study whether independent server data can overcome this limitation. We consider $m$ workers with $n$ observations each and a server with $p$ observations, all i.i.d., giving $N=mn+p$ observations in total. Under certain regularity conditions, a pooled-data ERM achieves MSE of order $\mathcal O(N^{-1})$. We analyze deterministic nonnegative averaging of convex-loss M-estimators, with equal worker weights and the server's own estimator included. Under our assumptions, including nonzero local bias of order $n^{-α}$, $α\geq1$, sample-size weighted averaging achieves the pooled-data MSE order whenever $m=\mathcal O(n^{2α-1})$. Above this worker scale, it does so if and only if $p=Ω(nm\cdot m/n^{2α-1})$. Hence, server-only estimation, whose MSE is of order $\mathcal{O}(p^{-1})$, can achieve pooled-data order while sample-size weighting fails. Analytical examples and synthetic experiments illustrate when averaging matches the pooled-data MSE order, complemented by CIFAR-10 experiments comparing aggregation strategies with linear and nonlinear classifiers.

title: Perceptual Weight Space Programming for Diffusion Super-Resolution
abstract: Diffusion models for image super-resolution can recover scene content while producing distracting artifacts or unbalanced colors. We study whether a large language model (LLM) can improve perceptual quality by editing a small subset of existing U-Net weights without a clean reference image. The proposed framework provides the editor with architecture code, selected weights, activation summaries, and sampling previews. It permits up to 1,020 candidate trials while limiting accepted changes to three layers and fewer than 0.1\% of model parameters. The evaluation protocol uses ResShift, SinSR, and SUPIR and compares GPT-6 Astra with a specified Qwen3-VL model under matched access. Feedback metrics guide editing, while separate quality metrics and blinded human comparisons evaluate the final weights. We also report an executed color calibration experiment using real photographs and two small residual networks. This experiment demonstrates correction of a fixed color shift and reveals that an improving feedback score can accompany worse performance on unseen scenes. A separate lightweight super-resolution experiment isolates modest changes in luminance detail while preserving color. The findings motivate restricted updates and independent evaluation of perceptual weight editing.

title: When Ground Truth Is Not Ground Truth: Automatic Labeling for Hallucination Detection
abstract: Hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs) remain a major challenge, as they can produce misleading, factually incorrect, or unverifiable information, thereby undermining their trustworthiness and reliability. However, reliable ground-truth labels remain a key challenge in evaluating hallucination detectors. Recent studies often construct labels automatically by comparing model generations with reference answers using similarity metrics such as BLEURT. This implicitly treats BLEURT similarity as a proxy for hallucination, despite its English-centric supervision, unbounded score range, and design as a similarity metric rather than a factuality measure, making threshold-based ground-truth construction potentially unreliable. Through comprehensive experiments using 15 automatic supervision judges, seven hallucination detection baselines, two generator models, two QA datasets, and five languages, we demonstrate that detector performance varies substantially with the choice of supervision judge. Human validation reveals substantial differences in labeling reliability, with QGen-9B achieving the lowest overall misclassification rate (12.86%), while BLEURT and BLEURT-n exhibit rates of 47.23% and 47.32%, respectively. Our findings highlight the limitations of automatic similarity-based labeling and the need for more reliable judging methods that better capture semantic and factual correctness.

title: Surrogate Models for Stochastic Al-Cu Phase-Field Solidification
abstract: Phase-field models resolve microstructural evolution during rapid alloy solidification, but their computational cost limits long trajectories, stochastic ensembles, and studies across process conditions. We compare a deterministic U-Net with conditional flow matching (Flow), conditional diffusion (EDM), and a variance-preserving denoising diffusion bridge (VP-DDBM) for two-dimensional Al-Cu solidification. Given the current phase, concentration, and prescribed temperature fields, each model predicts the subsequent state and is applied autoregressively. At two thermal gradients outside the training range, we compare surrogate rollouts spanning \(48{,}000\) phase-field Euler steps with five phase-field futures generated from a common restart at each gradient. With two network evaluations per transition, Flow achieves the lowest time-averaged fair continuous ranked probability score among the generative surrogates for mean phase, mean Cu concentration, interface length, and leading-tip position at both gradients. Flow also reproduces the cellular morphology and retains sharp solid--liquid interfaces. It generates a single future approximately \(107\times\) faster than the phase-field solver on the reported hardware, showing potential for faster process-condition screening and ensemble-based microstructure studies.

title: Quantum Simulation of Electronic Structure using Quantum Density Functional Theory on a Programmable Integrated Photonic Circuit
abstract: Quantum simulations of molecular electronic structure hold the potential for computational advantage but are inherently limited by the linear scaling of qubit requirements with respect to system size. Quantum Density Functional Theory (Q-DFT) addresses this constraint by reformulating the interacting many-body problem in terms of a non-interacting Kohn--Sham reference system. Here, we present and experimentally validate a Q-DFT algorithm that requires only $\mathcal{O}(\log_2(N))$ qubits to simulate a system of $N$ orbitals, thereby reducing resource overhead. More precisely, we solve the Kohn--Sham problem for the lithium hydride (LiH) molecule using the ensemble extension of the variational quantum eigensolver paradigm that minimizes the energy of the system in the subspace spanned by the ground and first excited states. To execute this task, we encode the problem with qubits on a quantum photonic platform, utilizing an architecture that combines a deterministic quantum dot single-photon source with a programmable integrated photonic circuit. By evaluating the molecular ground- and first excited-state properties, this work establishes a pathway for simulating larger molecular systems, demonstrating the viability of integrating qubit-efficient algorithms with advanced reconfigurable photonic hardware for near-term quantum chemistry applications.

title: HLA-Net: A Physics-Guided Skeleton-Based Framework for Automatic Gravitational Arc Detection in Astronomical Images
abstract: Gravitational arcs produced by strong gravitational lensing provide a unique approach for investigating dark matter distribution, galaxy cluster mass reconstruction and the structure of the Universe. Automated detection remains challenging because gravitational arcs are rare, often faint and morphologically similar to elongated galaxies.In this paper, we propose \textbf{HLA-Net (Hybrid Lens Arc Network)}, an interpretable multi-stage framework for automatic gravitational arc detection that explicitly exploits both the geometric morphology and physical characteristics of gravitational lensing without requiring manually annotated training datasets.The proposed framework was evaluated on astronomical FITS images containing complex galaxy cluster structures. Starting from 169 initial arc candidates extracted from ordered skeleton representations, the multi-stage verification pipeline reduced the search space to 83 geometrically consistent candidates, while robust circle fitting successfully modelled 113 candidate arc structures. The results demonstrate that HLA-Net effectively suppresses false-positive detections while preserving physically reasonable lens candidates through an interpretable and modular verification strategy.

title: CardioVascBench:Prioritized Diagnosis Generation from Real-World Chinese Cardiovascular Records
abstract: Identifying the primary diagnosis alone does not fully characterize a model's diagnosis-generation performance. We introduce CardioVascBench, a retrospective benchmark for prioritized diagnosis generation from real-world Chinese cardiovascular inpatient records. It contains 3,262 de-identified cases, with 2,174 for training and 1,088 for evaluation, linking clinical narratives and textual ECG reports to expert-verified, ordered discharge diagnoses standardized to ICD-10. An English translation of the evaluation set supports aligned cross-lingual comparison. Our evaluation protocol combines terminology normalization and rank-aware scoring to separately assess primary-diagnosis identification, reference-diagnosis coverage, and list precision. Evaluation across 36 systems shows that higher primary-diagnosis accuracy does not necessarily imply higher list precision against discharge references. We also provide CardioKG-Agent, a knowledge-enhanced baseline combining entity normalization, constrained graph retrieval, and guideline evidence. In a staged comparison of three baseline models, supervised fine-tuning plus the agent achieves a 73.5% higher mean composite score than fine-tuning alone, representing a system-level gain. These results measure retrospective agreement with recorded diagnoses; agreement between metric rankings and physician judgments remains to be validated. CardioVascBench supports research on diagnosis prioritization and knowledge-enhanced generation.
authors: Minghao Kong;Muyao Chen;Jianhao Wu;Yuqiang Zhang;Xiangbin Meng;Zirong Liu;Ting Cao;Kaida Ning;Zhen Song;Rongjie Wang

title: MIMIC-Note-Extract: A Large-Scale Structured Dataset Extracted from MIMIC-IV-Note Discharge Summaries
abstract: MIMIC is one of the most widely used public hospital datasets for machine learning on electronic health records, yet clinically important information, such as past medical history, allergies, and diagnostic findings, remains confined to free-text discharge summaries. Studies requiring this information must therefore build their own extraction pipelines, duplicating substantial effort across projects. We release MIMIC-Note-Extract (MNE), a large-scale dataset that uses a hybrid extraction pipeline combining deterministic parsing with schema-guided large language model generation to transform 16 sections from 300,720 discharge summaries into structured tables. MNE adds information that has no structured MIMIC counterpart and enriches related tables with broader coverage and greater clinical detail, including 10 times more patient-history entries and medication histories for more than twice as many admissions. Validation by medical doctors confirms extraction accuracy above 92% across sections. Using MNE, we construct a clinical decision-making benchmark for LLM agents, demonstrating how reusable structured representations of clinical narratives reduce data curation effort.

title: Phase-DGS: Phase-guided Dynamic Gaussian Splatting from Unsynchronized Multi-view Video
abstract: Spatiotemporal scene reconstruction with Dynamic Gaussian Splatting (DGS) fundamentally depends on perfect temporal synchronization across all cameras, an assumption rarely achievable in practice. Industry-standard synchronization requires expensive specialized hardware and complex setup, while data-driven alternatives including audio-based alignment, geometry matching, and pose tracking remain limited by restrictive environmental or scene-specific assumptions. To overcome these limitations, we propose Phase-DGS, a framework that replaces conventional timestamps with a semantic phase representing each frame's inherent state within the underlying motion cycle. Frames capturing the same motion state share the same phase regardless of which camera records them or when, naturally establishing spatiotemporal correspondence across unsynchronized cameras. We validate Phase-DGS under temporal offsets, frame drops, and camera freezes, achieving up to +8.5 dB PSNR improvement over baselines while enabling seamless integration with existing DGS backbones including RealTime-4DGS and FreeTimeGS.
