title: Random Projections for Spectral Algorithms: Optimal Rates in Sobolev Norms
abstract: Random projections (RP) offer an effective method for reducing computational and storage overhead while preserving the geometric structure of data. However, existing studies have primarily focused on the optimal generalization performance of specific kernel-regularized algorithms with RP in the well-specified setting and under restrictive conditions. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive and improved analysis of the generalization performance of RP-based spectral algorithms under general conditions \change{without sacrificing statistical efficiency}. By leveraging the embedding property of the reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) and a refined analysis of the operator similarity, we establish optimal learning rates in Sobolev norms that match the minimax lower bounds up to logarithmic factors. For two common implementations of RP, randomized sketches and Nyström sub-sampling (uniform or leverage-based), we show that the projection dimension required for optimality is proportional to the average or maximal effective dimension, yielding a significant reduction in computational cost while maintaining the statistical efficiency. Our results do not rely on the uniform boundedness assumption on the regression function and are valid across a wide range of source conditions, i.e., $s> α_0-1/β$, where $s,β$, and $α_0$ denote the smoothness index, capacity index, and the embedding index, respectively. In the benign case when $α_0=1/β$, the optimality holds for all $s\in (0,2τ]$ with $τ$ and $γ$ denoting the qualification index and norm index. Experimental results demonstrate both the theoretical validity and the practical effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Chiroptical Valleytronic in SnSe
abstract: Quantum geometric properties of Bloch electrons play a central role in governing light-matter interactions and transport phenomena in solids. Here, we report quantum-geometric chiroptical selection rules that generate a helicity-dependent momentum-space population imbalance in the group-IV monochalcogenide SnSe. By combining time- and angle-resolved extreme-ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy with ab initio real-time simulations of photoexcited carrier dynamics, we identify valley-selective excitation at opposite crystal momenta arising from the breaking of time-reversal symmetry under circularly polarized illumination. We theoretically demonstrate that the magnitude of valley circular dichroism is strongly constrained by crystal symmetry through its influence on the quantum geometric tensor, the key quantity underlying valley optical selection rules. The resulting chiroptically induced valley polarization decays on sub-picosecond timescales through intervalley scattering mediated by electron-phonon coupling. Furthermore, we show theoretically that the population imbalance between valleys at opposite momenta gives rise to a helicity-reversible transient photocurrent. These findings provide microscopic insight into how quantum geometry governs valley-selective light-matter interactions, valley polarization, and photocurrent generation in van der Waals materials exhibiting hidden and transient symmetry breaking.

title: Piezo-Kerr effect in altermagnets and noncollinear antiferromagnets
abstract: Symmetry is usually viewed as a constraint on physical responses, but it can also be used to design the fields that control them. Here, we adopt the representation-matching principle used to identify conjugate fields of order parameters and apply it to response tensors. A linear coupling, the key ingredient for sign-switching control, is symmetry-allowed when a component (or a combination of components) of the control field and the selected response component share the same irreducible representation of the magnetic point group (MPG) of the system. Applied to the magneto-optical Kerr effect, this principle yields a piezo-Kerr effect, in which specific strain combinations activate a Kerr response forbidden in the unstrained state. Enumerating all 122 MPGs, we identify 16 groups in which the unstrained Kerr response is forbidden while a linear strain-induced contribution is allowed. These groups are realized by altermagnets and noncollinear antiferromagnets with symmetry-enforced vanishing net magnetization. The active strain channels and the associated first-order sign reversals follow directly from symmetry. First-principles calculations for bulk MnTe$_{2}$ and CoF$_{2}$, and Cr$_{2}$Se$_{2}$O and Cr$_{2}$Te$_{2}$O monolayers confirm these predictions. In these materials, the Kerr rotation vanishes without strain, whereas 0.5-3% strain produces rotations ranging from tens to hundreds of millidegrees, and reversing the matched strain channel reverses the Kerr sign. These results establish a general route to large and switchable Kerr responses emerging from symmetry-forbidden states in compensated magnets.
authors: Yuqi Liu;Qiu-Shi Huang;Xinfeng Chen;Yilin Han;Run-Wu Zhang;Zhi-Ming Yu;Yugui Yao

title: Stability of rotation axis of galactic disks in HESTIA suite
abstract: We have found that in approximately 1/4 of Milky Way or M31 analogues in the HESTIA suite of simulations there is a significant, $>45^\circ$, change in the axis of rotation orientation of the gaseous disk during the last 6 Gyr. In 6 out of 7 such cases the change is likely caused by the accretion of individual satellites, while in one case such a connection is not obvious. All galaxies that underwent a significant change in rotation axis direction also had angular momentum amplitudes below the sample median 6 Gyr ago. Our findings support the idea that last 6~Gyr was a quiet phase of evolution in the LG. On the other hand, the mechanism we detect, that satellites can flip galaxy orientation, can explain the difficulties in identifying correlations between the rotation axis and the orientation of large-scale structure elements.
authors: Naira R. Arakelyan;Sergey V. Pilipenko;Stefan Gottlöber;Noam I. Libeskind;Gustavo Yepes;Yehuda Hoffman

title: Thermal expansion mechanisms, heat transport, and band-gap renormalization in strongly anharmonic Rb$_2$SO$_4$, Rb$_2$Ca$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$, and Ba$_3$Lu(BO$_3$)$_3$ from machine-learned interatomic potentials
abstract: Rb$_2$SO$_4$, Rb$_2$Ca$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$, and Ba$_3$Lu(BO$_3$)$_3$ are structurally complex materials whose thermal expansion has been interpreted, on the basis of high-temperature x-ray diffraction, in terms of specific polyhedral rearrangements. We study their lattice dynamics and its consequences for thermal and electronic properties using molecular dynamics with actively learned moment tensor potentials trained on density-functional theory data. The anharmonicity measure $σ^A$ (compares the anharmonic contribution to the interatomic forces with the total forces acting on atoms) reaches $\approx$0.3-0.5 for $β$-Rb$_2$SO$_4$, Rb$_2$Ca$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$, and Ba$_3$Lu(BO$_3$)$_3$ and $\approx$0.75 for orientationally disordered $α$-Rb$_2$SO$_4$, and the imaginary harmonic modes of Rb$_2$Ca$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$ and $α$-Rb$_2$SO$_4$ are stabilized at finite temperature. The simulations reproduce the measured thermal expansion and support the mechanisms proposed from diffraction: expansion along $c$ in $β$-Rb$_2$SO$_4$ arises from both elongation and straightening of corrugated Rb chains, BO$_3$ reorientation accompanies the anisotropic expansion of Ba$_3$Lu(BO$_3$)$_3$, and bending of polyhedral linkages limits expansion along the weakly expanding directions and in cubic Rb$_2$Ca$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$. Green-Kubo lattice thermal conductivities differ by more than an order of magnitude between compounds with comparable $σ^A$, showing that the anharmonicity measure alone does not determine heat transport. Phonon-induced band-gap renormalization, including lattice thermal expansion, reaches 2.7 and 1.7 eV at 1250 K in Rb$_2$Ca$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$ and Ba$_3$Lu(BO$_3$)$_3$ and 1.4 eV at 650 K in $β$-Rb$_2$SO$_4$, with zero-point renormalizations of 0.64, 0.70, and 0.31 eV for $β$-Rb$_2$SO$_4$, Rb$_2$Ca$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$, and Ba$_3$Lu(BO$_3$)$_3$, respectively.
authors: Ekaterina Spirande;Rustam Arabov;Sofya Demina;Nikita Rybin;Alexander Shapeev

title: Assortment optimization under the perception-adjusted Luce model
abstract: The Perception-Adjusted Luce Model (PALM) introduced by by Echenique et al. (2018) is a sequential choice model that can accommodate violations of regularity and choice overload, behaviors not captured by the utility-maximization framework. Flores et al. (2019) studied the assortment problem under the PALM and proved that, for the case of two levels, there is always an optimal solution that is revenue-ordered by level. They also conjectured that revenue-ordered by levels remain optimal for the general PALM with any number of levels. We resolve this question in the affirmative by showing that every PALM instance admits an optimal assortment that includes, within each level, all products at or above a level-specific revenue threshold. The proof involves first showing how the conjecture which deals with a discrete optimization problem, can be reduced to proving certain property of a related continuous optimization problem. Specifically, we study a continuous refinement of the assortment decision under the same PALM choice rule. Although the refinement permits partial utility selections, we prove it always has an optimum that selects complete revenue tiers. This allows us to show that the assortment problem is polynomial-time solvable when the number of levels is fixed.

title: Continuous-depth Deep Gaussian Processes
abstract: Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) are appealing Bayesian regression models, but their standard discrete-depth parameterization often becomes harder to optimize as depth grows. We argue that depth is better treated as a latent continuous evolution than as a long discrete stack. We therefore propose a continuous-depth formulation in which the latent representation follows a stochastic differential equation with a depth-indexed drift family equipped with a GP-based prior. This reframes the core design choice as the prior placed on that family, rather than adopting a purely neural continuous-depth parameterization as in neural ODE or neural SDE models. We study two instantiations of this idea: CDGP, a direct GP prior over the state--depth drift, and FlowDGP, a flow-evolved prior that captures richer depth dependence at lower training cost. To motivate the redesign, we analyze how the single-sample DGP objective can become increasingly sensitive under repeated layer composition, while residual DGP is a useful first repair that still remains a finite discrete construction. We also give pathwise sensitivity analysis for the continuous-depth formulation. Experiments on synthetic, benchmark, and large-scale regression tasks show that residual DGP improves over plain DGP, while CDGP and FlowDGP provide a stronger overall story across the regimes we study.
authors: Ying Li;Sanyou Wu;Zi Yang;Qiaochu Xu;Yuhao Liu;Zhidi Lin;Michael Minyi Zhang;Petar Djuric;Alexandre H. Thiery

title: Designing sustainable high-entropy alloys directly from mixed oxides: A thermodynamic perspective
abstract: Hydrogen-based direct reduction (HyDR) of mixed oxide precursors offers an alternative route to produce sustainable alloys, bypassing the sequential extraction, refining, and remelting steps that dominate the carbon footprint of conventional metallurgy and individual metal production. However, the thermodynamic limits and most effective H$_2$/H$_2$O ratio needed for full metallization of multicomponent oxides are not yet established. This is because the formation of metallic and oxide solid solutions alters the chemical activity of both the reduced metallic phases and the unreduced oxides, coupling their equilibria in ways that cannot be deduced from the stability of the pure individual oxides. Herein, we develop a CALPHAD-based thermodynamic framework to establish the compoistion-temperature-H$_2$/H$_2$O window for complete metallization of CoCrFeMnNi-based oxide mixtures. Mn and Cr generally increase oxide stability, while Co, Fe, and Ni decrease it, allowing reduction at lower H$_2$/H$_2$O ratios. The effect of each element is not fixed; it depends on the starting mixed oxide composition and can reverse when the last oxide to reduce changes. Furthermore, we show that the reduction pathway complexity does not correlate with the difficulty of removing the final oxygen: a system with few intermediate transformation steps can still terminate as a highly stable residual oxide, whereas extensive partial reduction may leave the stability of the final residual oxide essentially unchanged. By linking residual-oxide stability to the H$_2$/H$_2$O ratio, the framework identifies the thermodynamic limits and provides guidelines for designing sustainable multicomponent alloys directly from mixed oxide precursors.

title: Consensus-Based Distributed Filtering for Angles-Only Tracking in Cislunar Space
abstract: This paper investigates consensus-based distributed filtering strategies for multi-observer angles-only navigation in the cislunar space. The objective is to estimate the inertial state of a target spacecraft using only line-of-sight measurements collected by a network of observer spacecraft. This problem is particularly relevant for autonomous cislunar navigation, where ground support may be limited, and centralized fusion architectures may be problematic due to communication and computational constraints, and single-point failure risks. Three distributed filtering approaches are considered: the Distributed Extended Kalman Filter, the Information-Weighted Consensus Filter, and the Kalman Consensus Filter. All methods share the same local prediction and measurement-processing steps, but differ in the way information is exchanged and fused across the network. Their performance is evaluated and compared to a centralized Extended Kalman Filter, adopted as benchmark, and independent local filters in a high-fidelity cislunar scenario. Numerical simulations show that the distributed approaches significantly improve estimation accuracy with respect to independent filters. Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses are then conducted to characterize the robustness of the considered methods to finite consensus iterations and prior misalignment among the agents.

title: A neural-network model to find correlations in astrochemical space
abstract: The detection of new interstellar molecules is central to astrochemistry, and arguably the most transformative development in the field in past decade has been the increase in both number and diversity of detected species. Using natural language processing models, we develop a machine-learning pipeline, similar to other approaches reported in the literature, to connect molecular structures, encoded as chemical strings, and molecular column densities in TMC-1. The workflow generates astrochemically informed embeddings that can be employed in subsequent supervised learning tasks. These representations are used within a neural-network framework to perform column-density regression on both the original molecular inventory and out-of-distribution species. The resulting model achieves mean squared error values of 0.17/0.58 and mean absolute error values of 0.29/0.59, and coefficients of determination of 0.88/0.51 for the train+validation and validation datasets. The latent vectors learned by the model are rich mathematical objects that capture the underlying chemical relations and also the potential interstellar detectability of the molecule. Using these vectors in molecules obtained from systematic permutations of the TMC-1 inventory, we identify several promising candidates for future detection in this cloud, together with a large number of apolar species. By training the model on datasets reflecting different historical epochs of molecular detections in TMC-1, we show that recent molecular detections have substantially reshaped our understanding of interstellar chemistry, in a transformative, rather than incremental, way. Beyond accurate prediction of column-density trends for both in-distribution and out-of-distribution molecules, the latent-space representations produced by the model provide a stepping stone for developing new forms of data-driven astrochemical intuition and exploration.
authors: Daniel Giovanni Vargas;Darío Barreiro-Lage;Marcelino Agúndez;Carlos Cabezas;José Cernicharo;Germán Molpeceres

title: Discovering supernovae in the Virgo Cluster during the LSST era
abstract: In the era of unprecedentedly wide, deep and high-cadence sky surveys the chance for discovering new explosive transients in nearby, rich galaxy clusters within hours after explosion is expected to increase dramatically. In this paper we focus on the Virgo cluster ($D \simeq 16.5$ Mpc), and estimate the expected numbers of new, very young supernovae in different sub-structures and galaxy types of the cluster during the proposed lifetime (~10 years) of the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) by the Vera Rubin Observatory. These predictions will be tested observationally during the ongoing Shadow-LSST discovery and follow-up program led by University of Arizona in the upcoming years.

title: A recurring changing state AGN discovered in the SAMI Galaxy Survey and SDSS
abstract: We present a detailed analysis of the AGN in galaxy J085337.26+014303.6 at z=0.0582. A combination of SDSS and SAMI Galaxy Survey data shows that this object has gone through at least one full changing-look AGN cycle, from type 1.9 in 2001 to type 1 in 2015 and 2021, and then type 1.9 again in 2022. While the broad lines in this object show evidence of dust obscuration, detailed spectral analysis plus WISE photometry demonstrate that the changes in this object are related to a physical state change, not changing obscuration. In fact, the WISE light curve suggests that this object may have briefly returned to a type 1.9 state in 2020. In the optical, the host galaxy dominates the light (e.g. only ~10 per cent contribution from the AGN at 4000 Angstoms within a central aperture), even in the high state. In contrast, the brightest WISE W2-band measurements place the AGN at a similar luminosity to the entire host galaxy. The broad Balmer lines show evidence of multiple components, with a weak very-broad component (FWHM=5000-6000 km/s) visible in the low type 1.9 state, and a stronger broad component of FWHM~2000 km/s dominating in the high type 1 state. We propose that this is caused by two spatially distinct regions within the broad line region.

title: xVGAE: A Hierarchical Variational Graph Autoencoder for Exchangeable Graphs
abstract: Graphs play a crucial role in many applications, ranging from drug discovery to social network modeling and astronomy. Generative models for graphs have substantially advanced in recent years, but we identify relatively simple scenarios where state-of-the-art models struggle to converge within a standard compute budget, or exhibit prohibitively slow generation times. We propose a generative architecture that achieves quality competitive with state-of-the-art models and is orders of magnitude faster at generation. Our approach is inspired by the Aldous-Hoover theorem, a classic representation theorem that characterizes any probability distribution of graphs that is invariant to permutations of node indices or exchangeable. This theorem establishes that three ingredients suffice: a graph-level latent variable, a set of exchangeable node-specific latent variables, and a so-called graphon function that maps graph- and node-level variables to the probability of an edge between any node pair. Given a training set of graphs, our exchangeable Variational Graph AutoEncoder (xVGAE) learns an approximation to their underlying graphons, as well as graph- and node-level latent variables. We show that our xVGAE encodes latent representations that correlate with graph- and node-level properties, and can (quickly, in one shot) generate new graphs that closely match key training set statistics.
authors: Daniele Micheletti;Federica Zoe Ricci;Erik B. Sudderth

title: The ALMA-QUARKS survey: A Keplerian Circumbinary Disk Candidate in the High-mass Star-forming Region IRAS 08303-4303
abstract: We present the ALMA Band 6 continuum and molecular line observations of IRAS 08303-4303, a high-mass star-forming region, with an angular resolution of $\sim 0.3''$ ($\sim 700$ au at the distance of 2.35 kpc). Six dense condensations are identified in the 1.3 mm continuum, and at least four of them are associated with molecular outflows. The estimated outflow parameters, particularly mass outflow rates $\geq 10^{-4}$ $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$, suggest that the driving sources are high-mass young stellar objects. Two of the condensations are forming a wide protobinary system with a separation of $\sim 900$ au. They reside within a single rotating structure, identified as a circumbinary disk which has a mass of about 2 $M_{\odot}$. This structure is traced by multiple molecular lines and exhibits a Keplerian rotation pattern. Based on the Keplerian rotation assumption, the enclosed mass is derived to be between 32 and 61 $M_{\odot}$: 22-43 $M_{\odot}$ for the primary and 10-18 $M_{\odot}$ for the secondary. The circumbinary disk is on the whole gravitationally stable, yet some parts with Toomre $Q < 2$ indicate potential fragmentation. Various molecular lines reveal a streamer-like structure connecting to the circumbinary disk, suggesting transfer of material from the envelope to the protobinary system through it. Despite the observational rarity of such circumbinary disks around high-mass YSOs, the high binary fraction among massive stars underscores their significance. This source, therefore, serves as a key laboratory for understanding the formation of high-mass binary systems.

title: Numerical Solution of Large-Scale Low-Rank Coupled Generalized Sylvester Equations
abstract: This paper develops projection methods for computing low-rank solutions to large-scale coupled generalized Sylvester equations. The dominant subspaces of these solutions are shown to be spanned by specific resolvent directions, motivating a Petrov--Galerkin projection framework. Conditions for the unique solvability of the projected coupled generalized Sylvester equations are also discussed. Based on these dominant subspaces, two algorithms are proposed: an extended Krylov-based projection algorithm and a rational Krylov-based projection algorithm. The former uses fixed shifts, whereas the latter uses adaptive shifts. Numerical experiments on large-scale benchmark problems demonstrate that the proposed methods achieve high accuracy and fast convergence.

title: Simulated transcranial ultrasound of human language cortex: verifying heard speech needs far less data and signal than decoding it
abstract: Functional ultrasound could image cortical blood volume through the temporal bone, but the skull leaves a weak signal, and task-evoked cortical imaging through the intact adult skull has not yet been shown. We built a voxel-specific Monte Carlo link-budget simulation of a probe on the left temple and used it to degrade public fMRI of three people who heard 15 hours of stories. On the same anatomical voxels we trained a published state-of-the-art fMRI language decoder (Tang et al., 2023) and two verifiers that only check a candidate text. In clean data the verifiers needed far less training (11 to 12 minutes against 3.2 to 6.6 hours), but all three learned at a similar rate. Noise changed this qualitatively: the verifiers kept gaining evidence while the decoder slowed and, under simulated transcranial physics, stalled, whereas the verifiers still reached their goal under a favorable simulated link budget. This asymmetry suggests that low-SNR modalities such as transcranial ultrasound may support verification well before decoding.

title: Anomaly Score Preserving Data Poisoning Attacks on Data-Driven Controller Design
abstract: This paper investigates stealthy data poisoning attacks against data-driven controller synthesis and develops an attack generation method. During data collection, an attacker can sequentially manipulate state measurements, while the defender attempts to detect such manipulation using a residual-based anomaly score based on the Mahalanobis distance. Under suitable assumptions on the defender's prior knowledge, we characterize the class of time-varying affine transformations that preserve the anomaly score for arbitrary data and parameterize this class by the orthogonal group. Based on this characterization, we formulate attack design under the stealthiness condition as an optimization problem over the orthogonal group and propose a Riemannian gradient method. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed attack can degrade closed-loop performance while remaining stealthy.

title: Lomb-Scargle Recovery of Periodic Binary Signals across Black Hole Mass and Cadence
abstract: Searches for periodic supermassive black hole binaries in quasar light curves rely on recovery fractions, the share of injected signals detected, which forecasts use as detection efficiencies. Lin, Charisi, & Haiman (2026) measured them for the Lomb-Scargle periodogram on damped-random-walk light curves matched to 12,400 bright, high-mass Palomar Transient Factory (PTF) quasars with Sloan Digital Sky Survey Data Release 7 (DR7) masses. To test them over four decades of mass, we inject their sinusoidal and sawtooth signals into light curves of mergers in the TNG100-1 cosmological simulation, with magnitudes drawn from DR7 quasars of similar mass (extrapolated at low mass). We apply their threshold in each frequency bin, set by $10^5$ noise-only light curves per binary, on observed PTF cadences, one Stripe 82 cadence and an LSST-like cadence (Legacy Survey of Space and Time). At fixed absolute magnitude $M_i=-23$, sinusoid recovery falls toward high mass, and with DR7 magnitudes it climbs above about $10^8\,M_\odot$, so the magnitude assignment sets the sign of the trend. Above $10^8\,M_\odot$, where their sample lies, PTF sinusoid recovery is 39.8 against their 44.7 per cent. At LSST-like cadence sinusoid recovery is 76.9 per cent, about three times their 22.6 per cent, for reasons mostly unidentified. Denser sampling of the same PTF baselines did not lower recovery in any test. Even at LSST-like cadence we miss most sawtooth signals above $10^8\,M_\odot$. We tabulate recovery per 0.5-dex mass bin and cadence, with low-mass values likely too high for a deeper survey.

title: Universal Synthesis of Large-Area Hybrid Perovskite Monolayers Enabling Lithography-Free, Low-Static-Power Optoelectronics
abstract: Solution-phase synthesis of monolayer hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites is constrained by rapid out-of-plane crystal growth, uncontrolled nucleation, and strong interlayer aggregation, yielding flakes of only a few μm. We introduce a steric-engineering ternary-solvent growth strategy to synthesize monolayer and few-layer A2MX4 hybrid perovskites with exceptionally large surface areas. By combining alcohol cosolvents with an amine additive, out-of-plane stacking is suppressed. Using (PEA)2CuCl4 as a model system, monolayers with lateral areas exceeding 1000 μm2 are achieved, representing a massive dimensional increase over conventional methods. Molecular dynamics and quantum-chemical calculations show that longer-chain alcohols reorganize precursor solvation, while solvent volatility prolongs edge-mediated precursor transport during annealing. This strategy demonstrates universal applicability across diverse organic spacer cations (PEA+, F-PEA+, PentA+), metal centers (Cu2+, Mn2+, Pb2+), and halides (Cl-, Br-, I-). The large lateral dimensions enable direct, solvent-free electrical contact fabrication via physical shadow masking, bypassing chemical degradation from solvents used in conventional lithography. Planar devices fabricated from isolated ultrathin (PEA)2PbI4 channels exhibit ultra-low dark currents down to the 10^-15 - 10^-13 A range, enabling femtowatt-to-picowatt static power consumption, ~ 0.2 pW at 5 V, a 250-fold reduction relative to drop-cast films, while maintaining a high light-to-dark current ratio of 4.3 x 102. This work establishes precise steric and solvation control as a paradigm for scalable, compositionally diverse, low-static-power monolayer 2D perovskite optoelectronics.
authors: Shankeerthan Kalyanasundaram;Swarit Dwivedi;Sanje Mahasivam;Christopher R. McNeill;Sudha Mokkapati

title: Width and Depth Limits Commute During Training in Linear Residual Networks
abstract: Recent work established that the infinite-width and infinite-depth limits of residual networks commute at initialization when residual branches are scaled by $1/\sqrt{depth}$. In particular, the network output converges to the same limit whether width and depth tend to infinity sequentially or jointly. We extend this commutativity result to training in linear residual networks. Under the same $1/\sqrt{depth}$ residual-branch scaling (Depth-$μ$P) and the $μ$P width parameterization, we prove that, for any fixed number of gradient-descent steps with gradient clipping, the network output converges in $L^2$ along every joint width--depth growth path as both width and depth tend to infinity. Consequently, the infinite-width and infinite-depth limits commute throughout any finite training horizon. Without gradient clipping, the corresponding $L^2$ convergence does not hold in general, but we establish the weaker convergence in probability.

title: Incentive Mechanisms for Welfare Maximization Under Individual Rationality in Noncooperative Dynamical Systems
abstract: Human societies are shaped by strategic interactions among self-interested decision-makers, where conflicts between individual and social interests naturally arise. This paper investigates the design of incentive mechanism for multi-agent game systems to reconcile social welfare maximization with individual benefits under economic constraints. We develop a linear-quadratic incentive framework to reshape Nash equilibria while reconciling the constraints of Pareto efficiency, individual rationality, and budget balance. The optimal target state is identified as the solution of a constrained optimization problem associated with the social welfare and aggregated payoff functions. Our theoretical analysis characterizes the conditions of incentive functions that steer self-interested agents towards the optimal target state as a Pareto-efficient Nash equilibrium for achieving the maximum attainable social welfare. We further characterize how the choice of social welfare function constrains achievable individual outcomes, revealing a structural paradox associated with priority weighting under individual rationality. Several numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the efficacy of our results.

title: Hidden Convexity of the Joint Range of Three Quadratic Forms and Applications
abstract: We investigate a hidden convexity phenomenon for triples of homogeneous quadratic forms. We give a complete characterization of the convexity of the upper image obtained by adding the nonnegative orthant to their joint range. More precisely, the upper image is convex if and only if either a nonzero nonnegative linear combination of the three associated matrices is positive semidefinite, or the three quadratic forms admit a common strict negative direction. In particular, the upper image is convex whenever one of the three quadratic forms is convex. As applications, we establish the convexity of an associated value function and derive a generalized S-lemma for implications involving two quadratic inequalities and a strict theorem of the alternative for quadratic systems.

title: Half-Slot Link Scheduling for Open GNSS with $x$-Tx $y$-Rx Multibeam Phased Array Antennas
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSSs) are evolving from closed navigation constellations toward open space infrastructure capable of serving extensive spacecraft users. This evolution requires the constellation to support navigation ranging, telemetry (TM) return, and telecommand (TC) delivery for users while preserving its own ranging and communication functions.Existing phased-array payloads onboard BeiDou satellites provide one transmit (Tx) beam and one receive (Rx) beam. Such a configuration was designed mainly for intra-constellation operation, and can become a resource bottleneck when a large number of users share the same link opportunities. Upgrading GNSS satellites to phased-array terminals with $x$-Tx and $y$-Rx beams is therefore a natural enhancement. This paper develops a staged dynamic half-slot link scheduling framework (SDHSS) for open GNSS with $x$-Tx $y$-Rx multibeam phased-array antennas. The framework models navigation, TM, and TC as three different services, reserves the essential ranging and ground-access opportunities required by the GNSS constellation, and then allocates the remaining half-slot beam resources according to current service demand. To support multibeam concurrency, feasible links are selected through dynamic service-layer ordering and beam-copy matching. Simulations based on a BeiDou constellation show that the proposed method protects GNSS baseline operation and provides stronger external navigation, TM, and TC performance than fair contact planning. The results further show that additional Tx and Rx beams can be effectively converted into multi-service capability. This work establishes a link-scheduling approach for extending GNSS from constellation-internal operation to large-scale spacecraft service support.
authors: Huan Yan;Kanglian Zhao;Wenfeng Li;Jinjun Zheng;Ziyu Wang;Changgang Zheng

title: Impact of localized $4f$ magnetism on Berry curvature and the intrinsic anomalous Hall effect in CeRu$_2$Si$_2$
abstract: The intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (AHE), originating from Berry curvature, has been extensively studied in $f$-electron systems, including Ce-based compounds. However, how the magnetism of localized $f$ electrons affect the intrinsic AHE remains unclear. Here, we investigate this issue in CeRu$_2$Si$_2$ by calculating the intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) for several occupied Ce-$4f$ states using first-principles LDA+$U$ calculations combined with Wannier interpolation method. We find that the intrinsic AHC remains finite even when the Ce-$4f$ states are localized and do not contribute directly to the Fermi surface, and that its magnitude depends on which Ce-$4f$ state is occupied. We show that localized $4f$-electron magnetism induces exchange splitting in the conduction bands, generating Berry curvature in specific regions near the Fermi surface. This mechanism enables conduction bands that are derived from nonmagnetic orbitals and form the Fermi surface to contribute to the intrinsic AHE, suggesting a route to realizing large intrinsic AHE in $f$-electron materials.

title: Behavioral Mapping of Hierarchical Dynamical Models Accelerates Bayesian Parameter Inference
abstract: Bayesian parameter inference for complex nonlinear dynamical models is often limited by the cost of repeated model simulation. We present a behavioral mapping framework that uses the inferred posterior of a higher-level model to accelerate inference of a lower-level model without requiring state or parameter correspondence between them. Building on approximate simulation relations for hierarchically related models, we define the notion of behavioral compatibility and quantify the behavioral support of detailed model parameters using the reduced model posterior. We learn a level set of behavioral support using a Gaussian process and use it to filter detailed model parameter proposals before expensive simulations during Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) inference. We derive conditions under which the behavioral support level set retains all detailed model parameters that fit the experimental data within a prescribed tolerance. We apply this method to a hierarchy of gene-expression models fitted to cell-free experimental data. After initial setup costs, our approach speeds up MCMC by 8.02% for the phenomenological model and 15.21% for the mechanistic model.

title: A 13 Year Black Hole Microlensing Survey in Omega Centauri
abstract: Star clusters are born with massive stars that leave behind a large population of stellar mass black holes. These black holes may account for a large fraction of binary black hole mergers seen in gravitational waves as the dense environment enables retention of black holes and the formation of binaries. However, direct measurements of stellar mass black holes in globular clusters are limited, with just a few found in binary systems thus far. In this paper, we examine the possibility of detecting black holes through microlensing in the Milky Way's most massive star cluster, Omega Centauri. We take advantage of a unique dataset of nearly 200 single-band images taken over 13 years with the Hubble Space Telescope to look for the $\sim$1 year long events expected from microlensing of cluster stars by stellar mass black holes. We develop a novel cost function to fit the lensing signatures that we verify using synthetic events, quantifying our completeness. These synthetic events are based on a recent Monte Carlo simulation of Omega Centauri. We also use these synthetic events to train a neural network to most efficiently distinguish observed lensing events. Application of this algorithm to our observed data, and subsequent visual follow-up, show no convincing candidate black hole lensing events. Based on analysis of the simulation data and our completeness, we find that no events would be expected in the data contrary to the expectations from earlier work. We release the photometric dataset used in this work for future use.
authors: Zack Freeman;Maximilian Häberle;Anil Seth;John Zaris;Matthew Whitaker;Carl L. Rodriguez;Elena González Prieto;Andrea Bellini;Callie Clontz;Sebastian Kamann;Mattia Libralato;Nadine Neumayer;Jay Strader;Doğa Veske

title: From phase analysis to phase tracking: a robust approach to atomic-scale strain mapping
abstract: Atomic-scale strain governs the electronic, ferroic and mechanical properties of materials, and atomic-resolution microscopy measures it most directly. Geometric phase analysis (GPA) is the standard tool, but it fails when a Bragg reflection moves outside its fixed Fourier aperture under large strain or rotation, or in misoriented grains. Here we introduce geometric phase tracking analysis (GPTA), whose Fourier aperture tracks the Bragg reflection at each pixel in real space. A narrow aperture can therefore reject noise without losing a displaced reflection. On 13,795 simulated and experimental atomic-resolution images under various imaging conditions, GPTA reduces GPA's failure rate from 27% to 11.5% with up to 335 times better accuracy. It also gives strain and dislocation maps across grains, resistance to dynamical-scattering extinction, and a confidence map, capabilities that GPA lacks. Tracking the aperture combines reciprocal-space dose efficiency with real-space spatial resolution and extends atomic-scale strain metrology to beam-sensitive materials and challenging imaging conditions.

title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Predict Atomic Oxygen Erosion of Polymers in Low Earth Orbit
abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO), home to most active satellites, is projected to undergo a debris-fragmentation cascade known as Kessler Syndrome. In light of this eventuality, it is imperative to maximize the operational lifetime of LEO satellites. Instrumental to this goal is the development of next-generation polymeric materials with improved resistance to atomic oxygen (AO) erosion. Because genuine LEO exposure experiments are prohibitively expensive and LEO conditions are difficult to reproduce in the laboratory, data-driven approaches offer a promising alternative for accelerating materials discovery. Here, we develop a fine-tuned large language model (LLM) based on OpenAI's GPT-4o to predict the AO erosion yield ($E_y$) of polymers using a curated dataset of 201 measurements compiled from multiple NASA LEO exposure missions. The model achieves an order of magnitude error (OME) of 0.154 and a log-scaled coefficient of determination (log-$R^2$) of 0.719, outperforming conventional machine learning approaches while eliminating the need for extensive feature engineering. Notably, incorporating macroscopic descriptors such as film thickness and layering did not improve predictive performance, suggesting that AO erosion is governed primarily by chemical and environmental variables rather than bulk structural characteristics. This finding underscores the importance of chemically informed polymer design in developing materials with improved AO resistance, while demonstrating the ability of modern LLMs to effectively extract chemically meaningful relationships even when data is limited. Beyond its predictive accuracy, the proposed framework provides a scalable platform for rapidly screening candidate polymers, reducing reliance on costly spaceflight experiments.
authors: Jared Solovei;Sakshi Agarwal;Aubrey Toland;Jeffrey G. Ethier;Vikas Varshney;Lisa M. Hall;Wolfgang Windl;Rampi Ramprasad

title: The Milky Way's Early Disk Was Built in Bursts. II. The Multicomponent Age-Metallicity Structure of the High-$α$ Disk
abstract: Whether the high-$α$ disk experienced a continuous or episodic star-formation history remains an open question. Here we investigate the age--metallicity distribution of the high-$α$ disk using approximately 145,000 Gaia DR3 subgiants with $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]>-1$, 6.5~kpc $\lesssim R\lesssim9.5$~kpc, and $|Z|\lesssim1.5$~kpc. We adopt a forward-modelling framework that accounts for individual age and metallicity uncertainties and corrects for sample selection effects. The reconstructed distribution reveals two components: a broad, dominant population peaking at $\sim10.6$ Gyr and $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]\simeq-0.38$, and an older, more metal-poor population peaking at $\sim12.4$ Gyr and $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]\simeq-0.79$. These features suggest an episodic history of star formation and chemical enrichment in the high-$α$ disk, qualitatively consistent with cosmological simulations in which recurrent gas accretion drives variations in the star formation rate. The age of the older component is close to the $\sim12.3$~Gyr epoch inferred for the proposed Low-energy--Kraken--Heracles accretion event, suggesting a possible connection between this early interaction and enhanced disk star formation. There is tentative evidence that the dominant population is possibly composed of two sub-components with age distributions peaking at $\sim11.1$ Gyr and $\sim10.0$ Gyr, respectively. Together, these results favour a picture in which the high-$α$ disk was built through recurrent episodes of enhanced star formation rather than a single temporally smooth phase, even for the regime of ${\rm [Fe/H]}>-1$.
authors: Tiancheng Sun;Maosheng Xiang;Jifeng Liu;Meng Zhang;Yaqian Wu

title: Residual Calibration via Local Feature-Space Refinement
abstract: Deep neural networks often struggle to provide reliable confidence estimates, making post-hoc calibration essential for reliable decision-making. Existing post-hoc methods largely rely on score-based transformations, which improve marginal calibration but often fail to capture spatially varying miscalibration in local regions of the learned feature space. To address this gap, we propose Local Adaptive Probability Estimation (LAPE), a post-hoc residual calibration framework. Specifically, LAPE treats the global calibrator output as a stable anchor and refines the individual prediction by leveraging non-parametric local evidence from neighboring calibration samples. As a plug-and-play refinement module, LAPE effectively utilizes the information about feature-space geometry and can reuse the calibration data that are used to construct the global calibrator. Furthermore, we extend LAPE to the setting with multi-view inputs through Cascade Feature Augmentation Fusion (CFAF). Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed methods can improve the calibration quality of various existing baselines and remain efficient and robust across different settings.

title: Adaptive Restart under Unknown KL Geometry in Stochastic Weakly-Convex Optimization
abstract: KL geometry accelerates restart schedules in stochastic weakly-convex optimization, but the schedule depends jointly on an unknown and potentially nonunique geometric description. We introduce CARP-KL, a certified portfolio that adapts over valid KL descriptions while using the same primitive stochastic-subgradient oracle for both optimization and candidate selection. Over declared polynomial parameter ranges, CARP-KL competes with every affordable valid description and preserves the known-description polynomial Moreau-stationarity rate up to logarithmic factors, without objective values, an exact proximal map, direct Moreau-gradient access, or a bounded-domain assumption. Controlled experiments quantify the finite-budget price of this universality. The portfolio repeatedly contains strong candidates, while certification consumes a substantial share of the oracle budget and finite-sample ranking limits their recovery. A common conservative gap bound further reduces the portfolio from $O(\log^3 T)$ to $O(\log^2 T)$ candidates with an explicit scale-mismatch penalty. The theory and diagnostics together establish certified unknown-geometry adaptation and pinpoint selection as the principal practical frontier of the current construction.
authors: Binh T. Nguyen;Khoa D. Nguyen;Bao Thai Huynh

title: How good are universal MLIPs for alloys? A benchmark is only as trustworthy as its controls
abstract: Universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) are ranked by their formation-energy error against a DFT database, as if that database were ground truth, but independent DFT databases disagree. We benchmark fourteen uMLIPs on 1.45 million ordered intermetallics against AFLOW, which none trained on, and compare every energy and stability error with that disagreement. For half the structures, AFLOW, Alexandria, and OQMD differ by less than 6-8 meV/atom, but a minority differ by far more, raising the average to 16-30. That disagreement sets a floor on any model's measurable error. Re-referenced, the best uMLIP agrees with AFLOW as closely as Alexandria does, and the next four sit 2-7 meV/atom above the floor. Once broken elemental references are screened, the energy and stability rankings agree almost everywhere. Three apparent model failures shrink or vanish under the right control: poorly correlated shear moduli, thousands of "bad" DFT references, and the leader's inflated lead.
authors: Gus L. W. Hart;Jacob N. Pursley

title: Retraction-Free Nonsmooth Optimization on the Stiefel Manifold: Subgradient and Proximal Landing Methods
abstract: We develop three retraction-free Landing methods for nonsmooth composite optimization over the Stiefel manifold, combining an (approximately) tangential direction with an infeasibility-reducing normal direction. The subgradient Landing method, with normal stepsizes parameterized by $α\in[0,1]$, has best-iterate complexity bounds $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-4})$ for surrogate stationarity and $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2/(2-α)})$ for feasibility. For $α=0$, it converges locally $R$-linearly under local weak sharpness and mild assumptions. The proximal gradient Landing method computes a tangential direction by solving a proximal subproblem and combines it with the same normal direction. Moreover, the inexact proximal gradient Landing method allows the proximal subproblem to be solved approximately and applies an explicit correction to control violations of the tangency condition. Both proximal methods have outer-iteration complexity bounds $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2})$ for stationarity and $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-1})$ for feasibility, and every accumulation point is first-order stationary. Under an additional asymptotic Bregman-error condition and the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property of a suitable auxiliary function, the primal sequence of the inexact method converges to a first-order stationary point. Numerical experiments illustrate the effectiveness of all three methods. On the tested sparse principal component analysis instances, the inexact method has favorable running times, and both proximal methods maintain small feasibility residuals.

title: On the Structure of Quantum Finite-Level Systems: Decoherence-Free Subsystems, Quantum Nondemolition Variables, and Back-Action-Evading Measurements
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to conduct a comprehensive structural analysis of quantum finite-level systems in the Heisenberg picture, where the evolution of system observables is modeled by bilinear quantum stochastic differential equations (QSDEs). Firstly, real coordinate transformations that preserve commutation and anticommutation relations are characterized, and relative admissibility between different orthonormal Hermitian bases is formulated. Secondly, strongly aligned subspaces are introduced, based on which decoherence-free subsystems (DFSs) are constructed in general orthonormal Hermitian basis as well as the generalized Gell-Mann basis. Thirdly, conditions for the existence of quantum nondemolition (QND) variables are given in terms of both linear systems theory and spectral separation by output-signal observables. Finally, a sufficient condition for quantum back-action-evading (BAE) measurements is established. A four-qubit nearest-neighbor Heisenberg chain with collective dephasing illustrates these structural properties of quantum finite-level systems.

title: Multiwavelength Classification of Chandra Sources in Omega Centauri
abstract: We present a comprehensive study of X-ray sources in the globular cluster NGC 5139 to date. Over 200 Chandra sources are cross-matched to multiwavelength catalogs from HST, JWST, and MeerKAT. We employ a machine-learning classification pipeline (MUWCLASS) for the first time in such a crowded stellar environment and introduce the globular-cluster-specific training dataset, which compiles previously classified sources from 25 Galactic globular clusters. Given the challenges presented by the high-density environment, we compare the MUWCLASS results with traditional classification methods. We confirm counterpart associations suggested in previous works and also identify new confident and candidate associations. We discuss the implications of our classification results in light of models of cluster dynamical evolution and binary formation/destruction.
authors: Steven Chen;Oleg Kargaltsev;Jeremy Hare;Hui Yang;Oleg Smirnov;Ian Heywood;Talon Myburgh

title: Strain-induced structural transformations in hexagonal monolayer boron nitride. A density functional study
abstract: In this work we theoretically study the structural transformations occurring in monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) subjected to strong deformations. The first-principle computer simulations are based on the density functional theory employing the pseudopotentials with the exchange-correlation energy given in Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof form. Depending on the direction and the type of the strain, the simulations reveal different types of structural transformations in two-dimensional (2D) h-BN associated with the elastic failure. It is found that, under certain shear strains, there can form an ordered 2D orthorhombic phase with the 2D layer space symmetry pmmm. Thermal stability of the latter up to ~900 K is demonstrated by first-principle Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics. The examination of electronic structure indicates that, in contrast to the conventional h-BN, which is an insulator with the wide band gap, the predicted orthorhombic phase is expected to be a semiconductor with the narrow band gap of ~ 0.65 eV.
authors: O. Bystrenko;B. Ilkiv;S. Petrovska;O. Foia;T. Bystrenko;O. Khyzhun

title: Decoding Composition-Structure-Performance Relations in Sodium Layered Oxide Positive Electrode Materials
abstract: Layered sodium transition-metal (TM) oxides, Na$_x$TMO$_2$, are among the most promising sodium-ion positive electrode materials, yet their Na/vacancy orderings, layer stacking sequences, and cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions are known only for a few single-TM compounds. We compile the Na/vacancy orderings reported in earlier studies into a single library of 41 unique orderings and apply this uniformly to five single-TM and all ten Na$_x$TM$_{0.5}$TM$'_{0.5}$O$_2$ oxides (TM = Ti, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni), screening more than 120,000 structures with machine-learning interatomic potentials prior to 1,025 accurate first-principles calculations. The phase diagrams explain the observed O3/P3/O1 sequences and voltages, and the O3-to-P3 competition hinges on ordering energies of a few meV per atom that scalar descriptors, such as the cationic potential and the interlayer-slab distance, miss. Our extensive analysis reveals that the redox couples form a nearly partner-independent ladder, Ti$^{3+/4+}$ $<$ Mn$^{3+/4+}$ $<$ Co$^{3+/4+}$ $<$ Ni$^{2+/3+}$ $<$ Fe$^{3+/4+}$, explaining pristine charge transfer and the oxidation sequence. Van Vleck analysis of every TMO$_6$ octahedron reveals that TM mixing suppresses the cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions of Mn$^{3+}$ and Ni$^{3+}$ through charge transfer to Jahn--Teller-inactive states or dilution of Jahn--Teller-active centers. We formulate an energy-density-versus-strain map that yields a design rule: a high-voltage couple without Jahn--Teller strain, which Mn$^{4+}$/Ni$^{2+}$ charge transfer realizes in Na$_x$Mn$_{0.5}$Ni$_{0.5}$O$_2$, the most practical composition. We release the ordering-resolved dataset as a training set for subsequent training of accurate machine-learning interatomic potentials.
authors: Yunyeong Choi;Hasindhi H. Lokuge;Joshua D. Bocarsly;Pieremanuele Canepa

title: Multi-orbit S-star probes of Lorentz violation at the Galactic Center
abstract: We investigate the potential of Galactic-center S-star observations to probe Lorentz violation in the minimal pure-gravity Standard-Model Extension (SME), focusing on parameter degeneracies associated with anisotropic orbital signatures. We construct simulated astrometric and spectroscopic observations of S2 and S55 using fiducial orbital and Galactic-center parameters based on the multi-star solution from the GRAVITY Collaboration and evolve the stellar trajectories using the leading Lorentz-violating two-body dynamics supplemented by the Schwarzschild first-post-Newtonian (1PN) correction. Separate Fisher-matrix analyses of S2 and S55 each resolve seven of the eight independent SME directions, while their joint analysis resolves all eight directions by combining complementary projections from the differently oriented orbits. A subsequent Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis confirms the Fisher forecasts and reaches characteristic 95% credible-level sensitivities of approximately 10^(-3)-10^(-2) for the time-space components and 10^(-5)-10^(-4) for the spatial components. Our results demonstrate that combining S-stars with different orbital orientations is effective for breaking geometrical degeneracies and probing the tensor structure of Lorentz violation in the Galactic-center gravitational field.

title: Soft-Update MSA for Nonconvex Stochastic Optimal Control: Theory and Algorithms
abstract: For the method of successive approximations (MSA), a fundamental challenge is that the stochastic maximum principle (SMP) provides an optimality condition rather than a descent rule. To overcome this difficulty for nonconvex stochastic control problems, we develop a soft-update MSA (SU-MSA) with a second-order-adjoint correction of the Hamiltonian and a neural realization called DeepSMP. Both an explicit stepsize rule guaranteeing cost descent and the convergence of the algorithm are established. Moreover, the global SMP condition is asymptotically satisfied when the corrected Hamiltonian is convex, while in a special case the cost is further proved to converge to the global optimum. To extend SU-MSA to high dimensions, we develop DeepSMP using a differentiable smooth approximation of the corrected Hamiltonian and analyze the convergence of the resulting objective and its gradient. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

title: Rest-frame Ultraviolet Variability of Quasars in the Cosmic Himalayas Overdensity
abstract: Some high-redshift overdensities show an enhanced incidence of AGNs, suggesting that large-scale environment may influence supermassive black hole fuelling and triggering. Whether environment also affects AGN variability remains unclear. Using the Cosmic Himalayas (CH), an extreme concentration of 11 type 1 quasars at z=2.16-2.20, we investigate possible offsets in rest-frame ultraviolet variability relative to quasars with comparable redshifts, black hole masses, and Eddington ratios. We construct a parent sample of 1,138 Stripe 82 quasars at 2.11<=z<=2.25 and combine photometry from the SDSS, the PS1, and the ZTF to build observer-frame g- and r-band light curves spanning up to 27~yr. We compare DRW parameters and ensemble structure functions (SFs) with control pseudo-samples matched in black hole mass and Eddington ratio, and use injection--recovery simulations to forecast the detectability of a CH-like offset. The CH quasars show a tendency toward shorter DRW damping timescales (median offsets of -0.32 and -0.13 dex in g and r) and slightly higher asymptotic amplitudes. None of the four DRW comparisons is statistically significant, including the largest offset in the g-band damping timescale (p=0.16). Ensemble SFs generally exceed matched-control medians, although 18 of 19 lag bins per band remain within the 95% pointwise envelopes. Assuming a true uniform -0.32 dex g-band timescale offset, injection--recovery simulations predict an 80% probability of nominal 3sigma detection with approximately 60 quasars of comparable variability scatter and data quality. If confirmed, the tentative variability offsets may suggest that large-scale environment influences accretion-flow variability beyond its potential role in quasar triggering. Larger samples with higher-precision light curves, such as those expected from the LSST, are required to test this possibility.
authors: Jiaqi Lin;Zhenya Zheng;Bin Ma;Yongming Liang;Lin Long

title: Learning-Oriented Fault-Tolerant Control for UAVs with Time-Varying Fault Estimation
abstract: The increasing deployment of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in safety-critical applications has created a growing demand for control strategies that remain reliable in the presence of actuator and sensor faults. This paper presents a fault-tolerant control framework that combines constructive mathematical modeling, proportional--integral (PI) fault estimation, and learning-oriented control. A nonlinear quadcopter model is first developed using both the Newton--Euler and Euler--Lagrange formulations, from which a discrete-time linear model is derived for observer and controller design. A PI observer is then proposed to estimate actuator and sensor faults, with exponential estimation-error convergence established for constant faults in the absence of disturbances and ultimate boundedness established for slowly time-varying faults under bounded disturbances. The estimated fault signals are incorporated into an active fault-tolerant control architecture together with a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) controller, which is trained using only the yaw channel and subsequently applied to improve closed-loop tracking performance. Numerical simulations illustrate the observer's estimation performance under constant and slowly time-varying faults, including bounded disturbances, and the tracking performance of the integrated controller under multiple actuator and sensor fault scenarios. The proposed framework combines model-based fault estimation with learning-based control to improve fault accommodation and tracking performance in UAV systems.
comment: This is an extended version of the paper published in the proceedings of IEEE CoDIT

title: Lifetime-valid decisions by continually evolving AI analysts
abstract: AI agents increasingly act as analysts whose decision can often be cast as hypothesis tests. Classical tests control the Type I error rate, the probability of rejecting a true null hypothesis, for fixed procedures. However, AI analysts introduce internal randomness and can evolve continuously over time. As AI analysts evolve, the risk of approving versions with Type I error rates above the target can accumulate, and adaptive use of evaluation feedback can lead to overfitting. We introduce continual validation, which evaluates each proposed AI analyst version before deployment using simulated data under the null hypothesis, with scenarios that can be randomized and expanded over time. We prove that, regardless of how updates are chosen or how many are proposed, the lifetime probability of ever deploying a version whose Type I error rate exceeds the allowed level remains bounded. This guarantees that every subsequent decision controls the Type I error rate at the target level across these scenarios. At the same time, updates with sufficiently low Type I error rates pass validation with high probability, allowing the analyst to continuously improve its performance without sacrificing rigor. In two examples involving evolving AI analysts for bioequivalence studies and product A/B tests, Type I error rates reached 0.098 and 0.183 without continual validation, compared with at most 0.045 and 0.044 with it, while retaining 82% and 96% of the power from optimally selected valid updates.

title: Exact Characterization of Admissible Bandwidths for Linear Disturbance Observers
abstract: This paper characterizes the entire set of admissible Q-filter bandwidths, equivalently parameterized by the time constant $τ$, that guarantee robust internal stability of a linear disturbance observer (DOB) under parametric plant uncertainties. Classical small-$τ$ stability results provide a rigorous foundation for Q-filter bandwidth design. Building on this foundation, we formulate the $τ$-dependent robust internal-stability problem as a semialgebraic feasibility problem in bivariate polynomials and prove that the complete admissible set is a finite union of open intervals under the standing assumptions. A constructive procedure with exact membership tests recovers all stabilizing intervals. A numerical example with an uncertain plant family containing non-minimum-phase members illustrates a disconnected admissible set.

title: Field-free superconducting diode and tunable vortex dynamics in NbN/FePt stripe-domain heterostructures
abstract: We demonstrate reconfigurable, field-free superconducting diode behavior in NbN/FePt and NbN/AlN/FePt heterostructures with remanent stripe domains in the FePt layer. NbN films 10 nm thick are capped either directly with FePt or through a thin AlN spacer, which reduces electronic proximity effects while preserving magnetic coupling through stray fields. At zero applied magnetic field, the superconducting diode efficiency reaches approximately 50--60% in NbN/FePt when the stripes are perpendicular to the current and is strongly reduced when they are parallel. The diode effect persists in NbN/AlN/FePt with efficiencies reaching approximately 35--40%, supporting a magnetic origin of the nonreciprocity. We interpret the response as asymmetric vortex transport in the remanent magnetic landscape, with preferential edge vorticity and a Lorentz force that favors inward flux injection or outward motion depending on current polarity. Under applied perpendicular magnetic fields, the interplay between the external field and the magnetic stray fields modifies the flux-flow instability and the apparent instability velocity inferred from transport, with values below those reported for bare NbN films. These results show that stripe-domain ferromagnetic overlayers provide a reconfigurable route to control superconducting nonreciprocity and flux-flow stability in NbN-based heterostructures.
authors: Juan C. Zapata;Emilio De Biasi;Martin Sirena;Jeehoon Kim;Nestor Haberkorn

title: Using Finite-Time Control to Synthesize Dynamic Backup Control Barrier Functions
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for the construction of control barrier functions (CBFs) for controllable linear systems subject to multiple state and input constraints. The approach is based on the Dynamic Backup CBF (DB-CBF) framework, where the control policy is parametrized using the equilibrium subspace of the system. By using a minimum-energy finite-time controller, we show that the terminal set constraint trivially reduces to having an admissible equilibrium point. The proposed DB-CBF is easy to tune (one parameter), fully takes advantage of the input range (by minimizing the control effort), and guarantees constraint enforcement (by tracking a backup equilibrium point that can be reached safely in finite time).

title: LLM2Cert: LLM Synthesis of Certificates with SMT/Lean Verification
abstract: Lyapunov functions and barrier certificates give state-space guarantees of stability and safety, but synthesizing and verifying them---especially for nonlinear, high-dimensional systems---remains an open challenge. Existing pipelines verify candidates with numerical solvers (sum-of-squares programs), interval methods, or satisfiability-modulo-theories (SMT) solvers, which often require relaxations, are conservative, or scale poorly with model dimension and nonlinearity. These limitations have also shaped benchmark design: standard test suites are dominated by low-dimensional polynomial systems chosen to suit what solvers can handle rather than what engineering applications require. We address both sides of this challenge. First, we introduce DynaCertBench, a benchmark of 105 instances: 80 non-redundant systems curated from the literature, extended with high-dimensional and control-constrained variants and new nonlinearly coupled systems, comprehensively spanning stability, region-of-attraction, forward-invariance, and safety tasks. Second, we present LLM2Cert, an LLM-driven framework that synthesizes candidate certificates and verifies them against their proof obligations: each obligation is routed to an SMT solver or directly to the Lean Proof-Repair agent. On DynaCertBench, LLM2Cert verifies 81 of 105 instances ($77.1\%$), a $17.1$ percentage point improvement over one-shot proposal without feedback. On the 81 fixed certificates, LLM2Cert verifies 22 that All-SMT leaves unresolved. Code and data are available at https://github.com/FormalCert-AI/llm2cert.

title: A Potential New Dimension of Astrophysical Aromatic Functionalization: Phosphaethynyl (CP) Derivatives
abstract: Quantum chemical computations outline a thermodynamically viable, low-temperature, gas-phase formation pathway for phosphaethynyl cyclopropenylidene ($c$-C$_3$HCP), resulting from cyclopropenylidene ($c$-C$_3$H$_2$) and the phosphaethynyl (CP) radical. Given the detections of both $c$-C$_3$H$_2$ and the CP radical toward circumstellar shells along with the provided reaction pathway, $c$-C$_3$HCP is a potentially present astro-molecule which could be searched for in phosphorus rich environments. The reaction of CP and benzene (C$_6$H$_6$) to produce phosphaethynyl benzene (C$_6$H$_5$CP) is also explored. A marginally emerged, but tentative, transition state is identified for this reaction using certain quantum chemical approaches but not others. Consequently, the formation of CP-substituted benzoid polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in astrophysical environments from CP + PAH reactions is possible but currently uncertain. Additionally, explicitly correlated coupled cluster quartic force field and second-order vibrational perturbation theory rovibrational analysis of the vibrational frequencies and rotational constants of $c$-C$_3$HCP are provided, as well as density functional theory predictions of the same for CP-benzene (C$_6$H$_5$CP) and both isomers of CP-naphthalene (C$_1$$_0$H$_7$CP). Our results suggest that IR searches for these molecules would likely be unsuccessful due to the low intensities and coincidence with PAH features, but their large dipole moments could make them feasible to detect with radio astronomy. The barrierless formation of $c$-C$_3$HCP and possibly barrierless synthesis of C$_6$H$_5$CP stand as examples for future investigations of other CP-substituted aromatic molecules, marking the potential beginning of a new frontier of astronomical aromatic functionalization.
authors: Reace H. J. Willis;Vincent J. Esposito;Thomas H. Speak;Ilsa R. Cooke;Ryan C. Fortenberry

title: Chiral Cavity Vacua as Local Generators and Probes of Non-Abelian Kitaev Topology
abstract: We show how a gyrotropic cavity vacuum generates, probes, and spatially programs non-Abelian topology in the Kitaev honeycomb model. Gauge-consistent virtual-photon elimination produces a universal helicity-odd interaction $\mathrm{i}[P_x,P_y]$ alongside same-order even dressing. For the leading bond polarization, this commutator is exactly the Kitaev three-spin mass. Mode normalization imposes a thermodynamic constraint: one extended normalized mode gives a local mass that vanishes with sample area, whereas a localized mode writes a finite topological island and a finite mode density enables a bulk mass. The exact Majorana solution yields helicity-reversed Chern gaps and edge propagation, while integrated circular dichroism exactly measures the mass generator, $\langle\mathrm{i}[P_x,P_y]\rangle=-\sqrt3p^2\langle O_3\rangle$. Real-space calculations reveal a non-Abelian island and a helicity wall with two co-propagating Majorana modes. Uniform helicity reversal is a Dirac-mass quench with $n_{\rm ex}\proptoτ_Q^{-1}$, whereas moving a wall localizes the gap closing. The equilibrium vacuum kernel contains sum-frequency rather than resonant denominators. These results establish distinct criteria for local and bulk cavity-induced topology.

title: Monetary Policy Forecast Errors and Inflation Compensation under Sovereign Stress in Brazil
abstract: This paper examines whether inflation compensation around Brazilian monetary policy decisions is associated differently with policy forecast errors when sovereign spreads are relatively elevated. Public Tesouro Direto quotations, meeting-specific Focus forecasts and a lagged EMBI indicator yield 68 three-year and 60 five-year event observations. The outcome is a matched-horizon retail yield proxy; the policy variable is the announced Selic target minus a preceding-week survey mean. At three years, a 10-basis-point forecast error is associated with 4.14 basis points less compensation repricing in the high-spread state than in the low-spread state, but the restricted wild cluster test gives a two-sided p-value of 0.1018. The estimated total high-state response is -0.42 basis points, with a pointwise 95 percent interval of [-2.25, 1.41]. The five-year interaction is sensitive to pandemic meetings and changes sign when 2020 is excluded. A common sample of 43 events does not establish a maturity gradient. A supplementary comparison on extended windows is also sensitive to the policy measure. The evidence is therefore inconclusive about state dependence. Survey timing, sparse maturity support and daily retail quotations prevent these associations from identifying a structural monetary shock, a pure inflation-risk premium or fiscal dominance.

title: Learning to Incentivise: Using Reinforcement Learning for Sustainable Urban Mobility
abstract: Traffic management has traditionally focused on toll-based and road pricing solutions. However, road pricing often raises concerns about accessibility and public dissatisfaction, leading to its prohibition in some places, such as Finland. This study optimises the dynamic allocation of incentives to drivers, encouraging them to reroute onto alternative (potentially longer) paths to achieve greater societal benefit, reduced total travel time (TTT) and total emissions in the transportation network, contributing to sustainable urban mobility. We employ a multi-agent reinforcement learning approach to dynamically assign incentives to drivers to reduce both TTT and emissions, with travel times estimated using traffic simulation software. We demonstrate that, with an unlimited budget and an objective of minimising travel time, the incentive scheme reduces TTT by 16%, compared to the dynamic User-Equilibrium (UE) with a budget equivalent to about 11% of the UE total time. When the goal is to minimise emissions, a 9% reduction in CO2 emissions is observed under an unlimited budget. We demonstrate a critical trade-off: minimising TTT leads to an increase in emissions, while prioritising emission reductions raises TTT. However, with the right combination of weights in the multi-objective function, both TTT and total emissions are improved beyond the baseline.

title: Flow-based Spectral Kernel Learning for Nonstationary Attention
abstract: Kernelized attention provides a useful perspective for understanding self-attention as a similarity-based aggregation mechanism, but existing approaches often rely on fixed or stationary kernels, limiting their ability to adapt the similarity structure to complex token interactions. In this paper, we propose flow-based spectral kernel attention (FSKA), a framework for learning expressive nonstationary attention kernels. FSKA formulates kernelized attention through spectral density learning and parameterizes the resulting bivariate spectral density with normalizing flows. This design enables flexible and regularizable kernel learning while remaining compatible with scalable linear-attention computation. We further show that expressive kernel learning enables a simplified attention design with removed query--key projections and fixed orthogonal value projections, resulting in a more parameter-efficient architecture. Controlled experiments on classification, ablation, and scalability profiling show that FSKA achieves competitive or improved performance over existing attention mechanisms, while reducing projection-related trainable parameters by approximately $40\%$--$47\%$ compared with most baselines and maintaining favorable linear-attention memory scaling. Code Available: https://github.com/ziyang18/FSKA.

title: Suppression of Grain Boundary Nitrogen Degradation by Boron in Superalloys
abstract: Superalloys enable the hottest sections of jet engines to operate at high temperatures, but environmentally assisted degradation limits their lifetime. In polycrystalline alloys, nitrogen penetrates beneath the protective surface oxides, to produce embrittling grain boundary nitrides. Boron is added in trace amounts to improve grain boundary strength, yet its role, if any, in oxidation-related degradation remains unclear. Here we show that boron segregates to an internal nitride--matrix interface in a Ni/Co-base $γ$/$γ^{\prime}$ strengthened superalloy. Both B-free and B-containing alloys develop stratified chromia/alumina scales at 800~$^{\circ}$C in \SI{100}{\hour}, but the B-free variant produces larger, deeper and more elongated Ti/Nb-rich subsurface grain boundary nitrides. Correlative 4D S/TEM and atom probe tomography identify the particle as a chemically complex B1 nitride and reveal interfacial boron segregation. This shows that trace alloying as an alloy strategy can control damaging internal reaction product precipitation and growth by core-shell segregation.
authors: C. Crabb;G. Topore;J. O. Douglas;M. C. Hardy;M. S. Conroy;D. Dye

title: Strategic Arbitrage in Electricity Markets: A Multi-Agent Policy Optimization Framework
abstract: Grid-scale storage and load aggregators are growing quickly in wholesale electricity markets. If highly consolidated, these new participants may distort the competitive market equilibrium through strategic withholding behavior. Traditional market power mitigation techniques are ill-suited to arbitrage-based participants. We provide a multi-agent policy optimization model to study game-theoretic equilibria for real-time markets with consolidated storage and/or aggregators. The model is designed to facilitate natural first-order equilibrium-seeking update rules. We analyze the theoretical properties of different supply functions and their implications on the convergence of the gradient dynamics. Finally, we train equilibrium policies for a modified version of the IEEE RTS-GMLC benchmark across different levels of storage fleet consolidation, to demonstrate the potential of the framework as a tool to characterize and quantify strategic arbitrage.

title: JWST observations of the planetary nebula NGC 6302 IV: PAH spectral characteristics, formation and evolution
abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and carbonaceous dust have been observed in Oxygen-rich planetary nebulae (PNe), yet their formation and evolution in these environments is an open question. We aim to study the formation and evolution of the PAHs in the O-rich PN NGC 6302, by characterizing the PAH emission throughout this object. We obtained JWST MIRI IFU spectroscopic observations of NGC 6302 pointed at its central source. From these, we extract four template spectra that are representative of the variation in PAH emission throughout NGC 6302. We detect the major PAH features at 6.2, 7.7, 8.6, 11.2, and 12.7 $μ$m, and several minor PAH features. The template spectra vary in terms of their PAH feature widths, peak wavelengths, and relative intensities. The 11.2 $μ$m PAH feature is class B, typical for PNe. The 6-9 $μ$m PAH features are class A, which is less common for PNe. We estimate the PAH charge to be 75% cations on average, based on the 7.7/11.2 PAH feature ratio. The relative strengths of the 11-15 $μ$m PAH features indicate a range of PAH edge structures. To ensure consistency in our observations and explain variable PAH feature widths, we propose a variation in the size of the PAHs throughout NGC 6302, and suggest variation in the shielding of these PAHs. The PAHs range from large and non-compact, to small and compact. We find that NGC 6302 formed PAHs in-situ in the current PN phase, likely from small hydrocarbons formed by the photodissociation of CO.
