title: A Simple and General Approach to top-$k$ Selection
abstract: This paper considers the Bayesian top-$k$ identification problem, wherein a decision maker is tasked with selecting $k$ items from a pool of items of unknown quality. To assess the items, the decision maker adaptively allocates a fixed sampling budget, where each sample of an item yields a noisy observation of its quality, with the objective of minimizing the expected opportunity cost of the selected set. We propose an approach that allocates each batch of samples by minimizing a surrogate objective derived from an upper bound on the expected opportunity cost. The approach is general: samples can be allocated in batches, the selection size $k$ is arbitrary, and it applies to many sampling distributions. It is also simple and intuitive. We prove that the method's posterior expected opportunity cost decays at an exponential rate of at least half the best rate achievable by any sampling rule. In simulations across a wide range of settings, the method is competitive with, and often improves upon, the best existing algorithm in each setting.

title: One-Dimensional Symmetry Reductions of the Monge-Ampère Equation on Some Semi-Homogeneous Convex Cones in $\mathbb{R}^4$
abstract: Motivated by non-symmetric conic optimization, we construct six explicit families of semi-homogeneous proper convex cones $K$ in $\mathbb R^4$. For each family, a specified three-dimensional subgroup of linear automorphisms of $K$ has generic orbits of codimension one. This yields an orbit invariant $t$ and reduces the Monge-Ampère equation $\det F''=e^{2F}$, defining the canonical barrier on $K$, to an ordinary differential equation (ODE) with independent variable $t$. The families include asymmetric power, rotational-power, exponential, and nonabelian-type cones. For the power and exponential cases we derive first integrals and parametric solutions of the ODE. The reductions open the way for computing the canonical barrier on these cones numerically.

title: Selecting the Best Few with Human Evaluators: Adaptively Combining Ratings and Pairwise Comparisons
abstract: This paper considers a decision-maker tasked with identifying the $k$ best items from a large pool of candidates, such as job applicants, LLMs, award nominees, or new product ideas. The decision-maker learns about the items' quality by soliciting human evaluations. Each evaluation can be costly, so the decision-maker aims to use the limited evaluation budget efficiently by allocating evaluations adaptively. A key consideration is the form of evaluation to solicit, which should be something evaluators are comfortable providing. Two popular forms are ratings and pairwise comparisons, and we allow for both, as they may be especially useful in combination given the limited budget. Ratings can be used early on to get a coarse picture of which items are good and which are not. As that picture forms, comparisons can refine the ordering of the good items, narrowing in on the ultimate top-$k$ selection. To solve the allocation problem, we develop an adaptive algorithm built from two allocation policies. The first, our primary contribution, is based on a surrogate objective that is naturally forward-looking, valuing evaluations that help inform what to evaluate in future rounds, not just those that directly improve the selection decision. The decision rule is interpretable, and we prove that it is asymptotically consistent. Late in the evaluation process, when being forward-looking is less productive, we construct a myopic policy and a criterion for switching to it. In simulation, the method gives insight into how to combine these two types of evaluations, and beats the (limited) existing benchmarks.

title: Star formation history of Draco revealed by DESI DR1: suppressed early star formation efficiency for Milky Way dwarf galaxies
abstract: Dwarf galaxies serve as fossils for understanding the early star formation history of the local Universe. In this work, we use stellar abundances for individual stars derived from the first data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI DR1) to investigate the star formation history of the dwarf spheroidal galaxy Draco. We simultaneously fit the stellar metallicity distribution function (MDF) and the [Mg/Fe]-[Fe/H] trend using the galactic chemical evolution (GCE) model flexCE. Our best-fit models imply a low star formation efficiency (SFE) of $0.003$ to $0.007\,\mathrm{Gyr}^{-1}$, which is about ten times lower than values reported in the literature, but consistent with recent SFE estimates for ultra-faint dwarf galaxies. By combining recent literature measurements, we find that the SFEs of Milky Way dwarf galaxies scale with stellar mass as $\mathrm{SFE}\propto M_\star^{0.24}$. A low star formation efficiency is associated with a strong outflow efficiency; we estimate a large wind mass-loading factor $η_{\mathrm{wind}}$ of approximately 172-260. This is well in line with the observed outflow-stellar mass relation and with the Feedback in Realistic Environment (FIRE) cosmological simulations. Our results demonstrate the power of large-scale, low-to-medium resolution stellar spectroscopic surveys to deliver robust constraints on the early formation history of galaxies in the local Universe.
authors: Yujiao Yang;Maosheng Xiang;Yang Huang;Meng Zhang;Lanya Mou;Chao Liu;Jifeng Liu
comment: 19 pages, 10 figures, 2 tables. Accepted for publication in ApJ

title: The Milky Way's Early Disk Was Built in Bursts. I. Evidence from Low-angular-momentum, High-$α$ Stars Scattered Out of the Protodisk by Merger Events
abstract: Stars born in the high-$α$ disk can later acquire low angular momentum through dynamical scattering during early merger events. Their age--metallicity distribution thus provides a fossil record of the history of both star formation and dynamical perturbations in the early Milky Way disk. Here we identify a sample of 2,078 such stars from more than two million Gaia DR3 subgiants with robust determinations of ages, kinematics, and abundances. From this sample we reconstruct their intrinsic age--metallicity distribution with a forward modeling approach. Our results confirm that these scattered stars are older and more metal-poor than the bulk of the high-$α$ disk on average. In particular, the joint age--metallicity distribution reveals a robust two-component feature: a broad, dominant component with a peak age of $\sim$11.5~Gyr and ${\rm [Fe/H]}\simeq-0.59$, and an older and more metal-poor component with a peak age of $\sim$12.5~Gyr and ${\rm [Fe/H]}\simeq-0.86$. The presence of this two-component structure suggests that the high-$α$ disk experienced episodic phases of star formation and chemical enrichment. The age distribution of the younger Splash component, compared with that of the high-$α$ disk, provides evidence for a substantial dynamical perturbation at a lookback time of 10.8--11.5~Gyr, possibly associated with an early passage of Gaia--Sausage--Enceladus (GSE). The older Splash component, with a peak age of $\sim$12.5~Gyr, may preserve signatures of an earlier interaction, possibly associated with the proposed Low-energy--Kraken--Heracles (LKH) event.
authors: Tiancheng Sun;Maosheng Xiang;Shaolan Bi;Jifeng Liu;Meng Zhang;Yaqian Wu

title: Spatiotemporal Imaging of Thermally Driven Metal-Insulator Phase Domain Propagation in VO2
abstract: Achieving a detailed picture of the nature and dynamics of phase boundaries remains a major challenge, particularly solid-solid transitions central to phase-change materials. Here, we use stroboscopic optical scattering microscopy and finite-element simulations to study the nonlinear thermally driven motion of the mesoscale insulator-metal phase boundary in VO2 thin films. We visualize the lateral spatiotemporal evolution of a diffraction-limited photoinduced metallic phase domain, resolving its outward propagation, contraction, and ultimate disappearance. The phase boundary dynamics are governed by heat flow, which can be controlled by excitation fluence, film thickness, and substrate thermal conductivity. Parameter-free agreement between the data and nonlinear thermal transport simulations identify the phase boundary transport as locally diffusive under this regime. We quantify how the latent heat acts as a thermal inertia, suppressing transport and prolonging the phase coexistence. Paradoxically, despite being driven by the underlying thermal gradient locally described by Fourier's law, the mesoscale phase front propagates faster than expected from thermal diffusion. This phenomenon arises from the distinction between temperature-field evolution and phase-boundary isotherm motion. These results establish a link between heat dissipation and mesoscale phase-front motion, providing a framework for controlling phase-transition kinetics relevant to photonics applications of VO2. We anticipate that this approach generalizes to a broad class of first- and second-order transitions.
authors: Ilaria Delbono;Raouf Amara;Matias Feldman;Hankun Yang;Cédric Leau;Carlo Scian;Erwan Dandeu;Sébastien Royer;Debora Pierucci;Emmanuel Lhuillier;Franck Vidal;Tiziana Cesca;Hilton B. de Aguiar;Jose Ordonez-Miranda;Danièle Fournier;Raj Pandya;Boris Kalinic;Giovanni Mattei;James K. Utterback

title: Simulation-free approximate Bayesian computation for stochastic reaction networks
abstract: Uncovering stochastic reaction networks from data is central to single-cell biology. Simulation-based inference has evolved into a flexible paradigm for this purpose, circumventing the computational intractability of the likelihood. Notably, approximate Bayesian computation performs this inference by carrying out extensive Gillespie simulations, usually at a high computational cost. Here, we propose a simulation-free approximate Bayesian computation (SFABC) framework that avoids both simulation and explicit likelihood solutions of the network dynamics. Instead, SFABC exploits the Chemical Master Equation to formulate a tractable convex optimization with ensuing constraints, which are then used to accept sampled parameters consistent with the observed data. The resulting posterior approximation comes with theoretical guarantees: it can be tightened systematically, and it provably converges to the exact Bayesian posterior distributions. Using synthetic benchmarks, we show that SFABC matches the accuracy of standard simulation-based algorithms at a substantially reduced computational cost. We then showcase the applicability of SFABC to experimental systems biology by analyzing gene transcription bursting kinetics from snapshot, time-resolved, and cell-cycle-resolved single-cell data.

title: PhyPro-FM: A Physics and Prompt-Guided Graph Foundation Model for Contingency Analysis
abstract: The continuous evolution of next-generation power systems, characterized by the high penetration of renewable energy resources and dynamic topology variations, poses formidable challenges to traditional N-1/N-2 contingency analysis in terms of computational efficiency and scalability. While deep learning-based methods offer accelerated inference, existing studies predominantly treat contingency analysis as a pure regression problem, often overlooking the physical essence of grid operation and engineering requirements of real-world scenarios. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a physics and prompt-guided graph foundation model (PhyPro-FM) for generalizable and engineering-viable contingency analysis. The proposed architecture integrates graph neural networks with a learnable global query mechanism and, notably, introduces a prompt-guided learning paradigm. By leveraging historical snapshots as few-shot prompts, the model dynamically captures correlations between target and historical operating conditions, significantly enhancing generalization capabilities under unseen topologies. Furthermore, we design a physics-informed training mechanism that prioritizes branch power flow errors over nodal voltage errors, aligning the optimization objective with critical grid security constraints. To ensure engineering applicability, a physics-informed inference mechanism is also developed, incorporating a residual-based correction module and a specialized post-processing strategy for singular branches to circumvent numerical instability. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that PhyPro-FM outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy and generalization, validating its superior physical consistency and robustness for practical engineering applications.
authors: Xu Yang;Zhanyuan Sheng;Chenhui Lin;Haotian Liu;Qi Wang;Yue Yang;Wenchuan Wu

title: Affective Valence as the Interoceptive Rate of Change of Jacobian Scale
abstract: Affect is widely held to depend on interoception. This paper proposes that valence is the rate at which interoception moves a self-sustaining system's responsiveness relative to its terminal set (roughly, death). Responsiveness is formalised as the scale of the system's Jacobian and interoception as its internal inputs: receptors, signals and forecasts of its energy reserve. Changes in responsiveness that bypass interoception, such as brain damage, are not felt. Language models have no valence because they are not self-sustaining. The chain rule splits valence over the system's parts and the causes that affect its internal inputs. With the log scale, these splits account for need-dependent pleasure, diffuse hunger and localised pain, negativity bias, and relief when a threat fails to arrive. In a minimal model of a body: (1) Blocking the reserve signal leaves depletion unfelt, and driving it produces hunger with an undepleted reserve. (2) Removing receptors or their gain, or driving receptors, reproduces congenital insensitivity to pain, asymbolia and phantom pain. (3) A receptor gain learned to sustain the body signals local damage to the whole body, so an injury hurts in proportion to its cost. (4) If the reserve also modulates the gain, the body learns to suppress pain due to receptors as energy runs low. (5) When it learns to maximise its own scale, it becomes a wirehead. The account explains when changes are felt, where they are felt, and when feelings mislead.

title: Investigating relative population partitioning in the presence of B$^-_\text{C}$ defects in diamond
abstract: Leveraging our earlier formalism for charge-state decay [see R. Kuate Defo et al., 108 235208 (2023)], we investigate relative population partitioning in the presence of singly negatively charged substitutional boron impurities (B$^-_{\rm C}$) in diamond samples, where these diamond samples also contain substitutional nitrogen (N$_{\rm C }$) impurities and have ether-terminated surfaces. Effectively, given any two defects, one donor and one acceptor, such that their charge-transition levels, their relative populations, and the temperature are known, the timescale for charge transfer between the two defects is completely determined. We use this insight and experimental measurements for the timescale for charge transfer between NV$^-$ centers and N$_{\rm C}$ hybridized with the ether-terminated surface of diamond, as well as the temperature and the relative populations for the NV$^-$ centers, [see Z. Yuan et al., Phys. Rev. Res. 2, 033263 (2020)] to argue that an additional defect must be modulating the relative populations of N$_{\rm C}$ hybridized with the ether-terminated surface of diamond. The shifts in the local Fermi level for N$_{\rm C}$ hybridized with the ether-terminated surface of diamond are consistent with the additional defect being a substitutional boron impurity (B$_{\rm C}$). Ultimately, our results allow for the determination of local relative concentrations of ionized defects.

title: Beyond Observability: Sharp Sample Bounds for Minimax State Reconstruction
abstract: We study how many output samples match the worst-case state reconstruction error obtainable from a continuous history under bounded measurement noise. For observable scalar-output linear time-varying systems with $n$ states, $n$ samples suffice for exact reconstruction, whereas at most $n^2$ attain the continuous-history minimax error in the $\ell_\infty$ norm. An explicit construction proves sharpness even for real-analytic systems. For time-invariant systems, strict total positivity yields one $n$-sample schedule optimal for every state coordinate; endpoint-observed tridiagonal cooperative chains satisfy this conclusion in physical coordinates. Interior sensing behaves differently: an explicit three-state family requires four samples despite positivity and distinct real eigenvalues. The strict three-state gap persists under small stabilizing damping. A nilpotent four-state example and an interval proof for a six-state mechanical system give gaps. The results identify how temporal sampling and the prescribed state-error geometry determine the measurements required for minimax reconstruction. Time-domain experiments illustrate the resulting estimation bounds.
comment: Submitted to the International Journal of Control. 6 figures

title: Reassessing Clean Power 2030 Pathway Using Real Time Records
abstract: The National Energy System Operator (NESO) Clean Power 2030 advice to the government, accepted as United Kingdom (UK) government policy in December 2024, outlines a rapid increase in wind and solar generation capacities with the associated infrastructure by 2030, with the objective of reducing carbon dioxide emissions from the UK electricity system to 5.2 million tons per annum. Our previous paper used real-time records from 2017 to analyze Clean Power 2030 proposal. This paper extends the previous assessment, using real time records of 2017, 2018 and 2019 to test the resilience of the UK energy system under more diverse weather patterns. Two different modelling methods predict that the 2030 carbon dioxide emissions will be five times greater than Clean Power 2030 prediction. Furthermore, the projections show that, due to increased curtailment, only about half of NESO proposed increases in wind and solar capacities will be economically justified. NESO also advised the government that 35GW of unabated gas-fired generation would maintain security of supply, whereas our models suggest that at least 42 GW will be required during winter wind lulls. Recent events, such as grid stability problems in 2026, also discussed in the paper, validate our estimated and suggest the risk of blackouts in the UK is increasing.

title: Heat-current-induced nonreciprocal phonon damping
abstract: Time-reversal symmetry enforces equal equilibrium linewidths for time-reversed phonon modes at opposite wave vectors. Here we show that a steady heat current can produce nonreciprocal anharmonic damping even in centrosymmetric nonmagnetic crystals. The effect arises from nonequilibrium occupations of scattering partners, which change the statistical weights of time-reversed three-phonon channels while their squared matrix elements remain equal. Within the single-mode relaxation-time approximation, we derive a linewidth correction that is linear in the temperature gradient and odd under wave-vector reversal. The response depends on scattering-partner velocities and equilibrium lifetimes and retains signed channel weights absent from the equilibrium linewidth. First-principles calculations for centrosymmetric MgO and diamond yield nonzero, mode-dependent linewidth corrections at selected finite wave vectors, demonstrating the mechanism in both ionic and covalent crystals. Reversing the heat current at fixed local temperature exchanges the broadening and narrowing of paired modes. This current-reversible linewidth contrast provides a spectral signature of occupation feedback, with potential implications for nonlinear phonon transport.

title: The Central Molecular Zone of our Galaxy, a chemical complexity factory: first interstellar detections of molecules towards G+0.693
abstract: The Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) of our Galaxy is a prime laboratory for interstellar chemistry because of its extreme conditions, such as shocks and high cosmic-ray ionisation rates. It is an efficient factory of molecules, with many species first discovered in CMZ sources. This document reviews key results from the study of the CMZ G+0.693-0.027 molecular cloud. Using ultra-sensitive broadband spectral surveys together with laboratory spectroscopy, more than 140 molecules have been identified, including 28 detected for the first time in the interstellar medium (ISM). These discoveries include prebiotic precursors of biomolecules, increasingly complex members of known molecular families, molecules containing periodic third-row elements (S, P, Na, Mg), high-energy stereo- and structural isomers, and new cations. Overall, these findings extend the known limits of interstellar chemical complexity and highlight the CMZ's potential to provide the molecular ingredients for prebiotic chemistry.
comment: Part of "Traversing the Galactic Center in Space and Time Proceedings IAU Symposium No. 405", M. Zajaček, T. Jerábková, V. Karas, R. Schödel & P. Suková, eds

title: La14.33(CN3)8N, a Nitridocarbonate based on the (CN3)5- Ion
abstract: Metal nitridocarbonates containing the (NCN)2- ion are established for a multitude of metal atoms throughout the periodic table. The preparation of nitridocarbonate compounds containing a (CN3)5-, (C2N4)6-, or (C3N6)6- ion remains challenging, although corresponding species have been established. The new compound La14.33(CN3)8N was synthesized in a conventional solid-state metathesis reaction from a mixture of LaF3, Na2(CN2) and Li3N in an open system at 550 °C. The reaction conditions, including the formation and de-composition of La14.33(CN3)8N are analyzed on basis of thermoanalytic studies. The crystal structure of La14.33(CN3)8N was refined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, and the mid-IR frequencies resulting from two crystallographically distinct (CN3)5- ions in the structure are reported. 23Na, 7Li and 13C NMR studies provide additional support for the identity of the compound. The crystal structure of La14.33(CN3)8N is isotypic to that of Ce15(BN3)8N.
authors: Markus Ströbele;Mykhailo Brytskyi;Carl P. Romao;Scott Kroeker;Hans-Jürgen Meyer

title: PyGPLA: A Python Package for Generalized Phase Locking Analysis
abstract: Spike-field couplings measure the links between neuronal spiking and local field potential (LFP) and provide a tool to study how neural populations coordinate activity across spatial and temporal scales. While modern high-density electrophysiology enables the simultaneous recording of numerous LFP channels and neuronal units, this massive scale poses significant statistical and computational challenges for conventional pairwise coupling analyses. The number of channel-unit comparisons grows rapidly, and a coherent population-level structure can be obscured by high-dimensional coupling matrices. Generalized Phase Locking Analysis (GPLA) addresses this challenge by organizing spike-triggered LFP phase information into a complex coupling matrix and extracting dominant low-rank modes. These modes summarize whether a population is coupled to the field, which channels and units contribute to the coupling, and how their relative phases are organized. Here, we present PyGPLA, an open-source Python package implementing GPLA for high-density electrophysiological recordings. Designed for straightforward integration into existing neural data analysis pipelines, PyGPLA supports multivariate spike-LFP coupling analysis, from coupling estimation and interpretation to significance assessment using analytical and surrogate-based tests.

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Discovery of Carbon-Related Defect Formation Mechanisms in Diamond
abstract: Diamond is an important host material for functional defects such as solid-state spin qubits. During the defect creation by irradiation and subsequent thermal annealing, carbon-related defects, including vacancies and interstitials, are generated and can migrate to form new defect complexes. To investigate this kinetically driven process and reveal the formation mechanisms of the di-interstitials and di-vacancies in the neutral charge state, we fine-tuned a universal machine learning interatomic potential using a small dataset generated from density functional theory calculations. We obtained a barrier of 1.84 eV for mono-interstitial migration and found that two initially separated mono-interstitials only need to overcome a lower barrier to form di-interstitial configurations. Beyond the training data, the MLIP also identified the formation pathway for an additional di-interstitial configuration and a stepwise divacancy dissociation mechanism. These results reveal migration-assisted defect complex formation mechanisms and demonstrate how targeted MLIP training can identify reaction pathways.

title: Deep-$π^*$: A Neural Network Estimate of Trend Inflation
abstract: Most empirical models of trend inflation treat it as a latent random walk driven by unobserved shocks, so they cannot say which economic conditions move it. Deep-$π^*$ makes the innovations to the trend a possibly nonlinear function of a large number of macroeconomic indicators, estimated with neural networks, so that Shapley values can be used to attribute every movement of the trend to the indicators behind it. Two complementary loss functions define a current trend, which fits inflation today, and a forward-looking trend, which best predicts inflation over the next year. In US data, employment-related variables were the largest contributors to the post-pandemic rise of the current trend. However, the forward-looking trend rose earlier, with real activity, employment, and money and credit as the main drivers, and peaked eight to twelve months before the current trend. Both trends looked through most of the movements in energy and commodity prices. The contributions of the indicators are nonlinear, with sizeable interactions between them. Re-estimated every month during the surge, the model forecast inflation more accurately than the standard UC-SV model and a random walk, and in early 2021, when professional forecasters expected inflation of 3% or less, the forward-looking trend was already signalling an increase in persistent inflation.
comment: 75 pages, 16 figures, 20 tables. The views expressed are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect those of the ECB or the Eurosystem

title: Mobile Embodied Agent Network (MEAN): Integrated Framework, Enabling Technologies, and Task-Driven Deployment
abstract: Mobile networks are evolving from human-centered, data-oriented communication infrastructures toward machine- and/or agent-dominant, task-oriented platforms that are to serve the rapidly increasing networked machines and embodied agents. In order to fulfill the newly arose complex task objectives, the framework of future mobile network is to be innovated to reflect and facilitate the intrinsic interplay and integration of the underlying processes of perception, communication, computation, decision, action, and feedback, etc. This survey establishes the mobile embodied agent network (MEAN) as a task-oriented networking paradigm in which networking and distributed intelligence are jointly organized around closed-loop embodied task execution. We first establish a unified MEAN framework that explains how network resources and intelligent functions jointly support embodied task execution, and extend its performance indicators from conventional communication metrics to embodied task outcomes and cross-layer system effects. With this framework, we analyze three complementary enabling mechanisms that form a cognition-interaction-adaption loop. Large artificial intelligence (AI) models provide high-level cognition, token communication connects this cognition with distributed agents through shared semantic representations, and reinforcement learning closes the loop by adapting system operation to network, task, and physical feedback. We further investigate the bidirectional interplay between MEAN and emerging technologies, showing how they mutually extend system capabilities and reshape task-oriented network design. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future research directions toward the practical realization of MEAN over real joint communication and computation platform.
authors: Zhaoyang Zhang;Lingxiao Sun;Weijie Zhou;Chunhui Feng;Zhaohui Yang;Xuan Cheng;Tianyi Qin;Zhixian Kong;Baoping Cheng;Zijian Wu;Jingze Che

title: Hidden piezo-Hall effect
abstract: Extensive studies of hidden spin polarization have established a broad class of hidden phenomena in quantum materials. Here, we introduce the hidden piezo-Hall effect, in which strain induces finite anomalous Hall conductivities (AHCs) in individual sectors while the global AHC remains zero. At zero strain, neither the full system nor its sectors exhibit an anomalous Hall effect (AHE). Under uniaxial strain, however, opposite sector AHCs emerge while their sum remains canceled. We establish this effect for a $d$-wave hidden altermagnet using a tight-binding model and first-principles calculations for the experimentally synthesized material $\mathrm{RbV_2Te_2O}$. Rotating the strain direction from the $x$ to the $y$ axis reverses the signs of the sector AHCs without generating a net Hall response. The same symmetry mechanism may also give rise to hidden piezomagneto-optical, piezo-thermal Hall, piezo-Nernst, and piezo-Ettingshausen effects. Our work extends hidden physics to strain-controlled transport and identifies $\mathrm{RbV_2Te_2O}$ as a promising candidate for experimental verification.

title: Learning SOCP Solver Dynamics with Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Second-order cone programs (SOCPs) are a fundamental class of convex optimization problems widely applied across engineering domains. Classical interior-point methods are robust and accurate, but their iterative nature can be costly in real-time or repeated-solve settings. This has motivated learning-based solvers that approximate optimizer solutions with neural networks. Recent work has increasingly studied graph neural networks (GNNs) for linear, quadratic, and second-order cone optimization, leveraging their ability to model sparse relational structure among variables, constraints, and objective functions. Most existing GNN-based solvers compress the optimization process into a single forward pass, predicting the optimizer directly without using the intermediate trajectory produced by classical solvers. We introduce SOCPNet, a recursive GNN framework that uses solver trajectories to learn an iterative SOCP solution procedure. A shared GNN model is applied repeatedly, refining the current iterate at each step and enabling inference for a variable number of iterations. Rather than predicting the solution in a single pass, SOCPNet learns from intermediate iterates to progressively refine its estimates using a trajectory-regularized training procedure. We evaluate SOCPNet on multiple datasets spanning standard SOCP problem classes and show that it consistently reduces the final solution error relative to a SOCP-GNN baseline. Finally, we demonstrate how trained SOCPNet models can be used in a hybrid optimization pipeline by warm-starting a classical interior-point solver, reducing solver iterations without loss of accuracy.
authors: Adam Ghalem;Lou Salaün;Davide Rinaldi;Fragkiskos D. Malliaros

title: Optimizing Airport Electric Ground Support Fleets with Digital-Twin-Guided Predictive Control
abstract: Electrifying airport ground operations is a key step toward reducing aviation-related emissions, but it makes task assignment and charging coordination strongly coupled in real time. This paper develops a digital twin of airport ground handling operations for electric ground-support vehicles (EGSVs), combining an agent-based model of airport operations with live flight-schedule updates and vehicle-energy dynamics. On this platform, we compare three control strategies for EGSV dispatching and charging: a rule-based heuristic, a rolling-horizon model predictive controller (MPC), and a Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) controller. The controllers are evaluated on three representative Schiphol Airport operating days and for multiple fleet sizes. The results show a clear trade-off between delays and energy use. Across all tested scenarios, MCTS yields the lowest average flight delay, with a pooled delay of 4.09 min, improving on the heuristic and MPC controllers by 64.7\% and 31.5\%, but at an increased energy consumption of 1\% and 0.3\%, respectively.The MPC and MCTS controllers coordinate charging more effectively throughout the day and reduce the peak charging infrastructure required by 6.0 and 4.7 charger units, respectively. Additionally, we find more vehicles can result in lower overall energy consumption and lower charging infrastructure requirements for all controllers. These findings highlight the value of digital twins not only as offline design evaluation tools, but also as practical environments for real-time control policies in electrified airport operations.

title: Fast Reassessment of Prolonged Electricity Shortages under Shared Fuel Interruptions
abstract: When several generators share a fuel supply, one interruption can disable them together and cause electricity shortages lasting days. Such interruptions can be made less frequent, for example by weatherizing gas supply, or shorter, for example by on-site backup fuel. Yet traditional resource adequacy indices, expected unserved energy and loss-of-load hours, fail to distinguish such measures whenever they remove the same expected time without fuel, because for interruptions independent of system conditions these indices depend on the interruptions only through this time. Their difference is revealed by prolonged-shortage exposure, the expected annual hours in shortages of at least a given duration, whose exact chronological calculation must be repeated for every interruption scenario. To reduce this cost, a fast reassessment method with guaranteed accuracy is proposed. Network calculations are performed once and condensed into a restoration response, the additional prolonged-shortage hours caused by one interruption of each duration, from which any scenario is evaluated as a weighted sum without new simulation. An hour-by-hour error bound determines whether this evaluation is accurate enough, and exact dynamic programming is applied otherwise, so that every result lies within a requested tolerance of the exact value on the same Monte Carlo samples. On the Reliability Test System of the Grid Modernization Laboratory Consortium, most evaluations were accepted, fully accepted scenarios typically ran more than 200 times faster than exact calculation, and total computation time decreased in every workload. Measures against fuel interruptions can thus be screened quickly and accurately by their effect on prolonged shortages.
comment: 11 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Reliability. Code and data: https://github.com/DoganUrgun/Fast_Reassessment_Prolonged_Shortages

title: Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz-based convergence analysis with approximate weakly convex subdifferentials: bundle, quadratic penalty, and moving balls approximation methods
abstract: The Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz (KL) property has been widely used for establishing global sequential convergence and analyzing local convergence rate of optimization algorithms. Most existing analysis frameworks rely on the construction of a suitable KL potential function such that along the sequence generated, it admits sufficient descents and its exact subdifferentials are suitably controlled by successive changes of the iterates. Nevertheless, a handful of important algorithms, such as bundle methods and quadratic penalty methods, are not known to have potential functions verifying the aforementioned properties, rendering their convergence analysis out of the reach of existing KL-based convergence analysis template. In this paper, we develop a new convergence analysis framework to extend the applicability of KL-based analysis. Our framework is built on a weakly convex KL potential function $ψ$. It allows approximate sufficient descents, the use of diminishing stepsizes, and controls on enlarged subdifferentials of $ψ$ known as the $\varrho$-weakly-convex-$\varepsilon$-subdifferentials. We illustrate the usefulness of our framework by establishing the global sequential convergence and analyzing the local convergence rate of some recent variants of bundle method, quadratic penalty method and moving balls approximation method. Specifically, we show that these methods fall under our framework by presenting explicit and natural choices of $ψ$, and derive suitable choices of model parameters, penalty parameters and constraint shrinkage parameters, respectively, for establishing their global sequential convergence and local convergence rate based on the KL property and exponent of $ψ$.

title: Causal Robustness from Synthetic Environments
abstract: We study robust prediction when the training data come from a single observational distribution. Causality-oriented methods for robust prediction usually use heterogeneity across observed environments both to learn an invariant prediction function and to determine the perturbations against which it is robust. We show that both can be recovered from one distribution under a structural additive-noise mechanism for the response. Under the structural model considered here, the causal prediction function has constant conditional mean squared error given its prediction. We generate synthetic environments by reweighting the covariate distribution along the prediction and use a Cramér--von Mises criterion to measure departures from this invariance. The resulting penalised risk admits a regularised worst-case representation, linking the criterion to robustness against covariate shifts induced by reweighting observations according to their predicted values. Under an additional orthogonality condition, we identify the causal prediction function as the unique risk minimiser subject to this invariance restriction. We establish consistency and an explicit rate, derive a goodness-of-fit test for the invariance restriction, and characterise the population target under misspecification. With multiple observed environments, the construction applies environment by environment and can be combined with Distributional Robustness via Invariant Gradients (DRIG) to control two complementary classes of shifts.

title: The resource cost of cooperative invasion
abstract: A contact network can favor cooperation by sheltering a lineage until its descendants compete with defectors as a group. We determine the contact strengths, invasion times and measurement effort needed to realize this advantage at fixed population size. Individuals reproduce according to averaged cooperation payoffs, and offspring replace neighbors through contacts of equal weight in both directions. Contact contrast is the ratio of strongest to weakest contact. Under weak selection on a six-site path, the least contrast needed to favor a single cooperator over the reverse invasion by a defector grows as $656ε^{-2}$ for uniformly placed mutants and $4050ε^{-3}$ for mutations in newborn offspring, as the benefit-cost ratio $b/c=1+ε$ approaches one. The extra power arises because rare replacement protects a site while suppressing mutation arrival there. Global bounds force two weakly coupled groups and exact mirror symmetry of the least-contrast contacts for sufficiently small $ε$. Under uniform introduction, additional contrast shortens the leading mean time to extinction or fixation in the absence of selection, from $12/ε$ toward $6/ε$ reproduction attempts, and eventually breaks the mirror symmetry of the fastest design. Estimating the uniform-introduction advantage from fixation outcomes of independent completed invasions defines a third optimum. Within the six-site family with mirror-symmetric, strongly separated contacts, we optimize contacts and selection strength with reproduction weighted linearly or exponentially by payoff. At fixed relative precision, with contrast a fixed factor above its minimum, the leading summed trial duration grows as $ε^{-3}$. Efficient measurement accepts a smaller advantage in exchange for shorter trials. The cheapest, fastest and most efficiently measured networks therefore differ.

title: Who Breathes the Detour? A Coupled Traffic-Emission-Dispersion-Exposure Pipeline
abstract: Road traffic is among the largest sources of health-damaging air pollution in inhabited areas. Direct measurement of resident exposure at the scale of an entire corridor remains costly, and existing simulation approaches often target either high-fidelity local snapshots or regional averages, leaving the corridor scale underserved. We present a coupled, end-to-end pipeline that links four stages: (i) microscopic traffic simulation with SUMO, (ii) per-vehicle emissions from the HBEFA4 model, (iii) deterministic three-dimensional Eulerian diffusion solved with an implicit finite-difference scheme on a geometric vertical grid, and (iv) resident-level exposure expressed as an air quality index over a synthetic population. The design deliberately trades the fidelity of full CFD dispersion for a workflow that runs end-to-end for the residential areas of several settlements on a single laptop, and the complete implementation is released open source. We showcase the pipeline at the example of the Swiss Gotthard transit corridor, covering the residential areas of six villages, two days, four scenarios, and three pollutants, to enable assessment of congestion mitigation measures. Code & Material: https://github.com/cedriczeiter/zeiter_coupled_pipeline.

title: Sidewall Metrology Protocol for Superconducting Qubit Devices
abstract: Sidewall morphology is a potentially important factor influencing superconducting qubit performance, yet its quantitative characterization remains challenging due to the absence of standardized measurement protocols. In this work, we develop a scanning probe microscopy-based measurement framework for the quantitative characterization of superconducting qubit sidewalls. The framework introduces a refined root mean square lateral sidewall roughness descriptor and a new curvature-equivalent radius for quantifying vertical sidewall morphology. The descriptors and measurement procedures are applied to different components of qubit devices, forming the basis of a proposed sidewall characterization protocol. This provides a foundation for quantitative comparisons of fabrication processes across laboratories, enabling future investigations of correlations between sidewall geometry and qubit performance.
authors: Jørgen Garnæs;Henrik S. Guttesen;Astrid T. Rømer;Oscar Danielsson;Emily P. Duggan;Zhenhai Sun;Asen Lyubenov Georgiev;Li Wei Chang;Morten Kjaergaard;Mark Bieler;Lukas Grünhaupt;Sabbir A. Khan

title: Flux-Based Time Bounds for Harmonically Degenerate Quantum Systems
abstract: We study transfer-time estimates for finite-dimensional bilinear quantum control systems driven by an unbounded scalar control, in both the state-to-state setting (complex projective space) and the unitary synthesis setting (special unitary group). Lower bounds are recalled and refined via spectral and chordal methods. The main contribution is constructive upper bounds: we associate with the system a coupling graph whose edges correspond to non-resonant drift couplings, and construct transfer protocols along spanning trees. In contrast with earlier results requiring full rational independence of the spectrum of the control operator, our estimates allow rational resonances; they incorporate, via explicit correction factors derived from the arithmetic of the spectral gaps, the efficiency of the averaging procedure and of the phase adjustments. As an application, we consider finite-dimensional truncations of the planar quantum rotator under a dipolar electric field, and show that the transfer time between any two modes tends to zero as the truncation dimension grows.
affiliations: IRMA,UNISTRA

title: Hybrid metaheuristics for architectural design optimization under small evaluation and wall-clock budgets
abstract: Architectural and structural design optimization in parametric software affords about a thousand evaluations of an expensive model for problems with tens of variables, a regime for which most metaheuristics were not designed. On the side of artificial intelligence, two hybrid metaheuristics are proposed: a covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES) whose sampling is enriched with differential-evolution trial vectors, and a particle swarm with success-history parameter adaptation, differential-evolution injection and local refinement. A budget-aware delay of population-size reduction in adaptive differential evolution is also proposed. Under a hard cap of 1,200 evaluations, all counted, the CMA-ES hybrid ranks first on seven shifted and rotated functions at 10 and 30 variables and beats CMA-ES on six of seven functions at 30 variables. Ablations attribute this gain to the injection and show that a local search pays off only when its result re-enters the population. The delayed schedule improves three adaptive differential-evolution variants in 40 of 51 comparisons, with no loss. On the side of engineering application, in Grasshopper the CMA-ES hybrid and plain CMA-ES are never significantly worse than the optimizers of Galapagos, SilverEye, Opossum and Tunny on travelling-salesman instances and on a built 85-variable free-form shell, where they end 48 % below the best external tool in 15 minutes. On a 22-variable building-performance problem with binary choices, differential evolution leads instead. Shifting and rotating the functions reverses the rank of Harris hawks optimization. Solvers should therefore be selected by problem structure and stopping time, not by a single ranking.

title: A general condition for fast rates in multi-group learning
abstract: In multi-group learning, a single predictor must control its excess risk simultaneously over overlapping groups. Tosh and Hsu (2022) obtained $1/\sqrt{n}$ slow rates via a reduction to online learning with sleeping experts, and $1/n$ rates only under realizability (and for a different strategy). We identify a group-wise Bernstein condition under which the same adaptive predictor attains the fast rate $1/n$ without knowing whether the condition holds, while retaining the slow rates on the groups where it fails. The condition is implied by some natural assumptions weaker than realizability. Lower bounds show that weakened versions leave every learner with slow rates. Intermediate rates under relaxed conditions and an extension to VC classes are also obtained.

title: Robust Latent Variable Graphical Models: Exact Recovery and Fundamental Limits
abstract: We study robust estimation of a Gaussian precision matrix that decomposes as a sparse matrix minus a symmetric, possibly indefinite, low-rank matrix, a structure that arises when latent-variable marginalization is combined with conditioning on linear measurements. The proposed convex estimator replaces the sample covariance by the centered Gaussian measure-transformed (MT) covariance, which preserves the signed graph of the sparse component under the nominal model, and penalizes the low-rank component by the nuclear norm of a congruence transform, an atomic norm that encodes structural side information. Our main result is a primal--dual witness theorem: under restricted invertibility and irrepresentability conditions on the Fisher information, the raw convex optimizer is unique, has no false edges, recovers the signs of all sufficiently strong edges, and has exactly the true rank and inertia. These conditions reduce to the graphical-lasso conditions when the low-rank part is absent, and we verify them from primitive incoherence and near-isotropy assumptions. Over a class on which they hold uniformly, we prove information-theoretic limits for Frobenius estimation, signed graph recovery, and inertia recovery. In particular, inertia recovery requires $N\gtrsim p/ν_{\min}^2$ samples, where $ν_{\min}$ is the smallest nonzero eigenvalue modulus of the low-rank part; the spectral beta-min condition of the witness theorem is necessary up to a $\sqrt{\log p}$ factor; and the Frobenius risk attains the minimax rate up to a factor $\sqrt{μ(1+\min\{d,r\})\log p}$, where $μ$ is the incoherence parameter, $d$ the maximal degree, and $r$ the rank. We further quantify robustness under Huber contamination, with a bias bound that is sharp for the MT functional and vanishes for remote outliers, and give a globally convergent linearized ADMM with closed-form updates.

title: Competitive roles of turbulence and magnetic field on the formation of unipolar outflows in isolated molecular cloud cores
abstract: We investigate the impact of turbulence and magnetic field on the formation of unipolar outflows in the gravitational collapse of isolated low-mass cloud cores using three-dimensional non-ideal magnetohydrodynamics simulations. In the models explored in this study, we find that unipolar outflows are formed in cloud cores with the super-Alfvénic turbulence of $M_{\rm{A}}>1$, where $M_{\rm{A}}$ is the Alfvén Mach number of the initial cloud core. In contrast, bipolar outflows are formed in cloud cores with $M_{\rm{A}}\lesssim1$. Our results suggest that the relative strength of the turbulence to the magnetic field in the initial cloud core plays a key role in the formation of unipolar outflows. We also find that no outflow is formed in cloud cores with the strong magnetic field of the dimensionless mass-to-flux ratio $μ=2$. The outflow morphologies can be used as tracers to indirectly estimate the relative strengths of the turbulence and magnetic field of the parent cloud cores.
authors: Daisuke Takaishi;Yusuke Tsukamoto;Miyu Kido;Shigehisa Takakuwa;Yoshiaki Misugi;Yuki Kudoh;Yasushi Suto

title: Effect of galaxy mergers on dust masses
abstract: Dust mass (M$_{Dust}$) is one of the key physical properties of galaxies that track the cold interstellar medium. However, the M$_{Dust}$ in merging galaxies is poorly understood. We aim to derive how the cold dust mass of galaxies is affected by major mergers at low redshifts. M$_{Dust}$ was estimated for approximately 500 major mergers in the North Ecliptic Pole extragalactic field using spectral energy distribution fitting runs with CIGALE, with different dust attenuation and emission models. We also analysed over 12 000 mergers from the SIMBA simulation using its M$_{Dust}$. We matched merging and non-merging systems in stellar mass, redshift, and local density, to enable a comparison of M$_{Dust}$. We then performed a second comparison using a control sample also matched in SFR. AGN host galaxies were then removed, and this matching repeated. Observed mergers have larger M$_{Dust}$ than the non-mergers by up to a factor of 1.82$\pm$0.35, or 1.60$\pm$0.44 without AGN-hosts. When matched by SFR, observed mergers show no significant change in M$_{Dust}$, both when including and excluding AGN-hosts. SIMBA galaxies show similar trends when AGN-hosts are included but there is still an increase in M$_{Dust}$ when matched by SFR. When AGN-hosts are excluded, the SIMBA mergers show smaller M$_{Dust}$ by a factor of 0.98$\pm$0.03, or 0.97$\pm$0.02 when matched in SFR. The higher the mass of a merger, the greater M$_{Dust}$ increase for observations for two of the CIGALE runs, or the smaller the decrease for SIMBA. Observed mergers are typically more dusty than their non-merging counterparts but only because they typically have higher SFRs, regardless of whether they host AGN or not. SIMBA mergers follow observations when AGN hosts are included, but show reduced M$_{Dust}$ when AGN hosts are removed. M$_{Dust}$ in SIMBA is linked to AGN in a way not seen in observations.
authors: W. J. Pearson;M. Romano;K. Małek;D. Donevski;K. Lisiecki;A. P. Cotter;S. Dey;T. Goto;S. C. -C. Ho;D. J. Santos

title: Nanowire-Assisted Epitaxial Lateral Overgrowth of Planar GaN(0001) on Diamond(100)
abstract: GaN-on-diamond heterostructures are promising for high-power and high-frequency electronics, however, direct epi- taxial growth on diamond (100) remains challenging due to severe lattice and thermal mismatches, which induce high threading dislocation densities. To overcome this challenge, we have used Plasma Assisted Molecular Beam Epitaxy (PAMBE) to grow wurtzite GaN layers on diamond(100) substrates using nanowire-assisted epitaxial lateral overgrowth (ELOG). Two nanowire templates (NW100, NW600) were benchmarked against a nanowire-free reference (NW000). High-resolution XRD, φ -scans, (0002) pole figures, and reciprocal space mapping show that NW100 attains the lowest dislocation density (5.51 x 10-4 nm-2) and microstrain (2.736 x 10-3), the narrowest (0002) reflection, and a c-axis lattice parameter (5.1821 Å) within 0.06% of the bulk value; NW000, in contrast, exhibits a contracted c-axis (5.1633 Å) and elevated dislocation density (6.26 x 10-4 nm-2), consistent with residual tensile stress. Cross-sectional TEM con- firms the intended diamond/AlN/nanowire/ELOG/planar-GaN layer sequence and shows threading dislocations bending into near-lateral trajectories, directly evidencing defect filtering by the nanowire template. Together, these results estab- lish nanowire-assisted ELOG as an effective strategy to suppress dislocation propagation and recover near-bulk lattice parameters in GaN-on-diamond heteroepitaxy, providing a structurally well-defined platform for device integration.
authors: Brijmohan Paramanik;Mayur Shinde;Subhranshu Sekhar Sahu;Soumyadip Chatterjee;Prajwal Pandey;Anshul Jain;Himanjal Bhattacharyya;Alpesh Donga;Apurba Laha

title: The Douglas--Rachford algorithm for normal cones converges only weakly
abstract: We show that the Douglas--Rachford algorithm applied to two normal cone operators associated with closed convex sets can fail to converge strongly, even when one set is a closed vector subspace, the other is a closed convex cone, and their intersection is a singleton.

title: Structural conditions on trust-region radius updates. Part II: second-order convergence and asymptotic radius behaviour
abstract: Continuing Part I (arXiv:2606.30202), we ask not which structural conditions on $\{Δ_k\}$ suffice for global convergence but what the radius does; the answers separate the mechanisms by whether the radius is tied to a criticality measure. We identify three asymptotic regimes: the criticality-anchored rules give $\sum_k Δ_k^2/M_k < +\infty$, hence $\liminf_k Δ_k = 0$, and $Δ_k \to 0$ once the model Hessians are bounded; the step-driven rules inherit the summability of the step series, hence $\sum_k Δ_k < +\infty$; the fixed-factor rules keep $Δ_k$ bounded away from zero. Near a critical point with positive definite Hessian, convergence of a subsequence forces convergence of the full sequence. We then extend the framework to second-order criticality through $τ_k = \max\{\|g_k\|, -λ_k^-\}$, obtaining convergence to second-order critical points with the worst-case complexity $\mathcal{O}(\max\{\varepsilon_g^{-2}\varepsilon_H^{-1}, \varepsilon_H^{-3}\})$, which reduces to $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ for a common tolerance and is sharp for quadratic models. Finally we establish eventual inactivity of the constraint and superlinear convergence, isolating the two properties of the radius rule through which the mechanism enters; the rate itself is mechanism-independent. The criticality-anchored and capped gradient-scaled rules reach inactivity only under a side condition, $ζ> \overlineκ$ or $\overlineμ > \overlineκ$, with $\overlineκ$ a constant of the solution that cannot be checked in advance. These conditions are necessary, not artefacts: on $f(x) = \sin(x)/x$, $\overlineκ$ is unbounded over the minimisers, so no parameter value meets the condition at all of them. Among the rules tied to a criticality measure, only those with an unbounded multiplier escape such a constant.

title: Phonon-dominated thermal conductivity of a superconducting amorphous MoSi thin film
abstract: We use the differential 3ω method to directly measure the temperature dependent thermal conductivity for about 90 nm Mo0.78Si0.22 thin films. The measurements are performed in a closed-cycle cryostat to access the temperature range between 50 K and 300 K. The MoSi thin films are capped with Al2O3 and probed with a Pt wire. The results show that the thermal conductivity does not satisfy the Wiedemann-Franz law. This implies that thermal transport in MoSi is not dominated by electrons but by phonon-like excitations, contrary to what is assumed in many electro-thermal models of superconducting devices. We argue that this property might be related to the weak localization visible in the resistivity as a function of temperature curves of the superconductor.
authors: Jacopo Piantanida Chiesa;Tom Q. Post;Martin P. van Exter;Michiel J. A. de Dood

title: A numerical study of radius update rules in trust-region algorithms
abstract: Part I [arXiv:2606.30202] and Part II establish which trust-region radius update mechanisms can fail and under which hypotheses they must succeed. Neither says where the thresholds sit once a rule runs with real constants, or how the rule interacts with the model Hessian and the subproblem solver. This paper turns them into nine falsifiable claims and settles what it can, on four designed problems where the theory's quantities are computable and on CUTEst, where only aggregate cost is visible. Every mechanism runs in one Julia package written for this study, so two runs differing in one component differ in nothing else. The rule is worth less than the model and more than nothing. Crossing the mechanisms with four model Hessians puts $96.5$ per cent of the variation on the model and $1.6$ on the rule, and the rules separate most under the most accurate model rather than least. Uncapped R-grad is the robust default among the criticality-anchored rules, though the retrospective rule is ahead of it on this collection. No constant escapes the side conditions. For every cap there is a minimiser at which the constraint stays active, and for every anchoring constant a flatness on which escape takes arbitrarily long. The second of these is proved here as well as measured, and the proof uses no property of the model or of the subproblem solution beyond $\|s_k\| \leq Δ_k$. The radius rule governs the length of the step, and so the cost of a run. The model decides the search direction, and with it whether the run converges at all.

title: On the Peak Estimation of Scalar Polynomial Systems via Integrability
abstract: We develop a convergent occupation measure framework for peak estimation of scalar polynomial dynamical systems with no a priori state bound. The key observation is that scalar trajectories satisfy a uniform weighted integrability bound whose exponent precisely compensates for the singularity introduced by polynomial compactification. This yields a finite measure formulation with polynomial data. We establish a superposition principle for the resulting weighted continuity equation, prove no relaxation gap and establish convergence of the associated moment-sum-of-squares hierarchy.

title: Full-horizon magnetic control of the Vlasov--Poisson system for plasma confinement
abstract: We study the full-horizon control of a two-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system through an externally imposed magnetic field. The control is represented by time-dependent coefficients associated with smooth, spatially localized basis functions, and is designed to steer selected position and velocity moments of the distribution function while limiting particle dispersion and the control effort. Starting from the kinetic constrained optimization problem, we derive the continuous first-order optimality conditions, including a backward Vlasov equation, an elliptic adjoint equation, and the variational inequality associated with bounded controls. We then project this system onto a particle--grid representation and identify the resulting particle adjoints and control gradient. The full-horizon field is then computed on a reduced particle ensemble, initialized by an instantaneous control, and subsequently applied to a larger set of particles. Numerical experiments indicate that the instantaneous control field already provides an effective baseline, while the full-horizon correction can further reduce the relative thermal energy near the boundaries and improve confinement over the prescribed time interval.

title: PSR~B0355+54: An Unexpected Compendium of Nearly All Scintillation Arc Morphologies
abstract: Scintillation arcs are sensitive probes of multipath propagation, offering a window into the distribution of scattering material in the interstellar medium. Contrary to the common observational finding that individual pulsars exhibit only a limited range of scintillation arc morphologies, we report that PSR~B0355+54, observed simultaneously at 2.25/8.60~GHz with the Shanghai Tianma Radio Telescope, displays nearly the full range of known arc patterns, many of which evolve rapidly. Across 54 observations from 2020 to 2026, we detect scintillation arcs in 53/53 usable observations at 2.25~GHz and 33/49 at 8.60~GHz. At 2.25~GHz, the secondary spectra exhibit five broad morphological types: forward arcs, inverted arclets, diffuse arcs, diffuse power, and irregular structures, with prominent displaced arclets appearing in several observations. In contrast, the 8.60-GHz spectra are generally dominated by faint forward arcs. Despite these marked morphological differences, the scaled curvatures and their annual variations agree between the two frequencies, showing that both trace the same dominant scattering screen at a fractional distance of $s=0.069^{+0.015}_{-0.014}$ near the pulsar, further supporting a possible association with the \ion{H}{ii} region Sh~2-205. Simulations show that this diversity can arise from variations in the scattered-image distribution within this screen, while brightness reconstructions at 2.25~GHz resolve localized structure down to $\sim0.02~\mathrm{mas}$. Tracking four arclets over 10~h at 8.60~GHz, including two displaced arclets, reveals a common evolutionary trend consistent with the line of sight sweeping across small-scale scattering structure, helping explain the rapid arc evolution.
authors: Zhen-Long Liao;Zhen Yan;Zhi-Qiang Shen;Rui Wang;Xun Shi;Ke-Jia Lee;Ju-Mei Yao;Xiao-Wei Wang;Zhi-Peng Huang;Kuo Liu;Yong-Hua Xu;Chu-Yuan Zhang;Fan Yang;Yang-Yang Lin
comment: 12 pages, 8 figures, accepted by the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society (MNRAS)

title: Searching for lensed gravitational waves with unlensed templates
abstract: Gravitational lensing can split the signal of a binary merger into two images, which either overlap and interfere or arrive as separate events. We show that the matched-filter output of every two-image template can be straightforwardly constructed from the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) time series that searches already compute with unlensed templates. This enables a marginalized detection statistic that increases search sensitivity without additional matched filtering and is more than 150 times faster than an explicit lensed template bank. For overlapping images in the geometric-optics regime, our two-image method recovers $\gtrsim97\%$ of the optimal SNR from point-mass and singular isothermal lenses, compared with as little as $67\%$ captured by unlensed templates, with substantial gains also for Chang-Refsdal and cored isothermal lenses. Overlapping lensed signals moreover fail the signal-consistency test that is used to down-rank noise transients. Our two-image method restores the consistency and increases the sensitive volume by roughly $2$-$4\times$ for the strongly down-ranked signals. For separated images, our method enables an efficient coherent search for pairs in which neither image is significant alone. Near fold caustics, this increases the sensitive volume by factors of 1.8-2.6 over requiring two independent detections, and up to 1.6 over a targeted counterpart search. Our method is applicable to any matched-filtering search.
authors: Digvijay Wadekar;Barak Zackay;Mark Ho-Yeuk Cheung;Tousif Islam;Javier Roulet;Ajit Kumar Mehta;Tejaswi Venumadhav;Jonathan Mushkin;Miguel Zumalacarregui;Matias Zaldarriaga

title: Solving Classes of Linear Programs with Strongly Polynomial Straight Line Complexity in Strongly Polynomial Time
abstract: Recently, Allamigeon, Dadush, Loho, Natura, and Végh (ADLNV, SICOMP 2025) introduced an interior point method for linear programs whose number of iterations is bounded by the so-called straight line complexity (SLC) of the instance. This yields a strongly polynomial bound on the number of iterations of the corresponding interior point algorithm for broad classes of linear programs. In particular, in the companion paper we give a strongly polynomial straight line complexity bound for two-variable-per-inequality linear programs. However, in order to obtain a strongly polynomial algorithm for these classes, one also needs to address two important technical issues: initialization and bit-complexity bounds. Standard IPM initialization techniques either require numerical estimates that cannot be obtained in the strongly polynomial model, or involve modifying the instance in ways that do not preserve the geometry of the original LP, potentially affecting the SLC. In this work, we present an initialization framework for interior point methods for linear programming, along with a rounding procedure that ensures the continued feasibility of the IPM. We develop a multistage scheme in which each stage can be initialized in strongly polynomial time given the output of the previous stage. Additionally, we address the challenge of controlling the bit complexity of each iterate throughout the algorithm. To this end, we show that it is possible to represent iterates as low-complexity convex combinations of vertices and extreme rays. Our combinatorial rounding step is independent of the algorithm in ADLNV 2025, and can be applied more broadly in the context of path-following methods.
