title: AgentSoV: Virtual Sensing for LLM Multi-Agent Systems via Stream of Variation
abstract: Large language model (LLM) multi-agent systems (MASs) solve complex tasks through interacting agents, yet their reliability is difficult to analyze because failures depend on both individual agents and how information and errors propagate across the system. Existing approaches largely treat this as post-hoc failure attribution, but do not provide a common model across heterogeneous MAS architectures or support broader analysis of information influence and observability. We introduce AgentSoV, a virtual-sensing framework that models MAS execution as a stochastic dynamic system through Stream of Variation (SoV). AgentSoV maps heterogeneous trajectories into diagnostic stages, constructs virtual measurements from observable outputs, and learns cross-stage variation propagation with a state-space model. Its representation is architecture-aware in stage dependencies yet architecture-agnostic in analytical language, supporting chain-structured, orchestration-based, and directed acyclic graph (DAG)-structured MASs. Without re-executing the MAS, AgentSoV supports three system-level analyses: failure attribution identifies where abnormal variation enters; stage-input influence quantifies how strongly intermediate inputs affect downstream outcomes; and virtual-sensor placement selects complementary observations under a monitoring budget. Experiments across multiple MAS architectures demonstrate a unified approach to fault localization, information influence, and observability. AgentSoV reframes agentic execution as a dynamic system to model rather than merely text to inspect, providing insights for MAS structure and component design.
authors: Congjing Zhang;Siyuan Xu;Yunfei Bai;Ke Ren;Xiaoning Qian;Shuai Huang

title: Stochastic optimization methods through statistical whitening
abstract: We provide new statistical insights into designing stochastic optimization methods. By modeling the gradient via a normal distribution, we argue that the stochastic gradient should be whitened using its covariance. We give an online method for estimating the mean and variance of the gradients based on regularized likelihood or, equivalently, through a maximum a posteriori estimate. We then show how to use structured approximations to the covariance within this same framework, which includes diagonal and Kronecker-factored approximations. The diagonal approximation results in a method that is very closely related to Adam and performs as well in practice. The Kronecker approximation results in the new MN method, which is a variant of Shampoo and KL-Shampoo. We also recover Muon by applying this same statistical framework to the gradient direction rather than the full gradient. By combining this with a whitening step, we arrive at MN-Muon, a novel preconditioned version of Muon. Our experiments on GPT-2-type models at Chinchilla scale indicate that MND, the diagonal implementation of MN, outperforms both the Distributed Shampoo and the KL-Shampoo implementations in terms of stability, final validation loss and time taken. MND-Muon, the diagonal implementation of MN-Muon, improves on Muon in 21 of 24 paired GPT-small runs and achieves a lower best validation loss on GPT-medium, where it remains stable over the six tested learning rates. However, we found that NorMuon was comparable to MND-Muon and achieved a slightly lower validation loss on GPT-medium and at GPT-small batch 512 on FineWeb.

title: HEL: A Heterogeneous Extensible Layer for GPU-Resident Runtime Orchestration
abstract: We describe a GPU-resident runtime system, HEL, built on stateful services that persist throughout the lifespan of a user application. A HEL programmer expresses a workload as an application that spawns coroutine-like tasks, which are then scheduled and run by the HEL runtime. HEL supports synchronous and asynchronous tasks, tasks with runtime dependencies, batched task submission, and automatic retries. Applications and tasks run alongside each other on the spatially partitioned GPU. Using producer-consumer and host-RPC benchmarks together with a PFPL compression case study, we show that HEL demonstrates a performance advantage for underutilized GPUs and for scenarios where HEL enables hiding task latency.
authors: Agnieszka M. Łupińska;Serban D. Porumbescu;John D. Owens

title: Multi-property Feynman-Kac Steering of Crystal Diffusion Models
abstract: Pretrained diffusion models provide powerful priors for generating new materials, including inorganic crystals, but generating useful materials requires satisfying specific chemical and physical properties, from mechanical stiffness to bandgaps. Existing approaches either retrain models for new target properties or steer only the atom coordinates and lattice during generation, leaving composition unchanged despite its fundamental role in determining physical properties. We present FK-ReMask, an inference-time, gradient-free method that steers both the continuous and discrete channels of a pretrained crystal diffusion model. During generation, FK-ReMask maintains multiple denoising trajectories and replicates promising candidates using Feynman-Kac particle selection. However, selection alone is insufficient: in the atom-type channel, committed elements cannot be revised, so cloning propagates existing compositions and limits the population's ability to explore new ones. We address this with an atom re-masking mechanism, which reopens committed sites during the generation process and allows alternative compositions to emerge. Across four electronic, photovoltaic, and mechanical objectives, our method improves the yield of SUN (stable, unique, novel) and property-on-target materials. We further demonstrate joint steering of three photovoltaic properties, showing that multiple physical objectives can be specified entirely at inference time without retraining.
authors: Oded Mousai;Sapir Esther Yiflach;Barak Itzchak Davidovitch;Yuval Mualem;Sarit Kraus;Hannah-Noa Barad;Karsten Kreis;Gal Chechik

title: Abaqus implementation of the phase-field approach to fracture
abstract: In this paper, we introduce an Abaqus user-subroutine implementation of the phase-field model of fracture initiated by Kumar, Francfort, and Lopez-Pamies (\emph{J. Mech. Phys. Solids} 112, 523--551, 2018). The implementation is presented for the basic case of isotropic linear elastic brittle materials with a Drucker-Prager strength surface. The material inputs are therefore the Young's modulus $E$, the Poisson's ratio $ν$, the uniaxial tensile strength $\sts$, the uniaxial compressive strength $\scs$, and the fracture toughness $G_c$. The mathematical correspondence between the heat equation and the evolution equation for the phase field $v(\bfX,t)$ is exploited through a UMAT subroutine, wherein the driving force $c_{\texttt{e}}(\bfX,t)$ --- accounting for the material strength surface --- in the phase-field model plays the role of a heat source. To ensure that the equations for the displacement field $\bfu(\bfX,t)$ and the phase field $v(\bfX,t)$ are solved in a staggered manner --- a solution strategy that, as opposed to monolithic approaches, reliably yields the correct physical solution --- we make use of a combination of UEXTERNALDB, UAMP, MPC, and URDFIL subroutines. Within this approach, the MPC and URDFIL subroutines are additionally utilized to enforce the required bounding and irreversibility inequalities on $v(\bfX,t)$ via a primal-dual active set approach. The capabilities and robustness of the proposed implementation are demonstrated by simulating the ``Nine Circles of Elastic Brittle Fracture'' on a silicate glass --- a set of tests that span the entire range of well-settled experimental knowledge on fracture nucleation and propagation. These simulations also serve to illustrate the deployment of the code using several native Abaqus finite elements, including the simplicial elements CPS3, CAX3, and C3D4.

title: Tilted Mondrian: Triage and Mitigation of Fine-grained Disparities in Conformal Prediction
abstract: Fairness in conformal prediction is often pursued through Mondrian calibration, which provides finite-sample coverage guarantees separately across groups. These guarantees, however, are coarse: substantial disparities can remain within finer strata. This coarse-to-fine fairness issue raises two questions: how severe can such disparities be, and how can they be mitigated? Aggregate disparities can depend on how groups are distributed across strata. For severity assessment, we introduce propensity standardization to examine the effect of population composition, and show how group composition can induce disagreement between aggregate and finer-stratum comparisons. For mitigation, we develop Tilted Mondrian to improve fairness compared to group-Mondrian at a finer level without additional model training. Tilted Mondrian retains groupwise coverage guarantees and mitigates coverage and prediction set size disparities within finer strata. Finally, we derive a method-agnostic bound that quantifies how much reduction in finer-stratum coverage disparity can be achieved.
authors: Ziang Gao;Pengqi Liu;Archer Yi Yang;Mouloud Belbahri;Jesse C. Cresswell;Masoud Asgharian

title: Degradation Aware V2G Dispatch for Co-Optimization of Parking Facility and Edge Data Center Located in the Airport Campus
abstract: This paper studies an airport campus where long stay EV parking, airport buildings, and an AI data center share a single grid connection. The campus pays a commercial electricity tariff that charges for both the energy used and the highest power drawn during peak hours. Parked EVs can send power back to the campus through vehicle to grid (V2G) chargers and lower this peak. This paper proposes a two stage method. In the first stage, a linear program schedules EV charging and discharging to maximize the operator's profit and also sets a fixed daily payment to EV owners. In the second stage, a search chooses the share of energy savings paid to owners. The model guarantees that every owner is paid enough to take part, pays for battery wear so that EVs discharge only when it is worth the wear, and assigns charging ports on a first come, first served basis. In the case study, 400 V2G chargers are added to 1200 existing Level 2 chargers, serving 5000 expected sessions under summer and winter rates. In a summer week, V2G raises operator profit by $4978 compared with smart charging and lowers the high peak demand by 4400 kW (9%). The best contract gives owners 70% of the energy savings and earns 21% more than a fixed payment alone. Doubling the V2G ports to 800 lowers the peak further but reduces profit, because owner payments grow faster than the savings. V2G pays back within 10 years if a bidirectional charger costs less than about $1800 more than a standard one. Compared with a 5 MW/10 MWh stationary battery, V2G cuts more peak demand at $409 of investment per kW instead of $1522 and needs no extra land, while the battery does not pay back within its lifetime.

title: Martingale Posterior Cox Processes
abstract: Cox processes provide a principled Bayesian nonparametric framework for modeling event-based data through an underlying intensity function. However, existing inference methods for estimating the intensity typically rely on computationally expensive Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling or approximate inference techniques. In addition, to ensure tractability, these methods often define priors over indirect latent structures, making them challenging to interpret. In this paper, we introduce the Martingale Posterior Cox Process (MPCP), which recasts Bayesian intensity estimation as inference over unobserved events given the observed event history. This perspective avoids the need to define complex priors while retaining the flexibility of nonparametric modeling. We propose a scalable, GPU-friendly copula-based predictive update, and provide strong theoretical guarantees for the convergence of the predictive resampling algorithm. Empirically, we show that MPCP provides excellent performance in both simulations and real data at a fraction of the computational cost of competing Bayesian approaches.

title: The Impact of an AGN on PAH Spectral Features in Galaxy Evolution Simulations: Continuum Dilution and Excitation of PAHs
abstract: Galaxies hosting an active galactic nucleus (AGN) show diminished power and non-standard spectral feature ratios from polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) compared with normal star-forming galaxies. Proposed mechanisms for this difference include a combination of AGN-driven PAH grain processing, differential heating from the surrounding radiation field, and continuum dilution. These potentially competing factors are difficult to disentangle observationally. In this paper, we investigate the impact of the AGN radiation field on the excitation properties and potential dilution of the mid-IR emission features via constrained numerical experiments of idealized galaxies in simulations that include a self-consistent model for the evolution of dust. We find that, for the integrated spectrum of our simulated Milky Way analog and independent of grain-processing physics, the apparent PAH emission is progressively diminished as AGN luminosity is increased. For spectra within the central half kiloparsec, PAH features are entirely obfuscated when an AGN of any sampled luminosity is present. We additionally find that the UV radiation from an AGN is capable of impacting PAH band ratios, though note that we do not yet include a model for potential photodestruction of PAHs. Our model suggests that the inferred lack of PAHs via featureless mid-IR spectra from galaxies hosting AGN may simply owe to the direct continuum from the AGN overpowering mid-IR features from PAHs in the ISM of the host galaxy. Future work will investigate the relative role of AGN continuum dilution and PAH heating vs photodestruction/ionization of PAHs.
authors: Grant P. Donnelly;Desika Narayanan;Paul Torrey;J. -D. T. Smith;Helena M. Richie;Hui Li;Federico Marinacci

title: Molecular Doping of MoS$_2$ with N-Heterocyclic Carbenes: A Raman Study of Interfacial Charge Transfer
abstract: We demonstrate efficient electron doping of exfoliated MoS$_2$ through the deposition of N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) molecules onto its surface. Raman spectroscopy reveals a pronounced softening of the optical A$_{1g}$ phonon mode after NHC deposition, consistent with electron transfer from the NHC molecules to the MoS$_2$ layers. The largest phonon-energy shifts are observed in monolayer and bilayer flakes whereas changes in bulk-like MoS$_2$ are negligible, indicating that the doping efficiency depends on the number of layers. This thickness dependence highlights the dominant role of interfacial charge transfer at the NHC/MoS$_2$ interface. Quantitative analysis of the Raman modes of as-exfoliated and NHC-covered MoS$_2$, together with comparison with literature values, allows us to estimate an increase in the two-dimensional electron density of about two-orders of magnitude in MoS$_2$ mono- and bilayers. These results demonstrate that NHC-based surface deposition is a promising approach for chemically tuning the carrier density of semiconducting transition-metal dichalcogenides and provide a potential route toward molecularly tunable two-dimensional electronic devices, in which, analogous to modulation doping, the donors reside outside the semiconductor lattice.
authors: Ana Senkić;Arne Nalop;Xenia Sieverding;Ariane Ufer;Sebastian Roling;Frank Glorius;Ursula Wurstbauer

title: Epitaxial Displacement-etched GaAsSb Quantum Dots Emitting at Telecom Wavelengths
abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are essential components for integrated photonic and quantum information systems, yet current epitaxial growth techniques face significant limitations in complexity of growth, material selection, and density tunability. Here we report a displacement etch technique that enables controlled formation of GaAsSb QDs with emission at telecommunications wavelengths. Our approach uses arsenic molecular flux (As$_2$) to react with antimonide surfaces through thermodynamically favorable displacement reactions, creating three-dimensional quantum confined nanostructures without requiring strain-driven growth or complex droplet-based processes. Density functional theory shows the two competing As-for-Sb exchange pathways to be nearly equivalent in both reaction energy and activation barrier, which places morphological control in the subsequent adatom kinetics rather than in the surface reaction itself. A single process parameter, the As$_2$ exposure, sets the QD areal density across three orders of magnitude, from 10$^2$ to 10$^5$ $μm^{-2}$, covering both isolated emitters and dense gain media. Structural analysis reveals well-defined GaAsSb QDs with a mixed GaAs/GaSb composition and no extended defects. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence measurements confirm emission at 1550 nm (0.8 eV) within the telecommunications C-band, with characteristic QD-like temperature dependence. Because the QDs form on a lattice-matched GaSb surface in a single growth step, the technique offers a practical route to C-band emitters built into the GaSb/AlGaSb device family already used for mid-infrared sources and detectors.
authors: Sadhvikas Addamane;Sanghyeok Park;Quinn T. Campbell;Evan M. Anderson;Thomas Rotter;Darryl Shima;Julia Deitz;Paul Kotula;Ganesh Balakrishnan;Oleg Mitrofanov;Igal Brener;Prasad P. Iyer

title: Three Machines Suffice for Local Hardening of Electromechanical Oscillations
abstract: The single-degree-of-freedom swing equation with sinusoidal coupling is locally softening: its oscillation frequency decreases with oscillation level near a stable equilibrium. Nonlinear modal interaction, however, can reverse this trend in multimachine systems. This letter gives a necessary-and-sufficient condition for strict leading-order local hardening, measured with respect to canonical action, in two symmetric three-machine operating-point families with equal or opposite power injections at the equal-inertia machines. An exact two-coordinate reduction expresses the condition in terms of a squared modal-frequency ratio and a dimensionless nonlinear coupling measure. The proof retains the induced mean shift and second harmonic and shows that the companion modal family remains locally softening. The criterion recovers both an equal-inertia hardening example and an exact large-inertia threshold. Coherent aggregation recovers the two-machine softening law, whereas the infinite-bus limit retains two dynamic rotor angles and permits hardening. An exact coherent-group extension preserves the selected periodic family, frequency, and canonical action for every finite machine count greater than two. Thus, three finite-inertia machines are the minimum permitting local hardening in the stated undamped, lossless classical model.

title: Gaussian Process Bandits with Paired Auxiliary Observations
abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is widely used for expensive black-box optimization, yet observation noise makes each evaluation less informative and slows posterior learning. Standard BO learns from costly outcomes gathered during optimization. In many applications, however, low-cost auxiliary data are available beforehand. We introduce Auxiliary-Informed Gaussian Process Bandit (AI-GPB), a variance-reduction method that combines an offline estimate of the auxiliary mean with a correction coefficient learned from paired online observations. Notably, it exploits correlation between paired observation errors without requiring the auxiliary mean to approximate the objective. We establish finite-sample GP confidence bounds and regret guarantees, including explicit cumulative and simple regret rates for Matérn kernels. Numerical experiments across continuous BO benchmarks with varied landscapes and dimensions show consistent reductions in cumulative and simple regret relative to vanilla GP-UCB, even when within-pair correlation is moderate and the auxiliary mean is estimated from noisy offline data.

title: Comparison of Current-Limiting Strategies for Grid-Forming Converters Under Grid Faults
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of three state-of-the-art current-limiting strategies for grid-forming (GFM) converters under grid faults. These highly effective strategies include virtual admittance control, virtual admittance control enhanced with virtual power feedback, and the recently developed cross-forming control. The performance comparison addresses two crucial requirements for GFM converters under grid faults, namely transient stability and reactive current injection. The comparison indicates that the virtual admittance control enhanced with virtual power feedback shows the most promising transient stability performance, while the cross-forming control exhibits superior reactive current injection performance. Thus, individual benefits of each strategy can be obtained by properly combining them.
authors: Maitraya Avadhut Desai;Ramona Stoll;Xiuqiang He;Florian Dörfler;Gabriela Hug

title: Multilingual Brain Decoding Reveals Shared Cortical Semantic Geometry
abstract: Human languages differ markedly in lexical and syntactic form yet can convey similar semantic content. The neural basis of this cross-language semantic commonality remains unclear. Here we developed a multilingual brain decoding framework and analysed brain recordings from 227 participants spanning Chinese, English and French. We found that cortical semantic representations exhibited consistent semantic geometry relationships across languages and individuals, revealing a shared cortical semantic geometry. Importantly, the cross-language consistency of cortical semantic geometry increased from sensorimotor to higher-order association cortex, forming a shared semantic geometry gradient closely aligned with the principal cortical functional gradient. Our work establishes generalizable multilingual brain decoding and identifies stable cortical semantic geometry as a neural basis for semantic commonality across languages.
authors: Yi Guo;Yong Hu;Michael Kwok-Po Ng;Shuqiang Wang

title: Multi-Agentic AI for Intent-Driven and Conflict-Aware rApp Policy Orchestration in Open RAN
abstract: Open radio access network (O-RAN) enables a multi-vendor ecosystem that accelerates xApp development for near-real-time (RT) network management. However, this openness shifts a combinatorial coordination burden to the Non-RT layer, where rApp policies compose xApps from a growing catalog to realize operator intents. Coexisting intents further compound this challenge, as conflicts may arise among xApp actions, rApp policies, and their cross-layer interactions. To maximize intent admission while maintaining key performance indicator (KPI) compliance across incoming and incumbent intents, we propose a large language model-based Multi-Agentic AI framework. A Reasoning Agent screens candidate xApps against KPI contracts and produces a joint intent admission and xApp assignment decision. On post-deployment KPI violations, a Diagnosis Agent identifies the root causes of failure, labels the conflict mechanism, and guides the Reasoning Agent in subsequent attempts. Experimental results show that the framework based on GPT-OSS 120B achieves 28.6% more KPI-compliant cases and admits over 15* as many incoming intents as state-of-the-art baselines. Under the Qwen 72B variant, Diagnosis increases compliant cases by 50.0%, quadruples admitted intents, and reduces deployment attempts by 32.6%. A live deployment conforming to O-RAN specifications further validates the feasibility of the proposed solution for conflict-aware rApp policy orchestration in real networks.

title: Clumpy Outflows from Super-Eddington Accreting Black Holes. II. Conditions for Clump Formation
abstract: Active galactic nuclei (AGNs) commonly exhibit ultra-fast outflows (UFOs) with velocities of $0.03$--$0.3~c$. Recent high-resolution X-ray observations with XRISM/Resolve suggest that UFOs may have a clumpy structure. However, the formation and evolution of these clumpy outflows remain poorly understood. In the first paper of this series, we investigated the formation of clumpy outflows using numerical simulations and find that sufficiently high spatial resolution is required to reproduce clumpy structures numerically. In this second paper, we perform a series of numerical experiments to identify the key physical processes governing clump formation. We find that spatial fluctuations of physical quantities at the disk surface are essential for the formation of clumpy outflows, whereas spatial and temporal fluctuations at the inner boundary have only a minor effect. Furthermore, density structure-function analysis suggests that the high-density regions have an elongated morphology with characteristic transverse widths of several tens of $R_{\rm g}$, possibly produced by radiation Rayleigh--Taylor instability. A more comprehensive investigation of the instability in general-relativistic radiation magnetohydrodynamic simulations, where accretion disk structures emerge self-consistently, is expected to provide deeper insights into the physical origin of clumpy outflows.
authors: Haojie Hu;Yuta Asahina;Shogo Yoshioka;Hiroyuki R. Takahashi;Ken Ohsuga

title: Distributed Real-Time Cooperative Model Predictive Control
abstract: This paper presents a novel distributed real-time iterative method for cooperative linear Model Predictive Control (MPC) with polyhedral state and input constraints, implementing a relaxed, recentered logarithmic barrier function. The method transforms centralized MPC problems into a distributed framework using temporal-spatial splitting, facilitating efficient online implementation. To achieve real-time performance, we introduce a distributed convex nonlinear optimization solver with guaranteed global linear convergence. By executing this solver with a fixed number of iterations per sampling time, the resulting near-optimal MPC controller ensures closed-loop stability while maintaining fixed computational complexity. The proposed approach is validated through an illustrative example involving a spring-vehicle-damper system benchmark, demonstrating both its effectiveness and computational efficiency.
authors: Yuning Jiang;Kristína Fedorová;Roland Schwan;Juraj Oravec;Colin N. Jones

title: Shear SAW piezoelectricity of single-crystalline $\mathrm{LiNbO_3}$ films grown on $42^{\circ}$ YX-$\mathrm{LiTaO_3}$ substrates by DLI-CVD
abstract: Direct growth of single-crystalline $\mathrm{LiNbO_3}$ films with technologically relevant nonpolar orientations and a single ferroelectric domain state remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the epitaxial growth of a 320-nm-thick, single-domain $42°$ YX-oriented $\mathrm{LiNbO_3}$ film on a congruent $42°$ YX-cut $\mathrm{LiTaO_3}$ substrate by direct liquid injection chemical vapor deposition. The deposition temperature was limited to $600°\mathrm{C}$ to preserve the ferroelectric domain state of the $\mathrm{LiTaO_3}$ substrate. X-ray diffraction confirmed that the $\mathrm{LiNbO_3}$ film inherited the substrate orientation and domain state and exhibited no detectable secondary phases. The LN rocking-curve full width at half maximum was $0.011°$, approaching the instrumental resolution and demonstrating its high crystalline quality. Single-port leaky surface acoustic wave (LSAW) resonators with a wavelength of $4\,μ\mathrm{m}$ were fabricated on the $\mathrm{LiNbO_3/LiTaO_3}$ heterostructure and on a bare $\mathrm{LiTaO_3}$ reference substrate. At approximately 1 GHz, the $\mathrm{LiNbO_3/LiTaO_3}$-based resonators exhibited an electromechanical coupling coefficient of about 13%, compared to 8.5% for the reference $\mathrm{LiTaO_3}$-based resonators. These results demonstrate that direct epitaxial growth can produce high-quality, strongly piezoelectric $\mathrm{LiNbO_3}$ films and provide a route toward thickness-controlled layered substrates for high-performance acoustic devices.
authors: Mikhail Mirushchenko;Roland Salut;Ludovic Gauthier-Manuel;Vincent Astié;Samuel Margueron;Jean-Manuel Decams;Yuancheng Ji;Farshad F. Bolamiri;Ventsislav Yantchev;Ausrine Bartasyte

title: Optimal degree bounds for sum-of-squares representations
abstract: The moment-sum-of-squares (SOS) hierarchy provides a sequence of bounds on the minimum of a polynomial over a basic closed semialgebraic set, i.e., a subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ defined by finitely many polynomial constraints. We establish optimal bounds on the error of the SOS hierarchy in the following settings: 1. If the constraints define an Archimedean quadratic module: the error of the Putinar-based hierarchy at level $k$ is $Θ((\log k)^4/k^2)$ in the worst case. 2. If the constraints define a compact semialgebraic set: the error of the Schmüdgen-based hierarchy at level $k$ is $Θ((\log k)^2/k^2)$ in the worst case. 3. If the constraints define an Archimedean quadratic module and satisfy linear independence constraint qualification conditions (LICQ): the error of the hierarchy at level $k$ is $Θ(1/k^{4})$ in the worst case. Here, the upper bound holds already for the Putinar-based hierarchy, while the lower bound holds even against the Schmüdgen-based hierarchy. Equivalently, these give best-possible effective versions of Putinar's and Schmüdgen's Positivstellensätze for these settings (in terms of their dependence on $k$).
authors: Alexander Taveira Blomenhofer;Sander Gribling;Didier Henrion;Milan Korda;Poornendu Kumar;Victor Magron;Lucas Slot;Luis Felipe Vargas;Juan Vera

title: Theory of High-Temperature Fractional Chern Phases in Monolayer van der Waals Kagome Materials A$_2$T$_3$X$_4$
abstract: Fractional Chern insulators bring the fractional quantum Hall effect, with its anyonic excitations, to zero magnetic field. So far they have been realized in moiré materials, where the long superlattice period weakens electronic interactions and confines these phases to cryogenic temperatures. Early proposals instead envisioned topological flat bands on atomic-scale lattices, where fractionalization could persist to far higher temperatures, but a suitable material has been lacking. Here we theoretically identify monolayers of the van der Waals kagome family $\mathrm{A}_2\mathrm{T}_3\mathrm{X}_4$ as such a platform, combining intrinsic topological flat bands and strong Coulomb interactions with gate-tunable carrier density and layer assembly. Exact diagonalization of models derived from density functional theory reveals ferromagnetism over broad filling ranges, supporting diverse fractional Chern insulators, anomalous composite Fermi liquids, and charge-ordered phases. In particular, in $\mathrm{Cs}_2\mathrm{Pd}_3\mathrm{S}_4$, the fractional Chern insulator exhibits a many-body gap of approximately 26 meV in the largest system accessible with band mixing allowing at most one interband electron-hole excitation. Layer assembly further provides a natural route to fractional quantum spin Hall insulators: bilayers with antiparallel magnetizations support this phase at realistic separations. These results identify an experimentally accessible material family in which chemical composition, carrier density, and stacking offer complementary routes to fractionalization at enhanced energy scales and control over topological order.
authors: Soomin Oh;Jiyong Han;Jinhyeok Choi;Donghae Seo;Mingu Kang;Gil Young Cho

title: Galactic warps constrain equivalence-principle violation in the dark sector
abstract: Current measurements of the expansion of the Universe allow for the presence of evolving dark energy, distinct from a cosmological constant, with an equation of state that seems to violate the null energy condition. One notable explanation for this behaviour is that the dark energy interacts with the dark matter, violating the equivalence principle yet evading conventional laboratory and astrophysical constraints. Such models produce fifth forces acting only on dark matter. We show how such forces separate halo and stellar disk centres, creating a potential gradient across the disk that warps it into a cup shape. Measuring the warps of $4\times10^3$ edge-on disks in Sloan Digital Sky Survey images and modelling the fifth-force signal together with competing baryonic effects, we find no sign of the predicted correlation between the measured warps and the fifth-force field. This constrains the fifth-force strength relative to gravity to $ΔG/G_N<7.7\times10^{-4}$ at 95% credibility (or $<1.7\times10^{-3}$ once systematic uncertainties are included) for force ranges of 8 Mpc and above. In the infinite-range limit of a scalar rolling today, even the conservative bound is three times stronger than the tightest cosmological bound (which, unlike ours, depends on the scalar's cosmological evolution) and about two orders of magnitude below other astrophysical bounds. It disfavours at 2-3$σ$ the couplings preferred by recent fits of interacting dark energy to cosmological data unless gravitational screening is invoked.

title: Linear Approximations Provide Rigorous Conditions for Phase Locking in Oscillator Networks and Power Grids
abstract: Synchronization is a fundamental collective phenomenon in many natural and engineered networks. The stable operation of oscillator networks, such as electric power grids, requires phase locking with phase differences across edges below a given threshold. A central question is whether a given network supports such a state. In this contribution, we extend a convex optimization formulation of the nonlinear fixed point equations of the Kuramoto model, that also describe lossless power grids. Based on this formulation, we derive rigorous and tight bounds on the error introduced by an arbitrary approximation of the original model, in particular linear approximations. The bounds yield edge-wise regions of trust around the approximation, within which the true nonlinear solution must lie. They further provide sufficient and necessary conditions for phase locking under prescribed phase difference limits. Numerical experiments show that the bounds are tight over a broad range of parameters.
authors: Iva Bačić;Carsten Hartmann;Philipp C. Böttcher;David Gross;Andrea Benigni;Dirk Witthaut

title: Physics-Informed Koopman Learning for Data-Efficient System Identification of Automated Vehicle Dynamics
abstract: Understanding how a particular automated vehicle reacts to nearby traffic can improve motion prediction, control development, traffic simulation, and safety evaluation. However, commercial automated driving systems are proprietary, and single encounters may provide only a few seconds of noisy data. Standard physical models are interpretable but inflexible, whereas neural models are often data-hungry. We propose a physics-informed Koopman framework that combines a calibrated car-following law with a correction learned from the observations. A weak-form estimator learns this correction from velocity measurements integrated over time, avoiding noise-sensitive numerical differentiation. The resulting continuous-time model predicts the follower's response and provides interpretable measures of driving behavior. Experiments on OpenACC and CATS-CF evaluate 5-, 7-, and 11-second histories. Averaged over these histories, the constant-time-headway branch reduces speed prediction error by 16.0% and 15.4% on OpenACC and CATS-CF, respectively, relative to the best neural baselines. The PI-Koopman branches achieve the lowest mean speed and gap errors among the physical and neural comparators. Weak-form estimation reduces acceleration-field reconstruction error by 74.5% in noisy known-law simulations and noise-induced field perturbation by 91.6% in paired real-vehicle measurements. The same PI-Koopman system identification supports following-mode recognition with an approximately eleven-fold difference in median residual variance between human drivers and automated vehicles, and a single residual threshold achieves 85.4% balanced accuracy. The branch informed by the intelligent driver model takes a median 17 to 26 ms for identification and forecasting on the tested central processing units, supporting frequent target adaptation.
authors: Hangyu Li;Yiming Meng;Zhaohui Liang;Yunqing Xiao;Yuxuan Chen;Bofeng Cao;Shixiao Liang;Jiaxi Liu;Haotian Shi;Xiaopeng Li

title: Conditional Weight of Evidence for Gradient-Boosted Credit Models: Estimation, Additivity and Its Relation to Adverse Action Reasons
abstract: Traditional weight of evidence assigns a credit characteristic a value based on its association with default across a population. Credit analysis also requires an assessment of that characteristic in the context of an individual applicant's record. We study conditional weight of evidence for this purpose. It measures the change in default log odds from observing a characteristic after the remaining credit information is known. Its sign identifies whether the characteristic adds adverse or favorable information for that applicant, and its magnitude measures the strength of that information. The same characteristic value can therefore receive different assessments for applicants with different payment histories or other credit attributes. We develop estimators using gradient-boosted trees and evaluate their accuracy in a bureau-style simulation. Regressions of the full model's predicted probabilities recover conditional evidence more accurately than separate models fitted to default outcomes, provided the full model is accurate. They also recover a deliberately constructed file-age effect whose direction varies with utilization and is often missed by marginal weight of evidence. Local class-frequency estimates improve on marginal weight of evidence but remain inaccurate for some weak effects. An application to FICO HELOC data illustrates estimation when the population evidence is unknown. Conditional weight of evidence provides an applicant-specific interpretation of the information in a credit characteristic; its population summary, a conditional information value, splits the joint information in the record across blocks when averaged over orderings. Neither is an adverse action reason, which explains the fitted score difference between the applicant and chosen passing records.

title: Structural signatures of a topological transition in a disordered tetrahedral network
abstract: Topological transitions in disordered network materials are often characterised using descriptors of entanglement, such as ring linking and writhe, which can be difficult to access experimentally. Here we investigate whether a topological transition can instead be identified using structural descriptors more readily connected to experiment. We reanalyse configurations of a colloidal tetrahedral network model known to exhibit a pressure-driven transition between unentangled and and entangled states. We show that the cumulative all-rings vertex symbol (CARVS), a descriptor of medium-range network topology based on ring statistics, provides a clear signature of this transition despite containing no explicit information about ring linking. We further show that network entanglement produces characteristic changes in the radial distribution function and structure factor, including the emergence of short-range correlations between nonbonded nodes and the disappearance of a low-angle scattering pre-peak. These results establish experimentally accessible structural signatures of topological transitions in disordered tetrahedral networks. Comparison with canonical continuous random networks further suggests that framework materials with extended linkers may provide promising candidate systems in which to search experimentally for entanglement-driven topological transitions.
authors: Florence Ellary;Thomas C. Nicholas;Dwaipayan Chakrabarti;Andrew L. Goodwin

title: Forecasting the Resolvability of Stellar Velocity Dispersions in Ultra-faint Dwarf Galaxies
abstract: Ultra-faint dwarf galaxies (UFDs)---the smallest and most dark-matter dominated galactic systems---push the boundaries of our understanding of galaxy formation in the cold dark matter paradigm. As current and near-future imaging surveys continue to expand the known population of extremely faint systems, spectroscopic resources have become a major limitation in our ability to understand the physical nature of these systems. We present projections for the capability of Keck/DEIMOS, Magellan/IMACS, and future spectroscopic instruments (e.g., Magellan/Via and GMT/GMACS) to kinematically distinguish dark-matter-dominated UFDs from dark-matter-free star clusters in the ultra-faint regime. We simulate ensembles of mock observations of ultra-faint dwarf galaxies and apply a formal statistical framework, calibrated to observations, to systematically characterize the ability to resolve velocity dispersions as a function of satellite properties. Our projections suggest that current instruments will struggle to resolve many of systems that will be discovered by the Rubin Observatory. Near future instruments will be capable of resolving a majority of these systems, though they will fail for the faintest and most distant systems. Ultimately, we will require even more advanced instruments, with enhanced stability and velocity precision, to classify the full population of ultra-faint Milky Way satellites.
authors: Pierre Thibodeaux;Alex Drlica-Wagner;Alexander P. Ji;Chin Yi Tan;Ting S. Li;Andrew B. Pace;Louis E. Strigari

title: Discrete Phase-Shift Optimization of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces using Uniform Reference Directions
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) enable programmable control of the wireless propagation environment through adjustable reflecting elements. A fundamental challenge in RIS-assisted communications is the optimization of discrete phase shifts to maximize the received signal power. While recently developed algorithms can obtain optimal solutions with linear complexity, their computational cost may still be excessive in applications requiring large-scale simulations, real-time adaptation, or repeated optimization over numerous channel realizations. This paper proposes a low-complexity discrete phase-shift optimization algorithm based on multiple reference directions within the feasible optimality sector. By evaluating candidate phase configurations generated from uniformly distributed reference directions, the proposed method systematically improves upon existing approximation approaches that rely on a fixed set of reference directions. The number of reference directions serves as a design parameter that enables a controllable trade-off between computational complexity and optimality. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves substantial computational speedups while maintaining a small optimality gap relative to the optimal solution. The results further show that increasing the number of reference directions progressively reduces the optimality gap, providing flexible operating points that can be tailored to application-specific complexity and performance requirements.

title: Optimal Trading Filters and the Value of Predictive Signals
abstract: The value of a forecast depends on its accuracy, but also on its actionability. In trading, an investor must translate return forecasts into positions while accounting for trading costs and the lingering impact of earlier trades. We solve the stationary quadratic trading problem with transient price impact using tools from prediction theory: Wiener-Hopf factorization gives the optimal policy as the composition of a conditional forecast and an explicit causal linear filter. We recover the Gârleanu-Pedersen aim-portfolio under exponential resilience and derive fractional trading filters under power-law impact decay, requiring memory beyond finite-dimensional LQR control. At fixed positive risk penalty, signals of equal instantaneous predictive strength have equal frictionless Markowitz value. With trading costs, net attainable value is determined by the mean square of the friction-weighted conditional forecast. Under power-law impact with exposure bleeding, we find an intermediate optimal mean-reversion rate for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck signals.

title: Newly Identified Planetary Nebula Candidates in M31 using Deep-Learning Search of Hubble Space Telescope Images
abstract: The Hubble Space Telescope has imaged approximately a quarter of a billion stars in M31's disc, yet only slightly over a thousand planetary nebulae (PNe) are known, mostly from ground-based surveys. We show that deep learning can find them in broad-band images alone. In what is the first such search, we scan the Panchromatic Hubble Andromeda Treasury (PHAT) and the Panchromatic Hubble Andromeda Southern Treasury (PHAST) mosaics, nearly one square degree of the disk, where a PN is a faint blue point among crowded stars. Because the existing catalogs are incomplete, we train four Faster R-CNN detectors with partial supervision, so that uncataloged PNe are not taught as background, and combine their rankings into one candidate list, an ensemble. On spatially separate test fields, this list places 73% of the known PNe in its top 200, 4 to 6 times the purity of classical color-magnitude selection. Newer detection transformers and segmentation networks trained on the same data do not surpass our detectors. The ranking also follows classifications that the detectors never saw: emission-line objects that the literature calls PNe enter the list at 47%, against 0.6% for those called H II regions, which makes them candidates for reclassification. Among the top 400 candidates, 175 appear in no published catalog, 12 of them flagged as cosmic-ray residuals. One of them, a point source with [O III] emission in nine independent exposures, meets the PN criteria of the three major PN studies of M31, so by those criteria it is a PN. Most of the others lack strong [O III], as expected if narrow-band surveys have found the bright PNe, although some may be PNe with weak [O III]. These results support the near completeness of ground-based surveys for bright PNe and extend it from the PHAT area to PHAST. Finally, we identify evaluation pitfalls for detectors of rare objects and recommend simple remedies.
authors: Yiğit C. Atılgan;Aleyna Demirci;Nazım Aksaker;Ammar Abbas Elmas;Mehmet Sarıgül;Aysun Akyüz

title: Comment on "The polarization hierarchy for polynomial optimization over convex bodies, with applications to nonnegative matrix rank"
abstract: We revisit the feasibility and convergence claims for the polarization hierarchy of Plávala, Ligthart and Gross [Linear Algebra Appl.\ 723 (2025) 15--32]. Counterexamples show that the stated assumption is insufficient for the feasibility characterization and for convergence of the hierarchy with the polarization constraint. We establish corrected results under a stronger algebraic condition and supply a missing compactness argument.

title: Accelerating Finite-Sum Bilevel Optimization with Fully First-Order Oracles
abstract: We study nonconvex--strongly-convex bilevel optimization with finite-sum objectives and fully first-order oracles. We propose Sampled Implicit Corrections for Bilevel Optimization (SICBO), which combines a penalty approximation with variance-reduced corrections for the lower-level variables. Under componentwise lower strong convexity, SICBO finds a point $x$ satisfying $\mathbb{E}\|\nablaΦ(x)\|^2\le\varepsilon^2$ within $\tilde{O}(N+\sqrt{N}κ^{7/2}\varepsilon^{-2})$ component-gradient calls, where $N$ is the total number of components and $κ$ is the normalized lower-level condition number. The bound achieves square-root finite-sum dependence using only gradients and preserves the best known deterministic fully first-order condition-number exponent for smooth problems. Our improvement follows from a curvature-dependent bound for nonlinear correction errors, which permits epochs of length $\tildeΘ(\sqrt{N/κ})$ with batches of size $\tildeΘ(\sqrt{Nκ})$. A single-level reduction shows that the dependence on $N$ and $\varepsilon$ is optimal up to logarithmic factors for fixed $κ$.

title: Understanding compression-extension error asymmetry in universal machine-learning interatomic potentials
abstract: Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials are increasingly used across diverse materials, yet their reliability under directional deformation remains unclear. We compare compression and extension along paired deformation paths from the same parent structures for eleven pretrained potentials. The benchmark comprises 1,963 Materials Project trajectory (MPtrj) parents and 1,286 experimental-source MinX-Eq parents at six strain magnitudes from 1% to 10%. Density-functional theory provides references for isotropic, uniaxial and biaxial loading in MPtrj and isotropic loading in MinX-Eq. At $\pm 10\%$, every model has a larger median force error under compression, with pooled isotropic compression-to-extension ratios of 2.12 and 3.30 for MPtrj and MinX-Eq. Decomposing error growth into DFT force-scale growth and relative-error evolution shows that relative errors decrease on both branches, faster under compression in MPtrj but slower under compression in MinX-Eq. Force-scale matching moves the error ratios toward unity, although MinX-Eq retains a compression-side excess across models. Radial and SOAP analyses place compressed structures at shorter separations and farther from public reference pools, while readout-associated model features show larger compression-side displacements. These results distinguish stronger physical responses from changes in relative predictive accuracy and provide a basis for assessing universal potentials in deformation simulations.
authors: Hongwei Du;Dingyang Lv;Boyan Zhang;Yu Ren;Feng Yu;Xin He;Bonan Zhu;Yongda Huang;Jiahui Liu;Yongheng Li;Siqi Shi;Jianjun Liu;Ziheng Lu;Hong Wang

title: Denoising Implicit Variational Inference
abstract: Semi-implicit variational inference (SIVI) expands the representational capacity of variational families, but optimizing the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) remains challenging because the marginal score of the semi-implicit distribution is generally intractable. Unbiased Implicit Variational Inference (UIVI) and related methods address this difficulty through reparameterized ELBO gradients, but existing approaches estimate the required score indirectly through reverse-conditional sampling or approximation, which can be computationally costly and unstable. We propose Denoising Implicit Variational Inference (DIVI), which learns the marginal score directly via denoising score matching. The learned score is used as a plug-in estimator in the pathwise ELBO gradient, replacing inner reverse-conditional sampling with a score-network evaluation. We analyze DIVI as inexact stochastic gradient ascent and show, under stated assumptions, that the averaged stationarity measure is controlled by the usual optimization term and the average score-matching error. Empirically, we evaluate DIVI on both synthetic distributions and a variety of real-data Bayesian inference tasks. The results show that DIVI improves over the current UIVI baselines while reducing the cost of ELBO-gradient estimation.

title: StarMind: Challenges and Opportunities in Orbital Computing
abstract: Space-based artificial intelligence (AI) is moving beyond isolated onboard processing toward constellation-scale computing over optical inter-satellite links (OISLs). Yet current infrastructures remain fragmented, making end-to-end (E2E) coordination across heterogeneous and multi-vendor systems difficult. This article examines the StarMind vision and develops a reference framework for distributed orbital computing. It organizes the system into five layers and defines six standardizable interfaces that link mission intent to resource conditions and trustworthy result delivery. The framework also clarifies the operational constraints that determine whether orbital cooperation is worthwhile. In a representative synthetic aperture radar/interferometric SAR (SAR/InSAR) case study, the framework reduces E2E latency to 41-min, compared with 61-min for localized onboard computing and 146-min for ground-based processing. This gain does not rely on faster processors in orbit. Instead, it comes from reducing contact waiting and urgent Earth downlink traffic through resource-aware task placement and gateway selection. Feasibility analysis shows that the proposed framework is more effective when source datasets are large, output products are compact, and optical inter-satellite link capacity is sufficient. When these conditions are absent, conventional processing may remain preferable. Finally, we discuss research opportunities in joint task partitioning and cross-domain orchestration, hierarchical federated intelligence, and large model-enabled intelligence to advance an interoperable space-ground computing continuum.
authors: Zisheng Gong;Zhaoyu Liu;Houtianfu Wang;O. Tansel Baydas;Liu Cao;Xia Xu;Ozgur B. Akan
comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. 7 pages, 4 figures

title: Private Evaluation of High-Dimensional Functions
abstract: We study differentially private black-box evaluation of arbitrary high-dimensional functions. Given a dataset $S$ and query access to a function $f$---whose sensitivity may be unknown or unbounded---the goal is to privately output an approximation to $f(S)$. The black-box evaluator can only query the value of $f$ over a down neighborhood of $S$ (i.e., those subsets of $S$ that are obtained by removing a bounded number of elements from $S$). We design generic black-box evaluators for both pure and approximate differential privacy through a reduction to high-dimensional private quasi-concave optimization (QCO). Our black-box evaluator enjoys a geometric notion of utility. Consider the vectors obtained by applying $f$ on sets in a down neighborhood of $S$. With high probability, the evaluator's output is guaranteed to be in the convex hull of these vectors. Our work generalizes the result of Linder et al. [LRSS25] for real-valued function evaluation to high dimensions. It also recovers the private center-point guarantees of Beimel et al. [BMNS19], with an explicit additive approximation to maximum Tukey depth. We also apply our evaluators to user-level quasi-concave and convex optimization, showing how they can improve upon the sample-and-aggregate baseline of Nissim et al. [NRS07] by replacing the multiplicative data overhead with an additive overhead. Finally, we show that our formulation of high dimensional black-box evaluation and high dimensional private QCO are equivalent up to a factor of the dimension: the hardest private evaluation instances already arise from the cases that $f$ is a (non-private) quasi-concave optimizer.

title: Dynamic Regret and Tightened Constraint Violation for Communication-Efficient Distributed Online Bilevel Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the distributed online bilevel optimization problem with time-varying inequality constraints. In this setting, a multi-agent network is confronted with a hierarchical decision-making task characterized by coupling between the inner and outer optimization levels. We first propose a communication-efficient single-loop distributed online primal--dual algorithm based on communication compression, which tracks both the inner-level solution and the Hessian-inverse-vector product using only one update per-round. We show that this algorithm achieves a dynamic network regret bound of $\mathcal{O}(T^{\max\{θ_1,1-θ_1\}}+T^{θ_1 } P_T+H_{1,T}+E_{1,T})$, where~$θ_1 \in (0,1)$, $P_T$ is the outer-level path variation, $H_{1,T}$ is the inner-level path variation, and $E_{1,T}$ is the gradient path variation alongside a network cumulative constraint violation bound of $\mathcal{O}(T^{1-θ_1/2})$, which is further reduced to $\mathcal{O}(T^{1-θ_1})$ under Slater's condition. Furthermore, to eliminate the dependence of regret on the inner-level and gradient path variation, we propose a novel adaptive multi-loop distributed online algorithm to control the inner-level approximation accuracy at each round. By dynamically adjusting the number of inner-level updates based on a gradient-norm tolerance condition, this algorithm yields an improved dynamic network regret bound of $\mathcal{O}(T^{\max\{θ_1,1-θ_1\}}+T^{θ_1 } P_T)$ which depends solely on the outer-level path variation while maintaining the same network cumulative constraint violation bound. Finally, numerical simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.
authors: Fan Li;Xinlei Yi;Guanghui Wen;Yang Shi;Tianyou Chai;Tao Yang

title: Water-Driven Porous Silicon as a Platform for Blue Materials
abstract: Living organisms control water to transport matter, transfer energy and drive chemical reactions. In this perspective, we argue that porous silicon can give engineering materials comparable control over water. Its pore architecture, surface chemistry and semiconducting skeleton can be shaped across length scales with the precision of semiconductor processing and, like the water it can host, it relies on one of the most abundant chemical elements on Earth. Liquids in porous silicon, most often water, can flow as a continuum through pores a few nanometers wide, strain the skeleton through capillary and electrosorption stresses, shift structural color, switch transparency, and modulate or generate electrical signals. We describe three directions to combine and extend these effects and overcome their limitations. Pore hierarchy resolves the classical trade-off between interface area and transport speed by combining large and small pores and thereby allows functions to be scaled from thin planar films to three-dimensional components. Surface modification becomes a design variable that tunes the interaction between water and the pore wall. It can be set locally and, with switchable coatings, on demand. Finally, pores only a few molecules wide alter the properties of water itself. In the absence of a bulk-like volume, water can become dielectrically anisotropic and highly conductive. Altogether, these steps turn porous silicon from a responsive material into an adaptive, water-driven material.
authors: Marc Thelen;Julia Brandt;Stella Gries;Manuel Brinker;Alexander Petrov;Patrick Huber

title: Accurate Atomic Correlation Energies and Virial Trends for Correlation-Consistent Effective Core Potentials III: Quantitative Separation of Fixed-Node Biases and Localization Errors in Cs-Rn
abstract: Atomic benchmarks for sixth-period elements (Cs-Rn) are established to sub-millihartree precision under correlation-consistent effective core potentials (ccECPs) using coupled-cluster [up to CCSDT(Q)] and full configuration interaction methods. These references systematically characterize electron correlation, potential-to-kinetic energy partitioning, and combined fixed-node and locality biases ($η$) in fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo (FNDMC). The valence kinetic-to-total energy ratio ($ξ$) departs from the non-relativistic all-electron Coulombic virial limit ($ξ=100\%$), remaining confined between 25.8$\%$ and 37.6$\%$. The Un-pseudizing of semi-core shells decreases $ξ$ as the attractive potential energy deepens faster than the accompanying kinetic energy escalates. Periodic trends in $ξ$ reveal a $5d$ plateau near 34$\%$, with a lanthanide-contraction-driven maximum in Hf, followed by a sharp decline across the $6p$ block. In FNDMC, $η$ escalates rapidly at the onset of group-1/2 and toward the $6p$ closed-shell limit, peaking at 5.42$\%$ in Rn. Although fixed-node errors dominate $η$ in most sixth-period elements, a locality error inversion occurs in Bi, with Pb exhibiting comparable error magnitudes. Furthermore, core-valence partitioning alters trial wavefunction nodal topology: in Tl, three-dimensional nodal cross-sections reveal isolated toroidal domains that confine walkers. This work completes the periodic-table-wide ccECP database from H to Rn, revealing how pseudopotential choices govern energy partitioning, nodal topology, and the balance between fixed-node and localization errors.
comment: 11 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables. To be published in the Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: A Crawling Metric on the Space of Subtrees of a Tree
abstract: We propose a crawling metric on the space of subtrees of a tree. The symmetric difference cannot tell whether two disjoint subtrees are close or far; we halve it and add the gap between them. The result is a metric, one half is the smallest factor, and the tree embeds canonically. The metric equals the least cost of crawling between subtrees by growing and shrinking without jumping. With simultaneous growth and shrinkage, subtrees of fixed length form a geodesic space.
authors: Thu-Le Tran;Cao Minh Quang;Nguyen Chi Tam;Kien Trung Nguyen

title: Dynamic Programming for Value-at-Risk Markov Decision Processes in Continuous Spaces
abstract: Value-at-Risk (VaR) is a widely adopted quantile-based risk measure in practice, yet incorporating VaR objectives into Markov decision processes (VaR MDPs) remains a longstanding challenge. Recent work has derived dynamic programming equations for VaR MDPs in finite state and action spaces but left the case of more general spaces unresolved. This paper establishes, for the first time, the validity of these equations in continuous spaces, for both finite- and infinite-horizon settings. Such cases naturally arise in many real-world dynamic decision-making problems. As an application, we study an optimal execution problem with a VaR objective and demonstrate that our framework enables the characterization of optimal dynamic strategies, resolving an open question in the field.

title: Longitudinal fMRI reveals multi-network reconfiguration and a recurrent frontoparietal shift across rest and task states during adult aging
abstract: Functional connectivity changes across adult aging, but most evidence is cross-sectional, and covariance-based connectivity depends on blood oxygenation level dependent (BOLD) fluctuation amplitude. Covariance decline can reflect changing fluctuation amplitude, and its interpretation may depend on whether normalization uses signal amplitude or includes estimated noise. It is also unclear which longitudinal changes recur across brain states. We analyzed 852 adults (baseline age 36-89 years) from the Aging Adult Brain Connectome with repeated functional MRI (fMRI) during rest, inhibitory control, associative memory, and visual-motor processing (2,220 sessions; median follow-up 5.5 years). Baseline age and elapsed follow-up were modeled separately. Ten cortical networks were tested jointly across states, and covariance was normalized either by released signal amplitude or by a candidate total amplitude reconstructed from released signal and noise amplitudes. Native common covariance declined by 7-11% per 5 years, while signal pair amplitude declined by 9% on average across states, significantly more than estimated noise pair amplitude. Under signal normalization, the relative balance among networks reconfigured over follow-up and differed across states, and the frontoparietal network shifted positively relative to the other nine networks in all four states, by 5-8% per 5 years. The estimated common trajectory was near zero under signal normalization but declined by 4-7% per 5 years under candidate total normalization. The network reconfiguration and the positive frontoparietal-relative direction persisted under both. Within-person coupling between the frontoparietal shift and fluid cognition was not detected. Adult aging thus combines normalization-dependent overall change with a state-dependent redistribution among networks that includes a recurrent frontoparietal shift.
authors: Tingshan Liu;Wanxin Dong;Hairong Zheng;Dong Liang;Zhanli Hu;Guanxun Cheng;Na Zhang

title: A GRACE Interatomic Potential for W--Ta Systems: Application to Ta Segregation and Pinning of Shear-Coupled Grain-Boundary Migration
abstract: Tungsten-tantalum alloys are promising plasma-facing materials for fusion reactors, but simulations of their coupled defect, mechanical, and microstructural evolution require an interatomic potential that remains accurate across diverse atomic environments. We develop a transferable W-Ta potential within the GRaph Atomic Cluster Expansion (GRACE) framework. The primary training dataset was generated automatically by maximizing information entropy in an atomically relevant feature space, avoiding manual enumeration of the structures and processes required for specific downstream applications. Extensive validation demonstrates a consistent description of unary and binary phase stability, elasticity, phonons, high-pressure response, surfaces, point defects, dislocation energetics, transformation pathways, alloy thermodynamics, and melting behavior. As a demonstration, the potential is applied to Ta segregation and shear-coupled migration of a $\Sigma5(120)$ W GB. Simulations reveal strongly site-selective segregation: Ta preferentially occupies a small subset of crystallographically distinct atomic rows. Under shear, segregated Ta impedes disconnection-mediated grain boundary migration. The de-pinning stress initially increases with Ta concentration but plateaus as the dominant pinning environment becomes saturated, while increasing temperature weakens both segregation and pinning. These results establish a broadly validated W-Ta potential and demonstrate how automated entropy-maximized data generation can produce transferable atomistic models capable of resolving mechanisms not explicitly targeted during training.

title: Low-Bit Distributed Constrained Optimization with Application to Optimal Scheduling and Allocation
abstract: This paper proposes a distributed resource allocation algorithm in which each agent communicates only the sign of its local cost gradient, a single bit per directed link per iteration. The algorithm is based on Laplacian-gradient dynamics and preserves the equality (demand) constraint at every iterate, guaranteeing anytime feasibility irrespective of termination time. First, we provide a complete Lyapunov-based convergence analysis for the fixed-step-size regime: the iterates are shown to enter, in at most O(1/\varepsilon^2) iterations, a neighborhood of the optimizer whose radius scales as O(τ) in the decision variable and O(τ^2) in the cost residual, where $τ$ is the step-size. Crucially, the step-size bound is a time-invariant network constant (depending only on the graph Laplacian spectrum and the cost curvature bounds), so no adaptive tuning is required. Second, we characterize the invariant set under B-connected, weight-balanced digraphs, strictly weaker than the all-time connectivity and doubly-stochastic weights assumed in most prior work, and show that any odd, sign-preserving nonlinearity yields the same invariant-set and descent structure, with the single-bit protocol being the extreme communication-minimizing instance of a broader nonlinear class. Third, we address local box constraints via smooth penalty relaxation and quantify explicitly how the penalty weight interacts with the step-size bound and the optimality gap. Simulations on economic dispatch (1000 generators) and CPU scheduling (500 servers) demonstrate that the single-bit protocol achieves 5-60 times reduction in total communication cost relative to multi-bit baselines, at the price of a tunable and explicitly bounded optimality gap. A diminishing step-size schedule is shown empirically to eliminate this gap; its formal convergence analysis is identified as an open problem.

title: Statistical Strong Lensing V. Inference with Microlensed Quasars
abstract: Microlensing of strongly lensed quasars provides direct information on the stellar component of lens galaxies, and can help break the degeneracy between the stellar initial mass function (IMF) and the dark matter. However, a statistical framework to forward model microlensing data while accounting for strong lensing selection effects is still missing. We incorporated microlensing effects into the hierarchical model of Paper III, and investigated to what extent flux measurements of strongly lensed quasars can break the degeneracy between the stellar IMF and the dark matter distribution. We tested the method on a mock sample of 219 doubly imaged quasars, lensed by circularly symmetric lenses. When microlensing effects are modelled, the inference using image fluxes recovers the input foreground population parameters and provides tighter constraints than the inference without flux constraints. The improvement is clearest in the $μ_α-μ_5$ plane, where $μ_α$ describes the mean stellar population synthesis mismatch parameter $\logα_{\rm SPS}$ and $μ_5$ describes the mean projected dark matter mass within $5\,{\rm kpc}$. The 68% credible interval on $μ_α$ shrinks from 0.16 dex to 0.09 dex, with the degeneracy between $μ_α$ and $μ_5$ significantly reduced. By contrast, fitting the image fluxes without accounting for microlensing leads to large biases on the inferred parameters. This work is a first step towards an accurate modelling of microlensing data. Application to real lens samples will require dropping the circular symmetry assumption and adopting more realistic models for the microlensing magnification.
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics

title: Adding Heavy-Ball Momentum to Distributed Constrained Optimization for Energy Resource Management Subject to Time-Delays and Quantization
abstract: This paper studies a hybrid discrete-time signed gradient-consensus method with heavy-ball momentum, paired communication delays, and fixed logarithmic quantization. The method preserves the aggregate supply-demand equality at every iteration. For a static connected undirected graph and bounded delays, a Lyapunov-Krasovskii analysis establishes practical stability by isolating the discontinuous quantization error as an additive disturbance and closing a computable invariant-sublevel argument. The resulting ergodic residual bound is quadratic in the quantization resolution, and exact convergence to the smooth penalized equality-constrained optimizer is recovered in the unquantized case. For delay-free unquantized quadratic costs, an exact modal analysis identifies the heavy-ball stability region and optimal parameters, with the predicted rate validated on a fixed sparse network. A reproducible delayed experiment reports all constants and a certificate whose guaranteed steady-state level lies below the reported initialization. A separate mixed generator-battery experiment exercises the signed update directly. Finite smooth penalties approximate, but do not generally enforce, the local box constraints exactly.

title: New Results for Networked Control of Nonlinear Plants Subject to Transmission Delays
abstract: This paper studies networked control for nonlinear plants subject to several network-induced constraints, with a particular focus on transmission delays. In the context of general nonlinear networked control systems, a standard approach for guaranteeing stability is to construct a storage function, coupled with a single timer variable, to analyze the maximum allowable transmission interval (MATI) and maximum allowable transmission delay (MAD). In this paper, we propose a new approach that assigns each signal that is either \textit{in transit or most recently updated}, to an individual timer variable. This enables the individual characterization and compensation for the dynamics of each potential updating error. Subsequently, based on a novel construction of timer-coupled storage functions, the dynamics of these timer variables is designed and investigated, leading to less conservative conditions on the MATI and MAD than those by the standard approach while still ensuring closed-loop input-to-state stability with respect to external disturbances. Finally, simulation results are given to illustrate the advantages of these new results.

title: Reticulating Local Dynamics in Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: In covalent organic frameworks (COFs), the geometry of the building units predetermines the structure of the framework, yet comparable design principles relating the COF linkers to the local motions that govern guest adsorption and diffusion as well as mechanical response have remained beyond reach. Here, we combine synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function (PDF) analysis with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations accelerated by machine learning interatomic potentials to resolve and compare the local dynamics of two three-dimensional imine-linked COFs, chosen to differ in the geometry and rigidity of one of their two building units. Both are constructed from the same 4-connected square planar linker, $4,4',4'',4'''$-(pyrene-1,3,6,8-tetrayl)tetraaniline (PyTTA), reticulated with the 12-connected nanographene hexakis{[3,5-bis($p$-formylphenyl)-4,6-dimethoxyphenyl]}hexabenzocoronene to give COF-412, {[(HBC-LA$_{12}$)(PyTTA)$_3$]}$_{\mathit{imine}}$, and with the 6-connected triptycene 2,3,6,7,14,15-hexakis(4-formylphenyl)triptycene to give COF-564, {[(Trip-CHO)$_2$(PyTTA)$_3$]}$_{\mathit{imine}}$. The PDF-MD approach resolves the amplitude, the time scale, and the spatial extent of the motion of all COF linkers, separating the limited libration of the fused aromatic cores from the larger reorientational tilts of the pendant aryl rings they carry and from the translation of whole linkers within the net. The simulations further reveal that exchanging the nanographene- for the triptycene-based linker tunes the equilibrium tilt and the positional probability density of PyTTA, raising the tilt amplitude of its linker partner, and, notably, strengthens the coupling between the translations of neighbouring linkers. This approach provides a blueprint for understanding local dynamical properties in COFs, and shows them to be selectable through the choice of building unit and amenable to design.
authors: Francesco Tavani;Saber Mirzaei;M. Saeed Mirzaei;Jian Yin;Yen-Hsu Lin;Caden Myers;Cheng-Hung Lin;AM Milinda Abeykoon;Simon J. L. Billinge;Omar M. Yaghi
