title: Predicting Cognitive Tasks from Single-Channel EEG through Task-Semantic Alignment
abstract: Studies of data scaling in electroencephalography (EEG) and related noninvasive recordings suggest that simple wearable devices could eventually reveal more about cognitive states. However, publicly available EEG data are difficult to combine. Different laboratories record different tasks, participants, and devices. Task-agnostic self-supervised learning can exploit such data, but representations learned only with EEG signals have not consistently produced feature representations that are directly effective for decoding the cognitive state. We therefore aimed to incorporate task information by embedding experimental instructions, stimuli and response demands in a common semantic space, and trained an EEG encoder to align signals from a single anterior--posterior differential channel with those task vectors. This framework supports zero-shot prediction without target-condition calibration and few-shot prediction using labeled samples. On a reserved ten-class evaluation, the highest observed zero-shot balanced accuracy was 30.13% (chance 10%). In a separate developmental few-shot experiment, balanced accuracy reached 34.47% using 16 labeled EEG examples per class from another participant, and 74.99% using examples from the test participant's own task recording. Our experiments suggest that training models on datasets with multiple tasks per participant appeared useful, whereas adding datasets containing only one or a few tasks sometimes reduced established performance despite broader task coverage. These exploratory results suggest that EEG datasets that repeat varied cognitive tasks and everyday activities within the same individuals across days, devices and independent studies would be particularly useful for training an EEG foundation model for predicting cognitive states.

title: Role of defect trapping in the enhanced corrosion resistance of Ni-Mo alloys with yttrium and yttrium oxide additions
abstract: Corrosion of structural alloys remains a critical challenge for advanced molten salt reactors, where aggressive fluoride salts promote continuous dissolution at the salt-metal interface. While most mitigation strategies emphasize thermodynamic stability, kinetic control of atomic transport has received comparatively less attention. Here, we propose a corrosion mitigation strategy based on diffusion control and vacancy trapping by dilute yttrium (Y) solutes and yttrium oxide (Y$_2$O$_3$) dispersions in Ni alloys. A combined computational and experimental approach integrates density functional theory (DFT), self-consistent mean-field (SCMF) diffusion modeling, and an impurity trapping model to quantify the impact of defect trapping on effective vacancy mobility. Strong first-nearest-neighbor vacancy-Y binding, off-lattice vacancy configurations, and elevated rotational and dissociation barriers result in pronounced suppression of vacancy diffusivity, while Y$_2$O$_3$-associated sites treated as fixed traps in the model further reduce the mobile vacancy population. Ni-Mo (NM), Y-modified (NMY), and Y$_2$O$_3$-containing (NMYO) alloys were tested in molten fluoride salt at 750°C. Corrosion penetration decreases systematically from NM to NMY to NMYO, consistent with the predicted reduction in vacancy-mediated transport. The same trend is observed in mass change, with net weight loss decreasing from 0.52% for NM to 0.23% for NMY and 0.09% for NMYO. These results are consistent with an alloy-side transport contribution from defect trapping and reduced atomic transport. This study therefore suggests point defect engineering as a promising alloy design strategy for extreme nuclear environments.
authors: Jia-Hong Ke;Xinchang Zhang;Jingfan Yang;Qiufeng Yang;Ruchi Gakhar;Rongjie Song

title: On the minimizer of the barycentric isoperimetric ratio among connected planar sets
abstract: Among connected, planar sets, the ratio between the isoperimetric deficit and the squared barycentric asymmetry is known to be bounded from below by a strictly positive constant (as proved in recent papers by Bianchini-Croce-Henrot and Gambicchia-Pratelli). This opens the natural question whether the infimum is attained at some set. In this paper, we prove that a minimizer for this ratio actually exists, and moreover it is simply connected.

title: Duality Theory for Filter Stability in Hidden Markov Models
abstract: This article is concerned with the problem of nonlinear (stochastic) filter stability for a discrete time hidden Markov model (HMM) with finite state and observation spaces. For this purpose, a comprehensive duality theory is developed whereby the dual control system is a backward stochastic difference equation (BSDE). The duality is expressed in two inter-related forms. In its variational form, the minimum mean squared error of optimal filtering equals the value of a dual optimal control problem. In its structural form, controllability (resp. stabilizability) of the BSDE and observability (resp. detectability) of the HMM are dual properties. The dual optimal control problem supplies the Lyapunov function and the dissipation: the former is the value function (a variance), the latter the optimal running cost accumulated over the horizon. The main result is an invariance principle: under any one of three model properties---ergodicity of the Markov matrix, or observability or detectability of the HMM---zero dissipation over a finite horizon forces the Lyapunov function to vanish. A converse is also obtained: detectability is necessary. Two applications are given. The first is filter stability in chi-squared divergence: the invariance principle is applied in the manner of LaSalle, to limits of trajectories along which the dissipation vanishes asymptotically, the role of the model properties being to render the zero-dissipation set trivial. The second is a quantitative form of the invariance principle, through a Poincare constant, from which convergence rates follow. Both the model properties that govern stability and the Lyapunov function that certifies it are thus obtained from a dual optimal control problem, as in the classical theory for the linear Gaussian model.

title: UAV-Mounted Hybrid RIS-Assisted ISAC-RSMA: Performance Analysis with Imperfect CSI and SIC
abstract: In integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, strict sensing requirements can substantially constrain the transmit power available for communication. A hybrid reconfigurable intelligent surface (HRIS) with passive reflection and active amplification capabilities mounted on an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) can enhance coverage and strengthen communication links in such power-limited regimes. Meanwhile, rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) provides an effective transmission strategy for managing inter-user interference, particularly in dense multiuser wireless scenarios. Motivated by this, we analyze the performance of a UAV-mounted HRIS-assisted monostatic ISAC system employing RSMA scheme. We consider the imperfections in the channel state information and successive interference cancellation in the RSMA, which are inevitable in practical system implementations. We then derive highly accurate expressions for outage probability, ergodic rate, and throughput to evaluate communication performance over Nakagami-$m$ fading channels. These expressions reveal key insights into the diversity order and coding gain of the system in the high signal-to-noise ratio regime. To characterize the sensing performance, we derive expressions for the probability of detection, the probability of false alarm, and the Cramér-Rao lower bound. Numerical results validate the theoretical findings and highlight the performance gains of the proposed system over conventional multiple-access schemes and RIS-based systems.
authors: Chandan Kumar Singh;Arthur Sousa de Sena;Smriti Uniyal;Deepak Kumar;Prabhat K. Upadhyay;Matti Latva-aho

title: The NIVARIA-Local Group simulations: Unveiling the origin of rotation curve diversity in dwarf galaxies and its connection to galaxy morphology
abstract: Dwarf galaxies exhibit a large diversity in rotation curve shapes, challenging galaxy formation models within the $Λ$CDM paradigm. We present NIVARIA-LG, a new suite of cosmological simulations studying dwarf galaxy evolution in realistic Local Group environments. This intermediate-resolution pilot lays the groundwork for the full-scale NIVARIA project. The simulations combine constrained Local Group initial conditions from HESTIA with the NIHAO galaxy formation model. The simulated galaxies reproduce observed stellar-to-halo mass relations, match the Baryonic Tully-Fisher relation, and capture the distribution of stellar effective radii, including compact and diffuse galaxies. We analyse the structural and kinematic properties of isolated dwarf galaxies with $10^7 \lesssim M_\star/M_\odot \lesssim 10^{10}$, focusing on rotation curve diversity. NIVARIA-LG naturally produces a broad range of rotation curve shapes, including slowly rising systems underrepresented in previous simulations and steep rotation curves. We find that rotation curve diversity is primarily associated with gas extent and inner dark matter structure: more extended gas and shallower inner density profiles correspond to more slowly rising curves, while stellar effective radius shows little independent association. Individual galaxies show that rotation curve shapes change rapidly as gas is redistributed during assembly. Recent accretion events are also associated with more slowly rising curves in the most massive dwarfs. Together, these results suggest that rotation curve diversity is linked to the baryonic cycle, which shapes the inner dark matter distribution. The Local Group environment and its filaments influence this evolution by regulating gas accretion and redistribution, producing the observed diversity in rotation curve shapes.
authors: A. Contreras-Santos;A. Di Cintio;A. Negri;J. Sarrato-Alós;S. Cardona-Barrero;G. García-Bethencourt;C. Brook;N. I. Libeskind;A. Knebe;A. Macciò

title: Randomized Experiments with Ambiguous Record Linkage
abstract: Randomized experiments are often linked to administrative data to measure outcomes, but coarse identifiers can leave multiple administrative records consistent with each experimental unit. We show that unbiased estimation of the sample average treatment effect is possible without resolving these ambiguous links or specifying an outcome model. Our key linkage requirement is that the true administrative outcome is contained among the candidate outcomes for each experimental unit. We characterize the precision cost of linkage ambiguity and study two complementary ways to mitigate it: regression adjustment and reweighting based on observed linkage characteristics. We establish finite-sample and asymptotic properties of these estimators and develop valid randomization-based and large-sample inference.

title: On the Structural Optimization of Industrial Control Systems Using Metaheuristic Algorithms
abstract: The paper addresses the synthesis of a cost-optimal hardware architecture of the automated process control system (APCS) for continuous processes. The problem is formalized as the search for a minimum-cost rooted tree of devices subject to constraints on the number of I/O channels, the types and number of communication interfaces, the information capacity of processors, the regulation time and the reliability. The signals are grouped by control rooms. The problem is NP-hard, and a hybrid method is proposed that combines a deterministic hierarchy construction with a modified ant colony optimization (ACO) for device-type selection, enhanced by an adaptive heuristic. On ten instances the method is compared with a genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm optimization (PSO), simulated annealing (SA) and CP-SAT over 30 runs each. By the best found cost the hybrid ACO outperforms GA, PSO and SA on all instances with more than 100 IOs (by 14-38 %) and runs 9-14 times faster. By the median cost, however, the deterministic-greedy baselines are more reliable (GA attains the best Friedman rank) because the cost of the ACO runs is highly variable. All differences are confirmed by the Friedman and Wilcoxon tests. The method targets the early-design search for the cheapest feasible architecture and synthesizes one within minutes at industrial scale (A up to 1086).

title: Multilevel Monte Carlo for Zeroth-Order Stochastic Bilevel Optimization with Inexact Lower Level Solves
abstract: Variational regularization techniques are dominant in the field of mathematical imaging. The expressiveness of these methods heavily depends on the adopted regularization formulation which usually involves a number of parameters which have to be fine-tuned by the user. To circumvent the heavy computational costs associated with this parameter tuning, data-driven learning strategies have turned out to be a useful strategy. Selecting parameters by learning from data gives rise to a hierarchical (bilevel) optimization problem, which is in general computationally hard to solve. Our aim in this paper is to develop a data-efficient solution strategy for the bilevel learning problem. To that end, we propose a multilevel Monte Carlo derivative-free optimization method that couples Gaussian smoothing of the upper-level objective (parameter selection) with a hierarchy of lower-level (variational regularization) solution accuracies. Being agnostic towards the specific way the lower-level problem is solved, we derive explicit oracle complexity and computational cost statements for approximately solving the entire bilevel learning problem. Our statements are parameterized by the employed lower-level solution method, thus allowing for a direct cost accounting from the variational reconstruction method to the parameter selection problem. This enables us to give a universal end-to-end complexity analysis of bilevel learning, valid for the most important optimization routines in inverse problems, rather than for a specific choice of methods.
authors: Neil K. Chada;Mohammad S. Salehi;Mathias Staudigl;Simon Weissmann

title: Sparsity Saves Compute, Not Samples: Oracle Inequalities for Dense and Sparse Mixture of Experts
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models combine specialized experts through an input-dependent routing mechanism, and their sparse variants underpin many modern large-scale systems. Yet the statistical cost of adaptive routing remains only partially understood. We study the estimation error of least-squares MoE estimators when both the experts and the gating network are Lipschitz in their parameters. We represent each MoE as a gate--expert pair in a Gated Hilbert Space, whose norm $\|\cdot\|_Δ$ separates the contributions of routing and expert discrepancies. Using its empirical representation, we derive an oracle inequality with a fast rate of order $\tilde{\mathcal O}\big((Kd_{\mathrm{pr},e}+d_{\mathrm{pr},g})/n\big)$ for dense MoEs with $K$ experts. For sparse Top-$k$ and Top-$p$ routing, the selection map is discontinuous in the gating parameters. We handle this by partitioning the gating class according to the selection patterns it induces on the sample. The resulting bounds match the dense rate up to an additive routing cost governed by the Natarajan dimension of the selector. We show that such a routing-complexity condition cannot be dropped: Lipschitz continuity in the parameters alone does not suffice. For linear softmax gating, the routing cost is of the same order as the gating term. Finally, for linear experts, we establish a matching minimax lower bound of order $Kd_{\mathrm{pr},e}/n$, showing that the rates are optimal up to logarithmic factors.

title: Training-Free Multi-Agent Cooperative Embodied Search from Uncertain Vision-Language Priors
abstract: Real-world Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) requires agents to act under partial observability, where map structure, semantic cues, and target locations may be incomplete or incorrectly inferred by foundation models. This paper presents a lightweight, training-free, and uncertainty-aware framework for cooperative multi-agent multi-target search in mapless environments. Instead of learning an end-to-end navigation policy, the framework separates high-level semantic reasoning from low-level execution through a scalable graph-optimization backbone. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) serve only as hypothesis generators, proposing semantic zones, target-location cues, and possible navigable connections. These outputs are treated as uncertain priors and further refined using online observations and graph-context evidence. Cooperative navigation is then formulated as a rolling-horizon multi-agent mixed-integer linear program with a lexicographic objective that first maximizes target-directed reward and then reduces travel distance, uncertain-edge use, and repeated visits. Experiments derived from 100 Matterport3D test cases show that the proposed framework improves target coverage and search efficiency over representative baseline methods, while shared information and joint planning enable more balanced workloads across agents. By operating on an abstract graph without relying on embodiment-specific policy parameters, the framework scales across varying numbers of agents and targets, generalizes to unseen environments, and accommodates different perception modules and low-level controllers without task-specific retraining.
authors: Fan Pu;Keshu Wu;Jiwan Jiang;Shiyu Shen;Zhiwen Fan;Zhengzhong Tu;Jiachen Li;Yang Zhou

title: Photometric Identification and Dynamical Purification of Blue Horizontal Branch Stars in DESI MWS DR1
abstract: Blue horizontal-branch (BHB) stars are ideal tracers for mapping the structure of the Galactic stellar halo. However, traditional spectroscopic identification is limited by data quality and sample size, while broad-band photometric methods often achieve only moderate completeness and purity. Building upon the color-space BHB identification method of \citet{2025ApJS..278...62H}, we synthesize SkyMapper $(u,v,g,z)$ photometry from DESI MWS DR1 spectroscopy and identify 9,237 BHB candidates in the $(g-z)_0$--$(u-v)_0$ color space using the HDBSCAN clustering algorithm. We then construct a Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) Bayesian probability model with capture-recapture (C-R) prior to assign posterior membership probabilities, achieving a probability-weighted purity of 88.9\% and completeness of 94.2\%. Applying an escape-velocity cut based on the Galactic gravitational potential, we remove 1,461 contaminants with unphysical kinematic parameters, yielding a clean photometric BHB sample $\mathcal{S}_c$ of 7,776 stars (retention rate $R_{\rm keep} = 84.2\%$). Systematic analysis of the contaminants reveals that they are predominantly faint sources ($g\sim20$~mag) with very low signal-to-noise ratios (median SNR~$<$~5). When the BHB color--luminosity relation is incorrectly applied to these objects, their space velocities are amplified beyond the Galactic escape limit, confirming that the escape-velocity filter essentially acts as a physical detector of low-SNR--driven distance inflation.
authors: Shuai Zhang;Xiaolong Wang;Kai Xiao;Guozhen Hu;Wenyuan Cui;Ce Cai;Shuai Feng;Jie Ju

title: Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection: Statistical Properties and Distributionally Robust Optimization
abstract: We study Markowitz's mean-variance portfolio optimization problem. When practically using this model, the mean vector and the covariance matrix of the assets returns often need to be estimated from the sample data. The sample errors will be propagated to the optimization output. In this paper, we consider three commonly used mean-variance models and build the asymptotic properties for the conventional sample approximations that are widely adopted and studied, by leveraging the stochastic optimization theory. We show that for all three models, under certain conditions the sample approximations have the desired consistency and achieve a convergence rate of square root of sample size, and the asymptotic variance depends on the first four moments of the returns. To address the variability and the uncertainty in the data driven portfolio optimization, we further consider the distributionally robust optimization (DRO) for the mean-variance model. For the ambiguity sets constructed by the $φ$-divergence and the Wasserstein distance, we build the tractable reformulations for the DRO models. We conduct numerical experiments to test the asymptotic properties for the estimation. We also conduct experiments to illustrate that the asymptotic normality might not hold when the fourth moments of the returns do not exist.

title: Graphene-Confined Growth of Few-Layer PtSe2 via One-Step Selenization
abstract: Platinum diselenide (PtSe$_2$), a member of the transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) family, is a promising material for next-generation electronic and optoelectronic applications due to its thickness-dependent properties, transitioning from semimetallic in bulk to semiconducting behavior at the few-layer limit. However, the scalable fabrication of large-area ultrathin PtSe$_2$ films remains challenging, as conventional selenization of pre-deposited Pt layers often leads to undesired three-dimensional clustered growth. This work explores a novel strategy for promoting two-dimensional growth of PtSe$_2$ by employing a graphene-mediated confinement approach. The method involves coating a Pt layer with graphene oxide (GO), followed by annealing in a selenium atmosphere, which results in the simultaneous formation of PtSe$_2$ and the reduction of GO to graphene. The graphene overlayer acts as a physical confinement layer, suppressing vertical growth and enabling the synthesis of graphene-confined PtSe$_2$ heterostructures on centimetre-scale substrates and promoting lateral connectivity of PtSe$_2$ regions observed by STEM. Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), including temperature-resolved in situ atomic-resolution measurements, was used to investigate the influence of selenization temperature on the growth mechanism and structural evolution of PtSe$_2$ films. The results show that graphene confinement stabilizes lateral growth and promotes the formation of few-layer films with improved structural ordering. Beyond PtSe$_2$, this graphene-assisted approach provides a general strategy for fabricating and stabilizing ultrathin TMD layers, including those prone to environmental degradation, providing a new outlook for enabling detailed studies of their intrinsic properties.
authors: Timea Ema Krajčovičová;Peter Kotrusz;Viera Skákalová;Agáta Laurenčíková;Igor Píš;Martin Hulman;Kimmo Mustonen;Michaela Sojková

title: An Exact Branch-Price-and-Cut Algorithm for a Truck-as-Hub Vehicle Routing Problem with Drones
abstract: Rural last-mile logistics remains challenging because of sparse demand, limited road infrastructure, and long travel distances. We study a Truck-as-Hub Vehicle Routing Problem with Drones in Rural Areas, in which multiple trucks each carry a dedicated fleet of drones. Drone launch and retrieval are restricted to predesignated passive synchronization pads, where a visiting truck temporarily acts as a mobile hub, may dispatch multiple drones simultaneously, and must wait until all launched drones return before continuing its route. We formulate a mixed-integer quadratic programming model that jointly accounts for customer delivery delays, truck return times, and operating costs. To solve the problem exactly, we transform the original truck--drone network so that each feasible route can be represented as a single path and develop a branch-price-and-cut algorithm with tailored pricing, cutting, branching, and parallel-computing procedures. Computational experiments show that the proposed algorithm proves optimality for most large-scale test cases and achieves optimality gaps of no more than 4% for the remaining cases, whereas Gurobi reaches the 1,800-second time limit on all large-scale instances when applied directly to the compact formulation. Sensitivity analyses show that drone operating costs and managerial priorities substantially affect drone utilization and customer delays, providing practical guidance for balancing service quality and operating cost in rural delivery systems.
authors: Fan Pu;Sivakumar Rathinam;Yunlong Zhang;Xiaopeng Li;Xiubin Wang;Yang Zhou

title: The Galactic disk structure revealed by Gaia XP spectra
abstract: The spatial structures of chemical populations constrain Galactic disk evolution and its underlying physical processes. Gaia XP spectra provide one of the largest spectroscopic samples available. We use Gaia XP spectra to study Galactic disk mono-abundance populations (MAPs), measuring their scale heights as a function of radius and radial surface-mass-density profiles. We construct a red giant branch (RGB) sample and divide it into MAPs according to $[α/{\rm M}]$ and $[{\rm M/H}]$. The sample covers a $6\times6$ kpc region centered on the Sun in the Galactic plane and extends to $|Z|<3.7$ kpc. We estimate XP completeness using a Gaia photometric parent sample and combine PARSEC isochrones with a Kroupa initial mass function (IMF) to calculate the selection function and convert observed stellar counts into intrinsic stellar mass densities. We fit vertical density profiles with an exponential model to derive scale heights and integrate the fitted profiles to obtain surface mass densities. The resulting profiles are generally consistent with those from APOGEE. All MAPs show flaring, with the high-$α$ population exhibiting the strongest flaring and the metal-poor and sub-solar low-$α$ populations showing the weakest. Surface-mass-density profiles differ significantly among MAPs: the high-$α$ and metal-rich low-$α$ populations show approximately exponential declines, whereas the other low-$α$ populations exhibit plateau-like features, indicating that the Galactic disk cannot be described by a simple single-exponential profile. These differential structures suggest a complex Galactic disk assembly history likely regulated by birth conditions, secular dynamical heating, radial migration, and external perturbations.

title: Bayesian adaptive design for neural recruitment curves
abstract: Nonlinear response models remain ubiquitous across disciplines with recruitment curves describing muscle response to neural stimulation. Conventional acquisition methods typically rely on static uniform sampling, requiring many stimuli, while adaptive threshold-hunting designs such as ML-PEST forfeit accurate characterization of the overall curve. We present a Bayesian adaptive design that uses posterior uncertainty over curve parameters to propose stimuli that maximize information gain across the full recruitment curve. We additionally implement a focused acquisition method that can target arbitrary subset of curve parameters, which we use to evaluate and interpret our design. In simulations, our design outperforms uniform sampling in recovering threshold while matching ML-PEST, and outperforms ML-PEST in predictive curve accuracy while matching uniform. It likewise matches our threshold-focused acquisition, suggesting our design doesn't trade off threshold estimation for recovering the curve. We further show data collected using our design yields greater power when detecting a change in threshold in intervention studies. Our design proposes the next stimulus within 5 seconds, making it feasible for transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) experiments. Finally, we validate our design in TMS experiments and provide a library for Python, called onMEP, for online acquisition of neural recruitment curves.
authors: Vishweshwar Tyagi;Saihari S. Dukkipati;Daniel Twili;Jonas M. Mikhaeil;Andrew Gelman;Jason B. Carmel;James R. McIntosh

title: DiffGA: Steering Frozen Diffusion Models for Materials Design via Evolutionary Search
abstract: Steering candidate generation toward user-defined objectives is central to inverse materials design, yet remains difficult when objectives are black-box, changing, or non-differentiable, as in many simulation- and experiment-derived properties. Generative models offer a solution but typically require retraining or fine-tuning for each new objective, demanding labeled data and substantial compute, or rely on differentiable guidance that is brittle to gradient noise and undefined for many practical targets. We present DiffGA, a retraining-free framework that injects evolutionary search into the sampling trajectory of a retrained diffusion model, evolving partially denoised states under an arbitrary black-box oracle. Because oracle evaluation often dominates campaign cost, we couple DiffGA with an on-the-fly Bayesian surrogate that reuses representations from state-of-the-art machine-learned force fields (MLFFs). A Gaussian process is fit during the campaign on the force fields's graph embeddings and, once it demonstrably ranks an unseen generation, replaces expensive property evaluations under an uncertainty-aware acquisition rule, reducing oracle cost with negligible loss of accuracy. Across three crystal-design tasks using a frozen MatterGen backbone, DiffGA outperforms diffusion-only, compute-matched, purely evolutionary, and fine-tuned baselines in oracle-assessed rates of stable, unique, and novel hits. Rather than proposing scientific compounds, we use density functional theory to quantify MLFF oracle fidelity, showing that it is a faithful proxy in key regimes but systematically biased in others, delineating when proxy-driven generative discovery can be trusted. On a representative sample, DiffGA's top hits survive first principles re-evaluation as physically realistic hits, while the surrogate-accelerated pipeline preserves this fidelity at a fraction of the cost.
authors: Shivang Agarwal;Rodrigo Wang;Kevin Ryczko;Aayush R. Singh

title: EpNet-Si: Atomic Form Factors Learned from Band Structures
abstract: The empirical pseudopotential method (EPM) computes band structures with one diagonalization per $k$ point and no self-consistency, but its fixed atomic form factors do not transfer between crystal structures. To address this limitation, we introduce EpNet-Si, an EPM for silicon in which an equivariant network predicts each atom's plane-wave form factor from its local environment: a species potential plus monopole, dipole and quadrupole corrections, mixed by a learned router over atomic densities, together with an $s/p$ nonlocal projector. With 6{,}195 parameters, the model is trained through the eigensolver on reference density functional theory (DFT) band energies of only 77 cells. Among 231 distortions of the trained structure types, the 142 gapped cells have mean band and gap errors of 15 and 8\,meV; among 192 unseen structures, the 165 gapped cells have mean errors of 38 and 49\,meV. Physical properties derived from EpNet-Si, including effective masses, gap pressure coefficients, deformation potentials and the density of states at the Fermi level, agree with those obtained from the reference DFT calculations. These results suggest that the classical EPM, fitted to a small set of reference data, can be extended into a fast alternative for modern electronic band-structure calculations.

title: Characterizing the Separability Gap in Prior-Data Fitted Networks
abstract: Prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) are transformers pretrained on simulated datasets to approximate Bayesian posterior predictive distributions. Standard PFN theory assumes a separable task prior, under which the feature distribution and the mechanism generating labels from features are independent. We show that common PFN priors are non-separable, even in simple settings. Consequently, standard pretraining targets a predictive distribution based on a task posterior updated using both the labeled context and the query features. We characterize its difference from the predictive based on the context posterior alone and show that this difference vanishes under posterior concentration. Under misspecification (i.e., when the true joint distribution lies outside the prior's support), however, prior non-separability can favor better feature fit at the expense of conditional label fit. We illustrate the consequences for feature attribution, Bayesian optimization, and martingale checks of Bayesian behavior. The same dependence also enables PFNs to learn from additional unlabeled observations. We demonstrate this with SemiTabICL, a PFN explicitly pretrained to use these observations, which improves accuracy over a matched supervised baseline. Our findings highlight the need for explicit rules on unlabeled data use in PFN evaluation and establish the dependence between feature and label distributions as a consequential prior design choice.

title: Mixing Regularization for Average-Reward $Q$-Learning and $Q$-Planning
abstract: The average-reward setting for reinforcement learning is challenging because, without discounting, the span-contraction of the Bellman operator depends on the mixing properties of the underlying Markov dynamics. Whereas existing work typically assumes contraction, for instance through environment mixing, we study regularization toward a given reward-agnostic, $m$-step mixing policy to control the mixing properties of the learned policy. Our central mixing lemma quantifies how the reference policy's mixing properties transfer to the resulting learned policies. In particular, a single regularizer-dependent quantity simultaneously controls the contraction of the regularized Bellman operator and the exploration of the resulting policies. A second regularizer-dependent quantity controls the bias introduced by regularization, revealing a trade-off between convergence speed and approximation accuracy. Building on this result, we establish finite-time guarantees for regularized $Q$-iteration, synchronous and single-trajectory $Q$-learning, and $Q$-planning. Under one-step mixing, our bounds for approximating the regularized fixed point match the classical model-query bound for relative value iteration and, up to logarithmic factors, an existing sample-complexity bound for synchronous $Q$-learning. We also establish finite-time guarantees under multi-step mixing. For $Q$-planning, we characterize how the planning horizon trades off boundary bias against sample complexity. Finally, we present numerical studies validating the analysis: (i) knowledge of a strong mixing policy improves convergence and exploration, with larger benefits under more severe bottlenecks; and (ii) the observed rankings of $α$-divergence regularizers by bias and convergence speed are consistent with our theoretical analysis.
comment: 10 pages main body, 58 pages references and appendix, 11 figures. Under review

title: The $R$-Process Alliance: On J0010$-$1735, an Accreted, Chemically Unusual, Metal-poor Star with $R$-process Enhancement
abstract: We present a detailed chemo-dynamical analysis of the chemically peculiar very metal-poor ([Fe/H]$=-2.22\pm 0.11$) Milky Way (MW) halo star, 2MASS J00101758$-$1735387 (hereafter J0010-1735), discovered by the $R$-Process Alliance. We derive abundances for 45 elements, including 28 neutron-capture elements, and confirm that \thestar\ is highly $r$-process-enhanced, with [Eu/Fe]=$+1.30$. The light, $α$, and Fe-peak element abundances ratios relative to Fe are all sub-solar, aside from C, Si, and most extremely, Ca. We investigate three possible formation scenarios based on the star's chemical abundances and orbital kinematics: whether it formed in the \textit{in-situ} MW halo, in a MW dwarf galaxy satellite, or in a satellite of the Magellanic Cloud system. Using the position of \thestar\ in the [Mg/Mn]--[Al/Fe] plane, the abundance pattern of both the light and heavy elements, and the kinematics, we conclude that J0010-1735 most plausibly originated in a now-disrupted ultra-faint dwarf galaxy that was accreted into the MW halo. We examine potential chemical enrichment scenarios of J0010-1735, including one similar to the $r$-process-enhanced UFD Reticulum II, or enrichment via a sub-Chandrasekhar Type Ia SNe, potentially supplemented by a Ca-rich gap transient and by a separate neutron-rich site that facilitated $r$-process enrichment. A nuclear cosmochronometric age of $12.5\pm4.2$ Gyr is derived from the [Th/Eu] ratio, consistent with an ancient origin in one of the earliest star-forming systems in the universe.
authors: Zoe Hackshaw;Rana Ezzeddine;Shivani P. Shah;Terese T. Hansen;Ruijie Shi;Yangyang Li;Timothy C. Beers;Anna Frebel;Erika Holmbeck;Alexander P. Ji;Jeremy Kowkabany;Vinicius M. Placco;Ian U. Roederer;Charli M. Sakari

title: Time-temperature-composition equivalence of the glass transition in digitally mixed 3D-printed polymers
abstract: For more than seventy years, time-temperature equivalence (TTE) has enabled a few measurements to describe the linear viscoelasticity of polymers over many decades of frequency. Multimaterial 3D printing now combines elastomeric and glassy resins voxel by voxel into digitally mixed polymers. Composition shifts the glass transition along the frequency axis, as temperature does, but also broadens it and increases the rubbery plateau modulus. A translation, the only operation of TTE, cannot capture these changes. Here we establish a time-temperature-composition equivalence (TTCE) from dynamic mechanical measurements of five compositions of a printed family. A shift of the transition along the reduced-frequency axis, a stretch of its breadth and a normalization between its plateaus collapse the storage modulus onto one master curve. The collapse holds at every measured temperature, frequency and composition, through a single reduced variable. The position and breadth of the transition change linearly with the volume fraction of the glassy resin. The phase angle and the relaxation spectrum superpose with the same parameters, so the family shares one distribution of relaxation times. The resulting closed form gives the storage and loss moduli continuously in composition, temperature and frequency, and quantitatively predicts two further mixtures withheld from the calibration. The same shift, stretch and normalization also collapse published temperature sweeps of a patterned composite family of different resins, pointing to broader applicability. Composition thus joins temperature and frequency as a third variable of one equivalence, and the closed form can guide the design of graded and architected printed structures.
authors: Beijun Shen;Sanat K. Kumar;Mary C. Boyce
comment: 15 pages, 6 figures; Supporting Information appended (7 pages)

title: A Unified Kalman-Type Classification of Controllability for Linear Stochastic Systems
abstract: We provide a unified algebraic classification of approximate controllability, approximate null controllability, exact null controllability, and exact controllability for finite-dimensional linear stochastic control systems with constant coefficients and multidimensional Brownian noise. The controls may enter both the drift and the diffusion terms, and the joint diffusion-control matrix may have arbitrary rank. A finite decreasing sequence of subspaces defines a common geometric obstruction. Its vanishing characterizes the two approximate properties and exact null controllability. Exact controllability to arbitrary random targets additionally requires the joint diffusion-control matrix to be surjective. The codimension of the obstruction is given by a rank difference of explicit polynomial block matrices, yielding finite tests in the original coefficients. When the joint diffusion-control matrix is surjective, we obtain a finite Kalman-type full-rank condition for exact controllability. If the obstruction vanishes, a linear state feedback with a deterministic time-dependent gain drives every initial state to zero at any prescribed positive time with finite energy and polynomial small-time cost. An equivalent orthogonal elimination algorithm computes the rank differences with polynomial storage and cost, avoiding exponentially large block matrices. A two-noise example relates the input classification to terminal errors and control energy in penalized stochastic linear-quadratic control problems.

title: Risk-Constrained MPPI Tuning with Update-Aware MA-ES Racing
abstract: We formulate offline tuning of Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) controllers as a chance-constrained black-box optimization problem and develop an update-aware framework based on Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (MA-ES). We use statistical information from noisy controller evaluations to determine when the evolutionary update is sufficiently reliable. When the recombination direction is certified, a derivative-free nonmonotone line search (NMLS) is used to refine the candidate solution, and a separate validation stage assesses the final frozen controller. We establish a worst-case arithmetic-complexity bound for both online MPPI control and offline tuning. Numerical experiments on TurtleBot 4, Jackal-like, and Ackermann models show that the proposed NMLS refinement is competitive with standard MA-ES, transfers across the three vehicle models without model-specific retuning, and improves several cost and validation measures. Both MA-ES variants also compare favorably with the tested randomized derivative-free line search (VRBBO) configuration. The results support the practical applicability and transferability of the proposed framework, while not claiming universal superiority or hardware-level safety.

title: Non-convex integer programming: a deterministic solution method of the large block sale problem
abstract: We study a non-convex, nonlinear integer mathematical program with a linear constraint. This problem originates in finance and consists of selling a large predetermined quantity of a financial asset over a fixed time horizon, while maximizing the total proceeds. The selling price is modeled using a deterministic penalty function capturing the market's adverse reaction to the selling flow. From a complexity perspective, the problem is in NP. We first solve the problem exactly using dynamic programming and propose several heuristics that yield tight numerical lower bounds. We then reformulate the problem into an equivalent factorable form and derive a tight convex relaxation using McCormick inequalities. This relaxation is embedded within an adapted Branch & Bound algorithm to find the global optimum in finite time. Numerical experiments show that our methods outperform several widely used generic solvers (LocalSolver, Scip, Baron, Couenne, and Bonmin) for selected instances, but do not yield tight upper bounds, beyond small instances.

title: Investigation on Thermal Stability of Epi-GeSn Directly on Si (001)
abstract: In this paper we investigate the structural properties and thermal stability of metastable Ge1-xSnx epilayers (~4.5 at.% Sn) grown directly on Si(001) substrates by high-resolution X-ray diffraction (HRXRD) and Raman spectroscopy. Our results demonstrate that both 70 and 140 nm films are fully relaxed, with the thicker film exhibiting a small tensile strain (+0.09%). The thermal stability of the heterostructures was evaluated up to 813 K using temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy and scanning electron microscopy. The surface-weighted Raman response (532 nm excitation) and surface morphology of the 70 nm film remain highly stable. In contrast, the 140 nm film undergoes severe degradation, characterized by significant attenuation and broadening of the Ge-Ge longitudinal optical phonon mode, alongside enhanced surface Sn segregation. These findings demonstrate that the thermal stability of direct GeSn/Si heterostructures is governed by the initial defect structure established during epitaxial growth, providing key design rules for understanding the fabrication of GeSn-based optoelectronic devices.
authors: Tharundev V;Dushyant Singh;Vigneshswari SR;Subha Maity;Prince Rathor;Krista R Khiangte

title: Compositional Average Velocity Modeling for Efficient Diffusion Offline Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Diffusion-based policies have recently emerged as a powerful paradigm for offline reinforcement learning, but their reliance on multi-step denoising introduces substantial computational overhead and requires backpropagation through time during training, limiting scalability and practical deployment. In this work, we propose \textbf{Instant Flow Q-Learning (InsQL)}, a single-step generative policy learning framework that retains the expressive capacity of diffusion models while eliminating iterative sampling and BPTT. InsQL builds on the flow-matching perspective of diffusion policies, but replaces marginal velocity parameterization with \emph{average-velocity} modeling and introduces a principled compositional mechanism, yielding a theoretically grounded objective that learns average velocity consistently across scales. This formulation provides a direct noise-to-action mapping and enables single-step action generation. InsQL further unifies compositional average-velocity modeling with behavior-regularized actor--critic optimization in a single framework, requiring only a single policy network and avoiding distillation, multi-stage procedures, and Jacobian computations during training. At inference time, actions are generated in a single forward pass and can be refined via value-guided candidate selection to improve performance. Extensive experiments on standard offline RL benchmarks and real-world robotic manipulation tasks show that InsQL matches or surpasses state-of-the-art diffusion-based methods while substantially reducing both training and inference time. Overall, these results establish compositional average-velocity modeling as an efficient and scalable alternative to multi-step generative policies for offline RL.
authors: Thanh Nguyen;Abu Hanif Muhammad Syarubany;Hwanhee Kim;Chang D. Yoo

title: Predicting how model propensities generalize out of distribution
abstract: How do language models generalize from their training data? This is a central challenge for alignment: models reliably learn their training distribution given enough samples, but we want models that behave well when deployed in new contexts. We study out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization of propensities. Our central experiment uses a range of elicitation techniques -- system prompting, few-shot learning, SFT on reference answers, and GRPO -- to increase a target propensity in a model, then measures how it spills over onto others across the resulting cross-elicitation matrices. We find that spillover is highly correlated between models when the same elicitation technique is used, but our SFT and GRPO runs induce different spillover profiles. Elicitation of benign traits can sometimes generalize towards undesired traits, for example a model trained to claim that it is sentient often becomes more power-seeking. We further find that spillover partially resembles trait correlations found in humans and identify three clusters of traits that account for about half of the variance using exploratory factor analysis (EFA). Across many elicitation runs, we observe that models change in characteristic ways that don't depend on the targeted trait, a phenomenon we refer to as drift. Drift moves Qwen3.5-9B towards its base model. When investigating if LLMs are able to predict spillover, we find that Claude Opus 5.5 predicts spillover slightly better than the models themselves, but worse than data-driven approaches using alternative elicitation methods or models. Overall, no single dominant predictor emerges, and generalization remains hard to predict. Code and data are available at https://github.com/nielsrolf/propensity-spillover.
authors: June Hunter;Lily Wen;Owen Terry;Johannes Taraz;Ben Cohen;Niels Warncke

title: Full Lyapunov Spectra of Random Neural Networks, Part I: Finite-Time and Asymptotic Theory
abstract: We develop a dynamical mean-field framework for the full finite-time and stationary asymptotic Lyapunov spectra of random recurrent neural networks. At finite observation time, an exact log-determinant representation of tangent-propagator singular values leads to a closed-contour matrix Dyson equation for the smoothed spectral tail. In the stationary setting, a cocycle representation yields an operator equation for the asymptotic cumulative spectrum. Both formulations retain complete local gain histories and the repeated action of quenched connectivity. Direct singular-value calculations and network QR spectra support the predictions in the regimes examined, with sampling uncertainty and numerical cutoffs assessed separately. The stationary equation also recovers the known maximal exponent, and controlled gain-history replay illustrates how temporal correlations redistribute instability. This work was carried out in collaboration with ChatGPT 5.6 Sol. Toward the end of preparation we became aware of David G. Clark's contemporaneous work, \emph{Lyapunov spectrum of random neural networks}[arXiv:2610.12426], which reports overlapping mean-field results for the full Lyapunov spectrum using a cavity approach.

title: Pressure-Driven Evolution of the Physical Properties of Layered Y2GaB and Y2InB MAB Phases: A Comparative First-Principles Study
abstract: MAB phases are nanolaminated ternary borides in which strong in-plane M-B bonds and weaker interlayer interactions drive their distinctive stability and functionality. Hydrostatic pressure offers a direct route to tune the in-plane and interlayer interactions that govern the stability and functionality of layered Y2GaB and Y2InB borides. Here, first-principles calculations are used to compare their structural, elastic, thermophysical, electronic, bonding, optical, and vibrational responses from 0 to 20 GPa. Elastic criteria show that Y2GaB is stable at 0, 5, and 10 GPa, whereas Y2InB is stable only at ambient pressure. Within the stable Y2GaB range, compression increases the elastic moduli, acoustic velocities, Debye temperature, and lattice thermal conductivity while reducing the elastic anisotropy. Both compounds are multiband metals and spin-orbit coupling modifies local dispersions without opening a gap. Y2GaB retains nine Fermi-surface sheets from 0 to 10 GPa, whereas Y2InB has eight at ambient pressure, with no pressure-induced topological reconstruction. Charge-density and overlap analyses indicate mixed ionic-covalent Y-B bonding within a delocalized metallic background. Optical parameters are anisotropic. Unit-cell phonon spectra contain positive frequencies at 0 and 10 GPa, although expanded-supercell calculations reveal low-frequency sensitivity. These results establish mechanically viable pressure windows and clarify substitution-driven structure-property relationships for these borides.
authors: M. Rabi Us Sani Shapon;Md. Asif Afzal;Jubair Hossan Abir;Raihana Shams Islam;Saleh Hasan Naqib

title: Minimum Volume Optimal Transport for Multivariate Conformal Prediction
abstract: Optimal transport (OT) enables multivariate conformal prediction (CP) to construct flexible prediction sets that reflect the underlying complex distributional geometry while retaining distribution-free coverage guarantees. Existing OT-based methods typically rely on a fixed Euclidean transport cost, which can be suboptimal in terms of the volume of prediction sets. We propose Minimum-Volume OTCP, a framework that learns a Mahalanobis ground cost to directly minimize prediction-region volume over a class of positive-definite metrics. Using a metric Brenier representation, we derive a volume-based objective that depends explicitly on the Mahalanobis cost matrix and optimize it jointly with the transport map. We establish finite-sample marginal coverage of the output prediction sets and optimality of volume metrics. We further develop an individualized extension that learns covariate-dependent transport metrics, adapting the shape and orientation of prediction sets to heterogeneous conditional distributions. For this extension, we also show the asymptotic conditional coverage of our method. Simulations and real-data experiments demonstrate substantial reductions in prediction-set volume.
authors: Chuchen Zhang;Haojie Ren;Zhaojun Wang;Yajie Bao;Changliang Zou

title: Spiral Edge States in Topological 2D Sb2Te3 Crystals
abstract: This work explores the edge state conduction properties of twinned and spiraled, 2D Sb2Te3 topological insulator crystals. We show the structure supports spatially continuous edge states within two spiral and knotted edge conduction channels. The channels are connected through a topological defect. This geometry introduces boundary conditions into the 2D crystal that modifies the edge state dispersion. Using a combination of low loss Electron Energy Loss Spectroscopy, Magnetic Force Microscopy and traditional carrier transport measurements we identify a distinct excitation at 0.155 eV in the spiral that seems to be related to two isolated states within the gap. This state is localized to the crystal edges. The modification of edge state bands using manipulation of a systems quantum geometry may open new avenues for the use of 2D topological systems.
authors: Timothy Carlson;Daniel Lazega;Scott McGuire;Mihirangi Medahinne;Motahhare Mirhosseini;Gabriel Marcus;ChaoChao Dun;Maria Kolesnik-Gray;Vojislav Krstic;David Carroll

title: Prediction with Expert Advice under Heavy-Tailed Losses
abstract: We study prediction with expert advice over $T$ rounds with $K$ experts under heavy-tailed losses whose $(1+ε)$-moment is bounded by $θ>0$ for some $ε\in(0,1]$. In this setting, existing algorithms designed for the case $ε=1$ can be suboptimal when $ε<1$, suffering an additional polynomial dependence on $K$. We characterize the minimax pseudo-regret rate as $Θ((θT)^{\frac{1}{1+ε}}(\log K)^{\fracε{1+ε}})$ and establish gap-dependent lower bounds in a self-bounded environment. To attain this minimax rate without prior knowledge of either $ε$ or $θ$, we propose Adaptive Heavy-Tailed FTRL, which uses robust data-dependent scale adaptation together with truncation. We further develop Adaptive Heavy-Tailed OMD, which likewise requires neither $ε$ nor $θ$ and achieves near-optimal regret guarantees in both adversarial and self-bounded environments. Finally, when $ε$ and $θ$ are known, an FTRL algorithm with Shannon-entropy regularization achieves optimal regret guarantees in both environments.

title: Pressure-transferable universal machine-learning potentials: the WBM-MatPES benchmark and Tuga-FF
abstract: Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials hold the promise to replace costly ab initio calculations in materials science workflows. However, the accuracy and transferability of current models are limited by the availability of training data. We release WBM-MatPES, a dataset of 182 thousand structures recomputed with consistent MatPES settings, together with two reference convex hulls of different depths and test sets at six pressures up to 150 GPa. These datasets reproduce a realistic discovery workflow and allow potentials to be ranked systematically at this level of theory, similar to the Matbench Discovery leaderboard at the Materials Project settings. In this benchmark, five published MatPES potentials agree within 12 meV/atom at 25 GPa, yet their errors increase dramatically to 0.4-5 eV/atom at 150 GPa. To address this limitation, we develop Tuga-FF, a graph transformer trained on datasets spanning ambient and high-pressure configurations alike. Tuga-FF is the most accurate model in the benchmark at ambient pressure, with an energy error of 13.6 meV/atom, and maintains an error of just 21 meV/atom at 150 GPa. We believe this benchmark will encourage the community to train higher-accuracy models and generate richer datasets, advancing machine-learned interatomic potentials as a whole.
authors: Pierre-Paul De Breuck;Thalis H. B. da Silva;Antoine Loew;Silvana Botti;Miguel A. L. Marques

title: Relining or Replacement: How Timing, Costs, and Infrastructure Shape U.S. Primary Steel Decarbonization
abstract: Imminent blast furnace relinings create a consequential investment window for U.S. primary steel decarbonization. Using plant-level capacity planning and stochastic operations modeling, we quantify the costs, infrastructure, and fiscal requirements to transition legacy blast furnace sites to direct reduction under supply-side incentives. Under baseline assumptions, post-subsidy premiums above average blast furnace costs, including relining, are 272 to 427 dollars per ton of steel for near-zero-emission hydrogen-based direct reduction and 115 to 181 dollars for natural-gas-based production. Representative facilities producing two million tons of steel annually at legacy locations require approximately 4 to 6.5 and 0.7 to 1.1 GW of renewable generation and battery storage, respectively. This translates to 65 and 12 GW across the unrelined fleet for hydrogen- and natural gas-based pathways, respectively. These findings connect replacement timing to costs, infrastructure, and public support, motivating a sequenced transition through clean-powered natural-gas-based direct reduction to avert blast furnace relining, reduce emissions by 57 percent relative to blast furnaces, and preserve options for deeper decarbonization through hydrogen substitution or carbon capture.

title: An Adaptive Cyber-Resilient Framework for P2P Energy Trading under Optimal Stealthy Attacks
abstract: The increasing adoption of peer to peer energy trading has enabled prosumers to actively participate in decentralized energy markets. However, the growing dependence of P2P energy markets on communication infrastructures and distributed coordination mechanisms introduces an expanded cyberattack surface, enabling sophisticated adversaries to manipulate market interactions while remaining concealed from conventional detection mechanisms. This paper first designs an optimal stealthy attack that maximizes economic disruption of the MicroGrids, while preserving the apparent convergence characteristics of the ADMM based market-clearing process. To detect such attacks, a Mahalanobis Boosting detector is developed using market layer features to effectively capture inter feature dependencies and distinguish compromised updates from normal market operation. An adaptive rho based mitigation strategy is then introduced to limit the propagation of compromised information and restore robust market operation once an attack is flagged. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through comprehensive case studies, achieving an attack detection accuracy of 98.49% while the proposed mitigation strategy reduces the operating cost by approximately 18.43% compared to the unmitigated attack case. The proposed approach provides a practical pathway toward trustworthy and cyber-secure distributed P2P energy trading systems.

title: Physics-informed random neural architectures on compact boundaryless multiply connected manifolds for random-operator models in machine learning and uncertainty quantification
abstract: We introduce stochastic physics-informed neural networks (SPINNs) for stochastic boundary-value problems (SBVPs) with random operators. The method enforces physics through a structural probabilistic coupling: a common Gaussian stochastic germ drives both the SBVP random operator and a manifold-based stochastic neural architecture. The stochastic neural network is non-feedforward and intrinsically random. A latent Gaussian field and an inhomogeneous Poisson point process on a compact, boundaryless, multiply connected manifold generate random neuron locations, geodesically local sparse connectivity, and a sparse random weight matrix, all governed by a low-dimensional hyperparameter. For deterministic inputs, the network output is random and can represent non-Gaussian random operators. Training is performed in observation space: SBVP simulations produce random observables, while the SNN defines a predictive conditional probability density function. The supervised objective combines data fidelity, through negative log-likelihood, with a cross-entropy alignment term relative to the SBVP-induced conditional distribution. The resulting target is a convex mixture of observation-induced and SBVP-induced distributions, with a dimensionless parameter controlling robustness to model--data mismatch. The shared stochastic germ yields common-random-numbers Monte Carlo estimators and reduced-variance gradients. The method uses only evaluations of the SBVP solution mapping, without differentiating or modifying it, and avoids PDE-residual or boundary-penalty losses. A stochastic elliptic problem on a periodic cylindrical surface illustrates the approach in SBVP-consistent and SBVP-misspecified regimes. A generalized-posterior formulation is also outlined for hyperparameter inference and posterior averaging without per-query reoptimization.
comment: Published in Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering}, doi:10.1016/j.cma.2026.119437, 463, 119437 (2027)

title: Parameter-Free Adaptive Extragradient Methods for Generalized-Smooth Variational Inequalities
abstract: Variational inequalities (VIs) provide a unified framework for optimization, saddle-point, equilibrium, and learning problems, where operators need not be globally Lipschitz. The $α$-symmetric generalized-smoothness condition allows local operator variation to grow with the operator norm, but existing extragradient methods often require unknown problem-specific constants. To address this issue, we propose PF-AEG, an explicit, line-search-free extragradient method whose stepsizes use quantities generated during the iterations, without prior knowledge of these constants. Under $p$-quasi-sharpness, we prove full-sequence convergence and last-iterate squared-distance rates: linear convergence for $0<p\le2$ and $\mathcal{O}(k^{-2/(p-2)})$ for $p>2$. The latter matches existing parameter-dependent rates under comparable assumptions, while the linear guarantee extends the previous $p=2$ result to $0<p\le2$. Building on the idea of PF-AEG, we develop AEG-VR, a variance-reduced adaptive extragradient method for finite-sum VIs. We prove almost-sure convergence and, under mild conditions, obtain analogous expected last-iterate rates, while retaining independence from the unknown problem-specific constants in stepsize selection. Experiments on synthetic generalized-smooth VIs and several learning problems show that the proposed methods are competitive with, and in several tested regimes outperform, existing baselines.

title: Selective faceting induced by Hexagonal Boron Nitride on curved Platinum substrate
abstract: This work combines experimental investigations and first-principles calculations to study hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) growth on a curved Pt(331) substrate. Low-energy electron diffraction (LEED) and scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM) were employed to investigate the structural properties, observing that hBN growth led to faceting with several stable facets: Pt(111), Pt(221), Pt(441), Pt(881), and Pt(110). Additionally, the electronic properties were examined by X-ray photoemission spectroscopy (XPS) and near-edge X-ray absorption fine structure (NEXAFS), revealing an increase in the hBN-substrate interaction strength, from the weakest at the Pt(111) to the strongest at the Pt(110). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that the selective faceting mechanism is induced by hBN, which changes the order of relative stability of the uncovered facets. Although a complete understanding of the process is not achievable using only thermodynamical arguments, the comparison between hBN adhesion energies and clean surface free energies clearly indicates that some facets are stabilized with respect to others by stronger overlayer-substrate interaction, whereas for others the clean surface energetics plays the dominant role.
authors: Alaa Mohammed Idris Bakhit;Muhammad Saad Mahmood;Khadiza Ali;Anna A. Makarova;Igor Piš;Federica Bondino;Frederik Schiller;Maria Peressi

title: Ex Ante and Scenario-Conditional Value of Information in Dynamic Portfolio Choice
abstract: Portfolio decisions are often made under uncertainty about expected returns, and investors revise their beliefs as new information arrives. Although richer information generally cannot reduce optimized value ex ante, the trading strategy it induces need not improve on the strategy induced by a less informative information structure in every fixed-drift scenario. We introduce scenario-conditional expected utility and value of information to evaluate strategies selected under the investor's current belief. In a finite-horizon Gaussian portfolio choice model, we compare a fixed-belief investor, a price observer, and an attentive investor who also processes an auxiliary signal under an attention capacity constraint. Ex ante, price learning and auxiliary attention are valuable, and the total value of attention increases with capacity. Scenario-conditionally, learning creates a correction benefit by reducing the initial trading-position gap relative to the full-information strategy, but also a fluctuation cost through belief revisions, so the ex ante ranking can reverse. We derive the current-belief distribution of scenario-conditional value and the associated underperformance probability, defined as the probability of negative scenario-conditional value relative to fixed-belief choice. Over sufficiently short horizons, the scenario-conditional value of learning is negative when belief error is small relative to posterior uncertainty. For a given horizon, sufficiently high attention capacity yields a higher scenario-conditional value than any fixed finite-capacity benchmark across all drift scenarios. We also derive sharp convergence rates to full-information performance under Shannon and Tsallis technologies.

title: Decision-Focused Learning for Optimal Battery Scheduling Under Load and Photovoltaic Power Uncertainty in Microgrids
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources in microgrids demands accurate day-ahead forecasting to support optimal battery energy storage system (BESS) scheduling. Yet the conventional predict-then-optimize paradigm trains forecasters on statistical accuracy metrics that are agnostic to the asymmetric and time-varying cost impacts of forecast errors. This work proposes a decision-focused learning (DFL) framework that trains gated recurrent unit forecasters for both load demand and photovoltaic generation directly on the downstream operational cost of a two-stage energy management system, where day-ahead BESS commitments are fixed prior to real-time balancing. Gradients are backpropagated from the real-time operational cost through both optimization stages to the forecaster weights via implicit differentiation, enabling the forecasters to internalize the penalty structure of the scheduling problem. The framework is validated on the MG2Lab experimental microgrid testbed at Politecnico di Milano across two operational scenarios of increasing grid constraint and eight forecasting configurations comprising single-source and combined-forecaster settings. Results illustrate that the DFL-trained pipeline reduces operational cost by 3.78% under normal grid conditions and by 30.60% under grid-constrained conditions relative to the accuracy- optimized baseline, while nearly eliminating load shedding events. Notably, the DFL forecasters exhibit higher statistical errors than their accuracy-trained counterparts yet achieve consistently lower operational costs, confirming that forecast accuracy and decision quality do not share a monotonic relationship in constrained microgrid scheduling.

title: A Unified Framework for Randomized Row-Action Methods for Structured Data Fitting and Constraint Geometry
abstract: We study randomized row-action methods for problems with linear observations, convex constraints, and non-Euclidean geometry. Our starting point is a unified formulation in which the data-fitting term acts in observation space, while the feasible set and the regularizer encode structure in variable space. It covers constrained least squares, nonnegative and simplex-constrained models, regularized data fitting, and equality-constrained Bregman selection problems. The structure of these problems leads naturally to two algorithmic branches. The first uses primal Bregman-proximal row steps for soft data-fitting problems. The second uses dual Bregman--Kaczmarz steps for problems with hard equality constraints. We first derive a common one-step inequality. We then give deterministic and stochastic convergence results for the soft branch under relative smoothness. For constrained least squares, the normalized row oracle has exact first- and second-moment identities. They yield an expected ergodic bound in the inconsistent case, an $O(1/K)$ bound in the interpolating case, and linear convergence of the actual iterates under a residual error bound. For equality-constrained selectors, we prove linear convergence in expected Bregman distance under a residual-to-Bregman error bound. We recall global sufficient conditions for this bound and derive local constants for the nonnegative quadratic geometry and the entropy geometry on the simplex. Numerical experiments illustrate the noisy stepsize trade-off and the local entropy selector theory, and show that entropic row-action updates can recover interpretable factors in a simplex-structured nonnegative matrix factorization problem.

title: Inverse Designing Reconfigurable Piezoelectric Tensors via Architectural and Modal Programming
abstract: Piezoelectricity arises from the coupling between electric polarization and mechanical deformation, described by a third-rank tensor whose coefficients are constrained by crystal symmetry. In natural crystals, atomic periodicity and energetic stability restrict accessible symmetries, limited to 20 distinct anisotropies that can exist. Here we establish a general framework, based on graph representation, for controlling the full effective piezoelectric tensor through architecture by resolving how macroscopic symmetry, local polarization and deformation of structural elements act together. This enables each coefficient to be traced to the members that reinforce or cancel it and be controlled through targeted geometric changes. We further uncover frequency-selective tensor reconfiguration, in which excitation frequency switches the dominant piezoelectric coefficients of a single architecture. These principles open a broader class of applications in which a single piezoelectric architecture can deliver programmable sensing, actuation and mode conversion across multiple directions and deformation states. We realize a multi-degree-of-freedom actuator that integrates distinct actuation modes in one block and reduces volume by 90% relative to conventional multi-stack assemblies.
authors: Anish Satpati;Marco Maurizi;Hyunmoon Cho;Victor Couedel;Nicolas Mule;Xiaoyu;Zheng

title: Finite-temperature adiabatic-connection reduced density-matrix functional theory: a unified framework for i-DMFT and TAO-DFT
abstract: Accurately describing chemical bond breaking requires capturing strong/static electron correlation, a major challenge for single-reference self-consistent-field methods such as Hartree--Fock and Kohn--Sham density-functional theory (DFT). Fractional occupations substantially improve this situation, as demonstrated by information-density-matrix-functional theory (i-DMFT) and thermally-assisted-occupation DFT (TAO-DFT). Although useful, they are formulated within rather different theoretical frameworks, are somewhat semi-empirical, and their relationship remains unclear. Here we introduce finite-temperature adiabatic-connection reduced density-matrix functional theory (FT-AC-RDMFT), in which i-DMFT and TAO-DFT emerge as different reductions of a unified framework. The effective eigenvalue equation for natural orbitals and the Fermi--Dirac occupation numbers follow directly from the variational principle, while a thermal adiabatic connection relates the empirical entropy coefficient of i-DMFT to a characteristic temperature of the auxiliary non-interacting system. Within this framework, i-DMFT is the exact-exchange-based reduction, whereas TAO-DFT results when exact exchange is replaced by a density-based exchange-correlation functional. Numerical calculations confirm that i-DMFT, apart from a constant, coincides with the exact-exchange realization of the framework, and show that the improved dissociation behavior from finite-temperature occupations extends beyond exact exchange to hybrid and semilocal density functionals. For strongly correlated V2O3, finite-temperature occupations substantially reduce the severely overestimated non-magnetic LDA bulk modulus, bringing it close to experiment. These results establish FT-AC-RDMFT as a common theoretical foundation for finite-temperature occupation-based electronic-structure methods in molecular and solid-state systems.
authors: Jingang Han;Huanjing Gong;Kai Luo;Hongming Weng;Xinguo Ren

title: Understanding Hidden Spatial Preferences in Bayesian Optimization
abstract: Bayesian optimization uses posterior uncertainty to decide where to explore, but this uncertainty is not spatially neutral. On bounded domains, Gaussian-process posterior variance is typically larger near faces, edges, and corners, giving variance-based acquisition functions a systematic boundary bias. This spatial preference is usually inherited from the surrogate rather than chosen as part of the exploration strategy. We separate these roles by keeping the predictive model fixed and modifying the spatial preference of the exploration term. We control the preference with spatial weight fields and amortize their construction with neural surrogates. Controlled experiments show that the Gaussian process' default boundary bias changes which parts of the domain are explored and which optima are reached. We compare three alternative exploration principles and find, across standard benchmark functions and stochastic robot-pushing tasks, that they can often lower regret, particularly early in the optimization. The spatial structure of posterior uncertainty is therefore not a neutral default: it shapes the exploration strategy and can materially affect optimization performance.

title: Development and operational deployment of a staff rostering system using mathematical optimisation in a municipal water utility
abstract: We developed a staff rostering system for complex employment and staffing requirements at a municipal water utility and deployed it in routine operations at the Water Purification Office of Suita City Waterworks Bureau, Japan, in May 2026. We estimated that preparing a monthly roster took approximately 2-3 h after deployment, compared with 12-18 h previously. The system represents roster states, effective staffing and office assignments using binary and auxiliary integer variables and optimises the entire planning horizon. When the normal model yields no feasible solution, a second stage attempts to generate a reference roster by penalising weekly day-off shortages while retaining the other hard constraints. Outputs identify shortages and meeting-date changes applied before solving. Computational experiments used operational inputs for 14 staff over 245 days. The baseline was solved to optimality in approximately 177 s; a modified meeting-day scenario produced a reference roster with five staff-days of shortage. Independent monthly solving without history produced 16 staff-week cases of excess days off across two month-boundary weeks. This case demonstrates the practical value of optimisation-based decision support for staff rostering in municipal water utilities by showing how mathematical optimisation can be integrated into roster preparation and checking workflows with reduced preparation time.

title: Crossed Electric Spin Generation in Multilayers
abstract: We propose a crossed electric spin generation effect in multilayer structures. This effect combines the advantages of in-plane and gate electric fields for manipulating spin, and unveils a nice quantum geometric structure in terms of the underlying hybrid Berry curvatures that are unique to quasi-2D systems and manifest inherent spin-layer-orbital coupling. Combining our theory with first-principles calculations, we predict sizable spin generation in 2D ferromagnetic Fe3GeTe2 and altermagnetic V2Te2O. Our theory opens a new Berry-curvature route for all-electric spin manipulation in 2D materials
authors: Xukun Feng;Wei Du;Jin Cao;Qian Niu;Shengyuan A. Yang;Cong Xiao

title: Euler Cutting Planes for Fractional CVaR Programming
abstract: We maximise expected reward per unit of marginal tail risk, a reward-to-CVaR ratio against a baseline. The standard Dinkelbach route re-solves a Rockafellar--Uryasev LP or QP with one auxiliary variable per tail scenario at each multiplier update. Our method eliminates the multiplier iteration and keeps scenario auxiliaries out of the master, while still evaluating tail risk to generate cuts. A Charnes--Cooper/Schaible homogenisation removes the reward/risk multiplier, and the remaining convex constraint is separated on demand: each cut coefficient is an Euler allocation vector, read off a ranking and an average. The result is a single convex program, finitely terminating at the global optimum, with size independent of S --- an LP in $M{+}1$ variables, or a second-order cone program in $M{+}2$ for a concave quadratic numerator. The method runs 20--100 times faster than the exact Dinkelbach formulation and only needs single-digit cut counts.

title: Multiphase Analysis of (U)LIRG Nuclear Activity (MAUNA). I. Spatially Resolved Optical Emission-Line Diagnostics
abstract: We present resolved optical integral-field spectroscopy of the 32 luminous and ultraluminous infrared galaxy systems of the Multiphase Analysis of (U)LIRG Nuclear Activity (MAUNA) sample, drawn from the GOALS survey and selected to have JWST/MIRI medium-resolution spectrometer (MRS) observations. The data set combines new Keck/KCWI observations of 10 systems with archival VLT/MUSE cubes for 22 systems, covering H$β$ to [S II] at ~1 arcsecond spatial resolution (~0.9 kpc at the sample median distance). Using the optical [N II]/H$α$ BPT diagram, we find that composite and LINER-like excitation together account for most of the classified area (median fractions 0.44 and 0.26), while Seyfert-like gas covers a median fraction of 0.02 but carries a far larger proportion of the line luminosity where it is present. Both the projected size of the Seyfert-classified region, $R_{\rm Sy}=0.08$-$7.5$ kpc, and its [O III] luminosity increase with the bolometric AGN luminosity, with $R_{\rm Sy}\propto L_{\rm AGN,bol}^{0.54\pm0.18}$, as expected for gas photoionized at a constant ionization parameter. The scatter about the luminosity relation depends on dust opacity: the [O III] luminosity per unit AGN luminosity falls by $1.09\pm0.25$ dex per unit depth of the 9.7 $μ$m silicate absorption feature (Spearman $ρ=-0.60$, $p=0.001$). Optical excitation diagnostics therefore locate AGN-excited gas reliably but systematically underestimate the luminosity the AGN supplies to the host in the most obscured (U)LIRGs.
